_about: Astral space generator lists. environments: the kinds of place a space can be, each with read-aloud text, senses, rooms, features, hazards and the creature types that live there. traps, quirks, features, dressing, passages and doors are shared building blocks; bossRooms and endings describe the heart. {dc}, {dmg} and {half} are filled in from the space's rank. themeWords and themeFeatures are keyed by essence name, with 'default' as fallback. roomTypes with a weight can appear in middle rooms. puzzleBank holds whole puzzles (riddle, mechanism or split clues) with setup, clues, solution, hints (the app sets each hint DC by rank), failure, reward, table (how to run it at the table) and stuck (a way to force through); a puzzle with vary (lock, sigil, tally, houses, sins, lanterns, scale, gauges, sigils, furnace, floor or cells) gets its numbers, patterns and answer rolled fresh each time.

origins.text: Natural: it formed where the world's magic runs thin against the astral.
Charted and licensed by the Adventure Society; a permit is required to enter.
Unclaimed and unknown to the Society; whoever found it is keeping quiet.
Owned by a great house, which sends its young here to train.
A Magic Society research site, with notes left behind by the last team.
Made. Something built this place deliberately, and the workmanship matches other spaces the Builder cult has an interest in.
Sealed for centuries; it opened during the last surge and no one knows why.
Collapsing: it will close within days, with anyone still inside.
Natural: it grew around a monster core that was never harvested, and that core still beats somewhere near the heart.
Charted by the Adventure Society decades ago, then struck from the records after a whole team vanished inside.
Leased by a merchant consortium that pays Iron-rankers to clear it each month for the monster cores.
A temple claims it as holy ground; robed priests at the entrance ask every visitor to state their purpose.
Formed from a dead adventurer's unspent power; pieces of their gear turn up in the rooms.
Used by the Adventure Society for rank assessments; examiners may be watching from somewhere unseen.
Young and natural: it opened within the last month and its rooms are still settling into shape.
Drifting: its entrance appears somewhere new around Greenstone every few days.
A criminal crew hides stolen goods in the first rooms and does not welcome visitors.
Bound to a noble bloodline; it stays open only while one of the family's heirs is inside.
Ancient: its walls carry carvings from a people who lived here long before the Old City was built.
Seeded deliberately by the Magic Society as an experiment, and the experiment has gone badly wrong.
Twinned: it shares its heart with another astral space, and a second team entered from the far side.
Natural, but someone comes and goes, feeding and tending the monsters like livestock.
Cleared last year, yet it reopened with a new boss; the Society wants to know what changed.
A prison: someone sealed a dangerous being inside long ago, and the seal has cracked.

entrances: A shimmering tear in the air above a delta channel.
A doorframe standing alone in a farmer's field.
The back wall of a flooded cellar in the Old City.
A ring of standing stones that hum at dusk.
A reflection in a still marsh pool that does not match the sky.
A locked door in a Magic Society vault.
The mouth of a cave that was not there last season.
A crack in an old coin-farm wall, leaking pale blue light.
A drainage grate in Greenstone's lower market that breathes warm air at night.
The bottom of a dry well behind a Greenstone tavern, where the stones have turned to glass.
A painted door in the back room of a Greenstone pawnshop that the owner swears he never painted.
A sinkhole in the middle of a Greenstone street, roped off by the city watch.
A sandbar in the Delta that surfaces only at the lowest tide, ringed with dead fish.
The hollow trunk of a Delta mangrove, its roots glowing faintly underwater.
A whirlpool in a slow Delta channel that spins against the current.
The wreck of a river barge in the Delta whose hold opens onto somewhere far larger.
A patch of marsh where the reeds grow in a perfect spiral around a pool of mist.
A marsh hut on stilts whose only door opens onto a different sky.
A drowned shrine in the marshes, its archway visible only when the fog is thick.
A floating island of peat that drifts toward anyone carrying a spirit coin.
A collapsed bathhouse in the Old City whose deepest pool has no bottom.
A sealed crypt in the Old City, its door scratched from the inside.
An Old City staircase that goes down further than the ground beneath it.
An Old City fountain that runs with silver light instead of water on moonless nights.
A scarecrow in a wheat field whose open coat hides a doorway full of stars.
A farmstead barn door that opens onto cold wind and darkness on the first day of each week.
A circle of flattened crops that appeared overnight, with a hole of light at its centre.
A millpond where the wheel turns backward and the water glows green.
A milestone on the coast road with a keyhole carved into its back.
A crossroads shrine where travellers leave coins; the coins slip into a slit of light.
A bridge on the trade road whose shadow on the river below is a doorway.
An abandoned waystation where the hearth never goes out, and the chimney leads down instead of up.
A sea cave reachable only at low tide, where the back wall ripples like water.
A blowhole on the sea cliffs that exhales glittering dust instead of spray.
A sea cave lined with barnacles grown into the shape of an archway.
A grotto behind a waterfall on the sea cliffs, where the falling water parts for anyone who hums.
A hedge maze on a noble estate whose centre is not where the gardener planted it.
A portrait in a noble's gallery that now shows a corridor where its subject used to stand.
The wine cellar of a noble estate, behind a rack of bottles older than the house.
A noble family's private chapel, where the altar slides aside to reveal a pulse of light.
The reflecting pool in a temple courtyard, which shows stars at noon.
A temple bell tower where striking the largest bell splits the air beneath it.
A sealed reliquary in a temple undercroft, guarded by priests who will not say what it holds.
The empty grave of a saint in a temple cemetery, warm to the touch in winter.
A blue rift in a glacier far to the north, weeks of hard travel from any town.
An oasis in a distant desert where the palms cast shadows toward the sun.
A far mountain peak where snow falls upward into a glowing crack.
The heart of an ancient forest far from any road, inside a tree too wide for ten people to circle.
rules: No natural light exists here; every light source burns at half radius.
Gravity shifts every ten minutes; roll a d4 to see which wall becomes the floor.
Those who die here rise as hostile echoes at the next room transition.
The space resets every hour: doors relock and slain monsters respawn at half strength.
Short rests are impossible; the space will not let anyone feel safe.
Spoken lies become visible as drifting smoke.
Healing magic heals the maximum amount, but each heal grants the space's boss 5 temporary hit points.
Essence abilities glow brightly; Stealth checks by essence users have disadvantage.
Spirit coins eaten here work at one rank higher, without the exhaustion.
Time runs differently: each hour inside is a day outside.
Every creature can speak, including the monsters, and they will talk before they fight.
Magic items lose their properties inside but return to normal on exit.
The rooms are bigger on the inside of each door than the outside suggests; travel takes twice as long.
The space is hungry: anyone who leaves without the boss slain loses a random spirit coin's worth of vitality (1 level of exhaustion).
Water flows upward and fire burns cold.
Only one door can be open at a time across the whole space.
Monster cores here are twice as large and worth double.
A countdown voice announces how long until the space closes.
Every footstep echoes a second later from somewhere ahead, telling anything that listens where the party is.
Creatures cannot raise their voices; anything louder than a whisper makes no sound at all.
Each time a creature drops to 0 hit points, the light in every room dims for one minute.
Ranged attacks bend toward the largest creature within 30 feet of the target, whoever that is.
Nobody can sleep here, so long rests are impossible, but each short rest restores one extra Hit Die.
Doors open only for someone who has not attacked anything in the current room.
Monster cores dissolve one hour after harvesting unless kept in salt or running water.
Life affinity abilities are inverted: what normally heals deals necrotic damage, and what drains instead heals.
Every shadow is a separate creature that copies its owner one round late and can be attacked.
Spirit coins cannot be absorbed here; they taste of dust and do nothing.
A natural 1 on an attack roll pulls a minor monster out of the nearest wall.
The space remembers the first name spoken inside and calls every creature by it, including the boss.
Metal slowly warms; after two hours, anyone in metal armour gains 1 level of exhaustion.
Each room is colder than the last, and by the heart, breath freezes in the air.
Invisibility fails here: invisible creatures leave glowing footprints.
Anyone who bleeds leaves a scent trail that every monster can follow.
Teleportation always lands one room further than intended.
Food from outside spoils within an hour, but anything edible found inside is safe.
The boss sees through the eyes of every monster still alive in the space.
Dropped items sink into the floor after one minute and reappear in the heart.
Concentration spells last twice as long, but losing concentration deals 1d6 psychic damage to the caster.
Each time a cache is opened, a monster somewhere in the space grows one size larger.
Wind affinity abilities have double range, while Earth affinity abilities have their save DCs reduced by 2.
Writing fades within minutes, so maps and notes must be kept by memory.
A creature standing on bare stone regains 1 hit point at the start of each of its turns.
Music soothes the monsters: a creature playing an instrument is ignored unless it attacks.
Prayers go unheard; casting a divine spell requires a DC 12 Wisdom check or the slot is lost.
The space floods from the entrance inward, rising one foot every hour.
The way in seals behind the party; the only exit opens when the boss falls.
Gold and silver turn to lead while inside, though they recover their true metal on leaving.
hazards: A floor of thin crystal over a drop; DC 13 Dexterity save or fall 20 feet.
Raw magic leaks from the walls: each round in the room, DC 12 Constitution save or take 2d6 force damage.
Gravity is reversed in half the room.
A corridor that loops; DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) to find the real exit.
Mana-thick air: spell slot spells cost one extra round of concentration to cast.
Spores that cause hallucinations of fallen allies (DC 13 Wisdom save).
Walls that slowly close in; 3 rounds to get through.
A river of liquid magic; touching it restores 1d4 hit points but marks the creature for the boss.
Floor tiles marked with faded runes burst when stepped on; DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} force damage, half on a success.
A curtain of falling ash hides a pit; DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) to notice it, or fall 30 feet and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
Jets of steam blast from cracks every other round; creatures in a jet's line take {dmg} fire damage (DC {dc} Constitution save for half).
A swarm of glass moths shatters on contact; each round in the room, DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} slashing damage.
Black ice slicks a sloping floor; DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) or slide 20 feet into freezing water and take {half} cold damage.
A chandelier of monster bones hangs by a fraying chain; any loud noise drops it, dealing {dmg} bludgeoning damage in a 10-foot radius (DC {dc} Dexterity save for half).
Fog that drains body heat fills the hall; each minute inside, DC {dc} Constitution save or gain 1 level of exhaustion.
Quicksand of powdered crystal: a creature that sinks is restrained and takes {half} piercing damage each round until a DC {dc} Strength check pulls it free.
Lightning arcs between iron pillars whenever someone wearing metal passes; DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} lightning damage.
A pool of mirror-bright liquid; anyone who looks into it must succeed on a DC {dc} Wisdom save or be charmed and walk toward it.
Crystal bells ring when brushed; each chime forces a DC {dc} Constitution save or the creature takes {half} thunder damage and is deafened.
Grasping vines coil around ankles; DC {dc} Strength save or be restrained, taking {half} poison damage at the start of each turn until freed.
Stalactites drop in a rolling sequence across the ceiling; DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} piercing damage.
Corrosive mist hangs at chest height; each round, DC {dc} Constitution save or take {half} acid damage, and nonmagical metal gear takes a cumulative -1 penalty.
The floor tilts toward an open furnace; DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) each round to stay put, or slide 10 feet, taking {dmg} fire damage at the edge.
Shadow tendrils lash from dark corners; DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} necrotic damage and have speed halved until the end of the next turn.
Astral wind sweeps the bridge every third round; DC {dc} Strength save or be pushed 15 feet, likely off the edge.
Radiant runes scorch anyone carrying a monster core; DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} radiant damage.
A cloud of blood-gnats; DC {dc} Constitution save or lose {half} hit points, which the nearest monster gains.
Leaking time pools in the corners; a creature that fails a DC {dc} Wisdom save loses its next turn, frozen mid-step.
Sticky resin coats the corridor; moving through costs triple movement unless a creature succeeds on a DC {dc} Strength check.
A pane of clear glass looks like an open doorway; walking into it deals {half} slashing damage, and a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the real exit.
Crushing pressure presses down from above; each round, DC {dc} Strength save or be knocked prone and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
A whispering voice sows doubt; DC {dc} Wisdom save or be frightened of the nearest ally for 1 minute.
A strong current pulls through the flooded hall toward a grate; DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) each round or be pinned and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
Embers drift from the ceiling and catch on cloth; DC {dc} Dexterity save or ignite, taking {half} fire damage each round until an action puts it out.
Humming crystals resonate with essences; essence users must succeed on a DC {dc} Constitution save or be stunned until the end of their next turn.
Spinning blades rise from slots in a set pattern; DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) reveals it, otherwise DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} slashing damage.
Sleeping gas seeps in when the door shuts behind the party; DC {dc} Constitution save or fall unconscious for 1 minute.
Flesh-eating spores burst from the walls; DC {dc} Constitution save or be poisoned and take {half} necrotic damage at the start of each turn (repeat the save at the end of each turn).
A pressure plate releases a wall of water down the stairs; DC {dc} Strength save or be swept to the bottom, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Gravity is five times stronger along a 40-foot stretch; DC {dc} Constitution save or be restrained there until the start of the next turn.
Statues turn to watch intruders; anyone seen at the end of their turn must make a DC {dc} Constitution save or have speed 0 until their next turn as their skin greys.
Light so harsh it burns the eyes; DC {dc} Constitution save or be blinded for 1 minute unless the eyes are covered.
A ledge crumbles under more than one creature at a time; DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall 20 feet and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
Lodestone walls tear metal weapons from hands; DC {dc} Strength save or be disarmed, the weapon stuck fast to the far wall.
Hair-thin magical tripwires alert the boss unless spotted with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check.
Sound becomes force: casting a spell with a verbal component deals {half} thunder damage to the caster unless they pass a DC {dc} Constitution save.
Living sand slides toward a central maw; DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) to move against it, or be dragged 10 feet, taking {dmg} piercing damage on reaching the maw.
Mirrors release reflections of the party as hostile shades; smashing a mirror deals {half} psychic damage to the creature it showed unless it passes a DC {dc} Wisdom save.
puzzles: Three essence sigils must be lit in the order of a confluence.
A door that opens only for someone who speaks a true regret aloud.
Mirrors that show the room as it was before it was made; the path is only in the reflection.
Pressure plates that must hold the weight of exactly one rank's worth of spirit coins.
A riddle inscribed in a script only Runics can read without a DC 15 Intelligence check.
Floating platforms that move when no one is looking at them.
A locked chest with four keyholes and one key that changes shape each round.
A statue asks for a gift that matches its essence; the right gift opens the way.
A dry fountain with four basins labelled Dawn, Noon, Dusk and Night; pouring water into them in that order fills the central bowl and opens the floor beneath it.
A talking lock answers every question with another question; asking 'What opens you?' makes it reply 'Who asks?', and stating your true name opens it.
Six levers in a ring, each lighting its own lamp and toggling both neighbours; pulling any two levers directly opposite each other lights all six and unseals the door.
A bridge exists only while someone stands on the glowing tile at its start; matching tiles at the midpoint and far end also hold it, so the party crosses in relays.
A carved riddle reads 'The more you take, the more you leave behind.' Answering 'footsteps', or walking backward through the arch, opens it.
Five statues point in different directions and can only be turned while no one is looking at them; one person turns each statue toward the door while everyone else looks away.
A mosaic floor is missing one tile; a monster in the previous room wears it as an ornament, and setting it in place reveals the stairs.
A harp with eight strings sits beneath a carved melody of five notes; playing them as written does nothing, but playing them in reverse opens the door.
A room full of hourglasses; flipping all of them in the same moment freezes the room's time for one minute, letting the party walk past the stilled blades at the exit.
A chest with a mouth asks to be fed and accepts only something that was once alive; a strand of hair, a feather or a leaf will do.
An inscription in a dead tongue (DC 15 Intelligence (History) to translate) reads 'Kneel to rise'; kneeling on the dais lifts it to the upper level.
Two doors guarded by twin masks, one that always tells the truth and one that always lies; ask either 'Which door would the other mask call safe?' and take the opposite door.
Coloured stones on the bottom of a pool spell a word that reads correctly only in the reflection; speaking the reflected word opens the grate.
Sliding tiles form a scrambled star map; matching it to the stars visible through the ceiling dome (DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) per attempt) unlocks the vault.
Four braziers burn red, blue, yellow and white; carrying flame between them to blend a green fire and holding it to the painted door opens it.
A doorway that admits only someone carrying nothing; one person must set down all gear, walk through, and open the latch from the far side.
A sundial in a sunless room; shining any light at the right angle so the shadow falls on the scorched hour mark slides the wall aside.
Weighted chains hang from the ceiling, and pulling one raises its weight and lowers the next; the hatch opens when every weight hangs level, which takes pulling them in sequence from left to right.
A guardian statue asks the party to name what it guards; the answer is 'nothing', since the room behind it is empty and the true path lies beneath its plinth.
Nine pressure plates in a grid, each marked with an affinity; stepping only on those matching the last monster slain lets the party cross safely.
A clockwork bird sings a growing sequence of notes; whistling it back correctly for seven rounds (DC 12 Charisma (Performance) or Intelligence check each round) opens its cage and the key inside.
Masks hang on the wall, each with a different expression; wearing the grieving one, which matches the weeping figure carved on the door, opens it.
A doorway filled with solid darkness parts only for those holding no light; the party must snuff every flame and glow before walking through.
A flooded corridor with an air pocket every 30 feet; a lever in each pocket drains the next stretch, but only if all are pulled within the same minute, so swimmers must spread out and signal.
An altar with a knife and a bowl opens for any blood, but whoever bleeds is marked and the boss knows their name; a slain monster's blood works just as well.
A gallery of portraits whose eyes follow viewers, except one that looks away; pressing on that portrait's frame opens a hidden door.
Floating rings form a lock, and each turns when someone speaks a word with the right number of syllables; saying words of one, two, three and four syllables in order aligns them.
A feast table with one empty chair; sitting there and eating a single bite lowers the floor like a lift to the next chamber.
Three keys hang behind glass marked Iron, Silver and Gold; only the Iron key turns the rusted lock, and the others shatter when tried.
Flowers in this garden bloom in response to sound; humming a single low note opens every bloom at once and reveals a path through the thorns.
Sand pours from the ceiling and the room is filling fast; plugging the four hidden vents in the corners (DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) to find) stops it and uncovers a buried door.
A door with handles on both faces must be turned from each side at once; someone has to wriggle through a narrow crawlspace first (DC 12 Dexterity (Acrobatics)) to reach the far handle.
A beam balanced over a pit tips under uneven weight; the party crosses in pairs, starting from opposite ends and meeting in the middle.
A cracked mirror whose shards each show a different room; fitting them together so they form one complete scene turns the mirror into a doorway.
An answer stone responds only to written words; carving a question into it returns a hint, and carving the word 'open' unseals the vault.
Stepping stones sink under anyone carrying spirit coins; tossing the coins across first, or leaving them on the bank, lets the party pass.
A pipe organ with every pipe sealed in wax; clearing only the pipes stamped with the space's essence symbol and playing any chord opens the wall.
A huge guardian beast sleeps across the door and wakes at any sound; feeding it the glowing fungus from the side passage deepens its sleep long enough to slip past.
A wall carved with the numbers 1, 2, 4, 7, 11 above a row of studs; pressing the stud marked 16 opens it, because each gap grows by one.
A door etched with two monsters locked in battle; striking the stone figure beside it where the carving shows the winning wound swings the door open.
inhabitants: A lost Iron-rank team, out of food and arguing about whether to eat their spirit coins.
An echo of the space's maker who answers one question truthfully.
A Magic Society researcher hiding from whatever lives in the next room.
A friendly native creature that trades in memories.
A Church of Purity inquisitor hunting a cultist who fled in here.
A merchant who sells supplies at ten times the city price, and accepts monster cores.
A child who claims to have been born here.
A rival team led by a confident Bronze-ranker who wants the boss's essence.
A Normal-rank porter abandoned by her team, guarding their packs and hoping someone will escort her out.
An elderly hermit who walked in decades ago and trades a map of the next three rooms for news of Greenstone.
A talking monster cub whose mother is the boss; it begs to be carried somewhere safe before the fight.
A temple acolyte praying in a side chamber, convinced this place is a test of faith and refusing to leave without a relic.
A Delta fisher who rowed in by accident and wants help finding his boat, which is somewhere inside.
A disgraced Silver-ranker living as a recluse, offering advice on the boss if the party never mentions him to the Society.
The ghost of a scholar desperate to finish her book, who wants a description of every room the party has seen.
A merchant's apprentice whose master was eaten; he will hand over his whole stock to anyone who gets him home.
A sentient suit of armour that longs for a wearer and will fight for one battle if someone puts it on.
A magpie-like native creature that hoards shiny things and will trade a key for any piece of jewellery.
Twin heirs of a noble house, each blaming the other for getting lost; they will pay handsomely, but only if both make it out.
A monster that has learned to speak and only wants to be left alone; it knows a shortcut to the heart.
A wounded Adventure Society surveyor who needs healing and wants her measurements delivered even if she dies.
A tinker assembling a device from monster parts, who will let the party use it if they bring her three cores.
A choir of tiny light spirits whose singing keeps monsters at bay; they ask the party to relight their dying lantern.
A marsh witch who sells potions of uncertain effect and accepts payment only in secrets.
A smuggler sitting on a crate of contraband, offering a cut if the party forgets they saw him.
A sleepwalking farmer from the fields outside, wandering in a trance; waking him without care (DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine)) sends him screaming into the next room.
A being made of the space's essence that asks why the party came, and lets only honest answers pass.
A spirit bound inside an oil lamp who promises safe passage through one hazard if someone breaks the lamp.
A former cultist who fled her order and wants protection from the people hunting her.
A gambler who has bet heavily on the party surviving and offers healing potions to improve his odds.
A giant crab with a cracked shell that wants help evicting a monster from its home cave.
Two Bronze-rank lovers who eloped through the portal and now want an escort out, without anyone telling their families.
A Magic Society cartographer stuck reliving the same ten minutes until someone hands her the right page of her journal.
A starving monster too weak to fight, offering the boss's weakness in exchange for a meal.
A small clockwork servant still laying tables for a master long dead, who pours tea for anyone polite.
A temple archivist searching for a stolen holy text the boss is said to keep in its hoard.
A rival team's healer who walked out after a quarrel and wants to join the party for the boss fight.
A fungal colony that speaks through drifting spores and wants a sample carried out so it can spread.
A wandering knight under a vow of silence who draws in the dust to talk; he wants a worthy sparring match, not a fatal one.
The echo of a drowned sailor in a tidal chamber, asking for her ring to be returned to her daughter.
A dealer in awakening stones of dubious origin, who will swap one for a monster core of higher rank.
A frightened giant who means no harm and wants help pulling out a thorn the size of a spear.
A pair of Adventure Society examiners grading the party in secret, who reveal themselves only if someone is about to die.
A heron-headed being guarding a bridge, who asks each traveller for one honest compliment.
An old adventurer who claims she was the first ever to enter this space and wants to see the heart one last time.
A temple guardian slowly turning to stone, who asks to be carried into the light before the change finishes.
A swarm of mice sharing one mind, which knows every tunnel and offers guidance for a handful of grain or cheese.
A noble's hired bodyguard separated from his charge, who will fight beside the party until they find the missing heir.
restPoints: A quiet grove where short rests work normally.
An abandoned camp with supplies for one meal.
A spring whose water counts as a coin of the drinker's rank for food.
A sealed chamber where nothing can enter for one hour.
A dry alcove behind a waterfall whose roar hides every sound; short rests here cannot be interrupted.
A ring of pale stones that monsters will not cross for one hour.
A hollow in a fallen tree, lined with soft moss and big enough for four to sleep.
A tiny chapel with a candle that never burns down; anyone who rests here regains one extra Hit Die.
A pocket of warm air above a hot spring; a short rest here removes one level of exhaustion.
An old Adventure Society supply cache with bandages, rope and three days of rations.
A dead end where the walls fold shut behind the party and open again after exactly one hour.
A grove of luminous fruit; eating one restores 1d4 hit points, once per person.
A cottage that looks exactly like someone's childhood home, quiet and safe for one short rest.
A still pool that reflects the stars outside; gazing into it for a minute ends the frightened condition.
A treehouse high above the floor, reachable with a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) climb, beyond the reach of anything below.
Old bedrolls around a cold fire pit, beside a note warning visitors not to stay past the second hour.
A softly humming crystal chamber; a spellcaster who short rests here recovers one expended spell slot of 2nd level or lower.
An abandoned monster den, warm and dry, its lingering scent keeping other creatures away.
A shrine with an offering bowl; leaving a spirit coin guarantees a short rest with no wandering monsters.
A hidden ledge overlooking the next room, where the party can rest and scout at the same time.
A meadow of soft grass under a false sky; long rests work here, but take twelve hours.
A toppled wagon full of dried goods and a kettle, enough for a hot meal for everyone.
An eddy of slow time where an hour of rest passes as a single minute outside.
A cistern of clean water and a stone bench scratched with tally marks from earlier visitors.
bossFlavors: The guardian is bound to the space's core and grows stronger as it is damaged.
The boss speaks with the voice of whoever made this place.
Two creatures share one life; both must fall in the same round.
The boss is the space itself, and the room fights back.
The boss is wounded from a recent fight; someone else got here first.
The boss offers a bargain before fighting.
The boss heals while standing in the light of a central crystal; smashing the crystal (AC 15, 30 hit points) ends the healing.
At half hit points the boss splits into two smaller copies, each with half its remaining health.
The boss is chained to the floor; every chain broken frees it further, but also weakens the space around it.
The boss clutches a living hostage, so area attacks risk killing them.
The echoes of every adventurer who died here rise to fight beside the boss.
The boss is asleep; a quiet party gets a surprise round and overhears it muttering about escape.
Sections of floor collapse into the void each round, shrinking the battlefield.
The boss copies one ability of whoever last damaged it and uses it on its next turn.
The boss cannot be harmed while its servants live, and they are hiding around the room.
Each hit on the boss splashes essence that forms a minor minion at the start of the next round.
The boss was once an adventurer, still wearing a tarnished Society badge on its armour.
The boss shifts affinity each round, gaining resistance to that affinity's damage type.
The heart crystal pulses every third round; all creatures make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {half} force damage.
The boss stays calm until someone touches the treasure it guards.
The boss fights from a moving platform that circles the chamber, in and out of reach.
A second boss arrives halfway through, drawn by the noise, and the two monsters hate each other.
The boss steals the voice of the first creature it hits; that creature cannot speak until the boss falls.
The boss is invisible and can be seen only in reflections on the flooded floor.
At low health the boss begs for mercy and offers to reveal a secret about the space's origin.
The boss is a small, frail creature piloting a huge shell; cracking the shell exposes the real target.
The boss reforms one minute after dying unless the final blow carries a specific affinity hinted at in the room.
The party's own spells trigger the boss's lair actions, turning their magic back against them.
The boss guards a clutch of eggs; destroying them enrages it, while sparing them makes it fight defensively.
The first time the boss drops to 0 hit points, time snaps back one round.
An ancient oath forces the boss to answer three questions truthfully before it may attack.
Each time the boss falls below a quarter of its hit points, it grows a new head or limb and gains an extra attack.
The room is dark except for the boss's own glow, and looking directly at it requires a DC {dc} Constitution save against blindness.
The boss is a corrupted temple guardian, and a presented holy symbol makes it lose its next attack.
Any monsters left alive in the space feed the boss 10 temporary hit points at the start of each of its turns.
The boss is already locked in battle with a rival team, who may help the party or turn on them.
specialRewards: A map fragment pointing to another astral space.
A journal that hints at who made this space.
A cloud-substance cloak or tool, worth a lot to a crafter.
A sealed letter addressed to someone in Greenstone.
A rare crafting material that the Magic Society will pay well for.
An unidentified magic item of a rarity matching the space's rank.
A brass key on a tag stamped with an address in the Old City.
A Delta smuggling crew's logbook listing hidden caches along the channels.
A stoppered vial of liquid shadow that a Dark affinity crafter would pay dearly for.
A letter from a noble house promising a favour to whoever returns it.
A monster hide that never gets wet, ideal for crafting cloaks.
A partial map of the Old City sewers marked with three red circles.
A bone flute that calms marsh beasts when played.
A Magic Society seal good for one free consultation with a senior scholar.
A jar of embers that never go out, prized by smiths.
The diary of a missing adventurer, giving the location of their last camp.
A pouch of seeds that grow overnight into glowing vines.
A plain ring that hums faintly near other astral spaces; whatever else it does is unclear.
A sheaf of contracts showing a Greenstone merchant buys monster cores without a licence.
A carved token that a temple will accept in place of a large donation.
A shard of the heart crystal, still warm, useful in ritual magic.
A bundle of feathers that shift colour in the light, sought by fletchers and tailors.
A spool of astral spider silk, stronger than steel wire.
A small locked box that no key will open; something inside rattles.
An adventurer's badge from a rank the Society has no record of.
A compass that points to the nearest monster core instead of north.
A favour from a native creature, who promises to help once if called by name.
A preserved monster eye that a Magic Society alchemist wants for research.
A star chart of the astral marking the way to an uncharted space.
A noble's signet ring, lost decades ago, with the reward for its return still posted.
A sealed bottle of seawater that shows shipwrecks when held to the light.
A stone tablet bearing half the recipe for a powerful elixir.
A cracked mask that briefly lets the wearer see through illusions, and may hold more power once mended.
A list of names, some crossed out, of people the boss has taken.
A whetstone carved from a monster's tooth that never wears down.
A sealed invitation to a secret auction in Greenstone next month.
Three ingots of a blue metal that rings like a bell when struck.
A pressed flower that never wilts, said to bring luck to its bearer.
The deed to an abandoned farm outside the city, signed but never registered.
An armour pattern sewn into the lining of an old coat.
A small statue of a forgotten saint that a temple will badly want back.
A fishing net woven from glowing thread that draws Delta fish to it.
A cage holding a tiny native creature that could be tamed or sold.
A mirror shard that, for a heartbeat, shows the face of whoever made this space.
A bag of sand that weighs nothing and holds heat for days.
A torn page from a Society ledger proving a charted space was falsely reported empty.

atmosphere: The air tastes of static and old coins.
Darkness here has weight, and it presses on lanterns.
Shadows move a moment before their owners.
The walls pulse slowly, like something asleep.
Everything smells of iron and warm rain.
Every reflection here looks disappointed in you.
Voices confess crimes no one here committed.
Heat rises in waves and the ground glows through cracks.
Ash falls like snow and never settles.
Water hangs in the air in slow, floating globes.
Every surface is slick and every sound echoes like a cave.
The stone hums underfoot, and crystals light the way.
Dust drifts upward from the floor.
Islands of rock drift through a sky with no ground below.
The wind never stops and never comes from the same direction twice.
Light here is solid enough to lean on.
There are no shadows, which is more unsettling than it sounds.
Runes crawl across the walls like ants.
Spells cast here leave glowing afterimages for minutes.
Everything moves: floors, walls, even the doors.
Time stutters, and the same second sometimes repeats.
Everything is built for someone three times larger.
Distant impacts shake dust from the ceiling.

default: A room of smooth, seamless stone with no visible source of light
A long hall lined with empty pedestals
A round chamber with a dome of slowly turning stars
Dark: Pools of liquid shadow that swallow thrown objects
A chamber where light only reaches 5 feet
A gallery of statues facing the walls
A corridor of black glass that shows other people's reflections
Ropes of shadow hanging from an unseen ceiling
Blood: A chamber with veined, warm walls that flinch at blades
A shallow pool of red water that is not quite blood
Thorny vines with red fruit that heals and hungers
An altar stained a hundred times over
A ribbed tunnel that pulses slowly
Sin: A courtroom with no judge and a waiting dock
A treasure room where all the gold is painted lead
A confessional booth with a voice inside
A banquet hall with a feast that tastes of ash
Chains hanging from every wall, some still warm
Fire: Rivers of lava with narrow stone bridges
A forge still burning with no smith
A field of black glass that cracks underfoot
Pillars of flame that rise and fall in a rhythm
A library where the books burn but never turn to ash
Water: A flooded hall where the water is waist-deep and still
A waterfall that falls upward into darkness
A chamber of floating water globes holding small fish
A sunken chapel with air pockets
Coral grown into the shape of furniture
Earth: A cavern of glowing crystals that ring when struck
A quarry with half-carved giant statues
A chamber where the floor slowly rises and sinks
Roots of an impossible tree threading through rock
A geode the size of a house, open on one side
Wind: Floating stepping stones over an endless drop
A tower room with all its walls missing
A tunnel where the wind pushes everyone back
A chamber of chimes that play warnings
A cloud bank solid enough to walk on, mostly
Light: A chamber of mirrors that focuses light into beams
A garden of white flowers that turn to follow movement
A stained-glass hall that tells a story no one remembers
A room so bright it counts as heavily obscured
A fountain of light that pours like water
Magic: Shelves of books that rearrange themselves
A spinning orrery of the astral
A lattice of glowing threads that must be stepped through
A room where every spell's runes hang visible in the air
Swift: Rotating floors like the gears of a clock
A racetrack with lanes of different speeds
Doors that open only for a moment each round
A room where everything happens twice
A hallway that is longer when you run
Might: Giant weapons embedded in the walls
An arena floor with old bloodstains
Pillars thick as towers holding a sagging ceiling
A training hall with stone dummies that hit back
A stair built for giants, each step four feet high

bossRooms: A vast cavern with a glowing crystal hanging from the ceiling, its light swelling and fading like breath. Beneath it, the boss lies coiled around a ring of stalagmites.
Black stone forms a circular arena scarred with claw marks, and the boss stands at its centre among scattered bones.
Knee-deep water fills a long hall, and at the far end the boss lies half-submerged, only its eyes catching the light.
In a throne room of rusted iron, the boss sits on a seat welded together from broken weapons.
Hundreds of floating candles light this chamber, guttering whenever the boss shifts its weight.
Roots twist around a pulsing heart inside a hollow tree the size of a cathedral, and the boss rests in the branches overhead.
Channels of molten metal criss-cross the floor of a great forge where the boss hammers at something not yet finished.
Sunlight pours through walls of coloured glass onto the boss, kneeling before an empty altar.
A spiral stair descends into a pit of mist, ending at a single pillar where the boss waits.
Torn pages carpet a ruined library, and the boss perches on a mountain of paper at its centre.
Under a sky of cold stars, the boss paces a frozen lake, cracks spreading wherever it steps.
Cages hang from chains throughout the chamber, most empty, a few holding bones, and the boss sleeps in the largest.
Red petals fall like rain over a garden of thorned roses, where the boss tends the flowers with long, careful claws.
Golden eyes painted on every wall stare at the doorway, and the boss stands motionless in the middle of the room.
The ceiling opens onto a churning astral sky, and wind howls around the boss on a raised dais.
Rotten food is heaped along a banquet table, and the boss sits at its head as if waiting for guests.
Shattered idols and splintered pews fill a temple sanctuary, the boss looming behind the cracked altar.
Waves roll onto a beach of black sand from nowhere, and the boss rises dripping from the surf.
Giant gears turn in the walls with a deafening tick, and the boss is built into the central mechanism.
The party emerges on a narrow ledge high above a pit floor strewn with glowing monster cores, where the boss waits.
Every pane in this hall of mirrors holds the boss's reflection, but the creature itself is hard to find.
Standing stones ring a hilltop beneath a blood-red moon, and the boss sits cross-legged in their centre.
Over a lake of liquid light, the boss floats in the air, its outline blurred by the glare.
Chandeliers sway in a ruined ballroom while the boss dances alone to music only it can hear.
Dark water surrounds a small marsh island where the boss crouches on a mound of moss and bones, reeds whispering around it.
Carved faces cover every wall, mouths open in silent screams, and the boss stands among them with its arms raised.
Lightning flashes around an open tower top, where the boss grips the spire with taloned feet.
An underground river roars through the cavern, and the boss straddles the stone bridge that spans it.
Rows of open coffins line a crypt, and the boss stands upright in the largest sarcophagus as though it has just woken.
Stars turn slowly across a vast dome, the space's heart floats at its centre, and the boss is curled protectively around it.
endings: The walls begin to crumble, and a glowing portal tears open where the boss fell; the party has three rounds to reach it.
Light floods the room as the heart cracks, and everyone is hurled out of the space to land prone beside the entrance.
Rooms fold in on themselves one after another as the party runs back the way they came; each must make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} bludgeoning damage from falling stone.
Water surges in from every side and lifts the party up a shaft, spitting them out into shallow water a short walk from the entrance.
The boss's body dissolves into motes of light that settle into a staircase leading up to the exit.
Everything goes silent and still; there is no rush, but the exit does not open for one hour.
The heart chamber becomes a whirlpool dragging everything inward; those who hold on to something solid are flung out at the entrance.
Every door in the space swings open at once, and a gale shoves the party back toward the way in.
The floor drops away and the party falls slowly through cloud, landing in soft mud a stone's throw from the entrance.
Time rushes forward: plants sprout, stone erodes, and the party has one minute to grab what they can before the space crumbles to dust.
Ghostly voices of earlier victims thank the party and guide them out through a passage no one had noticed.
The space shatters like glass, and the party finds themselves back where they entered, shards fading around their feet.
Fire bursts from the boss's corpse and spreads fast; reaching the exit means leaping through flame (DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} fire damage).
The heart crystal floats to the nearest party member and shrinks into a small key that fits the only door out.
Gravity flips, and the party falls upward into the sky and through a portal back into the outside world.
Surviving monsters flee in panic, trampling anything in their path, while the exit opens behind a crumbling wall.
The space hums one long final note and is gone; the party wakes outside the entrance at dawn, the treasure beside them.
Darkness creeps in from the edges, and the only way out is to follow the faint glow of the boss's spilled essence.
The walls peel away like wet paper to reveal ordinary rock, and a rising tide of astral mist forces a quick climb out.
The space starts to shrink, and the party must squeeze through narrowing corridors before they close completely.

traps.name: Scything Pendulum Hall
traps.trigger: Stepping on any of the loose flagstones in the middle third of the hall
traps.effect: Three bronze blades swing across the corridor; each creature in the hall makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): thin slots in the ceiling and fresh arcs scratched into the floor
traps.disarm: DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools) to jam the pivot gears behind a wall panel, or crawl under the blade line at half speed

traps.name: Hinged Pit
traps.trigger: More than 50 pounds of weight on the false floor panel
traps.effect: The floor tips open into a 30-foot pit; DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): a hairline seam around a square of floor with no dust along its edge
traps.disarm: Wedge the hinge with iron spikes (DC {dc} Dexterity with thieves' tools) or lay a plank across the panel

traps.name: Spiked Pit of the Patient
traps.trigger: Walking over the reed mat that hides it
traps.effect: A 20-foot fall onto rusted spikes; DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} piercing damage and become poisoned for 1 hour
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): the mat sags slightly and smells of old blood
traps.disarm: Prod ahead with a pole to find the edge, then jump the 10-foot gap (DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) without a running start)

traps.name: Choking Spore Vents
traps.trigger: Opening the chest in the centre of the room
traps.effect: Yellow spores puff from wall vents; each creature within 20 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage and becoming poisoned for 1 minute on a failure, or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): fine yellow dust on the walls and dead beetles under the vents
traps.disarm: Stuff the vents with wet cloth (three actions), or open the chest from 20 feet away with a rope

traps.name: Rune of Searing Light
traps.trigger: A creature touches or reads the glowing glyph on the lintel
traps.effect: The rune flares; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage and being blinded until the end of their next turn on a failure, or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the rune is a ward, not an inscription, and its strokes hum faintly
traps.disarm: Dispel magic (DC {dc}), or drape an opaque cloth over it without reading it (DC {dc} Dexterity check)

traps.name: Collapsing Ceiling
traps.trigger: Pulling the rusted lever on the far wall
traps.effect: The ceiling drops in chunks; creatures in the room make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being restrained by rubble on a failure, or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): cracks in the ceiling radiate outward from the lever's mounting
traps.disarm: Leave the lever alone, or brace the ceiling with timber first (DC {dc} Strength (Athletics))

traps.name: Rising Water Chamber
traps.trigger: Closing the door behind the party
traps.effect: The door seals and water pours from grates; the room fills in 4 rounds, after which creatures must hold their breath. Swimming against the inflow takes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check each round
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): a waterline stain near the ceiling and drains clogged with silt
traps.disarm: Prop the door open with a spike, or find the drain valve under a loose tile and turn it (DC {dc} Strength check)

traps.name: Waltzing Armour
traps.trigger: A creature crosses the middle of the gallery
traps.effect: Two suits of armour step off their plinths and attack using animated armor statistics; they never leave the gallery
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): binding marks on the plinths and no dust in the armour's joints
traps.disarm: Speak the command word painted backwards beneath a plinth, or topple both suits before they wake (DC {dc} Strength (Athletics))

traps.name: Archway That Is Not There
traps.trigger: Walking through the apparent open archway
traps.effect: The archway is an illusion over a sheer drop; the true path is a narrow ledge beside it. A creature that steps through makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls 30 feet, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): a tossed coin passes through the arch and never lands
traps.disarm: Test the archway with a pole, then edge along the ledge (DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics))

traps.name: Curse of the Coveting Hand
traps.trigger: Picking up the gold coins scattered across the floor
traps.effect: DC {dc} Wisdom save or be cursed: the thief cannot willingly let go of any object they hold until remove curse or a night of prayer in a church
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion): the coins bear a penitent's mark, a known temple warning
traps.disarm: Leave the coins, or move them with mage hand or tongs

traps.name: Essence-Leech Glyph
traps.trigger: A creature with an awakened essence comes within 10 feet of the floor glyph
traps.effect: DC {dc} Constitution save or lose its highest available spell slot or one use of a limited ability; it takes {half} necrotic damage either way
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): faint lines run from the glyph into the walls, pulsing in time with your heartbeat
traps.disarm: Break a feed line in the wall with a pick (DC {dc} Strength), or keep to the unmarked tiles along the edge

traps.name: Inverted Gravity Well
traps.trigger: Entering the circular room
traps.effect: Gravity flips toward the ceiling 40 feet up; DC {dc} Dexterity save to grab something or fall upward, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage. After 1 minute gravity resets and everyone falls again
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): dust and bones cling to the ceiling instead of the floor
traps.disarm: Tie off to the iron ring by the door before entering, or deface the gravity sigil under the rug (DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana))

traps.name: Mimic Door
traps.trigger: Touching the door's handle
traps.effect: The door is a mimic; the creature is grappled (escape DC {dc}) and the mimic attacks
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): the wood grain shifts slowly and the handle is warm and damp
traps.disarm: Toss it raw meat to distract it for 1 minute; the real exit is a low hatch 10 feet to the left

traps.name: Swinging Log Ram
traps.trigger: Breaking the tripwire at ankle height
traps.effect: A spiked log swings out of the dark; one creature makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage, is pushed 10 feet and knocked prone
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): a thin waxed cord across the path
traps.disarm: Step over it, or cut it while holding the tension (DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools))

traps.name: Barbed Net Drop
traps.trigger: Crossing the centre of the courtyard
traps.effect: A weighted barbed net falls over a 20-foot square; DC {dc} Dexterity save or be restrained, taking {half} slashing damage each time you struggle. A DC {dc} Strength check frees one creature
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): ropes running up into the shadows overhead
traps.disarm: Cut the support ropes from the side wall, or sprint across (DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics))

traps.name: Hushing Bells
traps.trigger: Any sound louder than a whisper in the hall
traps.effect: Silver bells ring all at once; each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage and being deafened for 1 minute on a failure, or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): hundreds of tiny bells whose clappers have been oiled recently
traps.disarm: Cross in silence (DC {dc} Dexterity (Stealth) group check), or pack the bells with cloth one by one

traps.name: Light-Hungry Lenses
traps.trigger: Carrying any light source into the corridor
traps.effect: Lenses in the walls focus the light into beams aimed at its bearer; DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): scorched glass discs set into the walls at chest height
traps.disarm: Cross in darkness, or smear the lenses with mud

traps.name: Rank-Sensing Ward
traps.trigger: A creature of Silver rank or higher crosses the threshold
traps.effect: The ward detonates against that creature alone; DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} force damage and be stunned until the end of its next turn. Lower ranks pass unharmed
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the threshold rune weighs a creature's rank, an old Adventure Society testing pattern
traps.disarm: Hold your magic perfectly still as you pass (DC {dc} Wisdom check), or have a lower-rank ally scratch out the weighing rune from the far side

traps.name: Guardian's Summons
traps.trigger: Opening any of the sealed reliquaries
traps.effect: A gong booms somewhere deep; in 2 rounds two guardians suited to the space's rank rise from a circle in the floor
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the reliquary locks are threaded to a summoning circle under the rug
traps.disarm: Scrape a gap in the circle (DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana)) before opening anything

traps.name: The Repeating Minute
traps.trigger: Stepping on the hourglass mosaic
traps.effect: The room loops its last minute. Each loop, affected creatures make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or forget the loop happened; after three failed loops a creature gains a level of exhaustion
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight): strong deja vu, and footprints on the floor that match your own boots
traps.disarm: Smash the real hourglass hidden in a wall niche, which ends the loop for everyone

traps.name: Memory Thief Lanterns
traps.trigger: Gazing into the blue lanterns along the wall
traps.effect: DC {dc} Wisdom save or lose all memory of the last hour, including routes and passwords. A third failure also steals one known language until a long rest
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): tiny faces drift and mouth words inside the lantern glass
traps.disarm: Walk with eyes shut (blinded), or snuff each lantern with a wet rag

traps.name: Crushing Walls
traps.trigger: Lifting the idol from its pedestal
traps.effect: The walls grind inward over 5 rounds; from round three on, creatures inside make a DC {dc} Strength save each round or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): grooves in the floor show the walls have moved before
traps.disarm: Swap the idol for an equal weight (DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)), or jam the walls with iron bars

traps.name: Serpent-Mouth Darts
traps.trigger: Walking past the carved serpent heads
traps.effect: Darts hiss from the heads; each creature in the line makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): small holes in the serpent mouths and spent darts beneath them
traps.disarm: Plug the mouths with wax, or crawl beneath them

traps.name: Flame Jet Floor
traps.trigger: Stepping on a red-tinted tile
traps.effect: Columns of flame roar up; creatures within 10 feet of the tile make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): soot rings around certain tiles and a faint smell of lamp oil
traps.disarm: Step only on the blue tiles, or close the gas valve behind the third pillar

traps.name: Frostbite Corridor
traps.trigger: Ending a turn in the corridor
traps.effect: Air turns to frost; DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} cold damage and have speed halved until warmed by fire
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): breath hangs in the air as ice and weapons frost over
traps.disarm: Move through fast, or shatter the cold crystal set in the ceiling (AC 15, 10 hit points)

traps.name: Gaze of the Weeping Statue
traps.trigger: Meeting the eyes of the marble statue
traps.effect: DC {dc} Constitution save or be restrained as your legs calcify; repeat the save at the end of each turn, becoming petrified after three failures and freed after three successes
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): a ring of carved eyes around the statue's base, all looking inward
traps.disarm: Approach with eyes averted or blindfolded, or hood the statue

traps.name: Thirsty Altar
traps.trigger: Any creature bleeding within 30 feet of the altar
traps.effect: The altar pulls blood from every wounded creature; DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and nearby monsters heal by the same amount
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion): brown-stained channels in the floor all run toward the altar
traps.disarm: Pour salt into the channels, or bandage all wounds before entering

traps.name: Tripwire Crossbows
traps.trigger: Snapping the silver tripwire
traps.effect: Four crossbows fire from wall slits; each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} piercing damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): a silver thread glints when light passes over it
traps.disarm: Step over it, or cut it carefully (DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools))

traps.name: Hungry Shadows
traps.trigger: Standing in dim light or darkness for a full round
traps.effect: Your own shadow grips your ankles; DC {dc} Strength save or be grappled and take {half} cold damage at the start of each of your turns
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): shadows in the room lag a moment behind their owners
traps.disarm: Flood the room with bright light, which ends the effect

traps.name: Gale Gate
traps.trigger: Opening the gate at the end of the tunnel
traps.effect: Wind howls through; DC {dc} Strength save or be hurled 30 feet back into the wall, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): every loose stone is piled against one end of the tunnel
traps.disarm: Rope everyone together first, or ease the gate open a crack at a time (DC {dc} Strength (Athletics))

traps.name: Sinking Sand Hall
traps.trigger: Stepping onto the sandy floor
traps.effect: DC {dc} Dexterity save or sink to the waist and be restrained; after 3 rounds restrained a creature is submerged. A DC {dc} Strength check pulls a creature free
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival): the sand is unnaturally smooth and slightly damp
traps.disarm: Spread weight across planks or shields, or edge along the rim of the wall

traps.name: Copper Coil Arcs
traps.trigger: Touching metal in the room or crossing it in metal armour
traps.effect: Lightning leaps between coils; DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): humming copper coils and the smell of a storm
traps.disarm: Ground the coils by running a chain to the floor drain

traps.name: Needle Lock
traps.trigger: Picking the chest's lock without care
traps.effect: A hidden needle pricks; DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} poison damage and be poisoned for 1 hour
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): a pinprick hole beside the keyhole
traps.disarm: Plug the hole with wax before picking (DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools))

traps.name: Mirror of the Second Self
traps.trigger: Seeing your reflection in the tall silver mirror
traps.effect: Your reflection climbs out and fights you, with your hit points, AC and attacks but none of your magic items; it dissolves when reduced to 0 hit points
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the reflection blinks a heartbeat late
traps.disarm: Approach backwards with eyes shut, or throw a cloak over the mirror

traps.name: Tilting Bridge
traps.trigger: Two or more creatures on the bridge at once
traps.effect: The bridge pivots on a hidden axle; each creature on it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or slides into the chasm, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from a 40-foot fall
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): a bronze axle under the bridge's centre, polished from use
traps.disarm: Cross one at a time, or lash the bridge to the stone anchors at either end

traps.name: Acid Grate
traps.trigger: A creature steps onto the grate over the basin
traps.effect: The grate swings down, dropping the creature into knee-deep acid; DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} acid damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and again at the start of each turn it stays in
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): a sharp vinegar smell and pitted stone around the grate
traps.disarm: Walk the narrow lip beside the grate, or pin it shut with spikes

traps.name: Sleep Moth Cocoons
traps.trigger: Disturbing the pale cocoons on the walls
traps.effect: A cloud of moths erupts; creatures within 20 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save or fall unconscious for 1 minute or until shaken awake
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature): the cocoons belong to a dust-winged moth whose scales cause deep sleep
traps.disarm: Smoke the cocoons with a torch from the doorway, or cover mouths and noses for advantage on the save

traps.name: Floor of Grasping Hands
traps.trigger: Walking across the soft grey floor
traps.effect: Stone hands rise and grab; DC {dc} Dexterity save or be grappled (escape DC {dc}) and take {half} bludgeoning damage at the start of each turn
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): knuckle-shaped bumps under the stone surface
traps.disarm: Any fire or radiant damage dealt to the floor makes the hands recoil for 1 minute

traps.name: Tar Dome
traps.trigger: Raising your voice under the domed ceiling
traps.effect: The dome weeps hot black tar; creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage and having speed halved for 1 minute on a failure, or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): hardened tar splatters in a ring on the floor
traps.disarm: Hold shields overhead and stay silent, or burn the tar off from the doorway with a thrown torch

traps.name: Ward of the Open Hand
traps.trigger: Entering the room holding a drawn weapon
traps.effect: Every drawn weapon twists in its wielder's grip; DC {dc} Strength save or take {dmg} damage of the weapon's type from your own blade
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): runes on the doorframe that translate to 'enter empty-handed'
traps.disarm: Sheathe weapons before stepping in

traps.name: Rolling Boulder
traps.trigger: Taking the jeweled skull from the alcove
traps.effect: A boulder thunders down the sloped corridor; each creature in its path makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): a wide polished groove down the centre of the corridor
traps.disarm: Duck into the side niches, or chock the track with spikes before taking the skull

traps.name: Resounding Vault
traps.trigger: Shouting, casting a spell with a verbal component, or striking metal
traps.effect: The sound returns as a hammer of force; the source makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): every whisper comes back clearly, a beat late
traps.disarm: Communicate by gesture, or cast silence to blanket the vault

traps.name: Bridge of Brief Light
traps.trigger: Stepping onto the glowing bridge while carrying a light source
traps.effect: The bridge winks out; DC {dc} Dexterity save to leap back or fall into the void, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the bridge dims as you approach with a torch and brightens when you back away
traps.disarm: Douse all lights before crossing

traps.name: Spirit Coin Snare
traps.trigger: Picking up the spirit coins on the floor
traps.effect: Each coin unspools into a chain of light; DC {dc} Strength save or be restrained for 1 minute (escape DC {dc})
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the coins hum with magic that is not their own
traps.disarm: Leave them, or sweep them into a sack with a broom

traps.name: Thorn Hedge Corridor
traps.trigger: Touching the walls of woven vine
traps.effect: The vines lash out; DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage and being poisoned for 1 minute on a failure, or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature): the vines slowly turn toward body heat
traps.disarm: Burn a path (any fire damage clears a 5-foot section), or walk single file down the exact centre

traps.name: Lodestone Floor
traps.trigger: Carrying metal into the hall
traps.effect: Metal is dragged to the floor; a creature in metal armour makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained until it removes the armour, and dropped weapons cannot be lifted
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): nails, buckles and arrowheads stuck flat to the floor
traps.disarm: Strip metal gear and drag it across on a cloth or wooden sled

traps.name: Oil Flood Plate
traps.trigger: Stepping on the slightly raised central plate
traps.effect: Oil gushes over the floor and ignites; creatures in the room make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): oil glistening in the floor cracks around a raised plate
traps.disarm: Wedge the plate (DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools)) or step around it

traps.name: Sound-Swallowing Pit
traps.trigger: Walking onto the patch of floor where your footsteps make no sound
traps.effect: The floor is an illusion over a 20-foot pit; DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage. The pit walls are slick, requiring a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check to climb
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): your footsteps go silent a step before the edge
traps.disarm: Throw a stone ahead and listen, or tie off a rope before stepping

traps.name: Turning Room
traps.trigger: Pulling the brass ring set in the floor
traps.effect: The room spins and locks facing a new exit; creatures make a DC {dc} Constitution save or are incapacitated until the end of their next turn, and the original door now opens onto a different corridor
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): a perfect circle of scrape marks around the room's edge
traps.disarm: Pull the ring again to spin back, or chalk arrows on the walls to track the way you came

traps.name: Wailing Sarcophagus
traps.trigger: Opening the sarcophagus lid
traps.effect: A spectral wail rises; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or are frightened for 1 minute and take {half} psychic damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion): a funerary warning carved along the lid in an old tongue
traps.disarm: Speak a funeral blessing over it first (DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion)), then open

traps.name: Glass Floor
traps.trigger: Running, jumping or more than 200 pounds on one pane
traps.effect: The glass shatters; DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall 30 feet onto shards, taking {dmg} slashing damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): faint cracks spider out from the centre of each pane
traps.disarm: Crawl on the iron frames between panes at half speed

traps.name: Revel Mist
traps.trigger: Breathing the glittering mist that rolls in under the door
traps.effect: DC {dc} Wisdom save or be compelled to dance for 1 minute: you must use all movement to caper in place and attack rolls against you have advantage. Repeat the save at the end of each turn
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the mist sparkles with drifting coloured motes and smells of spiced wine
traps.disarm: Hold your breath crossing the room, or disperse the mist with strong wind

traps.name: Collapsing Stair
traps.trigger: Reaching the midpoint of the long stairway
traps.effect: The steps fold flat into a slick ramp; each creature makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or slides 40 feet down into a spiked trough, taking {dmg} piercing damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): each step has a thin hinge line at its back edge
traps.disarm: Hammer spikes into the step gaps as you climb, or rope the party together

traps.name: Breath-Stealing Seal
traps.trigger: Breaking the wax seal on the reliquary door
traps.effect: The air in the room vanishes; every creature inside must hold its breath or begin suffocating. The air returns after 1 minute or when the seal is mended
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the seal's crest is a closed mouth, and candles near it gutter
traps.disarm: Take a deep breath first, or press the broken seal back together with fresh wax (DC {dc} Dexterity check)

traps.name: Bloodline Lock
traps.trigger: Touching the vault door without the blood of its maker
traps.effect: Barbed tendrils lash from the door; DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): a small basin in the door's centre, crusted with old blood
traps.disarm: Offer blood from a creature native to the space, or fool it with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check while bleeding into the basin

traps.name: Sanctified Threshold
traps.trigger: An undead or cursed creature, or one carrying a cursed item, passes the doorway
traps.effect: Holy fire erupts; DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion): church sigils worn into the threshold stone
traps.disarm: Wrap cursed items in lead foil, or deface the sigils with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check

traps.name: Tipping Scales Room
traps.trigger: Placing any item on the brass scales by the door
traps.effect: The room's gravity tilts toward the heavier pan; creatures on that half are hurled into the wall, DC {dc} Strength save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage and be pinned (restrained) for 1 minute
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): floor tiles on each half of the room are worn on opposite edges
traps.disarm: Balance the pans exactly (DC {dc} Wisdom check), or leave the scales empty

traps.name: Clockwork Spiders
traps.trigger: Prying open the ticking brass box
traps.effect: Dozens of brass spiders burst out and swarm, using swarm of insects statistics with piercing bites; they stop when the box's spring runs down after 1 minute
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): faint ticking from inside the box and tiny scratches on its lid
traps.disarm: Wind the key on the box's side three turns backward before opening

traps.name: Kiln Room
traps.trigger: Closing all four doors at once
traps.effect: The room heats like an oven; at the end of each round, creatures inside make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} fire damage
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): glazed walls and a floor of fine ash
traps.disarm: Keep one door wedged open, which vents the heat

traps.name: Drowning Circle
traps.trigger: Stepping into the dry ring painted on the floor
traps.effect: A column of water rises inside the ring, engulfing the creature: it is restrained and cannot breathe until it escapes with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the paint is blue water-script and the stones inside are damp
traps.disarm: Smudge part of the circle (DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana)), or walk around it

traps.name: Lure Lights
traps.trigger: Watching the swaying glow at the end of the hall
traps.effect: DC {dc} Wisdom save or be charmed and walk toward the glow, into a chamber whose walls sprout teeth: DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight): the glow moves faster when you look away
traps.disarm: Look away and ignore it, or blindfold anyone who failed and lead them back

traps.name: Silent Alarm Band
traps.trigger: A creature not wearing the space's sigil crosses the rune band
traps.effect: Nothing visible happens; every guardian in the space learns the party's location and hunts them for the next hour
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): a faint band of runes under the floor that glimmers when stepped over
traps.disarm: Wear a sigil taken from a slain guardian, or leap the band (DC {dc} Strength (Athletics))

traps.name: Hall of Beckoning Reflections
traps.trigger: Walking the hall lined with mirrors
traps.effect: Reflections reach out; DC {dc} Wisdom save or be charmed and step into a mirror, trapped inside until an ally shatters that mirror (AC 13, 5 hit points)
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): the reflections smile when you do not
traps.disarm: Walk backwards with eyes shut, or break the mirrors one by one

traps.name: Mocking Portrait
traps.trigger: Turning your back on the painted lord in the gallery
traps.effect: The portrait shrieks your worst secret aloud; DC {dc} Wisdom save or take {dmg} psychic damage and have disadvantage on Charisma checks for 1 hour, and guardians within 300 feet hear it
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight): the painted eyes follow you, and the frame is gouged where others clawed at it
traps.disarm: Face the portrait while crossing at half speed, or slash the canvas (AC 10, 5 hit points)

traps.name: Rank Gate Sieve
traps.trigger: A creature below Bronze rank attempts to pass the shimmering curtain
traps.effect: The curtain hardens against anyone weaker than Bronze rank; forcing it deals {half} force damage and the creature is pushed back 10 feet
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): Adventure Society scratch-marks on the frame warning 'Bronze and up'
traps.disarm: A higher-rank ally can carry one weaker creature through per turn shielded by their own magic (DC {dc} Constitution save for the carrier or both are repelled)

traps.name: Starfall Ceiling
traps.trigger: Standing in the open when the painted stars align, once every 10 minutes
traps.effect: Motes of starlight fall like hail; creatures in the open make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the painted constellations are slowly sliding toward each other
traps.disarm: Shelter under the stone tables, or time the crossing between alignments (DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival))

traps.name: Dropping Spike Ceiling
traps.trigger: Walking past the middle pillar
traps.effect: A spiked ceiling section drops 6 feet; creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception): small holes in the floor that match a spike pattern above
traps.disarm: Crawl beneath it while prone, or jam the drop rails with iron spikes

traps.name: Marsh Gas Cellar
traps.trigger: Lighting any flame in the low cellar
traps.effect: Trapped marsh gas explodes; creatures in the cellar make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success
traps.detect: DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival): a rotten-egg smell and bubbles rising from floor puddles
traps.disarm: Open the ceiling hatch and let it vent for 10 minutes before lighting anything

traps.name: Ward of Wilting
traps.trigger: A living creature touches the flowering archway
traps.effect: Life drains from the toucher into the blossoms; DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the creature cannot regain hit points until the end of its next turn
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature): the flowers are too healthy, and dried husks of rats lie beneath them
traps.disarm: Pass through without touching (DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics)), or prune the flowers with fire

traps.name: Cascading Floor Tiles
traps.trigger: Stepping on the first tile of the gallery floor
traps.effect: Tiles behind the walker start falling into the abyss one per second; each creature must dash to the far side or make a DC {dc} Dexterity save to cling to a ledge, falling for {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure
traps.detect: DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation): each tile rests on a single narrow pillar
traps.disarm: Lay a rope line along the wall pegs first, or cross with a running Dash

quirks: Gravity shifts every ten minutes; roll a d4 to see which wall becomes the floor.
Healing magic restores the maximum possible hit points, but every creature healed this way ages one year.
Fire burns blue and cold here: fire damage is halved, but it also slows the target's speed by 10 feet until its next turn.
No one can speak above a whisper; spells with verbal components require a DC 12 Constitution check or they fail.
Short rests take only 10 minutes, but long rests are impossible until the heart is cleared.
The sky turns red once an hour as the space exhales; roll a d6 and on a 1 or 2 a patrol of guardians comes looking for intruders.
Shadows act a round late, so stealth checks made in dim light have advantage.
Time runs fast: each hour inside is a full day outside, and rations spoil at the same rate.
Water flows uphill, and swimming upward costs no extra movement while swimming downward costs double.
Spirit coins brought in grow warm and hum; spending one restores 1d4 hit points but alerts the nearest guardian.
Distances lie: anything more than 60 feet away is actually twice as far, so ranged attacks beyond that range have disadvantage.
