The space is silent: no sound carries more than 10 feet, giving advantage on Stealth checks but making shouted warnings impossible.
Each time a creature dies, the room it died in seals for 1 minute and the body sinks into the floor.
Monster cores harvested here are doubled, but each extra core is cursed with the creature's last thought.
Doors lead to a random room each time they are opened unless someone holds them open.
Magic missiles and other force effects bounce once, striking a second target of the DM's choice for half damage.
Everyone's reflection lags a moment behind, and mirrors cannot be used to see around corners.
Iron rusts in minutes; nonmagical iron and steel weapons take a cumulative -1 penalty to damage each hour.
Light sources burn twice as bright but last only half as long.
Essence abilities cost nothing to use once per room but fail on a d20 roll of 1.
Creatures with an awakened Life essence regain 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns.
Dark-affinity creatures have advantage on attack rolls here, and Light-affinity ones have disadvantage.
Lying is impossible; any creature that tries to speak a falsehood finds the words coming out as birdsong.
Every hour a bell rings and all creatures in the space trade places with the creature nearest to them.
Falling damage is reversed into healing for the first 20 feet of every fall, then deals double damage beyond.
Ranged attacks curve toward the closest creature, friend or foe, if the attacker rolls a 5 or lower.
Every natural 20 rolled here also grants the roller one awakening-stone glimmer, a mote that can be spent for +1d4 on any later roll before leaving.
The space remembers wounds: damage taken in one room reopens for 1 point when you return to it.
Food and water inside the space are plentiful but carry no nourishment; only rations from outside count.
Names have weight: a creature that speaks a guardian's true name aloud imposes disadvantage on that guardian's next attack.
Gravity is light: jump distances double and falling damage is halved.
The heart pulses every minute; on each pulse, creatures roll a d20 and on a 1 they are stunned until the end of their next turn.
Weapons wielded by creatures of lower rank than the space's guardians deal an extra 1d4 damage of their affinity type.
Fire cannot exist above knee height; torches gutter and only floor-level flames burn.
Echoes answer back in your own voice with one helpful truth per day; the DM gives a single yes or no about the nearest room.
Death saving throws are made with advantage, but anyone who drops to 0 hit points wakes with a white streak in their hair and a stranger's memory.
Magical darkness spreads 5 feet each round from any cast darkness effect until dispelled.
Prayer is heard clearly: a creature that spends an action praying regains one expended spell slot of 1st level, once per day, and every guardian in the space knows where it is.
The floor is soft as moss: no creature can be knocked prone, and falling damage is negligible.
Heavy things are light and light things are heavy: a feather weighs a stone, and creatures carrying more than 20 pounds move at normal speed while unencumbered creatures are slowed by 10 feet.
Initiative is rolled once when the party enters and never rerolled; the order holds for every fight in the space.
Every meal eaten here grants temporary hit points equal to the eater's level, but the next meal must be shared or it grants none.
The space feeds on fear: anyone frightened takes 1d6 psychic damage at the start of each of their turns.
Treasure chests rearrange themselves when no one is looking, and opening one shuffles all the others' contents.
Spells of 1st level or lower cost no slot but always have their minimum effect.
Water here heals 1d4 hit points per drink but turns the drinker's eyes silver for a day.
The ceiling is the floor of the room above; anything dropped falls upward into the next level.
Wounds bleed light instead of blood, so injured creatures cannot hide in darkness.
Sleep comes hard: finishing a long rest requires a DC 13 Wisdom save, and on a failure the rest counts only as a short rest.
Every spoken word leaves glowing letters in the air for 1 round, so speaking reveals your location.
Monsters here are made of mist; they take half damage from nonmagical weapons but double from fire.
Wind is constant and from one direction; ranged attacks against the wind have disadvantage.
Any creature that sleeps dreams of the heart, gaining a vision of one random room's contents.
Magic items glow brightly and cannot be hidden, and invisibility ends whenever a magic item is used.
The space hates silence: every round no one makes noise, the walls close in 5 feet.
All creatures can breathe water and air equally, and the corridors flood and drain each hour.
The exit portal drifts; each hour it moves to a random room, and finding it again takes a DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) check.
A creature that kills a guardian gains that guardian's affinity for an hour, granting resistance to its damage type.
Any spell or effect with a duration in minutes lasts twice as long, but concentration checks are made at disadvantage.
Bridges and ladders exist only while someone is touching them.
features: A fountain of pale green water: a creature that drinks regains 2d8 hit points, but a second drink in the same day poisons it for 1 hour.
A stone altar with a shallow bowl; placing a monster core in it converts the core into 1d6 spirit coins of the same rank.
A statue of a kneeling knight holding out an empty hand. Giving it a weapon makes that weapon magical (+1) until the party leaves the space, but the statue keeps the weapon's sheath.

A brass machine with three levers and a glass dome; pulling them in the right order (DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation)) dispenses a potion of healing, and the wrong order sprays scalding steam for 2d6 fire damage.
A portrait of a stern scholar who answers one question about the space truthfully, then demands a compliment; insulting it makes it scream for every guardian to hear.

A well of memory: looking into it shows a creature one forgotten memory, granting advantage on one Intelligence check related to that memory, but it also shows something they wished to forget (DC 12 Wisdom save or frightened for 1 minute).
An essence shrine of carved crystal: a creature with an awakened essence can meditate here for 10 minutes to recover one expended use of an essence ability.
Glowing blue moss across the ceiling; eating a handful grants darkvision 60 feet for 1 hour but turns the eater's skin faintly luminous, imposing disadvantage on Stealth checks.
A sealed sarcophagus with a bronze key-plate; prying it open (DC 16 Strength) reveals a mummified adventurer with a pouch of spirit coins and a chance (d6, on a 1) that the body rises.
A great set of scales: placing an item on one pan makes an equal-value item appear on the other, once per creature, but the original vanishes forever.
A tall mirror framed in silver vines; touching it lets a creature see through the eyes of a random monster in the space for 1 minute.
A music box that plays a lullaby when opened; any creature that listens to the whole tune regains 1d6 hit points, but all listeners must make a DC 12 Wisdom save or fall asleep for 10 minutes.
A basin of dark oil: a creature that dips a weapon in it adds 1d6 necrotic damage to its next three hits, after which the weapon rusts and loses 1 point of damage permanently.
A cracked pillar humming with stored lightning; striking it with a metal weapon releases a bolt (4d6 lightning damage) in a straight 60-foot line, which can be aimed at enemies.
A garden of tiny silver flowers that hum when touched; picking one grants advantage on one saving throw, but the flower wilts in an hour and the hum follows you.
A glass orb on a stand, swirling with images of the space; studying it for 1 minute reveals the location of the heart and one trap, but alerts the heart's boss.
A ring of standing stones where whispers are amplified; speaking a wish aloud has a 1 in 20 chance of granting a minor boon, but a 1 in 6 chance of drawing a guardian's attention.
An iron forge still warm with a blue flame; a creature with smith's tools can spend an hour to grant a weapon +1 to attack for a day, or ruin it on a failed DC 14 check.
A pool of mercury reflecting the ceiling stars; diving in reveals a hidden passage beneath, but touching the mercury for more than a minute causes 2d6 poison damage.
A bookshelf of blank books; writing in any of them makes the text appear in a random book in the Magic Society's library in Greenstone.
A cage holding a talking crow that offers directions for food; it tells the truth only if fed a monster core.
An obsidian throne; anyone who sits in it can command one guardian in the space to stand down, but must make a DC 15 Wisdom save or be unable to stand for 1 hour.
A pedestal with a cracked awakening stone; touching it grants a brief vision of an essence's power, but it shatters unless a DC 18 Arcana check stabilizes it.
A hanging chain of bells; ringing them in a melody from the walls' carvings opens a hidden vault, while a wrong tune summons a swarm of bats.
A rug woven with a map of the space that updates as monsters move; walking on it costs no movement but leaves wet footprints across the real floor.
A spring of sparkling water; bathing in it removes one curse or disease, but the bather's hair turns pure white.
A heap of rusted armour hiding a single pristine shield, which grants +1 AC but slowly turns its wielder's voice metallic.
A sundial in an underground room whose shadow points to the room with the most treasure, but only while a light source is held directly above it.
An arcane circle that can teleport a creature to the space's entrance, once per day, at the cost of 1 level of exhaustion.
A tree of crystal leaves; striking it scatters shards worth 2d10 spirit coins, but each strike has a 1 in 4 chance of the tree screaming and waking every guardian.
A hollow statue of a sleeping giant; climbing inside reveals a cozy room perfect for a long rest that cannot be interrupted, but you wake 2d4 hours later than you intended.
A wall of drawers labelled in an old script; each drawer contains a random small item, but one in ten contains a poisonous snake.

A great brass sextant bolted to the floor; sighting through it at the ceiling reveals the true layout of the next three rooms, but the user must make a DC 13 Constitution save or be blinded for 1 minute by a flash of starlight.
A painted mural of a battle that moves when watched; the figures mime the tactics of the boss, granting advantage on the first attack against it if studied for 10 minutes.
A hanging cage of light holding a fragment of a lost essence; freeing it grants a temporary boon (advantage on one type of saving throw for a day) but angers the space's guardian of light.
A pool of blood that never congeals; dipping a hand in reveals the last moments of anyone who died in the room, but also inflicts 1d6 necrotic damage.
A brass telescope pointed at a blank wall; looking through it shows the room on the other side, including any creatures and traps.
A grove of fungus that sprouts edible caps; eating one restores 1d4 hit points but has a 1 in 6 chance to cause hallucinations for an hour.
A narrow bridge of light that appears when someone sings; it holds as long as the song continues.
A crystal skull on a pedestal that speaks in riddles; answering three correctly grants a clue about the heart, while a wrong answer costs 2d6 psychic damage.
A spinning wheel of bone; spinning it lets a creature cast one random 1st-level spell once before leaving the space, but on a d20 roll of 1 the spinner is flung into a random room.
A puppet theatre with wooden figures of the party; moving a puppet's hand moves the real person's hand too, which can save someone from a fall or make them drop a weapon.
A cracked bell that rings with healing tones; ringing it restores 1d8 hit points to all within 30 feet but summons a monster to investigate.
A pit filled with glowing worms; reaching in finds 1d4 spirit coins but risks a bite (DC 12 Dexterity save or 1d6 piercing damage).
A chandelier of candles whose flames spell words in the smoke, answering one yes-or-no question per day.
A gate of thorns that blooms open when a creature sheds a drop of blood, granting access to a secret garden with healing herbs.
An ivory chessboard missing one piece; placing any small object on the empty square causes the pieces to move and open a hidden compartment.
A statue of a weeping woman whose tears are healing potions; collecting them takes 10 minutes and yields 1d4 potions, but she stops weeping and turns to face whoever took them.
A rotating column of runes; aligning them (DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana)) grants resistance to one damage type of the aligner's choice for 1 hour, while a failure deals 2d6 force damage.
A tank of murky water holding a single silver fish; whoever catches it (DC 15 Dexterity) may ask it where the nearest treasure lies, and it answers truthfully before dying.
A carved face in the wall that will swallow one mundane item and spit out a copy made of a different material: glass, bone, gold leaf or living wood (roll a d4).
A pool of oil with a burning wick floating on it; lighting it reveals hidden script on the walls, but the fire spreads unless controlled.
A stone wheel rimmed with bolted weapons; spinning it drops one random weapon at each creature's feet, and anyone who slays the next monster with that weapon may keep it as a +1 weapon.
A gallery of masks; wearing one grants the ability to speak with a specific kind of monster for an hour, but you cannot remove the mask for that hour.
A bronze astrolabe on a lectern; turning its rings lets the party walk on walls and ceilings for 10 minutes, but anyone still on a wall when it ends falls.

A bloodstained chopping block; offering a monster core here grants resistance to that core's affinity damage type for 1 hour, but the block demands a second core next time or deals 2d6 slashing damage to whoever approaches.
A glowing seed in a stone pot; planted in soil outside the space, it grows overnight into a shrub bearing 1d4 berries that each heal 1d8 hit points, and the Magic Society would pay well to study it.

A sword sunk to the hilt in a stone; pulling it free (DC 18 Strength) yields a +1 longsword that deals an extra 1d6 damage against the space's guardians, but the heart's boss knows where its wielder is at all times.
A quiet room with a single chair and a lantern; sitting here lets you remember any detail you have ever seen, once per visit.
A massive bell suspended over an abyss; striking it shatters all glass in the space and stuns every creature with hearing for 1 round.

a glass tube full of rushing air that carries travelers upward
a hall where gravity points toward the left wall
a dark corridor lit only by glowing moths

a corridor of drapes that ripple in no wind

a canal with a waiting flat-bottomed boat

a tunnel lined with portraits whose eyes follow you
a circular room that rotates to align with exits
a sand-filled hall where the floor slowly shifts
a hollow log large enough to walk through
a ladder that descends into a ceiling
a corridor where every step echoes a moment early
a stone ramp spiraling around a central pillar
a passage through a waterfall into a dry cave
a narrow gorge with walls covered in sleeping bats
a vine-choked archway that must be hacked through
doors: A door of stacked skulls that opens when someone tells it a joke that makes at least one skull laugh (DC 13 Charisma (Performance)).
A wall of water held upright by magic; walking through it requires holding your breath for 1 round and a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check against the current.
A door of polished bronze with no handle that swings open if someone presses their palm to its centre and states their rank honestly.
A portcullis of living vines that retracts when watered or burned, and grows back after 1 minute.
A stone slab carved with a riddle; answering correctly sinks it into the floor, while a wrong answer deals 2d6 thunder damage.
A door covered in locks of every kind; only one is real, found with a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, and the others are traps.
A curtain of falling sand that parts when someone sings a single sustained note.
An iron door hot to the touch; pouring water on it cools it for long enough to open it safely.
A door of glass so thin it ripples; tapping it in the rhythm carved above it opens it, while striking it shatters the glass and wakes the guardians.
A circular vault door with an essence-shaped keyhole; any awakened essence of the matching affinity, pressed to it, opens it.
A barrier of shimmering force that only creatures of Bronze rank or lower can pass through without harm.
A door of bone that opens when offered a monster core.
A heavy stone door that opens only when all present creatures stand on the pressure plates in front of it.
A wall of mist that blinds anyone inside; finding the true exit requires a DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) check.
A door of thorns that opens when someone sheds a drop of blood on the latch.
A clockwork door with gears that must be aligned in the correct sequence (DC 15 Dexterity (thieves' tools)).
A door that is painted on the wall and opens when someone steps into it believing it is real (DC 13 Wisdom save to commit).
An enormous mouth in the wall that opens if fed a ration and closes on anyone who enters without one.
A barrier of spinning blades that slow and stop when the lever across the room is pulled.
A door with a talking knocker that opens only if you tell it the name of the previous visitor.
A gate of ice that melts in the presence of fire and refreezes after 1 minute.
A pair of doors that open only when both are touched at the same moment by two different people.
A wall of shadow that dissipates when bright light is shone upon it.
A door covered in silver runes that opens to anyone who reads them aloud in the right order (DC 14 Intelligence (Arcana)).
A floor hatch held down by a sleeping guardian that must be lured away or defeated.
A curtain of hanging chains that rattle loudly when touched; moving through without noise requires a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check.
A door made of a single giant scale that slides open if someone holds a mirror to it.
A pool of black liquid in a doorway; diving through it leads to the next room, but each creature makes a DC 12 Constitution save or emerges poisoned.
A wall of carved faces whose mouths must all be closed at once to open the passage.
A heavy door locked by a combination of spirit coins inserted in the right denominations (DC 13 Intelligence).

environments.name: Drowned Cathedral
environments.summary: A great house of worship sank beneath a lake of mana long ago, and the astral space preserved it at the moment the water closed over the spire. Light still pours through stained glass from a sun that is not there, and the drowned faithful keep their services in the flooded nave. Devotion and grief, soaked into the stones, gave the space its shape.
readAloud: Cold water laps at your shins the moment you step through. Shafts of coloured light fall through tall windows and break into trembling coins on the surface, red and gold and violet. Somewhere deep in the nave, a bell rings once beneath the water, and the sound reaches you through your feet before your ears.

The portal spits you onto a stone stair that descends into green, still water. Above, vaulted arches drip steadily, each drop striking the surface with a sound like a soft amen. Pale shapes drift between the pillars below, and when one turns its face toward you, it has no eyes, only two small lamps of drowned light.

You smell wet limestone and old incense before your eyes adjust. Rows of pews float in slow circles across a flooded floor, bumping gently against marble saints who stand chest-deep with their hands raised in blessing. A hymn hums in the walls, so low it might be the water itself singing.
sights: Stained glass throwing coloured light onto rippling water
Pews drifting in lazy circles like boats with no rowers
Marble saints with algae beards and barnacled hands
Candles burning underwater with pale blue flames
Hymn books swollen fat, their pages fanned like gills
A drowned priest's vestments floating empty in a doorway
sounds: A bell tolling somewhere below the waterline
Dripping from the vaults in a steady, prayerful rhythm
Wood knocking softly against stone as pews collide
A choir humming one long note from inside the walls
Bubbles rising from the crypt in slow, heavy belches
smells: Stale incense dissolved into lake water
Green rot from the moss on the pillars
The clean, metallic scent of mana-rich water
rooms: A nave flooded to the knee, pews floating in slow circles around a sunken altar.
A baptistry where the font overflows endlessly, its water glowing faintly gold and running uphill along the walls.
A bell tower half-submerged, its great bronze bell hanging just beneath the surface and humming when anyone swims near.
A confessional booth bobbing on its side, the grille still whispering the last sins spoken into it.
A crypt fully underwater, stone coffins lidless, their occupants sitting upright with their hands folded.
A choir loft above the waterline, dry and dusty, with sheet music pinned to the rail by rusted knives.
A vestry where robes hang from hooks and sway as if worn by invisible priests walking in place.
A rose window chamber where the great round window has cracked, letting a waterfall of light and lake water pour in together.
A cloister garden drowned under ten feet of clear water, its hedges grown into tall swaying kelp shaped like praying figures.
The sanctuary heart, an air pocket beneath the dome where the drowned bishop stands on the altar, robes dripping and lamplit eyes open.
features: A choir of drowned statues that sing when touched; whoever touches one gains advantage on their next Charisma check, but the sound draws the nearest monsters.
Underwater candles that never go out; a creature holding one can breathe water for 10 minutes, after which the candle gutters and cannot be relit.
A collection plate full of spirit coins resting on the altar steps; taking them without leaving an offering of equal value curses the taker with disadvantage on saves against the drowned for 1 hour.

Stained glass panes that tell the story of the cathedral's sinking; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check reveals the safe route to the crypt, and a failure shows the route the dead want you to take.
A floating pulpit that can be poled across the nave like a raft, carrying up to four Medium creatures above the reach of the things in the water.
hazards: A sudden surge rolls through the nave when the bell tolls; each creature in the water makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is swept 20 feet and takes {half} bludgeoning damage against a pillar.
Grasping weeds coat the crypt floor; a creature that ends its turn on them makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained and begins drowning.
Holy water gone sour pools in the font; a creature that drinks or bathes in it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} radiant damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn.
The dome's air pocket thins as the fight drags on; after 5 rounds, each breathing creature beneath it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save at the start of each turn or gains a level of exhaustion.

environments.name: Inverted Forest
environments.summary: A forest hangs upside down from a ceiling of packed soil that stretches to every horizon, its crowns drooping toward an empty sky below. Visitors walk on roots and branches while clouds drift beneath their feet. The space formed where earth magic and wind magic tangled, and neither ever agreed which way was down.
readAloud: You step out onto a thick root and your stomach lurches. Above you is not sky but dirt, an endless brown ceiling where the trees are planted, and below you the forest hangs downward into blue nothing. Leaves fall upward past your face and stick to the soil overhead.

Wind howls up from the open sky beneath, carrying the smell of rain and distant storms. The trunks around you are wrapped in rope ladders and old knotted vines, swaying gently. Far below, a flock of birds flies in a slow spiral, and from here they look like ash drifting down a chimney.

Pebbles and clods rain softly from the earthen ceiling, pattering on the leaves. The branches beneath your boots creak like ship timbers. A little way off, something with too many limbs scurries along the underside of a bough, upside down even by the standards of this place.
sights: Tree crowns hanging toward an open sky like chandeliers
Clouds drifting slowly beneath your feet
Leaves falling upward to stick to the soil ceiling
Fruit dangling from branches, then rising when it drops
Rope bridges strung between trunks by long-dead climbers
Roots thrusting through the ceiling like the knuckles of buried hands
sounds: Wind moaning up through the canopy
Branches creaking like rigging
Clods of dirt pattering onto leaves
Birds calling from below instead of above
The hollow knock of a woodpecker working upside down
smells: Cold rain-heavy air from the sky below
Sweet rotting fruit wedged in branch forks
rooms: A grove where five great trunks meet at the ceiling, their roots woven into a natural dome you can stand inside.
A long branch walkway with no rail, its bark worn smooth by the feet of something that passes often.
A hollow trunk with a spiral staircase of shelf fungi leading up into the soil ceiling.
A nest of woven vines slung beneath a bough like a hammock, full of eggs the size of a human head.
A clearing where the soil ceiling has collapsed into a sinkhole, opening onto a second sky above the dirt.
A root cellar dug into the ceiling, its shelves still holding jars of preserves from a forgotten ranger camp.
A canopy pool where rainwater gathers in a cupped mass of leaves, held up by a lattice of twigs.
A fallen tree that fell up and lies along the ceiling, now a bridge between two distant groves.
A spider-silk net strung between trunks, glistening and wide enough to catch a horse.
The heart, a single colossal tree whose crown reaches down toward the sky like an open hand, cradling a throne of living wood at its tip.
features: Upward-falling fruit that can be eaten; each grants the eater the ability to walk on the soil ceiling as though it were the ground for 10 minutes.
Rope ladders left by previous explorers; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check identifies which ones are still sound, and each sound ladder lets the party move between levels without checks.
A great knot of roots that can be pulled like a bell rope; doing so shakes the whole grove, knocking flying creatures within 60 feet prone onto the nearest branch.
Updraft vents between branches; a creature that leaps into one can glide 60 feet in any direction before landing, as if under feather fall.
A shrine of carved acorns in a trunk hollow; leaving food there earns a fey guide who points the way to the heart, while taking an acorn summons its angry owner.
hazards: A brittle branch cracks under weight; a DC {dc} Dexterity save lets a creature catch hold, otherwise it falls 30 feet onto the bough below and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
A gust from the sky below roars up through the trees; each creature not holding on makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pushed 15 feet in a random direction.
A rain of clods and stones pours from a weakened patch of ceiling; creatures in a 20-foot area make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage, half on a success.

Hanging moss that looks like a safe rope is actually a feeding tendril; a creature grabbing it makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is lifted toward the ceiling and takes {half} acid damage each round until freed.

environments.name: Clockwork Foundry
environments.summary: A vast factory of gears, pistons and molten metal that keeps building machines no one ordered. Its furnaces are fed by bound fire spirits, and its assembly lines produce soldiers, servants and stranger things that wander off to guard the halls. The space grew from the stubborn will of a long-gone artificer who could not stop making.
readAloud: Heat slaps you across the face as the portal closes. Enormous gears turn in the walls, each tooth as tall as a person, and the whole floor shudders in time with a piston somewhere far below. Orange light spills from open furnace doors, and in its glow a line of half-built metal men hangs on hooks, swaying in unison.

The noise hits first: hammering, grinding, hissing steam, and under it all a steady heartbeat thump that never misses. A conveyor belt rattles past at waist height, carrying brass hands that twitch and grasp at the air. Something on a catwalk above clicks its head toward you and stops working.

Sparks drift through the air like lazy fireflies. Rails run overhead carrying buckets of glowing metal, tipping them into molds that hiss and smoke. The air tastes of copper and burnt oil, and every surface is warm enough that leaning on it feels like a hand pressing back.
sights: Gears the size of houses turning slowly in the walls
Molten metal pouring from swinging buckets
Half-assembled automatons hanging from hooks
Steam venting in sudden white plumes
A fire spirit pacing inside a furnace like a caged cat
Brass tools moving on their own along a workbench
sounds: A deep piston thump like a giant heartbeat
Hammers striking anvils with no smiths
Chains rattling through pulleys overhead
The hiss of hot metal plunged into quench tanks
Ticking from inside the walls, out of sync with everything else
rooms: An assembly hall where three conveyor lines carry limbs, torsos and heads toward a central press that stamps them together.
A casting floor with channels of molten bronze flowing between molds shaped like soldiers lying at attention.
A furnace room where a bound fire elemental burns behind a grille of runes, glaring at anyone who comes near.
A gear gallery where walkways thread between turning cogs, gaps opening and closing with each rotation.
A quench pool of black oil, steaming, with rejected automaton parts sunk to the bottom and still twitching.
A drafting office full of blueprints for machines that should not be possible, pinned in layers to the walls.
A storeroom of unfinished heads on shelves, their eyes following movement and mouths clicking open and shut.
A boiler chamber where pipes groan under pressure and gauges spin past their red markings.
A testing arena with scorched walls and a scoreboard of brass numbers that ticks up when anything dies there.
The heart, a cathedral-sized engine room where the master construct sits wired into the great central gear, its body half machine and half furnace.
features: A control lever bank labeled in an old artificer's script; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check halts one conveyor line, while a failure speeds it up and spills its contents onto the floor.
Unfinished automatons that can be activated with a monster core; each one obeys the party for 1 hour before its program reverts.
Quench tanks of cold oil; dousing a creature in one gives it resistance to fire damage for 1 minute but makes it flammable, granting vulnerability to fire after that minute ends.
A tool rack of self-moving brass tools; a creature using one gains advantage on checks with tinker's or smith's tools, but the tool tries to wander off when set down.
A furnace vent that can be opened or shut with a wheel; opening it fills a 30-foot corridor with superheated air for 1 minute, dealing fire damage to anything that enters.
hazards: A swinging bucket of molten metal tips without warning; creatures in a 10-foot line make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} fire damage, half on a success.
Gear teeth close on a walkway gap; a creature caught between them makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is grappled until a DC {dc} Strength check frees it.
A pressure valve bursts in a gout of steam; each creature within 15 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} fire damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn.

A conveyor belt drags anything on it toward the stamping press; a creature that starts its turn on the belt is moved 15 feet, and one that reaches the press makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Bone Orchard
environments.summary: Rows of trees grown from human and monster bone stretch under a bruised purple sky, their branches heavy with fruit that pulses like hearts. Someone planted the dead here on purpose, and the orchard has been harvesting them ever since. It feels quiet, tended and deeply wrong.
readAloud: The trees are white. It takes you a moment to understand why: their trunks are fused spines, their branches are long finger bones, and their leaves are thin curls of dried skin that whisper in the wind. Red fruit hangs from every bough, and each one beats, slowly, in time with the others.

A dim violet light hangs over orderly rows of pale trees that stretch further than you can see. The soil is dark and soft and smells of iron. Between two trunks, a scarecrow made of ribs turns its skull toward you on a creaking pole.

Your boot sinks into loam and something cracks beneath it, a knuckle bone, a tooth, a small curved rib. Baskets sit at the base of the nearest tree, full of fruit that drips red. Somewhere among the rows, someone is humming a harvest song and snipping with shears.
sights: Trees with trunks of fused vertebrae
Fruit that pulses like a slow heartbeat
Leaves of dried skin curling at the edges
Rib-cage scarecrows on tall poles
Rows of freshly turned graves between the trees
Red sap weeping from cracks in the bone bark
sounds: The soft rattle of bone branches in the wind
Slow, synchronized heartbeats from the fruit
Shears snipping somewhere out of sight
Crows that caw in human voices
Soil shifting as something buried rolls over
smells: Overripe fruit gone sweet and meaty
Copper sap like a fresh cut
rooms: A long avenue of bone trees, each one tagged with a wooden label bearing a name and a date of planting.
A press house where a great wooden press squeezes red fruit into vats of thick, warm juice.
A nursery bed where tiny finger-bone saplings sprout in neat rows, each pushing up from a shallow grave.
A tool shed hung with saws, shears, and bone hooks, a ledger of harvests open on a stool.
A rotten corner of the orchard where the trees have died and collapsed into heaps of brittle white.
A drying rack strung with flayed leaves like laundry, rustling in a breeze you cannot feel.
A well with a bucket of red water, its rope made of braided sinew.
A grafting barn where branches from different skeletons have been bound together onto a single monstrous trunk.
A compost heap taller than a house, steaming, with half-dissolved bodies at its base still reaching out.
The heart, the oldest tree, a giant's skeleton grown upright with its arms spread into a canopy, its skull hollowed into a nest for the orchard's keeper.
features: Heart-fruit that can be eaten raw; the eater regains hit points equal to 2d8 plus their level but makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or hears the dead tree's memories for 1 minute, becoming incapacitated.
Wooden name tags on the trees; a party member who finds a tree bearing a name they recognize can speak to it as if casting speak with dead.
A harvest bell on a post; ringing it summons every orchard worker to the bell within 3 rounds, emptying the rest of the orchard.
Barrels of pressed juice in the press house; pouring one over a corpse causes a sapling to sprout from it within a minute, blocking a 5-foot space with difficult terrain.
Bone scarecrows that turn to face living creatures; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Stealth) check passes one unseen, but on a failure it shrieks and all scarecrows within 120 feet join in.
hazards: Roots of bone burst from the soil to grab ankles; a creature in the area makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is restrained and takes {half} piercing damage at the start of each of its turns until it breaks free.
A freshly planted grave gives way; a creature stepping on it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or sinks to the waist, restrained, as cold hands drag it down for {half} necrotic damage per round.
The fruit bursts when struck; any creature within 5 feet of an exploding fruit makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} necrotic damage and is poisoned for 1 minute.

The orchard tends the living; a creature that rests here for more than 10 minutes makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or begins to sprout small bone buds under the skin, losing 1 hit point per hour until cured by lesser restoration.

environments.name: Endless Library
environments.summary: Shelves rise out of sight and corridors of books bend away into a maze that rearranges itself when no one is looking. The library is a hoard of knowledge that became too heavy and fell into its own pocket of reality. Its librarians are long dead but still on duty, and some of the books read back.
readAloud: Shelves tower above you, so high they vanish into a haze of golden dust. Ladders on brass rails creak along them by themselves, sliding from section to section. The silence here is enormous, the kind that makes your own breathing sound like a shout.

The portal leaves you standing on a carpet worn thin by centuries of soft shoes. Lamps of floating blue light drift down the aisles at walking pace, like readers browsing. Somewhere far off, a book slams shut, and a hundred whispering voices hush at once.

Paper and leather and ink, the smell is thick enough to taste. The aisle in front of you is straight for exactly as long as you watch it; when you blink, it has quietly turned left. On a nearby reading desk, an open book is turning its own pages, faster and faster, as though it has heard you arrive.
sights: Shelves rising into a golden haze
Floating lamps drifting down the aisles
Ladders sliding on their own along brass rails
A book turning its own pages
Ink stains that crawl slowly across the floor
Reading desks with skeletal readers still bent over them
sounds: Pages turning in every direction at once
A distant librarian hissing for silence
Ladder wheels creaking on rails
Whispers that almost form words when you stop moving
The dry click of a card catalog drawer sliding shut
smells: Dust that tastes faintly of cinnamon
Mildew from a flooded lower stack
rooms: A reading room of long tables where skeletons in scholar's robes sit with open books, their fingers still marking their place.
A card catalog hall with drawers stretching beyond sight, each card describing a book that may or may not exist.
A spiral stair of stacked encyclopedias wound around a central pillar that rises into darkness.
A restricted section behind a chained gate, where the books are locked inside iron cages and rattle against the bars.
A bindery where needles and thread stitch pages together in the air, and a stack of blank books waits to be filled.
A flooded lower stack where waterlogged volumes float like lily pads and ink clouds the water black.
A map room whose atlases show the library itself, but the maps disagree with one another.
A children's alcove with cushions, picture books, and a puppet theatre whose puppets turn their heads to watch.
An index chamber where a great brass orrery of floating books orbits a single lectern.
The heart, the head librarian's office, where a vast tome lies open on a desk and its reader, bound in parchment skin, waits to stamp your card.
features: Library cards on a desk; a creature that signs one may borrow a single book, which grants advantage on one Intelligence check of the DM's choice, but the book must be returned before leaving or its borrower is hunted.
Sliding ladders that move on command; a creature that says a section name aloud is carried there at 60 feet per round, which can be a fast route or a dangerous one.
A catalog drawer that holds a card for every person who enters; reading a creature's card reveals its weaknesses, granting advantage on the first attack against it.
Books that read back; a creature that opens one makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is pulled into its story for 1 minute, appearing elsewhere in the library when released.
Silence runes carved into the floor; inside them no sound can be made, which defeats spellcasters but also hides the party from the hunting librarians.
hazards: A shelf topples in a cascade of heavy tomes; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage and are buried, restrained until they spend an action digging free.
Ink stains crawl toward warmth; a creature that touches one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} necrotic damage as words are written into its skin, and it cannot speak for 1 minute.
The aisle rearranges behind the party; the group makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check or loses an hour wandering and must succeed on a DC {dc} Constitution save or gain a level of exhaustion.
A book of forbidden lore shrieks when touched; each creature within 30 feet makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or takes {dmg} psychic damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn.

environments.name: Frozen Battlefield
environments.summary: Two armies met on a winter plain and a killing frost fell on them mid-charge, freezing every soldier where they stood. The astral space holds that last moment forever, a field of ice statues, broken banners and frozen blood. When the wind rises, the dead remember the battle and rise to finish it.
readAloud: Snow crunches under your boots and the cold bites straight through your clothes. All around you, frozen in mid-stride, stand soldiers sheathed in blue ice, swords raised, mouths open in silent war cries. A banner stands rigid as a sheet of glass, its colours still bright beneath the frost.

A grey sky presses down on a plain of trampled snow and splintered spears. Wind sweeps the field, and as it passes, the frozen soldiers creak, every one of them, a sound like a forest of trees bending under weight. Far off, a war horn sounds, thin and ragged, though no one is there to blow it.

Your breath fogs and hangs in front of you. A siege giant lies half-buried in a drift ahead, a frozen arrow in its eye, its great hand still curled around a boulder. Between its fingers, something small and pale is moving.
sights: Soldiers frozen mid-charge in sheaths of blue ice
Banners stiff as glass
Red ice in the hollows where blood pooled
Arrows hanging motionless in the air
A fallen giant half-buried in a drift
Crows frozen in flight above the field
sounds: Ice creaking as the wind passes over the soldiers
A distant war horn with no one blowing it
Snow hissing across hard crust
The crack of ice splitting from a statue
Phantom shouts of command on the wind
smells: Burnt pitch from an extinguished siege fire
Iron of a thousand cold blades
rooms: The front line, a wall of frozen soldiers locked in the moment of collision, shields pressed together and spears tangled.
A command tent stiff with frost, its maps pinned to a table with frozen daggers and a general slumped over them.
A siege trebuchet mid-swing, its stone hanging motionless at the top of its arc above the field.
A field hospital of icy cots where frozen healers lean over frozen wounded.
A frozen river crossing where soldiers stand waist-deep beneath clear ice, faces pressed to the surface.
A supply wagon circle with barrels of frozen ale and crates of iron rations, half buried in drifts.
A chapel tent where a priest's raised hands still glow faintly through the ice with a blessing never finished.
A ditch full of fallen horses, their manes frozen into spikes and their riders tangled beneath them.
A hilltop where the two opposing commanders stand face to face, swords crossed, neither one ever winning.
The heart, the dead giant's ribcage on the hill, where the frost itself has taken a shape like a crowned warlord on a throne of shields.
features: Frozen weapons that can be broken free with a DC {dc} Strength check; each one deals an extra 1d6 cold damage for 1 hour before it thaws and crumbles.
War horns scattered on the field; blowing one makes every undead soldier within 300 feet turn toward the sound, drawing them away from the party or toward it.
A brazier in the command tent that can be relit; while it burns, creatures within 20 feet are immune to the field's cold and the frozen dead will not approach.
Banners of the two armies; a creature carrying one is treated as an ally by that army's dead, but the other army attacks it on sight.
The general's frozen maps; a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check reveals where the battle's treasure chest was hidden before the frost fell.
hazards: Killing cold rolls across the field at dusk; each creature without cold protection makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} cold damage and gains a level of exhaustion.
The frozen river cracks under weight; a creature on it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls into freezing water, taking {half} cold damage each round it remains submerged.
Arrows frozen in the air shatter loose when the wind shifts; creatures in a 30-foot area make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} piercing damage, half on a success.

Touching a frozen soldier bare-handed sticks the skin fast; the creature takes {half} cold damage and is grappled until it succeeds on a DC {dc} Strength check, tearing free for another {half} damage.

environments.name: Fungal Undercity
environments.summary: A buried city where every street, home and temple has been overgrown and replaced by fungus, until the mushrooms themselves became the architecture. Spore-ridden citizens still go about their business in the glow of bioluminescent caps, speaking in slow, damp voices. The colony is one mind, patient and curious, and very interested in new hosts.
readAloud: Soft light glows in blues and greens all around you, coming from mushrooms taller than towers. Their caps form roofs, their gills hang like curtains, and between their stalks run streets paved with spongy, yielding growth. A drifting haze of spores makes everything shimmer.

You step into a marketplace that should be empty and is not. Figures stand at stalls, swaying, their bodies furred with white mold and their faces sprouting delicate fans of fungus. One turns toward you slowly and says, in a voice like wet cloth tearing, 'Welcome. Stay.'

The air is warm and close and sweet, like bread rising. Underfoot, the ground gives with every step and springs back, leaving no footprints. Above, so high it looks like a night sky, the cavern roof is speckled with glowing spores that drift down like slow snow.
sights: Mushroom towers with glowing caps
Spore haze glittering in the light
Mold-furred citizens tending fungal stalls
Streets of springy white growth
Shelf fungi stacked into staircases
Old stone buildings cracked open by stalks
sounds: The soft puff of spores bursting
Slow, damp voices calling out market wares
Dripping from every gill and cap
A low creaking as stalks grow
Breathing from inside the walls
smells: Something like mushrooms frying in butter
rooms: A market square where infected merchants stand behind stalls of glowing caps, endlessly weighing spores on brass scales.
A temple whose dome has become a single enormous puffball, breathing in and out with the congregation.
A row of houses where every window is choked with gill-curtains, and something moves behind each one.
A fungal farm of neat beds where living people lie half buried, mushrooms growing from their chests.
A bridge of braided mycelium spanning a black chasm, swaying when walked.
A sewer channel running with grey slime that pulses with faint light.
A council chamber where the old city's leaders sit in a ring, their heads fused into a single great cap.
A spore-silo, a tall stalk-tower venting clouds that drift out over the city in slow tides.
A library whose books have sprouted, pages blooming into delicate fungal frills.
The heart, a vast cavern where the colony's mother-growth fills the ceiling like a pale sky, threads dangling down to every corner of the city.
features: Glowing caps that can be picked and carried; each sheds dim light in a 15-foot radius for 8 hours and attracts curious citizens rather than hostile ones.
The colony can be bargained with; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check lets the party trade a monster core for safe passage through one district.
Brass scales in the market weigh anything placed on them; setting a creature's possession on one tells the colony that creature's name and intentions.
A pulsing slime channel that can be flooded into the streets by breaking a dam of growth; it fills a 60-foot area with difficult terrain that damages fungal creatures for 2d6 acid damage per turn.
Spore-masks hanging in a guard post; wearing one grants advantage on saves against spores but makes the wearer appear to the colony as one of its own.
hazards: A puffball bursts underfoot; each creature within 15 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} poison damage and is poisoned for 1 minute, half damage and not poisoned on a success.
Infection takes root; a creature that fails a save against spores twice makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each long rest or gains one level of exhaustion as mushrooms sprout from its skin.
The mycelium bridge sags; a creature crossing makes a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or slips, falling 40 feet onto soft growth for {half} bludgeoning damage.
The ground swallows; a creature that stands still for a full round makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pulled in up to the knees and restrained as threads of fungus wrap its legs.

environments.name: Glass Desert
environments.summary: A desert whose sand was fused to glass by some ancient blast of fire, leaving dunes of rippled green and amber crystal under two merciless suns. Light bounces everywhere, blinding and burning, and the creatures here hunt by heat and reflection. It is beautiful at a distance and lethal up close.
readAloud: Light explodes around you as you step through, and you throw up a hand against it. The dunes are glass, smooth green waves of it frozen mid-roll, catching two suns and throwing them back a thousand times. The air above them shimmers like water.

Your boots ring on the ground with every step, a hollow chiming sound. Heat rises in waves that bend the horizon. Half-buried in the glass ahead lies the skeleton of some huge animal, its bones fused into the crystal, sunlight burning white through the hollows of its skull.

The wind blows grit that stings like thrown needles, and somewhere a dune sings, a long glassy note that rises and falls. Far off, a tower of mirrored stone points at the sky, and from its tip a beam of focused light sweeps slowly across the desert like a lighthouse searching for ships.
sights: Rolling dunes of green and amber glass
Two suns burning in a white sky
Heat shimmer bending the horizon
Creatures fused mid-stride inside the glass
A sweeping beam of focused sunlight
Cracked glass plains glittering like spilled jewels
sounds: Boots ringing on glass
Dunes singing a long rising note
Grit hissing across slick surfaces
Sharp cracks as glass cools at dusk
A distant chime like windblown bells
smells: Cooked meat from something caught in the beam
rooms: A dune valley where the glass has been ground smooth into a mirror floor, reflecting the sky so perfectly it feels like walking on air.
A buried caravan, wagons and camels encased in amber glass, their cargo still visible within.
A glass cave where a bubble formed in the cooling sand, now a cool blue grotto lit from above.
A field of glass spires jutting like spears, each one humming in the wind.
A cracked basin where the glass has split into a maze of deep, narrow canyons.
An oasis of molten glass that bubbles in a sunken crater, its surface rippling like a slow pond.
A shadow shrine, a ring of dark obsidian slabs that casts the only shade for miles.
A nest of glass-backed lizards, their eggs like blown-glass orbs nestled in warm sand.
The mirrored tower's base, ringed with angled glass panels that focus sunlight upward.
The heart, the top of the mirror tower, where a creature of living flame and prism stands inside the burning lens that makes the beam.
features: Mirror plates that can be angled; a creature with an action can redirect the tower's beam to strike a target within 60 feet for 4d10 radiant damage, DC {dc} Dexterity save for half.
The shadow shrine; creatures resting inside it suffer no heat exhaustion and recover from one level of exhaustion during a short rest.
Fused caravan cargo; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check with a heavy tool breaks the glass and recovers crates of spirit coins and trade goods.
Singing dunes; a creature that matches the dune's note with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check calms nearby glass-born creatures for 10 minutes.

Blown-glass eggs; each can be thrown as a fragile flask that bursts into blinding light, forcing creatures within 10 feet to make a DC {dc} Constitution save or be blinded until the end of their next turn.
hazards: Two suns at zenith; each hour without shade or protection, a creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} fire damage and gains a level of exhaustion.
Reflected glare off a mirror floor; creatures crossing it make a DC {dc} Constitution save or are blinded for 1 minute.
A thin crust of glass over a hollow; a creature that steps on it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls 20 feet onto jagged shards, taking {dmg} slashing damage.

The searching beam sweeps the dunes; a creature caught in the open when it passes makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} fire damage, half on a success, and its position is revealed to the heart.

environments.name: Storm-Wracked Sky Islands
environments.summary: Chunks of earth float in an endless storm, tethered together by frayed chains and swinging rope bridges. Lightning crawls through the clouds and wind tears at everything not lashed down. Something huge and winged circles the largest island, and the storm seems to answer to it.
readAloud: Wind hits you like a slammed door the instant you arrive. You stand on a slab of grassy rock floating in a sky full of churning grey cloud, and other islands drift around you, rising and falling like boats on a swell. Lightning forks between them, close enough that your hair stands on end.

A rope bridge stretches away from your feet toward the next island, bucking and twisting in the gale. Rain lashes sideways. Below the bridge there is nothing at all, only cloud and the distant flicker of lightning far, far down.

The thunder never stops; it rolls and rolls, one peal blending into the next. Between gusts you catch a glimpse of the largest island, a mountain of rock with a crumbling fortress at its peak, and around it, half hidden in the clouds, a long dark shape with wings.
sights: Islands rising and falling on unseen currents
Lightning forking between floating rocks
Rope bridges twisting in the gale
Waterfalls pouring off island edges into nothing
Chains thick as tree trunks stretched taut between islands
A winged shadow moving through the storm
sounds: Constant rolling thunder
Wind shrieking across the rock
Chains groaning under strain
Rope bridges snapping taut
A distant roar that answers the thunder
smells: Musk of a large reptile on the wind
rooms: A small island no bigger than a cottage, holding a single bent tree and a shrine to forgotten sky spirits.
A rope bridge with half its planks missing, stretched over a hundred feet of empty sky.
A chain-linked island where great iron links are anchored into the rock, each one humming in the wind.
A ruined watchtower clinging to an island's edge, its bell long gone and its stairs open to the storm.
A waterfall island, where rain collects in a pool and pours off the edge in a ribbon that never reaches the ground.
A nest of storm birds wedged into a rocky crevice, bright eggs crackling with static.
A wrecked airship lodged between two islands, its hull split and its balloon a shredded flag.
A grassy meadow island where the wind is calm in a perfect circle, protected by standing stones.
A lightning rod garden of iron spikes driven into the rock, each one charred and smoking.
The heart, the fortress on the largest island, its roof torn away, where a storm drake coils around a throne in the eye of the tempest.
features: Lightning rods that can be pulled free; a creature holding one is immune to the next lightning bolt that would strike it, after which the rod melts.
The calm meadow's standing stones; creatures inside the circle can take a short rest undisturbed by wind and gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to watch the sky.
The wrecked airship's sails; a DC {dc} Intelligence check rigs a sail into a glider that carries up to two creatures 300 feet to another island.
Iron chains between islands; a creature can climb hand over hand along one with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check instead of crossing a bridge.
Storm bird eggs; each crackles with stored lightning and can be thrown to deal 3d8 lightning damage in a 10-foot radius, DC {dc} Dexterity save for half.
hazards: A gale gust sweeps across an island; each creature makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pushed 20 feet toward the nearest edge, and a creature pushed off falls into the clouds.
Lightning strikes metal; a creature wearing metal armour or holding a metal weapon in the open makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save each hour or takes {dmg} lightning damage.

A rope bridge snaps mid-crossing; creatures on it make a DC {dc} Dexterity save to grab the rope, otherwise they fall, and a creature that grabs on takes {half} bludgeoning damage swinging into the cliff.
Two islands drift together and collide; creatures near the edge of either make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage from falling rock, half on a success.

environments.name: Living Flesh-Hive
environments.summary: The walls are meat, the floors are muscle, and the doors are sphincters that clench shut behind you. This astral space is the inside of something alive, a hive of flesh that grows its own guardians from pustules and fluid. It breathes, it bleeds, and it knows exactly where you are.
readAloud: The floor is warm and soft and it moves under you, a slow rhythmic flex like the chest of a sleeping animal. The walls are pink and glistening, threaded with blue veins as thick as your arm, and they pulse with a heartbeat you can feel in your teeth.

Wet heat closes around you like a mouth. A tunnel of ribbed red flesh stretches ahead, lit by sacs of yellow fluid that glow from within. Somewhere deep in the hive, something gurgles, and the whole passage contracts gently around you before relaxing again.

A sound like breathing fills the chamber, huge and slow. Drops of clear fluid fall from the ceiling and sizzle where they hit your armour. In the wall beside you, a cluster of eyes opens all at once, wet and blinking, and stares.
sights: Walls of glistening pink flesh veined with blue
Glowing sacs of yellow fluid
Clusters of eyes opening in the walls
Doorways that clench shut like mouths
Pods with shapes curled inside
Rivulets of blood running along grooves in the floor
sounds: A slow, enormous heartbeat
Wet gurgling from deep passages
Breathing that fills the chambers
The squelch of every footstep
Distant chittering from the brood chambers
rooms: A ribbed tunnel that slowly constricts every few minutes, squeezing anything inside toward the next chamber.
A brood chamber lined with translucent pods, each holding a curled creature that twitches in its sleep.
A digestion pit, a basin of green fluid where half-dissolved armour and bones bob on the surface.
A heart chamber where a fleshy organ the size of a cottage beats against the ceiling.
A lung hall of spongy pink walls that swell inward and deflate, pushing and pulling the air.
A nerve gallery where glowing white fibers stretch across the room like harp strings, twitching at every touch.
A gland grotto dripping with sweet-smelling nectar that draws insects and worse.
A gullet shaft dropping straight down into darkness, its walls lined with tiny teeth pointed inward.
A trophy wall where the hive has absorbed adventurers into its flesh, their faces still visible beneath a thin pink skin.
The heart, the queen chamber, where the hive mother fills the room, a swollen mass of flesh and limbs fused into the walls with a dozen mouths that sing.
features: Nerve fibers that can be cut; severing one with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check blinds the hive's eyes in that region for 10 minutes, granting advantage on Stealth checks.
Glowing fluid sacs that can be harvested; drinking one heals 2d8 hit points but the drinker must make a DC {dc} Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour.
Sphincter doors; striking one deals pain to the hive and makes it open, but every guardian within 120 feet knows the door was forced.
Absorbed adventurers in the trophy wall; cutting one free with a DC {dc} Strength check recovers their gear, and one in four is still alive and grateful.
Gland nectar; smearing it on a creature makes the hive's guardians treat it as kin for 10 minutes, though the smell lingers for a day.
hazards: The tunnel contracts; each creature inside makes a DC {dc} Strength save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is pushed 30 feet deeper into the hive, half damage and not moved on a success.

Acidic drips from the ceiling; a creature that lingers in a digestion area for a full round makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} acid damage and its armour suffers a permanent -1 to AC until repaired.
The floor swallows; a creature that falls prone sinks into the flesh and makes a DC {dc} Strength save each round or is restrained and takes {half} acid damage.
Spore-laden breath from the lung hall; creatures inside when it exhales make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} poison damage and are poisoned for 1 minute.

environments.name: Mirror Palace
environments.summary: A palace of silvered glass where every wall is a mirror and every reflection has opinions. A vain sorcerer-prince built it to admire himself forever, and the mirrors absorbed his vanity and now hunger for faces of their own. Reflections step out to replace the people they copy.
readAloud: Ten thousand versions of you stand in every direction, stretching away in endless silver corridors. When you move, they move. When you stop, a few of them keep going, just for a moment, before they notice and catch up.

Chandeliers of crystal hang overhead, throwing rainbows across walls of perfect polished glass. Your footsteps echo strangely, as though the room is slightly larger than it looks. In the nearest mirror, your reflection smiles at you, and you are certain your own face is not smiling.

Soft music drifts through the hall, a waltz played by no instrument you can see. A long gallery of mirrors stretches ahead, each one framed in gold, and each one shows a different version of the room. In one, the floor is covered in blood. In another, you are already dead.
sights: Infinite reflections stretching away in every direction
Reflections that move a heartbeat too late
Crystal chandeliers scattering rainbows
Golden frames around mirrors showing other places
Cracked mirrors leaking silver light
A throne of glass facing a wall of mirrors
sounds: A waltz with no players
Glass chiming as you walk past
Whispers coming from behind the mirrors
Your own voice repeating words you did not say
The sudden sharp crack of breaking glass
rooms: A hall of infinite reflections, where the true exit is the only mirror that does not show you.
A dressing room of vanity tables, each with a mirror that shows the viewer as they wish to be.
A ballroom of glass floors and glass ceilings, where reflected dancers waltz beneath your feet.
A gallery of framed mirrors, each showing a different astral space like windows into elsewhere.
A shattered chamber where a mirror was broken from within, glass shards scattered outward across the floor.
A portrait room where every portrait is a mirror and the reflections wear the clothes of the old court.
A maze of mirrored hedges in a glass garden, where wrong turns lead back to the start.
A dungeon of black mirrors where reflections that misbehaved are imprisoned, hammering silently on the glass.
A bedchamber with a canopy of mirrors, the prince's reflection still asleep in a bed that is empty.
The heart, the prince's throne room, where a single colossal mirror holds his reflection, and it steps out wearing a crown of glass.
features: Mirrors that show what is behind you; a creature watching one gains advantage on Perception checks and cannot be surprised.
Vanity mirrors that grant a wish of appearance; a creature that gazes in one gains advantage on Charisma checks for 1 hour, but its reflection now wants to be it and stalks it.
Breaking a mirror frees whatever is inside it; roll a d6 when one shatters, on a 1 a hostile reflection emerges, on a 6 a grateful prisoner offers information.
Gallery windows to other spaces; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check reveals a mirror can be stepped through to reach another part of the palace instantly.
The black mirrors in the dungeon; a creature that speaks to an imprisoned reflection can learn the heart's weakness, but must promise to free it.
hazards: A reflection steps out and attacks its original, using the same statistics and weapons, and it can be told apart only with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check.
A wall of glass shatters in a spray; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} slashing damage, half on a success.
Endless reflections bewilder the mind; a creature lost in the hall of infinite reflections makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is confused for 1 minute, as the confusion spell.
Concentrated light from the chandeliers focuses into a beam; a creature in the beam's path makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} radiant damage, half on a success.

environments.name: Sunken Ship Graveyard
environments.summary: A drowned sea floor littered with hundreds of wrecked ships, stacked and tangled where some terrible current dragged them together. A bubble of breathable air hangs above the wreckage, but the deep water below is home to drowned sailors and hungry things. The space is ruled by the ghost of a captain who never stopped looking for land.
readAloud: You stand on a slanted deck slick with weed, and everywhere around you are ships, hundreds of them, piled one upon another like toys in a drain. Masts stick up at crazy angles. Above, the sea forms a dark green ceiling, held back by some strange force, rippling with the movements of something huge swimming past.

The air is cold and smells of salt and rotting wood. Lanterns hang from broken spars, still burning with a greenish light. On a nearby deck, a sailor in a waterlogged coat coils a rope over and over, his face hidden under his hat, humming a sea shanty in a voice full of water.

Water drips from every surface, pooling in your footprints. Barnacled hulls creak and groan as the wreckage shifts. Far below, through the gaps between broken ships, you catch a glimpse of open water and a pale shape gliding through it, circling slowly.
sights: Ships piled on ships at impossible angles
A sea held overhead like a green ceiling
Green lanterns burning on broken spars
Drowned sailors still working the rigging
Barnacle-crusted figureheads with weeping eyes
Tattered sails hanging like burial shrouds
sounds: Wood groaning as the wreckage shifts
A sea shanty sung by drowned voices
Bells clanging from sunken masts
Water dripping and trickling everywhere
Something huge bumping against the hulls from below
smells: Rum gone sour in broken casks
rooms: A capsized galleon whose upside-down hold forms a long dark cavern of hanging cargo nets.
A merchant ship's cabin full of spilled spirit coins scattered among waterlogged ledgers.
A bridge of lashed-together masts spanning a gap between two wrecks, swaying over open water.
A gun deck where rows of rusted cannons point at nothing, and a skeletal crew stands ready at each.
A flooded bilge where knee-deep water hides fallen cargo and things that bite.
A crow's nest perched at the top of the tallest mast, offering a view across the entire graveyard.
A galley where the cook still stirs a pot of grey stew over a cold stove.
A figurehead garden where dozens of carved figures have been gathered and arranged in a ring, as if in council.
A shark-infested channel of open water winding between the wrecks like a street.
The heart, the ghost captain's flagship, perched on top of the pile, its wheel spinning endlessly as he steers toward a shore that never comes.
features: Ship bells that can be rung; each one summons the drowned crew of that ship, who will either fight for the ringer or against, depending on whether the ringer can name the ship.
The captain's charts; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Navigation tools) check finds the course the captain dreams of, and showing it to him ends the fight peacefully.
Cannons on the gun deck; with powder found in the hold, a cannon can be fired once for 6d10 bludgeoning damage, DC {dc} Dexterity save for half, against a target within 300 feet.
Air pockets in capsized hulls; creatures can rest safely inside, but the air lasts only 1 hour per creature.
Spilled rum casks; pouring rum onto the deck draws the drowned sailors to drink, distracting them for 1d4 rounds.
hazards: The wreckage shifts and slides; creatures on the moving deck make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall prone and slide 20 feet, taking {half} bludgeoning damage.
The sea ceiling dips and water crashes down; creatures in a 30-foot area make a DC {dc} Strength save or are knocked prone and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Rotten planks give way; a creature crossing makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls through into the flooded hold below, landing in deep water with whatever lives there.
Drowning song; creatures that hear the drowned crew's shanty make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or are charmed and walk toward the water for 1 minute.

environments.name: The Repeating Manor
environments.summary: An aristocratic manor whose hallways loop back on themselves, so that every door leads to another copy of the same rooms with small and growing differences. A family that hoarded secrets and spite lived here, and their last evening repeats endlessly in slightly worsening versions. Somewhere in the loop is the original house, and in it the family's terrible secret.
readAloud: Warm candlelight spills across polished floors and walls of dark wood paneling. A grandfather clock ticks in the entry hall. Portraits of stern men and women in fine clothes watch from the walls. Everything is perfectly tidy, perfectly quiet, and perfectly ordinary, which is the most unsettling thing about it.

You open a door and step into the same entry hall you just left. The clock still ticks. The portraits still watch. But now one of them is crying, and the candle on the side table has burned down a little further.

Laughter and the clink of glasses drift from a dining room down the hall. A butler in black passes you without looking, carrying a silver tray with a single covered dish. As he turns the corner, you notice he leaves no footprints in the dust, and the dish beneath the cover is rattling.
sights: Portraits whose expressions change between loops
A grandfather clock always showing a quarter to nine
Candles burning down a little more each loop
Footprints in dust that match your own boots
A dining table set for a family dinner that never ends
Doors with numbers painted on in red that increase
sounds: A clock ticking slightly too slowly
Laughter from a distant dining room
Footsteps upstairs when no one is there
A piano playing the same lullaby over and over
A child counting slowly, as in hide and seek
smells: A faint sweetness like poisoned wine
rooms: An entry hall with a grandfather clock, portraits and a grand staircase that always leads back down to this same hall.
A dining room where the family sits at dinner, ghostly and smiling, raising toasts to a chair left empty for a guest.
A nursery with a rocking horse that rocks by itself and a crib with something whimpering under the blanket.
A study lined with ledgers that record debts, secrets, and the names of people the family ruined.
A conservatory of dead roses, their petals falling and reattaching in endless repetition.
A servant's passage behind the walls, narrow and dusty, which connects loops in unexpected ways.
A master bedroom where the lady of the house brushes her hair at a mirror and her reflection weeps.
A wine cellar with racks of bottles, one of which is labeled with a skull and the date of the fatal dinner.
A locked attic where the family's forgotten heir was kept, the walls covered in scratched tally marks.
The heart, the original dining room, decaying and real, where the poisoner waits at the head of the table with a glass raised.
features: The grandfather clock; adjusting its hands with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check sends the party to an earlier, safer version of the loop, but it can be done only once.
Changing portraits; a creature who studies them across three loops learns which family member is the poisoner, gaining advantage on attacks against them.
The family ledgers; a DC {dc} Intelligence check reveals a debt that can be paid in spirit coins at the dining table, which makes one family ghost a friend.
Chalk marks on doors; the party can mark doors to track loops, and a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check finds the way toward the original house.
The empty chair at dinner; a creature that sits in it is greeted as an honoured guest, and the ghosts answer one question honestly before the meal turns sour.
hazards: Each loop worsens; every time the party passes through a door, roll a d6, and on a 1 the next copy is hostile and the ghosts attack.
The poisoned wine; a creature that drinks from a glass at dinner makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} poison damage and is poisoned for 1 hour.
Losing yourself in the loop; a creature that spends more than an hour inside makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or forgets why it came, and has disadvantage on Intelligence checks until it leaves.
The stair collapses into itself; creatures on the grand staircase when the loop resets make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall, taking {half} bludgeoning damage and arriving in a random room.

environments.name: Salt Mines
environments.summary: Pale tunnels of crystalline salt descend into the dark, worked by miners who long ago turned into salt pillars where they stood. The space grew from the dried-out bed of an ancient sea, and the brine left behind still remembers the water. Thirst is a constant companion and the walls sparkle with a cruel beauty.
readAloud: The walls glitter white and pink under your lantern, each facet catching the light like frost on a window. Your lips taste of salt before you have even spoken. Old mine cart rails curve away into the dark, crusted over with crystals.

Picks and shovels lean against the tunnel walls, as if the miners just stepped away for lunch. Then you see the miners. They stand along the walls, frozen mid-swing, their bodies turned entirely to pale salt, their faces worn smooth by the slow drip of brine.

A deep cavern opens below you, its floor a perfect mirror of still brine reflecting a ceiling hung with pink salt stalactites. A wooden staircase spirals down the wall toward it, and from the water drifts a faint, rhythmic sound like waves on a beach that is not there.
sights: White and pink salt walls that glitter in lamplight
Miners frozen into salt pillars mid-swing
Mine carts crusted with crystals
A mirror lake of still brine
Salt stalactites like icicles
Carved salt chapels deep in the tunnels
sounds: Brine dripping slowly
The crunch of salt underfoot
Phantom picks striking stone in distant tunnels
Waves lapping on a shore that is not there
The groan of old timber supports
smells: Dry dust that stings the nose
rooms: A main shaft where a great wooden lift hangs from frayed ropes, descending into darkness.
A miners' chapel carved entirely from salt, its altar and pews glowing faintly pink in lantern light.
A brine lake cavern, its surface perfectly still and reflecting the ceiling so that the room seems twice as tall.
A cart junction where rails branch in five directions, a lever station rusted but workable.
A barracks of salt bunks where the miners slept, their belongings crusted over and preserved.
A collapsed tunnel where a cave-in trapped a crew, their salt shapes reaching for the light.
A crystal gallery where salt has grown into huge clear cubes the size of wagons.
A foreman's office with ledgers of daily quotas and a lockbox half-buried in salt.
An ancient seabed layer, where fossilized sea creatures are embedded in the walls and sometimes twitch.
The heart, the deepest chamber, where the brine has risen into a living tide of salt and water around the first miner to be taken.
features: Mine carts on working rails; a DC {dc} Dexterity check with land vehicles sends the party racing 300 feet per round through the tunnels, outpacing pursuit.
The salt chapel; a creature that prays there and leaves an offering of water is protected from the dehydrating effect of the mines for 24 hours.
Salt pillars of miners; touching one and speaking their name, found in the foreman's ledgers, returns them briefly to speech to warn of nearby danger.
Brine lake reflections show hidden passages; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check spots a doorway visible only in the reflection.
Raw salt crystals can be thrown at salt and brine elementals; a creature struck takes 2d6 extra damage as the crystal disrupts its form.
hazards: The salt draws moisture; each hour in the mines, a creature without extra water makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
A brittle ceiling of salt stalactites; loud noise brings them down, and creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} piercing damage.

Brine pools sting open wounds; a creature with fewer than half its hit points that enters one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} acid damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn.

Slow petrification; a creature that touches a salt miner barehanded makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or begins turning to salt, restrained, and petrified after a second failed save at the end of its next turn.

environments.name: Giant's Ribcage
environments.summary: The skeleton of a titan lies across a grassy valley, its ribs arching overhead like the beams of a great hall. Life has crept in: moss on the bones, birds nesting in the eye sockets, and scavenger tribes camping in the hollows of the spine. The giant's strength still lingers in its marrow, and some of what lives here has grown huge on it.
readAloud: Ribs rise around you like the arches of a cathedral, each one as thick as an old oak and green with moss. Sunlight falls between them in long golden bars. Far ahead, the skull lies on its side on a distant hill, and something has built a nest inside its open jaw.

Wind whistles through the bones with a low hollow moan. The ground here is soft and lumpy, and it takes you a moment to realize you are standing in what was once the creature's chest, now filled with soil and wildflowers. A spring bubbles up where its heart should be.
