Smoke rises from campfires along the giant's spine. Huts of hide and bone cling to the vertebrae, each one the size of a small house. Someone up there is beating a drum, slow and heavy, and the sound echoes through the empty ribs like a heartbeat.
sights: Ribs arching overhead like cathedral beams
Moss and wildflowers growing on old bone
A skull on a distant hill with a nest in its jaw
Huts built along the vertebrae
A spring bubbling up where the heart once beat
Marrow seeping golden from cracked bones
sounds: Wind moaning through hollow bones
Drums from the spine camps
Birdsong echoing in the ribs
The creak of old bone settling
Something large chewing in the dark of a broken femur
rooms: The chest cavity, a meadow under curving ribs where wildflowers grow thick around the heart spring.
A broken femur hollow, a long tunnel of bone where something has been gnawing the marrow for years.
A spine village of hide tents clinging to the vertebrae, linked by ladders and rope bridges.
The skull, lying on its side, its eye sockets now caves full of nesting birds.
A hand lying open on the ground, each finger a ridge of bone, the palm cupped into a shallow pond.
A pelvis arena, a wide bowl of bone where tribes settle disputes by combat.
A jaw nest built of tree trunks and bones, where a giant raptor guards its brood.
A cracked sternum overlooking the valley, used by the tribes as a lookout post.
A marrow pit where golden fluid pools in the broken end of a great bone, thick and slow-moving.
The heart, the inside of the skull, where the giant's lingering spirit gathers into a towering figure of moss, bone and light.
features: Giant marrow; a creature that drinks a cup of it gains advantage on Strength checks and saves for 1 hour, but makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for the same duration.
The heart spring; a creature that drinks from it regains one spent Hit Die and is cured of one disease.
The spine tribes; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check earns a guide, and offering monster cores earns warriors for the fight at the heart.
The pelvis arena; a party member who wins a duel there earns the tribes' respect and safe passage through the giant's body.
Hollow bones that amplify sound; a creature that shouts into one can be heard anywhere in the valley, useful for signals or for drawing monsters away.
hazards: A rib cracks and sheds a slab of bone; creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Marrow ooze lurks in the femur; a creature that touches the golden fluid makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} acid damage and is restrained as the ooze clings.
A climb up the slick moss of a rib; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check is needed, and a failure means a fall of 30 feet for {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
The giant's spirit stirs; when the heart is approached, the whole skeleton shudders, and each creature on the bones makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls prone.

environments.name: Candlelit Catacombs
environments.summary: Endless tunnels of skulls and bones are lit by thousands of candles that never burn down, placed by mourners who never stopped coming. The candles hold back the dark and what dwells in it, but each one is tied to a soul. When a candle goes out, its dead wake up.
readAloud: Candlelight flickers across walls made of skulls, row upon row of them, stacked like bricks and staring with empty eyes. Hundreds of small flames burn in niches and on ledges, dripping wax in long white beards that pool on the floor.

It is warm here, warmer than any tomb should be. The air is thick with the sweet smell of wax and the faint tang of old bone. Somewhere ahead, a single candle gutters and goes out, and in the sudden darkness something scrapes along the stone.

Narrow passages twist away in every direction, each lined with shelves of bones and lit by trembling flames. Tiny inscriptions are carved beneath every skull, names and dates, and beside many of them are fresh flowers that cannot be more than a day old.
sights: Walls of stacked skulls staring outward
Thousands of candles in niches
Wax pooled on the floor in long rivers
Fresh flowers beside ancient names
Shadows that move against the candlelight
Bones arranged into elaborate patterns and mosaics
sounds: The soft hiss of burning wicks
Wax dripping onto stone
Distant whispered prayers
Bones shifting in their niches
A sudden draft snuffing a candle
rooms: A skull gallery where the bones are arranged in perfect rows, each skull with a candle on its crown.
An ossuary chapel where altars, pews and a chandelier are built entirely from bones.
A wax river cavern where melted wax flows slowly down the passages into a glowing white lake.
A mourners' alcove with kneeling stools and baskets of candles waiting to be lit.
A dark section where the candles have all gone out and the bones have climbed down from their shelves.
A chandler's workshop with molds, wicks, and vats of warm tallow made from something best not considered.
A child's crypt where small skulls are decorated with painted flowers and toy offerings.
A crossroads of four tunnels with a great iron candelabrum at the centre, its forty candles burning blue.
A sealed vault of noble dead in gilded coffins, candles in gold holders guarding each.
The heart, the first candle's chamber, where a vast pillar of wax holds a single flame that is the catacomb's soul, guarded by the keeper of the dead.
features: Unlit candles in the mourners' alcove; lighting one and placing it in a dark section makes the undead there return to their niches.
Snuffing a candle wakes its dead; the party can deliberately snuff candles behind them to set the undead against pursuers.
The great candelabrum; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check reveals the pattern of lit and unlit candles that opens the sealed vault.
Wax river; a creature coated in warm wax gains resistance to cold damage for 1 hour, but has disadvantage on Dexterity checks.
Bone mosaics; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check finds a story told in bone that hints at the keeper's weakness, granting advantage on the first attack against it.
hazards: A cold draft rushes through the tunnels, snuffing candles in a 30-foot area; the undead there rise and attack immediately.
Molten wax drips from a ceiling of candles; creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} fire damage and are restrained as the wax hardens.
A pile of bones collapses into a rattling wave; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Strength save or are knocked prone and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
The keeper's curse; a creature that steals a candle makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is haunted, and its own light sources go out at the worst moment, at the DM's discretion, once per hour.

environments.name: Marsh of Drowned Bells
environments.summary: A misty marsh where a whole town sank into the mud, its bells still ringing beneath the black water. The tolling draws listeners into the reeds, and fey lights dance over the sunken rooftops. It feels melancholy and dreamlike, like a funeral that never ended.
readAloud: Mist curls thick around your knees, hiding the water until your boot sinks into cold mud. Reeds rise taller than your head, rustling. And from somewhere below the surface, a bell rings, slow and muffled, as though tolling from the bottom of a well.

Pale lights drift between the reeds, bobbing like lanterns carried by invisible hands. Ahead, the tip of a church spire juts from the black water, a bronze weathervane spinning lazily on top. As you watch, a second bell answers the first from somewhere in the fog.

The air is heavy and damp and smells of rot and lilies. Frogs fall silent all at once. Through the mist you glimpse rooftops just above the water, shingled and mossy, and on one of them sits a pale figure in a soaked dress, ringing a tiny handbell.
sights: Spires and rooftops poking from black water
Will-o'-wisps bobbing between reeds
Mist rolling across the surface
Bronze bells visible beneath the water
Lily pads as wide as tables
Pale faces under the surface, eyes open
sounds: Muffled bells tolling under the water
Frogs croaking, then falling silent
Reeds rustling with no wind
A handbell ringing far away
Mud sucking at your boots
rooms: A sunken town square where only the top of a fountain shows above the water, a stone fish spouting mud.
A bell tower rising from the marsh, its bell hanging just below the surface, ringing when the water stirs.
A drowned inn whose upper floor is still dry, with a fire burning in the hearth and no one tending it.
A reed maze where paths of solid ground twist through towering grass and dead-end in deep water.
A lily pad crossing where giant pads float in a line, strong enough to hold a person if they move quickly.
A graveyard where headstones lean out of the water and the graves have been opened from below.
A heron rookery in a stand of dead trees, the great birds watching the party with sharp eyes.
A wisp grove where dozens of floating lights hover over a single dry hummock of moss.
A sunken chapel where the pews are submerged and the altar sits on a small island of mud.
The heart, the drowned belfry, where the town's great bell hangs over a black pool, and the bell-ringer waits for someone to take her place.
features: Handbells scattered on rooftops; ringing one calms the drowned for 1 minute, but each ring draws the wisps closer.
Will-o'-wisps can be followed; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check tells false lights from true, and true lights lead to dry ground and treasure.
The drowned inn's hearth; creatures resting by it can take a short rest safely, but must make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or fall into a dreamless sleep for 8 hours.
The sunken bells can be silenced; a creature that dives and wedges cloth into a bell with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check stops its tolling and weakens the drowned in that area.
Lily pad flowers; a creature that eats one can breathe water for 1 hour but hears the drowned whispering for a day.
hazards: The bells toll and call; each creature that hears them makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed and walks toward the deepest water for 1 minute.
Sucking mud; a creature that steps off the path makes a DC {dc} Strength save or sinks to the waist and is restrained, sinking further each round.
Drowned hands from below; a creature in the water makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pulled under and takes {half} necrotic damage each round it is held.
Marsh fever; creatures who spend a night in the marsh make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} poison damage and have disadvantage on Constitution checks for a day.

environments.name: Perpetual Masquerade
environments.summary: A grand ballroom where the dance has gone on for centuries, its guests masked, gorgeous, and unable to stop. A bargain with something from below made the party eternal, and the price was everyone who attended. Newcomers are welcomed warmly, handed a mask, and invited to dance forever.
readAloud: Music sweeps over you as you arrive, a lilting waltz played by an orchestra in gilded masks. The ballroom glitters with gold leaf and crystal, and hundreds of masked dancers whirl across a marble floor in perfect unison. Every one of them turns their head to look at you at exactly the same moment.

A servant in a porcelain mask glides up and offers you a tray of masks, each one more beautiful than the last: feathered, jeweled, painted with laughing faces. 'You cannot stay without one,' she says sweetly. 'And you will want to stay.'

Laughter and conversation swell around you, but none of the words quite make sense. The dancers' shoes are worn to ragged leather and their feet beneath are bloody, yet they keep smiling. Far across the room, on a balcony draped in red velvet, a figure with horns curling from beneath a silver mask raises a glass to you.
sights: Masked dancers whirling in perfect unison
Gold leaf and crystal chandeliers
A table of food that never empties
Worn shoes and bloody feet beneath gowns
A horned host on a velvet balcony
Masks of every kind on a servant's tray
sounds: A waltz that never ends
Laughter that never quite reaches the eyes
The rustle of silk and the click of heels
Glasses chiming in toasts
Whispered bargains in shadowed alcoves
rooms: The grand ballroom, where hundreds of dancers spin under three vast chandeliers and the floor never stops shining.
A banquet hall with a table stretching out of sight, laden with feasts that taste of ash to the unmasked.
A card room where gamblers stake memories, years and names on hands of a strange deck.
A garden terrace under a starless sky, hedges trimmed into dancers frozen mid-step.
A cloakroom full of the coats of guests who arrived and never left, their pockets still holding letters home.
An orchestra pit where the musicians' hands have worn through to bone on their instruments.
A mask-maker's studio where blank masks hang drying and a crafter shapes new faces from old ones.
A retiring room of velvet couches where exhausted guests sleep standing up, still swaying to the music.
A hall of portraits showing each guest unmasked, faces aging with each painting.
The heart, the host's balcony, a velvet stage above the dance where the horned host holds the contract that binds the ball.
features: Masks from the servant's tray; wearing one makes the guests friendly and lets the wearer move freely, but each hour the wearer makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or begins to dance and cannot stop.
The card room; a creature can gamble with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) or gaming set check, winning information about the host or losing a memory chosen by the DM.
The cloakroom letters; reading a guest's letter aloud to them breaks the spell on that guest for 1 minute, and a freed guest may help the party.
The orchestra; stopping the music for a round with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) or Strength check makes every dancer collapse, giving the party a round of freedom.
The host's contract; it can be read with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check, revealing a loophole that ends the ball if exploited.
hazards: The dance pulls in the unmasked; a creature that steps onto the ballroom floor makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is compelled to dance for 1 minute, unable to take actions or move except in a waltz.
Feast of ash; a creature that eats the banquet food makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} necrotic damage and gains a level of exhaustion.
A broken bargain; a creature that refuses the host's toast makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or takes {dmg} fire damage from a sudden flame of brimstone.
The swirl of dancers; creatures moving through the crowd must succeed on a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or be knocked prone and trampled for {half} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Amber Hive
environments.summary: A colossal beehive of glowing amber honeycomb, buzzing with insects the size of dogs and dripping with honey that has gone hard and golden over centuries. Creatures that wandered in are sealed in amber walls, perfectly preserved. It is warm, sweet and humming with life.
readAloud: Golden light surrounds you, warm and syrupy, glowing through walls of translucent amber. The honeycomb cells are each as tall as a person, and in some of them, fat white larvae curl and stir. The buzzing is everywhere, a low thrumming that vibrates through your chest.

Honey drips from the ceiling in slow, glistening strands, and the floor is sticky beneath your boots. Inside the amber walls, you see shapes frozen in place: insects, birds, a deer mid-leap, and an armoured adventurer reaching for the surface with one hand.

The air is thick and sweet and warm, almost too warm to breathe. A bee the size of a hound lands on the wall beside you, its wings whirring like a saw, and turns its great black eyes toward you with mild interest.
sights: Glowing amber walls of honeycomb
Creatures frozen inside the amber
Honey dripping from the ceiling in long strands
Larvae curling in open cells
Giant bees with wings like stained glass
Pollen drifting in golden clouds
sounds: A deep, constant buzzing
Wings whirring like saws
The slow drip of honey
The scrape of wax being built
A chorus of humming that rises when the queen moves
smells: Warm air like a summer field
A sharp, chemical alarm scent when bees are threatened
rooms: A honeycomb gallery where cells line the walls floor to ceiling, many sealed with wax caps.
A nursery chamber full of larvae, tended by worker bees that bristle at intruders.
A honey pool cavern where a lake of thick golden honey glows softly, sweet steam rising from it.
A pollen hall where giant bees dance in intricate patterns, communicating directions.
An amber tomb where dozens of creatures are sealed in the walls, including several adventurers with their gear.
A wax workshop where workers chew and shape fresh comb, the walls soft and warm.
A guard tunnel lined with soldier bees, their stingers longer than swords.
A garden chamber where flowers grow from honey-soaked soil, their blooms enormous and fragrant.
A royal jelly vault with cells of glowing white jelly, each one a treasure to any alchemist.
The heart, the queen's chamber, a vast cathedral of amber where the queen bee, larger than an elephant, rests on a throne of comb.
features: Royal jelly; a creature that eats a spoonful regains all hit points and is cured of poison, but the bees can smell it on the eater for a day.
The bees' dance; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Nature) check to read it reveals the fastest route to any chamber in the hive.
Amber-sealed adventurers; cutting one free with a DC {dc} Strength check takes 10 minutes and recovers their gear, and they may still be alive.
Smoke calms bees; burning green wood creates smoke that grants advantage on Stealth checks and makes bees passive for 10 minutes.
Honey as a trap; pouring honey on the floor creates a 10-foot area of difficult terrain where creatures must succeed on a DC {dc} Strength save each turn or be restrained.
hazards: A swarm of workers rises in alarm; each creature in a 20-foot cube makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} piercing damage from stings and is poisoned for 1 minute.
The sticky floor; a creature that moves more than half its speed in one turn makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or becomes stuck, restrained until it spends an action to pull free.
Amber sealing; a creature that falls into fresh honey makes a DC {dc} Strength save each round or is slowly sealed, becoming paralyzed after three failures.
Overheating; the hive's warmth makes heavy armour a burden, and a creature in heavy armour makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each hour or gains a level of exhaustion.

environments.name: Coral Reef in Air
environments.summary: A living reef hangs in open sky, its branches swaying in a tide no one can feel, while fish, rays and turtles swim through air as if it were warm lagoon water. The space was born from the last dream of a vast reef spirit that died when a Delta lagoon silted over, and it rebuilt its home in the only medium it had left. It wants to keep growing, and it feeds the visitors it catches to the coral so the reef can spread a little further into the sky.
readAloud: Colour floods your eyes before your feet find purchase. Branches of coral in salmon, violet and lemon rise around you, rocking slowly in a current you cannot feel, and a school of silver fish parts around your head like a curtain. Far below, the reef fades into a blue haze where long ripples of light crawl across nothing at all.

Your boots settle onto a dome of brain coral, spongy and warm as bread. Bubbles drift up from its grooves and pop with tiny glass chimes. A sea turtle the width of a cart glides past at eye level, regards you with one ancient eye, and banks away as something long and grey slides through the haze beneath it.

Salt prickles your tongue on the first breath, and the air feels heavy, almost liquid, pressing gently on your ears. A jellyfish drifts by, glowing the soft pink of a lantern behind paper, its tendrils trailing a hand's width above the coral. Somewhere below, a whale sings a single falling note that seems to come from the whole sky at once.
sights: Coral branches swaying in a current that leaves your hair untouched
A silver school of fish turning as one through open air
Rippling bands of light crawling across empty sky
Glowing jellyfish trailing tendrils just above the reef
A sailing ship wedged in staghorn coral, its sails bellied by no wind
Anemones opening like slow fists to taste the air
Pearl-white sand drifting upward in thin streams instead of falling
A grey fin cutting lazy circles through the blue haze below
sounds: Bubbles bursting with tiny glassy chimes
The soft swish of a ray's wings passing overhead
Snapping shrimp crackling inside the coral like frying fat
Whale song rolling through the sky from no direction
A muffled pressure in the ears, as if everything is underwater
The groan of old ship timbers flexing in the coral
smells: Sharp salt that dries the lips
Cloying sweetness from the anemone beds
Tar and wet canvas near the wreck
Sulfur from the black coral far below
rooms: A staghorn garden where schools of striped fish weave between the branches and scatter in a glittering burst whenever a sword is drawn.
An anemone meadow of waist-high tendrils that lean toward warmth; a thin path of bare coral winds through it, visible only from above.
A wrecked merchant ship caught in the coral, hanging bow-down with its sails puffed full, its hold still sealed and creaking.
A hollow coral grotto where an old octopus has heaped a hoard of lost rings, buttons, bottle glass and one spirit coin it refuses to part with.
A kelp spire growing straight up into the sky, its fronds thick as ship ropes and crowded with seahorses clinging by their tails.
A clam terrace where giant clams yawn open in slow rhythm, each one holding a pearl that glows faintly in time with its breathing.
A jellyfish bloom, a drifting cloud of glowing bells filling a gap in the reef, pulsing brighter whenever someone speaks aloud.
A shark run, a long open channel of empty blue between two reef walls, where grey shapes patrol just beyond torchlight.
A coral-crusted temple fragment on a ledge, three fallen columns and an altar holding a spiral conch the colour of dawn.
A cleaning station where small blue fish pick parasites from larger beasts, and even predators hold still and peaceful within its bounds.
A tide pool turned upside down, a bowl of real seawater floating in the air with a crab colony living on its underside.
The heart, the black reef at the bottom of the haze, where a pale many-armed horror coils through dead coral, its body flickering with stolen bioluminescence and its eyes set into the reef itself.
features: Sky-swimming; any creature can swim through the air at its swimming speed (or half its walking speed), but a creature that stops swimming sinks 30 feet per round toward the deep reef.
Giant clam pearls; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check pries a clam open for a pearl worth 2d6 spirit coins, but failing by 5 or more traps the arm and the creature is restrained until it escapes.
The dawn conch on the temple altar; blowing it summons a pod of friendly dolphins that carry up to six creatures anywhere in the reef within 1 round, usable once per day.

The octopus's hoard; offering it any shiny object earns directions to the heart that grant advantage on checks to navigate the deep reef, while stealing from it sets off an ink cloud that heavily obscures a 20-foot sphere.
Kelp climbing; a creature among the kelp fronds has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and predators in the shark run lose track of it.
The cleaning station truce; no beast will attack within it, and a creature that rests there for 10 minutes ends one poison effect on itself.
The wreck's sealed hold; forcing the hatch takes a DC {dc} Strength check and reveals waterlogged cargo with an awakening stone of Water inside a lead box, but the noise draws the nearest shark.
hazards: Anemone tendrils; a creature that touches them makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} poison damage and is paralyzed until the end of its next turn.

A shark strike from the blue; a creature crossing open channel must succeed on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check or be surprised by a hunting shark that deals {dmg} piercing damage on its first bite.
Jellyfish drift; a creature moving through the bloom makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} lightning damage from a dozen stings.
Fire coral; a creature brushing the bright orange branches makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} fire damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 minute.
The sinking pull; a creature knocked unconscious or restrained drifts 30 feet down each round, and a creature that reaches the black reef takes {half} necrotic damage at the start of each turn there.
Pressure gulf; descending more than 200 feet in a single minute requires a DC {dc} Constitution save or the creature takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is deafened for 1 hour.

environments.name: Brass Smithy-City
environments.summary: An entire city of brass, copper and soot sprawls under an orange furnace sky, peopled by constructs who hammer, haggle, gossip and vote as if they were citizens of Greenstone. A guild of artificers built it as a workshop that would never need sleeping hands, binding a great fire elemental beneath the streets to power every forge, and then they died and left the machines running. The city wants to keep working forever, and its council has decided that flesh visitors are either raw materials or competition.
readAloud: Brass rooftops gleam under a sky the colour of a forge mouth, and the streets ring with a hundred hammers striking a hundred anvils, never quite in time. Copper porters trundle past with baskets of bolts, iron watchmen march in squads of four, and a clockwork sparrow lands on your shoulder, ticks twice, and flies off to report. Nobody here has seen a face like yours in a very long time.

Steam blasts from a grate at your feet and fogs your vision in a hot, wet roar. When it clears, a market stretches ahead, its stalls heaped with gears, oil flasks, polished plates and spare hands. A brass merchant with lamp eyes leans across the counter and says, 'Soft one. Are you buying, or are you for sale?'

A clock tower looms above the city, its face showing not hours but a slowly turning knot of gears. A bell booms. Every construct in the street stops mid-stride, turns toward the tower and lowers its head for exactly three seconds, then resumes work as if nothing happened, except the watchmen, who keep staring at you.
sights: Brass rooftops gleaming under a furnace-orange sky
Copper porters carrying baskets of bolts on their heads
Steam blasting from street grates in white columns
A clock tower whose face is a knot of turning gears
Market stalls stacked with spare limbs sorted by size
Clockwork sparrows hopping along gutters and watching
Rivers of molten bronze flowing down open channels between streets
Faded portraits of human artificers hung in a shrine and polished daily
sounds: Hundreds of hammers ringing slightly out of rhythm
Steam shrieking from pressure valves
Metallic voices haggling over the price of a gear
The deep boom of the tower bell every hour
Ticking from inside every wall
A furious roar rising through the grates from far below
smells: Coal smoke that coats the back of the throat
Burning sulfur leaking up from the deep furnace
rooms: A gear market where constructs trade parts by weight on a great balance scale, and a vendor will swap secrets for a pound of iron.
A council chamber of copper benches where automatons debate in clicks and whistles, voting by raising one rusty hand.
A foundry floor where molten bronze pours from crucibles into molds shaped like constructs not yet born.
An assembly hall lined with half-built bodies on hooks, some of which twitch and turn their heads to follow movement.
A scrap yard heaped with broken constructs, where scavenger machines strip the dead for parts and fight over the good pieces.
A brass chapel where constructs kneel before portraits of their makers and pray in grinding voices for instructions that never come.
A gearworks beneath the clock tower, a vertical maze of turning cogs where one wrong step means being crushed.
A pressure station of valves, gauges and wheels that controls steam across the whole city.
The archive of plans, a vault of copper sheets etched with schematics for every construct ever built, guarded by a librarian with six arms.
A quench pool, a vast steaming tank where newly forged bodies are plunged, the water hissing and boiling at its edges.
The makers' house, a single cozy human dwelling with wooden furniture and a cold hearth, kept perfectly dusted by a grieving butler construct.
The heart, the great furnace beneath the city, where a fire elemental the size of a manor is bound by brass chains and runes, and its warden, a towering iron foreman, keeps it burning at any cost.
features: The balance scale market; any item placed on it is weighed in iron, and a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check sells loot for spirit coins or buys a single working construct part.
The pressure station valves; a DC {dc} Intelligence check can vent steam into a chosen district, heavily obscuring it for 1 minute or dealing {half} fire damage to everything in one street.
The council vote; a party that addresses the council and succeeds on a DC {dc} Charisma check earns a citizen token, and watchmen will not attack anyone carrying one.
The archive of plans; studying a construct's schematic for 10 minutes grants advantage on attacks against that kind of construct, as the reader knows where its seams are.
The makers' house; returning the butler's lost master key, found in the scrap yard, earns its loyalty and a map of every secret passage in the city.
Spare bodies in the assembly hall; a creature with tinker's tools can activate one with a DC {dc} Intelligence check to serve as an ally for 1 hour, though a failure makes it hostile.
The furnace runes; each rune broken weakens the chains, giving the elemental advantage but stripping the foreman of 20 temporary hit points.
hazards: Steam vents; a creature crossing a grate when it blasts makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} fire damage.
Molten spill; a crucible tips when struck or jostled, and each creature in a 15-foot line makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Grinding gears; a creature falling or shoved into the gearworks makes a DC {dc} Strength save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is restrained between the teeth.
Watchman alarm; any violence in the streets brings a squad of iron watchmen in 1d4 rounds, and a creature caught alone must make a DC {dc} Strength save or be grappled and dragged toward the furnace.
Soot-choked alleys; a creature that spends more than 10 minutes in the lower districts makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
The bell's command; when the tower bell tolls during combat, each creature with metal armour makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is stunned until the end of its next turn as the armour locks rigid.

environments.name: Moonlit Orchard
environments.summary: Rows of silver-barked trees stretch beneath a moon hung so close you can see shadow in its craters, their pale fruit glowing like lanterns and their grass beaded with luminous dew. A fey sovereign planted the orchard in exile, after losing a court of her own, and she rules it with impeccable manners and a bookkeeper's memory for debts. The orchard wants guests, gifts and obligations, and anyone who takes without asking becomes part of its harvest.
readAloud: A full moon hangs so low and enormous that you could count the shadows in its craters. Beneath it, slender silver trees march away in perfect rows, their branches bowed with fruit that glows like paper lanterns. Every blade of grass holds a bead of dew lit from within, so the ground itself seems to shine.

A flute plays somewhere between the trees, soft and wandering, never quite repeating its tune. The air is cool and heavy with blossom. A white stag with silver-tipped antlers lifts its head from the grass to study you, then walks unhurried into the shadows, leaving hoofprints that glow for a breath and fade.

Moths with wings as broad as your palm drift between the branches, shedding silver dust that sparkles as it falls. Petals spiral down like slow snow. A small figure with skin the green of new leaves sits swinging its feet on a low bough and calls, 'Look all you like, darlings. Picking is a different matter.'
sights: A moon so close that its craters cast visible shadows
Silver-barked trees standing in perfectly measured rows
Fruit glowing like paper lanterns among the leaves
Dewdrops lit from within across every blade of grass
Broad silver moths shedding sparkling dust
Petals spiraling down like slow snow
A white stag leaving footprints of light
Tiny ledgers of bark nailed to tree trunks, each listing a debt
sounds: A wandering flute tune that never repeats
Polite laughter drifting from a revel just out of sight
The papery rustle of moth wings
Leaves chiming like tiny bells in a breeze
A nightingale singing a song that answers your words
The soft creak of a branch bending toward you
smells: Sweet blossom thick enough to taste
Cool night air with a hint of frost
Ripe pears split open on the grass
Fermenting fruit and something like candied rot near the roots
rooms: A long avenue of silver trees whose fruit lights the way like streetlamps, each lamp dimming as you pass and brightening behind you.
A moon pool, a perfectly round pond reflecting the huge moon, where the reflection shows the orchard as it looked a hundred years ago.
A revel glade where fey courtiers dance in a ring of pale mushrooms and invite anyone watching to join the next song.
A moth roost in a hollow giant tree, its inner walls carpeted with sleeping moths that wake in a blinding silver cloud if disturbed.
A harvest shed where fey gardeners sort glowing fruit into baskets labeled with the names of mortals who owe them something.
A tangle of briars at the orchard's edge, where the trees grow twisted and black and the fruit is bruised purple.
A sundial garden where the shadow of the moon moves backward, and a sign reads that hours spent here are paid back later.
A white stag's clearing, a ring of soft moss where the stag lies resting, ringed by fallen antler tines that glow faintly.
The debtors' row, a line of trees with human features grown into their bark, each one murmuring the thing it took.
A honeysuckle bower where a lute lies on a cushion and a table is set for two with untouched wine.
A beehive tower, a pillar of pale wax humming with moon-bees whose honey shines like liquid light.

The heart, the moon tree, a vast silver giant whose roots drink directly from the moonlight, where the orchard's sovereign sits on a throne of living bark beside the single golden fruit she will never let anyone pick.
features: Glowing fruit; eating one with permission restores 2d8 hit points and grants darkvision for 1 hour, while eating one without permission marks the eater, and every fey in the orchard knows it.
The moon pool; gazing into it for 1 minute and succeeding on a DC {dc} Wisdom check reveals one secret about the sovereign's past, including the name of the court she lost.

The revel ring; joining the dance and succeeding on a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check earns a fey favour that can be spent to end one charm or curse, but failure means dancing until dawn unless an ally drags you out.
The sundial garden; time spent there passes at half speed, so a short rest takes 30 minutes, but the lost time is collected as one level of exhaustion when the creature leaves the orchard.
Moon-bee honey; a creature who calms the hive with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check collects a jar that heals {dmg} hit points when eaten, once.
The debtors' row; settling a tree's debt with a gift worth at least 10 spirit coins frees the trapped mortal, who knows a safe path through the briars.
The set table in the bower; sitting and drinking the wine summons a fey courtier who will answer three questions truthfully but expects a story in return.
hazards: The gardener's debt; a creature who picks fruit without permission makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed by the nearest fey and compelled to work the harvest for 1 hour.
Moth swarm; waking the roost releases a silver cloud, and each creature within 30 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded for 1 minute.

Briar tangle; moving through the black briars costs 4 feet per foot, and a creature that ends its turn there takes {half} piercing damage and makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour.
Dreaming dew; a creature that sleeps or rests on the glowing grass makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or falls into a fey sleep that only a kiss, a slap or a remove curse ends.
The bark grip; a creature that breaks a promise within the orchard makes a DC {dc} Strength save or begins to turn to wood, restrained, and petrified into a tree after three failed saves.
Moonlight lance; when the sovereign is angered, the moon flares and each creature in open ground makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Sand-Buried Temple
environments.summary: A colossal temple to a sun deity lies swallowed by desert drifts, its pillared halls knee-deep in sand and its priests still standing at their posts as dry, wrapped guardians. A king who feared death ordered the priesthood to bind his soul to the sun's fire, and the ritual worked too well, folding his tomb into an astral space that burns and never cools. The temple wants to keep its king alive and its gold untouched, and every trap in it still clicks in the dark.
readAloud: A thin golden stream of sand pours from a crack high above, caught in a single blade of daylight. The hall it falls into is enormous, its columns carved with sun disks and hawk-headed figures, its floor buried knee-deep in drifts that whisper as they shift. Heat beats off the walls like an open oven.

Painted figures in faded gold and blue cover every surface, telling the story of a king who refused to die and the priests who granted his wish. Your torchlight trembles. Somewhere ahead, stone grinds against stone, and a dry voice begins to recite something in a rhythm like a heartbeat.

Your light falls on a corridor lined with sandstone guardians, each holding a spear across its chest, sand piled around their feet like snow against a fence. As you pass the third statue, something cracks, and a trickle of dust spills from its stone eyes like tears. The spear in its hands begins, very slowly, to lower.
sights: Sand streaming in golden threads from cracks in the ceiling
Columns carved with sun disks and hawk-headed figures
Faded gold and blue murals of a king refusing death
Sandstone guardians with spears held across their chests
Wrapped priests still standing at their posts
Gold coins glinting half-buried in the drifts
Scorpions the size of dogs basking on sun-warmed stone
A shaft of daylight crawling across the floor like a living thing
sounds: Sand hissing as it pours from above
Stone grinding on stone somewhere behind the walls
A dry voice reciting prayers in a heartbeat rhythm
The soft click of a pressure plate settling
Wind moaning through ventilation shafts
The rattle of a scorpion tail against stone
smells: Hot dust that dries the nostrils
Stale, sealed air that tastes of tin
Scorched stone near the sun shafts
rooms: A hypostyle hall of towering columns half buried in sand, where shafts of sunlight fall through cracks and move faster than the true sun should.
A guardian corridor lined with sandstone statues, three of which are not statues at all.
An embalming chamber with stone slabs, jars of preserved organs and a priest still at work on a body that is not finished.
A treasury buried under a dune of coins, where the sand is mixed with gold and every step sinks deeper.
A chamber of offerings, its walls lined with shelves of clay jars, dried bread and wine gone to vinegar centuries ago.
A scorpion nest in a collapsed side chapel, where giant scorpions bask beneath a sun shaft on the warm stone.
A hall of the sun barque, a ceremonial golden boat on a track that once carried the king's body through the temple.
A sand-filled shaft, a vertical well where the floor has given way, sand falling into a hollow far below.
A hall of judgment with a great balance scale, one pan holding a feather and the other waiting for something.
A priests' dormitory of stone bunks, each with a sleeping wrapped figure that sits up when a name is spoken.
A mural gallery where the paintings show the temple's construction, including the location of every trap.
The heart, the king's burial chamber, a sun-blazing vault where the undying king rises from a golden sarcophagus wreathed in solar fire, flanked by his two sandstone hounds.
features: The mural gallery; a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check deciphers the paintings and reveals the location of every trap in one wing, granting advantage on checks to avoid them.

The hall of judgment scale; a creature who places its heart-hand on the empty pan makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, and success grants resistance to necrotic damage for 1 hour while failure deals {half} psychic damage.
The sun barque; pushing the golden boat along its track with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check carries the party straight to the antechamber of the heart, bypassing three rooms.
Canopic jars in the embalming chamber; breaking the king's jars before the final fight reduces his maximum hit points by 10 each, and there are four.
The treasury dune; a creature who spends 10 minutes digging collects 4d10 spirit coins and an awakening stone of Fire, but every 10 minutes also triggers a roll on the hazard table.
Sleeping priests; speaking a priest's name aloud from the dormitory murals causes that priest to obey one simple command before crumbling to dust.
Sun shafts; a creature who angles a polished shield or mirror into a sun shaft can blast a 30-foot line with daylight, dealing {half} radiant damage to undead in it.
hazards: Pressure plates; a creature who steps on one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save as blades swing from the walls, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Sinking sand; a creature in the treasury or sand shaft makes a DC {dc} Strength save each round or sinks 1 foot, becoming restrained at 3 feet and beginning to suffocate at 5 feet.
Collapsing ceiling; loud noise or explosions bring down a section of roof, and each creature in a 20-foot square makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is buried.
Mummy rot; a creature struck by a wrapped priest makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is cursed and cannot regain hit points until the curse is removed.
Furnace heat; a creature in heavy armour in the deep halls makes a DC {dc} Constitution save every hour or gains a level of exhaustion.
Scorpion venom; a creature stung by a giant scorpion makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Crystal Geode Caverns
environments.summary: A web of caverns runs through the inside of one impossibly large geode, every wall bristling with amethyst, blue quartz and clear crystal that hums with stored mana. The space formed where a mana vein under the Old City pooled for a thousand years and slowly crystallized, and it has since grown a mind as slow and patient as the stone itself. Its one desire is to climb toward the light it cannot reach, and it absorbs living mana from visitors to fuel each new spire.
readAloud: Violet light washes over you as you step through. Crystals as tall as old oaks jut from floor, wall and ceiling, amethyst and smoky quartz and a deep blue stone that glows from within. They hum together on one low note that you feel more in your back teeth than your ears.

Your reflection splinters into a hundred faces across the crystal facets as you walk, each one a heartbeat late. Rainbows slide across the walls. A lizard made of clear glass scurries along the ceiling, its insides glittering, and slips into a crack so narrow you would swear it folded itself.

The tunnel opens onto a hollow vast enough to hold a town, its walls studded with crystals that all point inward toward a glowing core far below. The hum swells here into something like a chord. Your skin prickles with mana, and every breath tastes of copper and lightning.
sights: Amethyst spires as tall as old oaks
Rainbows sliding across faceted walls
Glass lizards scurrying along the ceiling
A distant glowing core at the bottom of the hollow
Reflections that move a heartbeat after you do
Mana veins pulsing blue through the bedrock
Crystal flowers blooming from cracks in real time
A clear ooze sliding over the walls, crystals forming in its wake
sounds: A low hum felt in the teeth
Bright chimes when a crystal is brushed
Sharp cracking as new crystals push out of the stone
Echoes that ring on long after the sound ends
A high, clean note rising from the core
The tinkle of glass feet skittering overhead
smells: Air so dry it hurts the nose
A faint honeyed sweetness of raw mana
rooms: An amethyst nave where violet crystals arch overhead like ribs, and a whisper at one end is heard clearly at the other.
A mirror gallery of polished clear quartz where the party sees countless reflections, and one of them does not copy their movements.
A singing grotto of thin crystal pipes that play notes when air moves through them, forming a melody that changes with each footstep.
A mana spring where liquid light seeps from the rock and pools in a basin, glowing too bright to look at directly.
A shattered hall, its crystals broken into razor shards by some long-ago battle, the floor glittering like a field of knives.
A crystal nursery where tiny elementals grow inside geodes and crack free, blinking and confused.
A collapsed miners' camp with rusted picks, bedrolls and a journal, where a team from the Adventure Society tried to harvest the walls.
A prism bridge spanning a chasm, made of a single beam of solid light that holds only while the crystals at each end stay lit.
A gravity well where crystal growth has bent space, letting creatures walk on walls and ceiling.
An echo vault where every sound repeats three times, the third echo always slightly wrong.
A frozen sea of quartz, a lake that crystallized mid-wave, its surface a field of glassy crests.
The heart, the geode core, a perfect sphere of light where a crystal golem stands with its arms grown into the floor, guarding a mana stone the size of a wagon that beats like a heart.
features: Harvestable crystal; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) or tool check breaks off a mana crystal worth 2d6 spirit coins, but the noise rings through the caverns and draws the nearest elemental.
The singing grotto; playing its pipes in the correct order, found with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check, opens a hidden passage to the core.

The mana spring; a spellcaster who drinks from it regains one expended spell slot of 3rd level or lower once per day, but must make a DC {dc} Constitution save or be poisoned by the glut of mana for 1 hour.
The prism bridge; keeping both end crystals lit by light or magic lets the party cross, and dousing one drops anything on the bridge into the chasm.
The miners' journal; reading it reveals which crystals are hollow and which are guardians in disguise, granting advantage on initiative in the shattered hall.
Crystal nursery hatchlings; a creature who speaks gently to a newborn elemental and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom check gains a tiny companion that sheds bright light and warns of danger for one day.
Golem roots; shattering the four crystals that bind the golem's arms to the floor frees it from the core, ending its regeneration but letting it pursue the party.
hazards: Razor shards; moving through the shattered hall at more than half speed requires a DC {dc} Dexterity save or the creature takes {dmg} slashing damage.

Resonance shatter; a loud noise in the singing grotto sets off a shockwave, and each creature within 20 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Mana overload; a creature that touches the glowing core makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} force damage as excess magic floods through it.
Blinding refraction; light cast in the mirror gallery bounces wildly, and each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded until the end of its next turn.
Creeping crystal; a creature that stays still for 10 minutes makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or its feet are crystallized to the floor, restraining it until freed.
Gravity snap; when a creature in the gravity well takes damage, it makes a DC {dc} Strength save or falls toward the nearest wall and takes {half} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Ruined Observatory
environments.summary: An astronomer's tower drifts among unfamiliar stars, its great dome split open to the void and its telescopes still trained on a constellation that one night looked back. A scholar of the Magic Society built it to chart the heavens, and when she opened the great lens too wide, something from between the stars noticed her and pulled the tower loose from the world. The thing that came through wants a body made of starlight and a door home, while the brass servants she left behind only want to finish her final chart.
readAloud: Stars blaze on every side, nearer and fiercer than any you have known. You stand on cracked white marble inside a dome split wide open, and beyond its broken edge there is no ground at all, only a field of cold light falling away forever. Your breath steams, though there is no wind.

Brass telescopes as long as war galleys aim upward through the shattered dome, their lenses fractured into spiderwebs and their gears rusted green. Star charts drift through the air like slow autumn leaves, circling. The quiet here is so complete that you hear your own heart and the faint tick of someone else's.

Directly overhead, one constellation burns brighter than the rest. As you watch, its stars slide into a new arrangement, the shape of an eye. Out in the dark beyond it, something vast shifts, and every telescope in the room turns on its mount with a grinding shriek to follow.
sights: Stars burning cold and close on every side
A marble dome split open to the void
Brass telescopes as long as war galleys
Star charts circling slowly through the air
A constellation rearranging itself into an eye
An orrery of floating planets turning on invisible threads
Chalk equations scrawled across the walls in a frantic hand
Shadows that fall toward the light instead of away
sounds: A silence deep enough to hear blood moving
Gears creaking as telescopes adjust themselves
The papery rustle of drifting charts
A thin ringing like starlight given a voice
Whispers from the dark that use your name
The steady tick of a brass servant counting stars
smells: Cold metal that frosts the nose
Nothing at all in the void-facing rooms
Burnt lamp oil from the scholar's study
A sweet, rotten tang like spoiled plums near the great lens
rooms: The main dome, open to the stars, where the great telescope points at the watching constellation and refuses to be turned away.
The astronomer's study, papers everywhere, with a final journal entry left mid-sentence and the ink still wet.
An orrery chamber where a great model of the heavens turns, its brass planets heavy enough to crush anyone in their path.
A lens workshop full of ground glass, half-finished lenses and a polishing wheel that still spins.
A star-chart library where maps of the sky cover every wall, and some of them show stars that have not yet been born.
A broken stair that spirals around the tower's outside, open to the void, missing every third step.
The scholar's bedchamber, neat and cold, with a portrait of her family facing the wall.
A celestial chapel where a radiant figure kneels in chains of light, pleading in a tongue that sounds like bells.
A void balcony jutting into nothing, where the stars below are as bright as the stars above.
A servants' alcove where brass assistants stand idle, waiting for orders that never come.
A collapsed lower floor drifting free of the tower, connected only by a chain of floating rubble.
The heart, the great lens chamber at the top of the tower, where the thing from between the stars pours through the cracked lens and knits itself a body of light, eyes and cold geometry.
features: The great telescope; peering through it with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check reveals the entity's weakness, granting advantage on the first attack against it, but failure deals {half} psychic damage.
The orrery; aligning its brass planets correctly with a DC {dc} Intelligence check unlocks a hidden vault holding an awakening stone of Magic and a starmetal astrolabe.
The chained celestial; freeing it requires breaking three chains of light (AC 15, 20 hit points each), and once free it heals the party fully and fights at their side in the heart for 3 rounds.
The scholar's journal; reading it reveals the ritual phrase that closes the great lens, which can banish the entity if spoken while it is below half its hit points.
Brass servants; a creature who finds the scholar's command rod in her bedchamber can direct the servants to fight, carry or open sealed doors.
The lens workshop; a creature with tools can polish a fragment into a viewing lens that shows invisible creatures and hidden doors within 30 feet for 1 hour.
The void balcony; a creature who steps off it in faith and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom save drifts gently down to the floating lower floor instead of falling forever.
hazards: The void edge; a creature knocked off the tower makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save to catch the ledge, or drifts out into the stars and must be pulled back with a rope or magic within 3 rounds or is lost.
Starfall; meteors of cold light rain through the open dome, and each creature in the open makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The watching constellation; a creature who meets the eye's gaze makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is frightened for 1 minute and hears whispers that grant disadvantage on concentration saves.
Crushing orrery; a creature in the path of a moving planet makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone.
Thinning air; the void-facing rooms have little breath in them, and a creature that stays more than 10 minutes makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
Mind-geometry; a creature who studies the entity's body makes a DC {dc} Intelligence save or takes {half} psychic damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn.

environments.name: Lightning-Struck Tower
environments.summary: A wizard's tower of black stone was hit by a bolt of wild lightning and never stopped being struck, so that electricity crawls up its walls like ivy and arcs between its floors to power the strange machines its master left running. The wizard was trying to capture a living storm as a source of endless power, and in the instant he succeeded, the storm captured him, and his tower became its body. The storm wants to keep growing louder and brighter, and it feeds on every spark of mana that climbs its stairs.
readAloud: Thunder cracks so close that you feel it in your teeth and the soles of your feet. You stand at the base of a tower of black stone scarred white by a thousand strikes, and lightning crawls up its walls in branching vines of light. Rain lashes sideways, steaming where it lands on the charged stone.

Inside, the air crackles with static, and every hair on your arms lifts. Copper coils run up the walls, spitting sparks every few seconds, and the smell of burnt air coats your tongue. A staircase spirals upward into stuttering blue light, and somewhere above, a machine is laughing.

Each flash lights the room bright as noon, then drops it into black. In each flash you see a different scene: a bookshelf, a cage of glowing glass, a figure in robes standing perfectly still at the top of the stair. In the last flash, the figure has moved one step closer.
sights: Lightning crawling up the walls in branching vines
Copper coils spitting sparks every few seconds
Flashes that freeze the room in stark white
Black stone scarred white by countless strikes
Glass orbs swirling with trapped lightning
Spark-sprites racing along iron rails
Scorch marks shaped like the wizard's silhouette on every floor
Rain falling upward through an open stairwell
sounds: Thunder that rattles loose stones from the walls
Crackling static like frying fat
The steady hum of charged machinery
Rain hissing on hot stone
A shriek of power surging through copper
A mechanical laugh echoing down the stairwell
smells: Ozone thick enough to sting the eyes
rooms: The entry hall, scorched black, where a great copper coil spirals up the central column and hums louder whenever someone carries metal near it.
A library of charred books, pages fused together, with a few still readable if the sparks are kept off them.
A laboratory of humming machines, glass orbs full of trapped lightning and a workbench where something is still being built by itself.
A conduit shaft, a hollow column where lightning surges upward in great pulses, climbable only between strikes.
A storm cage, a chamber of iron bars where a captured air elemental hurls itself against its prison.
A capacitor vault lined with brass jars charged to bursting, each one labeled in the wizard's hand.
The wizard's quarters, a ruined bed and a mirror that shows the room as it was before the lightning came.
A broken bridge between the tower and a crumbling outer turret, slick with rain and lashed by wind.
A spark foundry where constructs of copper and glass are assembled and jolted to life with lightning.
A weather chamber with a domed ceiling painted as a sky, where small clouds form and drift over the floor.
A grounding pit at the tower's base, a pool of black water where lightning drains away and the water is warm.
The heart, the tower crown, open to the sky, where the living storm takes the shape of a giant made of lightning and wind, the wizard's frozen body hanging in its chest like a heart.
features: Lightning orbs; a creature can pry one loose with a DC {dc} Dexterity check and throw it as an action, dealing {dmg} lightning damage in a 10-foot radius, but a failed check shocks the holder for {half}.
The storm cage; freeing the air elemental with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check on the lock earns an ally that grants the party resistance to lightning damage for the fight in the heart.

The capacitor vault; each jar can be drained into a spellcaster to restore one 1st-level spell slot, but each draining requires a DC {dc} Constitution save or the creature is stunned until the end of its next turn.
The wizard's mirror; studying it reveals where his storm-binding rod was hidden, and wielding the rod in the heart gives the storm disadvantage on saving throws.
Grounding rods; a creature who drives a rod from the laboratory into the floor creates a 10-foot zone where lightning damage is halved.
The weather chamber; a creature who succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check can steer its clouds to rain on the heart, dampening the storm's next lightning attack.
Spark foundry constructs; activating one with a DC {dc} Intelligence check creates a copper servant that obeys for 1 hour and can carry a lightning orb safely.
hazards: Arcing walls; a creature that touches the walls makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} lightning damage.
Surging conduit; a creature in the conduit shaft when lightning pulses makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Metal attraction; a creature wearing metal armour makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save at the start of each turn in the coil hall or is struck for {half} lightning damage.
Bridge winds; a creature crossing the broken bridge makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is blown off and falls 1d4 floors.
Bursting capacitors; any lightning damage in the vault makes the jars explode, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} lightning damage and is deafened.
Static lock; a creature hit by lightning twice in one round makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is paralyzed until the end of its next turn.

environments.name: Overgrown Greenhouse
environments.summary: Under a ribbed glass roof the size of a cathedral, a botanist's collection has run riot, rare specimens from every coast and jungle cross-breeding into strains with teeth, appetites and opinions. She was a Life-affinity healer from Greenstone who built the conservatory to save plants dying out in the wild, and when the beds began to wither she fed them her own blood until she put down roots herself. The greenhouse wants to keep its collection alive at any cost, and it sees warm-blooded visitors as the richest mulch it has ever been offered.
readAloud: The air closes over you like a wet towel, heavy with steam and perfume. Fronds wider than tabletops sag from rusted iron ribs overhead, beading every glass pane with condensation that runs down in slow crooked streams. Something in the green clicks its tongue twice, then goes still.

A cracked tile path leads away between raised beds that have burst their brick edges, roots bulging out like knuckles. Every few paces a brass plaque names a plant in neat engraved letters, and every plant beside its plaque is wrong: too large, too many leaves, a flower where a mouth should not be. A watering can lies tipped on the path, and a pale tendril curls out of its spout and turns to face your warmth.

Gold light slants through a smashed pane far above, thick with drifting spores that turn in it like dust in a barn. Insects drone in a wall of sound. Nailed to a post at a fork in the path is a painted board, its letters flaking: Feed Before Sunset. Do Not Feed After. Below it, the soil is freshly turned.
sights: Iron roof ribs furred orange with rust and hung with dripping moss
Brass name plaques beside plants that no longer match them
Pitcher plants the height of a door, lids lifting slowly as you pass
A tree trunk that has grown around a wrought-iron bench and swallowed half of it
Spores turning lazily in shafts of hazy gold light
A gardener's apron hanging on a hook, stiff with old blood
A translucent green ooze in a planter, a sparrow skeleton visible inside it
Petals that slowly close like eyelids when torchlight touches them
sounds: Condensation pattering onto leaves like light rain
A drone of insects that never rises or falls
The squeal of glass panes flexing in their iron frames
Roots creaking as they push through brick
A wet, contented gulp from a pitcher plant lid snapping shut
A woman's humming rising faintly out of the soil
smells: Warm black loam and leaf mold
Lily perfume so dense it makes the head swim
Crushed sap, sharp and green, on boots and hands
Carrion sweetness rising from the carnivorous beds
Iron and rust where blood once soaked the potting tables
rooms: A rotunda under a cracked glass dome where a single banyan has grown up through the roof, its hanging roots forming curtains that hide a spiral stair to the catwalks.
A carnivorous wing lined with pitcher plants and flytraps big enough to swallow a dog, their lids pulsing open in rhythm with any heartbeat that comes near.
A potting house of clay pots stacked to the ceiling, where seedlings sprout in seconds when touched by a drop of blood.
A lily house built around a steaming pool, its giant round pads strong enough to stand on and its water hiding a snapping turtle older than the building.
A puffball cellar under the floor, low and warm, where fungus heads as big as pumpkins burst into golden clouds at the faintest footstep.
A cold seed vault behind a steel door, walls of labeled glass jars, the only room where no plant grows and the air smells clean.
An orchid gallery whose blooms swivel to track motion and mimic voices they have heard, repeating the last words of past visitors.
A cactus dome kept dry and hot under clear glass, its tall twisted cacti studded with the bleached bones of beasts that tried to drink from them.
A butterfly house sealed by hanging curtains, its warm air full of drifting wings patterned with eyes that blink in unison.
A compost yard where a great green ooze has bloated among the mulch heaps, sorting scraps with lazy pseudopods.
The botanist's study, its desk furred with moss and its papers swollen with damp, her last notebook open to a page that reads I am the cure and the mistake.

The heart, the walled garden at the centre, where the botanist has become a towering flowering tree, her face set in the bark, her blossoms singing in her voice as her vine arms reach for anything with blood in it.
features: Brass name plaques; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature) check comparing a plaque to its plant reveals what the plant was before it changed, granting advantage on saves against that plant's attacks.
The seed vault; each labeled jar holds 1d4 rare seeds worth 3 spirit coins apiece to the Magic Society, and one jar labeled Climber grows into a 60-foot vine ladder within 1 round of planting.

The banyan stair; climbing the root curtain with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check reaches the roof catwalks, letting the party cross the greenhouse above the beds and enter the heart from overhead.

Blood seedlings in the potting house; a creature who feeds a seedling a drop of blood (1 hit point) grows a loyal sprout that can be thrown as an action to entangle one creature, which makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained for 1 minute.
The botanist's notebook; reading it reveals an antidote brewed from the cactus dome's sap, which, poured on the heart tree's roots, stuns it until the end of its next turn.
The clean cistern; water drawn from it and poured over a hostile plant makes that plant indifferent for 1 minute, and a full bucket calms the ooze long enough to search the compost yard.
Healing moss; a creature who finds the pale blue moss with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check can chew it to regain {half} hit points, once per day.
hazards: Pitcher swallow; a creature that brushes a pitcher plant makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is pulled inside, restrained and taking {dmg} acid damage at the start of each of its turns until cut free (AC 12, 30 hit points).

Puffball cloud; a creature in the cellar that moves more than 5 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned and racked by coughing, unable to speak or cast spells with verbal components for 1 minute.
Strangler vines; a creature pushing through dense growth makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is grappled and hoisted 15 feet into the canopy, taking {half} bludgeoning damage each round it stays caught.
Hothouse steam; a creature in medium or heavy armour makes a DC {dc} Constitution save every 10 minutes or gains a level of exhaustion.
Ooze slick; a creature that steps into a mulch heap makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or its feet are engulfed, restraining it and dealing {half} acid damage each round.
Cactus spines; a creature shoved into the cactus dome's plants takes {dmg} piercing damage and makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour.

environments.name: Prison of Chains
environments.summary: Iron chains thick as ship's hawsers hang in every direction through a lightless void, and from them dangle cages, cells and walkways where prisoners mutter, plead and claw at their bars. A church raised the first cells as a place to hold demons and the worst of the wicked, and centuries of guilt rusted into the iron until the prison tore itself loose from the world and began collecting inmates without any help. It wants every soul it catches to confess and serve a sentence, and its warden has never once judged a visitor innocent.
readAloud: You arrive on a swaying cage roof, and the first thing you hear is iron, everywhere, links grinding against links in a slow ceaseless clatter like hail on a tin roof. Chains rise into black and drop into black. Hundreds of cages hang between them, each one lit by a single candle stub, and in each one a face turns toward you.

A grated walkway runs off into the dark, its iron mesh flexing under your weight above a drop that swallows your torchlight whole. Far below, someone is screaming the same word over and over. A hooded jailer strolls past with a ring of keys as large as a cartwheel, pauses, sniffs, and writes something in a small black book.

A wet hand shoots through the bars of the nearest cage and grips your sleeve. 'Your crime,' a voice rasps, 'what is your crime? Tell them first, before they decide for you.' Behind the speaker, in the same cell, a horned shape chuckles, and the candle between them gutters green.
sights: Chains as thick as a hawser vanishing into black above and below
Hundreds of hanging cages, each lit by a single candle stub
Grated walkways flexing over a drop with no visible floor
Jailers in hoods writing in small black books
Crimes etched into cell bars in shaky, scratched letters
A cartwheel-sized key ring swinging from a jailer's belt
Green candle flames that flicker when a lie is told nearby
A demon's red eyes in a cell of black iron sealed with silver rivets
sounds: Link grinding on link like endless hail on tin
A distant prisoner screaming one word over and over
The jangle of an enormous key ring
Whispered bargains from every cage you pass
A cell door slamming with a boom that sets the chains swinging
The tap of a forge hammer riveting new links somewhere above
smells: Rust that leaves a taste like a bitten tongue
Cold tallow smoke from a thousand candle stubs
Damp mildew in the cage floors
Lamp oil and old ink near the jailers' posts
rooms: A hanging cell block, a forest of cages joined by tilting walkways, where the prisoners rock their cages deliberately to knock intruders off.
A jailers' guardroom on a broad iron platform, with a dice table, a weapon rack and a sentencing ledger open to a fresh page with blank spaces for the party's names.
A penance chamber of rusted wheels and racks, still in use, where a prisoner strapped down begs to be told what he did.
A demon vault, a sphere of silver-riveted black iron where bound fiends hang in runed chains, the wards flickering weaker each hour.
A chain forge where sweating jailers hammer fresh links from the iron of collapsed cells, sparks tumbling endlessly into the void.
An oubliette, a narrow iron tube with a grate on top and an old prisoner at the bottom who has forgotten her name but remembers every guard's.
A visiting hall with one long iron table, where the dead come to speak to the living through a grille and lie about their wills.
A confession booth suspended alone on a single chain, its priestly jailer waiting behind the screen with a sentencing hammer.
A mess deck where shackled inmates eat grey gruel under crossbows, passing spoons sharpened into knives beneath the benches.
The key loft, a cage-shaped vault where every key in the prison hangs on its own hook, chiming softly when its matching cell is opened.
A burst cell, its bars bent outward and its chain snapped, claw marks leading off into the dark where an escaped thing now hunts.
The heart, the warden's seat, a throne woven from a thousand chains where the warden sits, its body made of links and padlocks, every chain in the prison answering its voice.
features: The sentencing ledger; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals which prisoners were wrongly jailed and which fiends will bargain, and writing a false crime beside a jailer's name makes the other jailers arrest him.
Opening cells; a key or a DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools) check frees a prisoner as an ally, but roll a d4: on a 1, the prisoner is a disguised fiend that turns on the party at the worst moment.
The key loft; taking the master ring lets the party open any cell or cage, but the keys' chime warns the warden, who sends two jailers at once.
The confession booth; a creature that confesses a true wrong and succeeds on a DC {dc} Charisma save receives a brand of penance, and jailers ignore it for 1 hour.
Fiend bargains; a bound demon grants advantage on attack rolls for 1 minute in exchange for loosening one chain, and after three chains are loosened it breaks free.
The mess deck riot; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion or Intimidation) check sparks an uprising that pulls every jailer in the block away for 10 minutes.
Green candles; a creature carrying one sees its flame flicker whenever a creature within 10 feet tells a lie.
hazards: Rocking cages; a creature on a walkway when prisoners swing their cages into it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is knocked off and must catch a chain.
Living chains; when the warden is angered, chains whip out of the dark, and each creature in range makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is restrained.
The weight of guilt; a creature that has done a cruel deed makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save on entering or has its speed halved for 1 hour as phantom shackles drag at its ankles.
Brimstone seep; a creature in the demon vault makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each minute or takes {half} fire damage and is poisoned.
The long drop; a falling creature makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save to snatch a chain, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage as it catches, or landing on the cage block below for the same damage.
Shackle grates; a hidden grate snaps manacles shut on a creature that steps on it, which makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is restrained until it succeeds on a DC {dc} Strength check.

environments.name: Cult Slaughterhouse
environments.summary: A sprawling abattoir of red brick and black timber stretches through endless killing halls, where aproned cultists butcher monsters, and sometimes marsh villagers, to feed a god-thing that lives in the cellars. A congregation of exiles from Greenstone founded it in a flooded tannery in the Delta, and the blood they poured into the drains for a generation pooled into an astral space where the knives never rest. Their god wants to be fed until it grows large enough to fill the portal and crawl out into the marshes, and the cult is delighted to have fresh offerings walk in on their own.
readAloud: The smell reaches you before your eyes adjust: copper, bowel and old smoke, so thick you feel it coat your teeth. Carcasses sway from iron hooks in long rows, owlbears, giant boars and things with too many legs, all slit and emptied. Stone gutters run red toward a central drain, and the drain is gurgling like a contented baby.

A handbell clangs three times, and somewhere ahead a choir begins to sing in time with the falling of a cleaver. Robed figures in leather aprons cross a gallery overhead, buckets sloshing in both hands. One of them stops at the rail, looks down at you with mild interest, and smiles to show teeth filed into neat points.

Every wall is painted with the same circular sigil, layered in brown and red so many times that the brick has disappeared beneath a crust as thick as a thumb. Flies rise in fat droning clouds as you pass. At the end of the hall stands a door of black oak carved with one word in an old marsh tongue, and the word is wet.
sights: Monster carcasses swaying on hooks in rows that run out of sight
Gutters cut in the floor, all running toward one gurgling drain
Leather aprons worn over hooded robes, stiff with old stains
A circular sigil painted over itself until it stands out from the wall
Flies rising in clouds dense enough to dim a lantern
Cleavers hung on pegboards with votive candles beneath each one
Iron cages of caught beasts, each tagged with a feeding date
A huge iron trapdoor set in the floor, warm to the touch and breathing
sounds: A cleaver falling on the beat of a hymn
A choir singing hymns about appetite
Gurgling and slurping from every drain
Hook trolleys squealing along overhead rails
Slow, enormous breaths rising through the floor
Caged beasts howling and battering their bars
smells: Raw copper blood and opened bowel
Rendering tallow bubbling in iron vats
Sweet, clinging rot in the cloth of every robe
Harsh lye from the scrubbing troughs
Marsh mud and stagnant water seeping up from the cellars
rooms: A killing floor of grooved stone where three cultists work a monster on a slab broad enough to lay out an ox, chanting one line of hymn per stroke.
A hook gallery where carcasses ride an endless squealing rail toward a hatch in the far wall, and a person could ride a hook unseen.
A rendering house of steaming vats where fat is boiled down into black candles, the floor slick and the air too thick to see across.
Holding pens of iron cages, half filled with snarling beasts and half with marsh villagers wearing feeding tags.
A tannery yard of stretched hides on frames, some scaled, some furred, a few unmistakably human with tattoos still visible.
A chapel of bone pews and an altar of salted meat, where the high butcher preaches each hour to a congregation in bloody aprons.
A blood cistern, a brick tank as large as a mill pond, skinned with a dark crust that heaves where something moves underneath.
A smokehouse thick with blue haze, hams and haunches hanging in rows, and cultists waiting in the smoke with skinning knives.
A salting cellar of crusted barrels where a terrified apprentice has hidden for days, ready to trade secrets for escape.
A dormitory of straw pallets and rope beds, with a loose floorboard under the high butcher's cot.
A beast pit where the cult's newest catch, a chained manticore, thrashes and spits tail spikes at anyone who walks the rim.

The heart, the cellar pit, a cavern drowned in blood where the cult's god coils, a swollen grey bulk with a dozen mouths along its flanks, while the high butcher stands on the lip ringing the feeding bell.
features: Holding pen locks; opening them with a DC {dc} Dexterity (thieves' tools) or Strength check frees villagers who know the cellar route and will create a distraction at the party's signal.
The chained manticore; striking its chains with a DC {dc} Strength check sets it loose, and it attacks the nearest cultists first, though it remembers no friends after the first round.

Robes and aprons; a creature in cult dress has advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks to pass as a member, but must sing the hymn aloud, and the high butcher can tell a false voice with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check.
The bone chapel; interrupting a sermon and succeeding on a DC {dc} Charisma (Intimidation) check breaks the congregation's nerve, imposing disadvantage on their saves for 1 minute.
The loose floorboard; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check in the dormitory finds 3d10 spirit coins, the high butcher's key to the cellar and an awakening stone of Blood.
The cistern valve; opening it drains the tank into the marsh tunnels, starving the god-thing so it has disadvantage on its first two attacks in the heart.
The feeding bell; stealing it before the fight means the god-thing cannot be called to a target, and ringing it yourself turns its attention onto the high butcher for 1 round.
hazards: Blood-slick stone; a creature that moves more than half its speed on the killing floor makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls prone in the gutters.
