The hook rail; a creature snagged by a passing hook makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is carried toward the cellar hatch, taking {half} piercing damage each round until it pulls free.
Rendering vats; a creature knocked into a vat takes {dmg} fire damage at the start of each turn until it climbs out with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check.
Blood frenzy; a creature that swallows cistern blood makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or must attack the nearest creature on its next turn.
Manticore spikes; a creature walking the beast pit rim makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} piercing damage from a volley of tail spikes.

The god's thirst; when the feeding bell rings, each creature within 30 feet of the pit makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success as blood seeps out through its skin.

environments.name: Cliffside Roc Nests
environments.summary: Sheer granite cliffs plunge into a sea of cloud with no ground beneath, every ledge crusted with nests built from whole pine trunks, ship timbers and the bones of things that once flew. The space formed where the oldest roc in the world died on a mountaintop, its last thoughts of wind and hunting folding into a place where the gale never stops and the sky is always full of wings. It wants its eggs hatched and its brood fed, and anything that climbs its cliffs without wings counts as food.
readAloud: Your boots land on a shelf of granite no wider than a dining table, and below it there is only cloud, white and endless, rolling like surf. Wind hammers up the cliff face so hard you lean into it to stand. A feather as long as a lance tumbles past your face, and high above, something screams loud enough to drown the gale.

A path of crumbling ledges zigzags across the rock, streaked white with droppings and littered with snapped bones. Just above, a nest woven from pine trunks and a ship's broken mast cradles three eggs as large as barrels, blue and brown like river stones. A shadow sweeps across the ledge, and the cliff shudders as something heavy lands on the nest.

Cold air bites your lungs and smells of wet feathers, lichen and old meat. Across the gulf, a waterfall pours off a ledge and frays into mist long before it can reach the clouds. A row of harpies perches on a rock spur nearby, preening, and one begins to sing a tune so sweet that your feet take a step toward the edge before you notice.
sights: Cliffs dropping into a rolling sea of white cloud
Nests woven from pine trunks and broken ship masts
Rocs circling so high they look like slow drifting ash
Eggs the size of barrels, speckled like river stones
A lance-long feather spinning past on the wind
Picked bones stacked on ledges like firewood
A row of harpies preening on a spur of rock
A waterfall shredding into mist halfway down the cliff
sounds: A gale that never pauses for breath
Hatchlings shrieking with mouths open to the sky
Wingbeats deep as a drum struck underwater
Pebbles rattling down the rock and never landing
Harpy song, honeyed and almost a lullaby
A roc's scream that makes the cliff hum
smells: Old meat rotting in the nest linings
Thin air with a bite of snow
Warm musky fur in the griffon caves
rooms: A ledge path of crumbling granite that zigzags up the face, every third handhold marked with old pitons left by earlier climbers.
A roc nest of pine trunks and ship timbers holding three barrel-sized eggs and a lining of torn sails and armour plates.
A griffon aerie, a deep cave mouth carpeted in molted feathers where griffon kits play-fight and their mother watches from the shadows.
A harpy roost on a jagged spur, its perches tied with trophies: helmets, holy symbols and a single child's shoe.
A waterfall ledge where icy water pours past, hiding a dry cave behind the curtain with an old campfire ring.
A bone midden heaped on a wide shelf, where the gear of fallen climbers lies tangled among ribs and skulls.
An updraft chimney, a vertical crack where the wind roars upward hard enough to lift a grown person off their feet.
A hatchery shelf where a newborn roc, already the size of a horse, screams for food and lunges at anything that moves.
A broken rope bridge between two crags, most of its planks gone, its frayed lines snapping like whips in the wind.
A storm ledge scorched black by frequent lightning, scattered with the charred bodies of birds that roosted too long.
A drift of shed feathers in a cleft, soft and waist-deep, where a stalking monstrosity lies buried with only its eyes showing.
The heart, the summit nest at the top of the world, where the oldest roc, white with age and as long as a galley, broods over a single golden egg and rises screaming into the wind.
features: The updraft chimney; a creature that leaps in rises 60 feet per round, and a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check lets it steer onto any ledge it can see.
Roc eggs; one egg sells to the Adventure Society for 50 spirit coins, but the parent roc follows the thief's scent across the whole space and attacks at the first open sky.
The bone midden; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check finds 100 feet of good rope, a set of climbing pitons and a griffon's monster core.
Griffon kits; a creature that approaches the aerie with raw meat and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check befriends the mother, who will carry one rider for the rest of the space.
The waterfall cave; it is the one place in the space where fliers cannot reach, and the party can take a long rest there undisturbed.
The old pitons; a creature that follows them and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check finds a safe route that halves the number of ledge checks needed to reach the summit.
The golden egg; touching it bestows an awakening stone of Wind, but the old roc gains advantage on attacks against whoever holds it.
hazards: Rotten granite; a creature that moves faster than half speed on a ledge makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or the rock crumbles beneath it.
Gale burst; at the start of each round roll a d6, and on a 1 each creature on the cliff face makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is shoved 10 feet toward the drop.
Roc dive; a creature in open air or on an exposed ledge makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is grappled in talons, taking {dmg} piercing damage and being carried 1d6 x 10 feet upward.
Harpy lullaby; a creature hearing the song makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed and walks toward the nearest edge on its turn.
Landing tremor; when a roc lands, each creature on the ledges below makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success from falling stone.
Snapping bridge lines; a creature crossing the broken bridge makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is lashed by a frayed rope for {half} slashing damage and knocked off its feet.

environments.name: Underground River Docks
environments.summary: A river black as lamp soot races through a cavern too vast for any torch, its banks crowded with sagging docks, lantern-hung warehouses and flat barges that ferry cargo between ports that should be a world apart. A smuggling guild from the Delta found the first passage and built the wharves, and only later learned the river was alive and had always expected payment. The river wants its toll from every hull, and what it takes is never coin alone: a memory, a name, a finger or a passenger.
readAloud: Lantern light shivers across water so black it looks solid, every reflection stretched into a long trembling ribbon. Docks of grey timber line the bank, piled with crates stenciled in a dozen alphabets, and barges knock gently at their moorings. A crowd of smugglers haggles, shouts and spits, and not one of them stops talking when you arrive, though several shift their hands closer to their knives.

The current slides past without a ripple, fast as a galloping horse and utterly silent. A flat barge drifts by under a hooded pole-man, its cargo hidden beneath tarps that bulge outward as if something underneath is breathing. As it passes, the boatman lifts his head, and in place of eyes he has two tarnished coins.

Far overhead, stalactites drip into the dark, each drop landing in the river with a small bright plink. A sign hangs on chains above a warehouse door, its painted letters reading Tolls Paid Here. Beneath it, scratched into the wood by some desperate blade, are two more words: Or Else.
sights: Lantern reflections stretched into trembling ribbons
Crates stenciled in a dozen alphabets
Coin-eyed boatmen poling barges without a sound
Tarps over cargo that swells and settles like breathing
Stalactites dripping from a ceiling lost in darkness
A toll house on stilts with a scale for weighing coins
Drowned spirit coins glittering on the riverbed far below
A pale tentacle tip rising briefly beside a moored hull
sounds: Water lapping at hulls in a soft, even rhythm
Haggling in many tongues, all of it fast
Mooring ropes groaning against bollards
A bright plink from every falling drip
Deep bubbling from the middle of the channel
The toll bell, rung once for each boat that pays
smells: Cold limestone breath from the cavern walls
Lamp oil smoke hanging low over the water
Saffron, pepper and clove from smuggled cargo
A rank tidal stink rising whenever the channel bubbles
rooms: The main wharf, a maze of jetties where smugglers unload crates, settle debts with fists and auction goods with no questions asked.
A toll house on spindly stilts where a pale clerk weighs every payment on a brass scale and writes each boat into a ledger bound in fish skin.
A bonded warehouse stacked to the rafters with crates, some holding brandy and silk, some holding caged creatures that knock to get out.
A ferry landing where a coin-eyed boatman offers passage for one spirit coin a head and promises never to ask where you are going.
A tavern carved into the cavern wall, smoky and roaring, where every booth sells something different: a map, a rumour, a forged license.
A collapsed jetty half sunk in the river, its pilings furred with pale weed that sways against the current.
A shipwright's slip where a half-built barge sits on rollers and a cauldron of pitch bubbles over a driftwood fire.
A river shrine in a side grotto, its walls pressed full of coins, tiny carved boats and locks of hair left as offerings.
A rapids gorge where the river narrows and roars white over jagged rocks, the one stretch where the water makes noise.
A boat graveyard in the shallows, dozens of wrecks lying on their sides, their holds still sealed and their names still painted.
An eel pen fenced off with iron stakes, where the guild keeps giant shocking eels for anyone who will not pay.

The heart, the drowned lake where the river widens and stops, and the toll-taker rises from the black water, a vast pale thing of tentacles crowned with a heap of drowned coins, every one a toll someone failed to pay.
features: The toll house; a boat that pays one spirit coin per passenger travels the river safely, and a boat that does not is marked by a ripple that follows it downstream.

Tavern booths; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check and 5 spirit coins buys the toll-taker's weakness: it cannot abide a coin offered freely, and a gift thrown into the lake stuns it until the end of its next turn.
The coin-eyed boatman; he ferries the party to any landing in a single round of travel, and for double fare he will answer one question about where the river goes.
The river shrine; leaving an offering worth at least 1 spirit coin grants advantage on saves against drowning, currents and the toll-taker for 1 hour.
Sealed wrecks; a creature who dives into the boat graveyard and succeeds on a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check recovers 2d10 spirit coins of contraband or an awakening stone of Water.

The fish-skin ledger; stealing it with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check reveals every unpaid debt, and reading a debtor's name aloud at the lake makes the toll-taker attack that debtor first.
The eel pen gate; opening it with a DC {dc} Strength check spills the eels into the wharf, causing 10 minutes of chaos in which the party can move unseen.
hazards: The silent current; a creature that falls in makes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check each round or is swept 30 feet downstream toward the lake.
Weed-rotted pilings; a creature crossing the collapsed jetty makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls through into the river.
The unpaid toll; tentacles rise beside a boat that has not paid, and each creature aboard makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is dragged under and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
White rapids; steering through the gorge takes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check, and a failure capsizes the boat, dealing {half} bludgeoning damage to everyone aboard.
Eel shock; a creature in the eel pen makes a DC {dc} Constitution save at the start of each turn, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Numbing cold; a creature submerged for more than 1 minute makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each minute or gains a level of exhaustion.

environments.name: Village at Endless Dusk
environments.summary: A hundred years ago the farmers of Ashby Lea locked a hedge-witch in her own house and set it alight at sundown, and her dying curse froze that evening in place around them. The astral space grew from that single guilty hour, so the sun hangs a hand's breadth above the hills, the bread is always nearly baked, and every villager smiles to keep the secret buried. What the place wants is a confession spoken aloud in the church, and until it gets one, it feeds each visitor's shadow to the dark that waits behind the houses.
readAloud: Warm orange light pours over thatched roofs and a crooked cobbled lane, and the sun sits swollen and red just above the hills, refusing to sink. Every shadow in the village stretches impossibly long, reaching east toward a blackened ruin at the edge of the fields. Chimney smoke curls into a violet sky, and from somewhere close comes the smell of bread that is almost, but never quite, ready.

A plump woman in a flour-dusted apron waves from her garden gate. 'Travelers! You look worn to the bone. Come in, there's stew on and beds aired.' In the doorway behind her a small boy stands perfectly still, and on the wall beside him his shadow is pressing both hands over its mouth.

Crickets saw away in the wheat and lamps glow in every window, though it is not yet dark and never will be. Faces turn toward you from porches and half-drawn curtains, all of them smiling, none of them blinking. At the far end of the lane a church stands with planks nailed across its doors, and the frayed end of a bell rope sways in a breeze you cannot feel.
sights: A bloated red sun pinned a hand's breadth above the western hills
Shadows forty feet long that point at the burned house no matter where the light falls
Villagers whose smiles never falter, even when they sneeze
A church door crossed with planks and bent coffin nails
Washing on a line that has been drying for a century and is still damp
Moths circling lanterns in perfect, unbroken rings
Children playing a clapping game that always stops on the same verse
A soot handprint on every doorframe, at the height of a grown woman's shoulder
sounds: Crickets singing in a rhythm that matches a slow heartbeat
Dough slapped on a board, over and over, from the bakery
A dog that barks once at strangers and then whimpers into silence
Whispering from the well, too faint to make out without leaning close
The church bell's clapper knocking softly, though no one rings it
A woman's voice humming a lullaby from inside the burned house
smells: Fresh bread with a crust that never browns
Applewood smoke from a dozen chimneys
Cut hay sweetened by evening dew
Wet ash and scorched hair under every other scent
Crushed elderflower from the hedges by the graveyard
rooms: A village green where a maypole wrapped in sun-bleached ribbons leans over a mossy stone well; the ribbons spell a woman's name if unwound in order.
A bakery where the baker kneads the same loaf with floury, trembling hands, weeping softly and insisting the oven is not hot enough yet.
The Plough and Penny tavern, warm and crowded, where every patron falls silent when strangers enter and then resumes the exact sentence they stopped mid-word.
A boarded church with a cut bell rope, its pews draped in dust sheets and its altar stacked with unopened letters of apology.
A farmhouse kitchen where a family of five eats supper while their shadows sit at the far end of the table, eating nothing and staring at the door.
A wheat field taller than a man that whispers names on the wind, including the names of the party if they linger more than a minute.
A blacksmith's shed hung with a hundred iron keys, every one of them cut to fit the same burned door.
A watermill whose wheel turns without water, grinding ash instead of grain into sacks stamped with the village seal.
A churchyard where fresh flowers lie on every grave except a bare patch of earth by the hedge, where nothing has ever grown.
A schoolhouse with a slate board that rewrites itself each time it is wiped, always the same line: 'We only meant to frighten her.'
The reeve's manor, where the village elder sleeps in a chair by the window with a tinderbox clutched to his chest and wakes screaming if touched.

The heart, the cellar beneath the burned house, where the hedge-witch sits in a circle of melted candles holding the last light of the sun cupped in her charred hands, and every lost shadow in the village kneels around her.
features: The villagers' supper; accepting a meal grants the benefits of a short rest, but the creature must succeed on a DC {dc} Wisdom save or its shadow slips away to the burned house, giving it disadvantage on Stealth checks and immunity to being seen in mirrors until the shadow is reclaimed in the heart.

The boarded church; prying the planks loose takes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check and reveals the parish ledger recording the burning, and reading it aloud makes every villager's shadow turn on its owner for 1 minute.
The bare grave by the hedge; planting flowers there and speaking the witch's name makes her hesitate on the first round in the heart, giving the party a surprise round.

The cut bell rope; splicing it with a DC {dc} Dexterity check using thieves' tools or rope and ringing the bell drops the sun one finger lower, and each ring after the first summons 1d4 undead villagers to the church.

The whispering well; a creature that lowers its head inside and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check hears the full story of the burning and gains advantage on Charisma checks against the witch.
The blacksmith's key rack; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the one true key, which opens the burned house without triggering its fire ward.

The baker's oven; a creature that pulls the eternal loaf free and breaks it releases a puff of warm light that restores {half} hit points to everyone within 10 feet, but the baker's grief turns to rage.
hazards: Shadows at the edge of lamplight reach out to drag the living into them; a creature that starts its turn in dim light makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is grappled by its own shadow and takes {half} necrotic damage each round until it breaks free.
Relentless hospitality; a creature that refuses a villager's invitation three times makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or is bundled indoors by a crowd of smiling hands and charmed for 1 hour.
The whispering wheat; a creature walking through the field makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is frightened for 1 minute and wanders 1d4 x 10 feet deeper before it can turn back.
Lengthening dusk; every hour the party spends in the village, the shadows creep 10 feet closer, and creatures without a light source make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} necrotic damage.

The burned house's threshold; stepping through without the true key makes the doorframe flare with old fire, and each creature in the doorway makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

A sudden tolling of the church bell when no one touches it; every creature in the village makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or drops whatever it is holding and spends its next turn walking toward the churchyard.

environments.name: Living Painting
environments.summary: A Magic Society portraitist named Odile Varre fell in love with the fey muse who inspired her, and when it tried to leave she painted a canvas large enough to hold it forever, then stepped inside to keep painting. The astral space is that canvas, a sprawl of meadows, ballrooms and storm-skies built from thick visible brushstrokes, still wet in places and smearing under every footstep. It wants to be finished, and it will gladly use visitors as pigment to fill its last bare patches of white.
readAloud: You land on a hillside of grass made from a thousand bold green strokes, each blade with a ridge of paint you can feel through your boots. The sky is a sweep of cerulean with clouds dabbed on by a thick brush, and a sun of pure lead white glows without warmth. Where your heel scuffs the ground, the green smears into the brown beneath, and somewhere a voice sighs in irritation.

The portal closes behind you with the soft rasp of a palette knife. A painted river flows downhill in curling blue loops, and painted swans glide on it, their necks a single elegant stroke. One swan turns its head toward you, and you see that it has no back half at all, only a ragged edge of bare canvas where the artist stopped.

A smell of linseed oil and turpentine fills your lungs as the colours settle around you. You stand in a ballroom of gilded ochre where painted dancers turn in slow circles, their faces blurred where someone wiped them out with a rag. Far above, through a skylight of raw canvas, an enormous shadowed hand holding a brush moves slowly across the heavens.
sights: Grass made of ridged green brushstrokes that hold a footprint for a minute before smoothing
A lead-white sun that casts light but no warmth
Painted dancers with wiped-out faces, smudged into a flesh-coloured blur
Patches of bare canvas where the world simply stops, edged with pencil sketch lines
Drips of crimson running up the walls instead of down
A painted cat that walks in a loop, reappearing in the corner of every scene
Gold leaf flaking from the edges of a painted chandelier
A giant signature in the corner of the sky, the last letter never finished
sounds: The wet scrape of a palette knife from somewhere overhead
Bristles whispering across canvas like distant rain
A painted string quartet playing a waltz a beat out of time
The crackle of drying varnish as a scene sets
A woman's voice muttering 'no, no, wrong' and the sound of a rag scrubbing
A soft chime, like a glass bell, every time a colour changes
smells: Turpentine that makes the eyes water
Rabbit-skin glue warming on a stove
Sweet honeysuckle that is only painted, yet still smells
rooms: A pastoral meadow of ridged green strokes where painted sheep graze; touching one smears it, and it bleats in a voice made of falling colour.
A gilded ballroom where faceless dancers spin endlessly and pull any guest into the waltz, leaving ochre handprints on their clothes.
A storm-sky gallery where lightning is a single jagged stroke of white that can be peeled off the sky and carried like a spear.
A still life chamber where a giant bowl of fruit, a wine jug and a skull sit on a velvet cloth, and anything eaten tastes of the colour it is painted.
A sketchbook corridor drawn only in charcoal and pencil, unfinished and grey, where shapes not yet painted lurk behind the guidelines.
A portrait hall lined with hundreds of versions of the same face, each a failed attempt to capture the muse, all of them watching and commenting.
A seascape cove where waves are thick curls of blue and white impasto that crash in slow motion and can be climbed like hills.
A palette plain, a flat wasteland of mixed colours in great blotches, each blotch a different affinity of raw paint that hums with power.
A varnish lake, glassy and amber, that preserves anything that falls into it in a shining permanent coat.
A cracked-paint ruin where an old layer of the painting shows through, an earlier world the artist painted over, darker and stranger.
The artist's studio corner, a bare wooden easel standing in a rectangle of untouched white, with brushes in jars and a half-finished sketch of each party member.

The heart, the centre of the canvas, where the muse hangs bound in ribbons of liquid gold and the painted ghost of Odile Varre stands at a cosmic easel, brush raised, ready to paint the party into the final empty space.
features: The palette plain's colour blotches; a creature that dips a weapon in a blotch can deal an extra {half} damage of a matching type (red for fire, blue for cold, yellow for lightning) on its next three hits, but on a natural 1 the colour spreads to its skin and it is restrained for a round as the paint dries.
Peelable lightning in the storm gallery; a creature can tear free one bolt with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check and throw it once as a ranged attack dealing {dmg} lightning damage.

The varnish lake; dipping an item fully in it makes the item immune to damage for 24 hours, but a creature that falls in makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is petrified in a shining glaze for 1 minute.

The portrait hall's failed muses; a creature that succeeds on a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check convinces one portrait to reveal the muse's true name, which can be used to break the gold ribbons in the heart.

A drawer of unused brushes in the studio corner; a creature that paints a simple object (a door, a rope, a bridge) on any bare canvas with a DC {dc} Dexterity check using painter's supplies makes it real for 10 minutes.
The cracked-paint ruin; scraping away the top layer with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check reveals a tin box of spirit coins and a varnished monster core that the artist painted over decades ago.
Washing out a painted figure; a creature that douses a paint construct with turpentine or a gallon of water deals {dmg} acid damage to it as its colours run.
hazards: Wet paint underfoot in freshly painted scenes; a creature moving more than half its speed makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or slips prone and is stuck, restrained until it uses an action to pull free.

The artist's rag sweeps across a scene to erase a mistake; each creature in a 30-foot line makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} force damage and loses one random sense (sight, hearing or speech) for 1 minute as it is wiped out.
Bare canvas edges; a creature that steps into raw white makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or forgets its name for 1 hour and has disadvantage on all Intelligence checks.
Turpentine fumes thicken in the studio corner; a creature breathing them at the end of its turn makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned until the end of its next turn.

The painted swans and other half-finished creatures attack any colour that is not their own; a creature wearing bright clothing has disadvantage on Stealth checks and takes {half} slashing damage when it first enters a scene.

A layer of varnish dries over a room every ten minutes; any creature still inside makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained in hardening glaze, taking {half} bludgeoning damage when it breaks free.

environments.name: Volcano Forge
environments.summary: Fire giant smith-lords carved this forge into the throat of a living volcano to arm a war whose name has burned out of every history, and their hammer-songs taught the mountain itself to crave the making of weapons. The astral space keeps the bellows breathing and the lava running in its stone channels, and the anvils still glow from a heat the giants poured into them centuries ago. A red dragon named Cinder-Queen Vathrask now coils on the forge's hoard in the caldera, and the mountain wants a new smith worthy of its fire, testing everyone who enters with heat, hammer and flame.
readAloud: Heat slams into you like an open furnace door, and the air shimmers so hard the far wall wavers. You stand on a ledge of black basalt above a workshop the size of a cathedral, where rivers of orange lava run through stone troughs between anvils as tall as houses. Somewhere below, a hammer strikes iron, and the whole mountain answers with a low, approving rumble.

The portal opens onto a bridge of iron plates riveted over a lava channel, each plate ticking as it expands. Ahead, a pair of bellows the size of barns wheeze in and out on their own, and each breath makes the coals in the great hearth flare white. Ash drifts down from the vents like grey snow and settles hot on your shoulders.

Sulfur stings your nose and the soles of your boots begin to soften. Racks of half-finished swords taller than you line the walls, still glowing cherry red at the tips. From high above, past a vent where the roof opens to a sky of smoke, comes the slow, heavy breathing of something enormous asleep on a bed of gold.
sights: Lava sliding through carved stone troughs like molten honey
Anvils the size of wagons, still glowing dull red
Giant swords on racks, cooling from white to cherry to black
Bellows the size of barns breathing on their own
Grey ash snowing from vents in the ceiling
Rune-carved quench pools steaming with oily black water
Obsidian shards glittering in the walls like frozen glass
A heap of gold and weapons in the caldera, shimmering under a dragon's sleeping bulk
sounds: A hammer ringing on iron somewhere deep below
Bellows wheezing and roaring in slow rhythm
Lava bubbling and popping in the channels
The tick and groan of metal plates expanding
A low rumble from the mountain, like a satisfied growl
The slow, rasping breath of a dragon in the caldera
smells: Molten rock with a flinty, metallic bite
rooms: An entry bridge of riveted iron plates over a lava channel, each plate hot enough to brand and wide enough for two to cross abreast.
The great workshop, a cavern of giant anvils and stone troughs where lava flows like water through a mill race and hammers lie abandoned mid-swing.
A bellows hall where two barn-sized bellows breathe on their own, their gusts strong enough to knock a Medium creature off its feet.
A quenching pool chamber where giant blades cool in black oil, the surface steaming and slick, hiding things that bite.
An ore pit where molten metal of every colour pools in separate basins, gold, silver, copper and a strange blue metal that hums.
A weapon rack gallery where hundreds of giant-sized swords, axes and mauls hang on chains, swaying in the updraft.
A rune-carving room where a fire giant's ghost still chisels glowing sigils into a blade, ignoring visitors unless they hand him a tool.
An obsidian mirror hall where the walls are polished volcanic glass, reflecting the party as figures of living flame.
A slag heap tunnel, a crawlspace through cooling waste rock that cracks and leaks hot gas with every step.
The giants' feast hall, carved with tables and benches for beings twenty feet tall, where cups of molten wine still steam.
A magma lift, a stone platform on chains above the volcano's throat that rises toward the caldera when its crank is turned.
The heart, the caldera at the volcano's summit, where Cinder-Queen Vathrask sleeps coiled on a mountain of gold and giant weapons beneath a sky of churning smoke, the lava lake glowing around her.
features: The giant anvils; a creature with smith's tools that spends 10 minutes at one and succeeds on a DC {dc} Strength check can reforge a weapon so that it deals an extra {half} fire damage for 24 hours, but a failure shatters the weapon.
The ore pit's blue metal; a creature that collects it with tongs and a DC {dc} Dexterity check gains a bar of star-iron worth 500 spirit coins, prized by the Magic Society.
The bellows; a creature that works the lever can blast a 30-foot cone of superheated air through the hearth, dealing {dmg} fire damage to each creature in it (DC {dc} Dexterity save for half).
The ghost rune-carver; handing him a hammer or chisel lets him inscribe a rune on a party member's armour that grants resistance to fire for 1 hour.

The quenching pools; plunging a hot weapon into the oil cools it instantly, and a creature that bathes in the oil gains resistance to fire for 10 minutes but is vulnerable to cold for the same duration.
The magma lift; turning its crank requires a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, and it carries the party straight to the caldera, skipping three rooms but announcing their arrival to the dragon.
The weapon rack chains; cutting them with a DC {dc} Strength check drops a giant blade across a lava channel as a bridge, or onto an enemy for {dmg} slashing damage.
hazards: Lava splash from a channel when something heavy falls in; each creature within 10 feet makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
Extreme heat; each hour in the forge without fire resistance, a creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion, with disadvantage if it wears medium or heavy armour.
Volcanic gas vents in the slag tunnel; a creature that breathes the gas makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 minute and takes {half} poison damage.

Cracking floor plates over the lava; a creature heavier than 300 pounds causes a plate to buckle, and it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls into the channel, taking {dmg} fire damage at the start of each turn it remains.
The mountain's tremor when the dragon stirs; every creature in the forge makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is knocked prone, and loose ore and ash rain from the ceiling for {half} bludgeoning damage.
Molten metal from the ore pits; a creature touching one of the basins takes {dmg} fire damage, and a metal weapon dipped in it melts unless magical.

environments.name: Winter Palace of Ice
environments.summary: A frost queen of the fey courts, Ysolde of the Long Night, raised this palace from a single glacier when a mortal king broke his vow to her, and she froze her entire court into sculpture so none of them could ever betray her again. The astral space preserves her perfect winter, every hall of blue ice polished like glass, every snowflake suspended for the beauty of it. She wants company that will never leave, and she offers each visitor a place in her frozen gallery, by courtesy or by force.
readAloud: Cold bites your lungs like a blade drawn across your throat, and your breath crystallizes in the air before you. You stand in a grand hall of translucent blue ice, its pillars carved into slender figures holding up a ceiling of glittering frost. Snow drifts down in slow spirals from nowhere, and every flake hangs for a moment in the air before it lands, as if waiting for permission.

The portal closes with the crack of a frozen lake splitting. Lining the corridor ahead are courtiers frozen mid-bow, mid-laugh, mid-whisper, their silks stiff with frost and their eyes open beneath a glaze of ice. As you pass, the nearest one's eyes follow you, slow as a thaw.

Somewhere far off a harp plays, each note shattering into a tinkle of falling ice. The floor beneath you is so clear that you can see a second palace below, upside down, and figures walking in it on the ceiling. A wind sweeps through the hall carrying a voice like falling snow: 'Guests. How long it has been since anyone came to stay.'
sights: Pillars carved as slender ice maidens holding up the vaults
Courtiers frozen mid-gesture, their silks stiff with hoarfrost
Snowflakes hanging motionless in the air before they fall
A reflected palace beneath the glassy floor, upside down
Icicle chandeliers that refract light into tiny rainbows
Frozen fountains caught mid-splash in sculpted arcs
A throne carved from a single sapphire-blue block of glacier
Frost ferns spreading across any warm surface in seconds
sounds: A distant harp whose notes shatter into tinkling ice
Ice cracking deep in the walls, like distant thunder
Wind moaning through hollow pillars
Footsteps echoing for far too long
The soft crunch of fresh snow on polished floors
A frozen courtier's teeth chattering in the dark
smells: Clean, sharp cold that numbs the nose
Pine resin frozen in the cracks of the walls
Wet wool steaming off cold travelers
Mint and frost on the queen's breath
rooms: An entry hall of ice maiden pillars, where the snow hangs in the air and the floor reflects an upside-down palace below.
A frozen court gallery where dozens of courtiers stand trapped in ice mid-gesture, some of them still blinking.
A ballroom with a floor of black ice, where spectral dancers of drifting snow waltz to an unseen harp and pull guests into the dance.
A frozen fountain courtyard, the water caught mid-splash in arcs of ice that can be climbed to reach a high balcony.
An icicle forest corridor, a hallway of hanging icicles so thick that passing requires breaking them or squeezing between.
A winter garden where flowers of frost bloom on glass stems and give off a faint blue light and a smell of mint.
A kitchen where a frost giant cook stirs a cauldron of iced soup and serves bowls of snow to any guest, offended if refused.
A mirror chamber of polished ice where each reflection shows the viewer as a frozen statue, smiling.
A crevasse bridge, a span of clear ice over a bottomless blue chasm that groans with every step.
A snow-drift library where books of ice can be read only by warming their pages, which melt as they are read.
The queen's wardrobe, a chamber of gowns woven from frost and snow, each one granting cold resistance and a heavy chill to the heart.
The heart, the throne room of glacier blue, where Ysolde of the Long Night sits on a sapphire throne with a crown of icicles, her frozen king kneeling at her feet in a block of clear ice.
features: The frozen courtiers; thawing one with fire damage or a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check revives a fey noble who knows the queen's weakness and lets the party ignore her first use of frozen breath.
The frost gowns in the wardrobe; a creature that wears one gains resistance to cold damage but makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save each hour or becomes charmed by the queen.
The frozen fountain; a creature that climbs the ice arcs with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check reaches a balcony overlooking the throne room, allowing the party to approach unseen.
The ice library's books; warming and reading one with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check reveals the vow the king broke, which can be spoken to the queen to shatter her concentration.
The frost giant cook's soup; eating a bowl grants cold immunity for 1 hour, but refusing makes the cook hostile.
The crevasse bridge's anchor stones; a creature that studies them with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a cache of frozen spirit coins and a cold-aspected monster core.
The kneeling king in clear ice; shattering his block with {dmg} worth of bludgeoning damage frees him, and he begs the queen's forgiveness, ending the fight if the party protects him for 3 rounds.
hazards: Black ice in the ballroom; a creature moving faster than half its speed makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls prone and slides 10 feet in a random direction.
The queen's breath sweeping the halls; each creature in a 60-foot cone makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} cold damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
Falling icicles in the icicle forest; a loud noise brings them down, and each creature in the corridor makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} piercing damage.

Creeping frost; a creature that stands still for more than 1 minute makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or its feet freeze to the floor, restraining it until it takes {half} fire damage or breaks free with a DC {dc} Strength check.
The crevasse bridge groans and cracks; a creature crossing it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or the ice gives way, dropping it 60 feet into the chasm.
Frostbite from the bitter cold; each hour without cold protection, a creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.

environments.name: Slime-Filled Sewer
environments.summary: This space began as a forgotten stretch of the Old City's drains, where three centuries of alchemists poured failed tinctures, essences and dissolved monster cores down the same grate until the sludge woke and started to think. The astral space swelled around that thinking slime, stretching brick tunnels into a maze of overflow chambers, cisterns and spillways it can digest at leisure. It wants to grow, and it keeps visitors alive just long enough to learn what they are made of, then adds them to its colours.
readAloud: The stench hits before your eyes adjust: rot, old eggs and something chemical that makes your teeth itch. You stand on a narrow brick ledge above a channel of slow green sludge that glows faintly from within, lighting the curved ceiling in sickly ripples. Something in the channel shifts, and a lazy bubble rises and pops, releasing a puff of yellow vapour that smells like burnt sugar.

Water drips from the vaulted brick in a dozen places, each drop hissing when it strikes the slime below. Along the far ledge, red eyes catch your lantern light, six pairs, then twelve, each set the size of copper coins. A rat as large as a hound sits up on its haunches and sniffs, whiskers twitching, and the others begin to creep forward.

Your boots sink to the ankle in something warm and yielding that clings when you lift your foot. The tunnel ahead opens into a great round cistern where the slime is piled in a translucent mound, and suspended inside it like fruit in jelly are coins, rings, a rusted helmet and the pale shape of a hand. The mound pulses once, slowly, as if it has noticed you.
sights: Green sludge glowing faintly from within, casting rippling light on brick
Coins, rings and bones suspended in translucent slime like fruit in jelly
Rats the size of hounds watching from dry ledges
Crusted alchemical stains in purple, orange and acid yellow
Rusted grates choked with hair, rags and lost gloves
Bubbles rising and popping with puffs of coloured vapour
Old brickwork stamped with the seals of long-dead guilds
A slime trail climbing straight up a wall and across the ceiling
sounds: Slow, wet dripping from the vaulted ceiling
Gurgling and belching from deep in the channels
The skitter of claws on brick ledges
A faint, sucking slurp as slime pulls back from stone
Rushing water from a distant spillway
A low, rhythmic throb like a heartbeat in the walls
smells: Burnt sugar from the yellow gas
Copper and old blood near the cistern
rooms: A main channel tunnel with narrow ledges on each side and a river of glowing sludge flowing slowly down the middle.
A rat warren in a collapsed side tunnel, piled with nesting rags and gnawed bones, where giant rats breed in stinking heaps.
An overflow chamber where rainwater from the city above pours down a shaft, mixing with slime into a churning green pool.
An alchemist's dump, a small room where barrels of failed tinctures leak into the floor, each puddle a different colour and hazard.
A grate junction where five tunnels meet at a rusted iron grate, and something large has pressed its body through the bars.
A sunken shrine to a forgotten god of drains, with a stone altar half-buried in sludge and offerings still glinting in the muck.
A collapsed cellar where a building above fell into the sewer long ago, its rotting furniture and shelves now home to fat white grubs.
A spillway, a steep brick slope where water and slime rush down into darkness, slick and fast.
A dry vault, the only clean room in the sewer, where a lost Iron-rank team has barricaded themselves, starving and feverish.
An egg chamber where slime clings to the walls in great translucent sacs, each one holding a curled shape twitching inside.
A crumbling aqueduct bridge spanning a great cistern, its supports eaten away by acid.

The heart, the great cistern at the bottom of the sewer, where the mother slime has grown into a mound of glowing jelly forty feet across, its surface full of swallowed treasures and half-dissolved adventurers who still move.
features: The suspended treasures in the slime; a creature that reaches into a mound with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check can pull out 2d6 spirit coins or a random trinket, but takes {half} acid damage either way.
The alchemist's dump barrels; a creature that succeeds on a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check can identify and salvage one working potion from among the failures.
The overflow shaft; climbing it with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check leads to a grate beneath a Greenstone street and a safe exit, but the slime follows anyone who carries its treasures.
The sunken shrine; leaving an offering of spirit coins on the altar grants advantage on Constitution saves against disease and poison for 24 hours.
The lost Iron-rank team in the dry vault; sharing food and healing with them wins over a ragged guide who can lead the party straight to the egg chamber.
The egg sacs; burning them with fire damage destroys the slime's spawn, and the mother slime takes {dmg} psychic damage at the start of the boss fight.
Fresh water from the overflow shaft; a creature that washes in it removes slime from its gear, ending any ongoing acid damage.
hazards: Acidic slime underfoot in the channels; a creature wading through it takes {half} acid damage at the end of each turn, and nonmagical boots dissolve after 3 turns.
Toxic gas bubbles; when one pops near a creature, it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 minute and takes {half} poison damage.

Sewer fever; a creature that is bitten by a giant rat or takes acid damage from the slime makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or contracts a disease that gives disadvantage on Strength checks until cured.
The spillway slope; a creature that steps onto it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or slides 40 feet into the cistern below, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and landing in slime.
Grasping slime tendrils rise from the channels; a creature within 5 feet of the sludge makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is grappled and pulled 10 feet into it.
The crumbling aqueduct bridge; a creature crossing makes a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or the stone breaks beneath it, dropping it 30 feet into the cistern.

environments.name: Hall of Statues
environments.summary: A sculptor born with a basilisk's gaze, known only as the Curator, hated the way living models moved and fidgeted and aged, so he built a hall where they would hold their poses forever. The astral space grew around his collection of petrified visitors, a vast marble gallery where the stone remembers every life it has stolen and whispers about it in the dust. It rewards stillness and punishes curiosity, and the Curator wants one perfect new piece to complete the exhibit he has spent centuries planning.
readAloud: The quiet presses against your ears like cotton wool, so complete you can hear your own blood. Before you stretches a gallery of white marble, its floor polished to a mirror and its pillars carved with laurel wreaths, lined on both sides by statues so lifelike that you half expect them to turn. A warrior with a raised sword, a crying child, a dog mid-leap, all perfectly still and perfectly detailed down to the pores of their skin.

Your footsteps ring on the marble and echo for far too long, and every echo sounds slightly louder than the step that made it. Dust lies thick on the floor except in a narrow path down the centre, worn smooth by someone walking it every day. At the end of the hall, a pedestal stands empty, with a small brass plaque that reads, 'Reserved.'

A cold draft carries the smell of stone dust and old flowers. The statues on either side are arranged in tableaux: a family at dinner, a scholar reading, a pair of lovers reaching for each other with an inch of air between their fingers. As you pass, one statue's eyes are wet, and a single tear of stone dust rolls down its cheek.
sights: Statues so lifelike their pores and eyelashes are carved in perfect detail
Lovers reaching for each other, frozen an inch apart
A worn path through the dust down the centre of the gallery
Empty pedestals with brass plaques reading 'Reserved'
A statue whose stone tears leave trails of dust on its cheeks
Marble pillars carved with laurel wreaths and grasping hands
Broken statues swept into a pile in a corner, faces staring
A tall figure in a silver veil walking the gallery at night
sounds: Total quiet that makes the ears ring
Footsteps echoing louder than the step that made them
The scrape of stone shifting when no one is looking
A faint whisper from inside the statues, too quiet to understand
A chisel tapping somewhere far off
The creak of a heavy door closing at the end of the hall
smells: Dried flowers left as offerings at the statues' feet
Cold, mineral air like a cave
Faint lavender perfume from the veiled figure
The flat, chalky scent of fear-sweat turned to stone
rooms: The grand gallery, a long marble hall lined with statues of former visitors arranged in lifelike poses.
A garden of statues where petrified beasts stand among stone hedges, a stag mid-leap, a wolf mid-howl, an owlbear rearing.
A workshop where half-carved statues stand among chisels and hammers, some of them showing the outlines of living faces trapped beneath the marble.
A reading room of stone scholars bent over stone books, one of which can be opened to reveal a record of the Curator's victims.
A tableau chamber where an entire wedding party has been turned to stone, the bride's veil caught mid-flutter.
A gallery of broken statues swept into a heap, their faces staring from the rubble, still whispering.
A mirror room where the walls are polished obsidian, and anyone who looks at their reflection feels their limbs stiffen.
A pedestal hall with a dozen empty plinths, each with a brass plaque bearing the name of a party member.
A crypt below the gallery where crumbling statues of the Curator's earliest works lie in rows, some of them cracked open like eggs.
A stone forest corridor where the pillars are carved into twisting trees and the branches move when no one is watching.
The Curator's quarters, a bare cell with a cot, a silver veil hanging on a hook, and a sketchbook of planned poses.
The heart, the centrepiece gallery under a dome of white marble, where the Curator stands veiled before a towering statue of his own masterpiece, waiting for the last piece to be placed.
features: The statues' whispers; a creature that presses its ear to a statue and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check learns the victim's name and how they were caught, granting advantage on saves against petrification.
The reading room's stone book; opening it with a DC {dc} Strength check reveals the Curator's true name, which can be spoken to make him hesitate for one round.

The workshop's chisels; a creature that carves at a half-finished statue with mason's tools and a DC {dc} Dexterity check can free the living face trapped inside, gaining an ally who knows the hall's secrets.
The broken statue heap; searching it with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check uncovers a pouch of spirit coins and an awakening stone dropped by a victim.
The pedestal plaques; scratching out a name with a dagger protects that creature from being petrified for 1 hour.
The Curator's silver veil; stealing it from his quarters leaves him without protection, so meeting his gaze in the heart forces him to make his own save against petrification.
A vial of stone-salve in the crypt; applying it to a petrified creature with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check reverses the curse over 1 minute.
hazards: The Curator's gaze; any creature that meets his eyes makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or begins to turn to stone, restrained, and petrified if it fails again at the end of its next turn.
The mirror room's obsidian walls; a creature that looks at its reflection makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is slowed as its limbs stiffen for 1 minute.
Statues that move when unobserved; each time the party turns its back on the gallery, 1d4 statues shift closer, and if any reach a creature they attack for {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Breaking the quiet; any loud noise makes the stone dust rise, and each creature within 30 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded by dust for 1 round.
The stone forest's branches; a creature that walks between the pillars makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is grappled by a stone branch and takes {half} bludgeoning damage.

Creeping petrification on the dusty path; a creature that steps off the worn centre path makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or its feet turn to stone, reducing its speed to 0 until the end of its next turn.

environments.name: Carnival of Masks and Teeth
environments.summary: A wandering fiend called Mister Grinmarrow once ran a traveling carnival through the Delta towns, collecting the greed and envy of everyone who played his games, until he bought this astral space with a bargain no one knows the terms of. The space feeds on wanting, so the lanterns burn brighter for every coin wagered and the rides spin faster for every scream. Every prize is a temptation, every game is rigged, and the carnival wants each visitor to stake something more precious than coin before the last bell rings.
readAloud: Coloured lanterns swing overhead in strings of red, gold and green, and a brass band plays a jaunty tune just slightly off-key. The smell of fried dough, caramelized sugar and hot oil is so thick you can taste it. A barker in a striped coat and a grinning porcelain mask leans out of a booth and calls, 'Step right up, step right up! Every game a winner, every winner a king!'

The portal spits you out beside a carousel where the horses are carved with too many teeth and the riders laugh without stopping. Beyond it, tents of crimson and black canvas sway in a warm wind, each one with a painted sign promising marvels: the Two-Headed Prince, the Woman Who Eats Her Shadow, the Wheel of Your Heart's Desire. Somewhere a calliope shrieks, and the laughter of the riders grows louder.

A girl in a feathered mask presses a paper ticket into your hand and skips away before you can speak. The ticket reads, in elegant gold letters, 'Admit one. Payment due at closing.' All around you, crowds in masks move between the booths, and when one turns its head too quickly, you glimpse rows of needle-thin teeth beneath the painted smile.
sights: Strings of coloured lanterns swaying overhead
A carousel of horses carved with too many teeth
Barkers in porcelain masks leaning out of booths
Prize shelves stacked with gold, gems and awakening stones
Crimson and black tents with painted signs promising marvels
A Ferris wheel whose cars hang empty except for one that holds a skeleton
Masked crowds moving through the booths with jerky, puppet-like steps
A mirror maze glittering beyond the last row of booths
sounds: A brass band playing a jaunty tune slightly off-key
Barkers calling 'Step right up!' from every booth
A calliope shrieking above the crowd
Laughter from the carousel riders that never stops
The clatter of wooden balls knocking over milk bottles
A bell ringing once every hour, and a voice counting down to closing
smells: Hot oil from the food stalls
Brimstone, faint and sweet, under everything
rooms: The midway, a long avenue of game booths and food stalls under strings of lanterns, crowded with masked revelers.
A ring toss booth where the prize is an awakening stone, and the rings shrink in midair to never fit the pegs.
A carousel of toothed horses that spins faster with every scream, and riders who cannot dismount.
A freak show tent where the exhibits are former visitors twisted into monsters by their own losing bets.
A fortune teller's wagon where a veiled crone reads cards that always predict the reader's death, in vivid detail.
A mirror maze that reflects each viewer as the person they most envy, and the reflections step out of the glass.
A strongman's stage where a horned giant challenges anyone to lift a bell hammer, with a chest of spirit coins as the prize.
A Ferris wheel that carries riders high above the carnival, revealing that it sits on a floating island in an endless void.
A haunted house ride where the cars roll through dark tunnels and the scares are real.
A cotton candy stall where the candy is spun from captured dreams, and eating it shows visions of the dreamer's life.
A ticket booth where a fiend clerk keeps ledgers of every bet and debt, and a locked drawer of signed contracts.

The heart, the big top, where Mister Grinmarrow stands in the centre ring under a spotlight, a whip in one hand and the contracts of every soul he owns in the other, and his masked troupe circles the ring waiting for the show to begin.
features: The rigged games; a creature that wins a game with a DC {dc} Dexterity check (with disadvantage, since the game is rigged) earns a prize of 2d6 spirit coins or an awakening stone, but losing costs a memory chosen by the barker.
The strongman's bell hammer; a creature that rings the bell with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check wins a chest of spirit coins, but the giant demands a rematch with fists if he loses.

The fortune teller's cards; a creature that asks for a reading and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check learns Mister Grinmarrow's weakness, so the party's first hit against him in the big top is automatically a critical hit.
The ticket booth's contracts; stealing them with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check and burning them frees the souls bound to the carnival, who rise up against their master in the heart.
The cotton candy of captured dreams; eating it grants a vision that reveals the location of one hidden treasure, but the creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or falls asleep for 1 minute.
The Ferris wheel's view; riding it to the top reveals the layout of the entire carnival and the secret entrance to the big top.
Masks from a costume stall; a creature that wears one can move among the revelers unnoticed, gaining advantage on Stealth checks, but must succeed on a DC {dc} Charisma save to take it off.
hazards: Temptation of the prizes; a creature that sees a prize it desires makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is compelled to play the game until it wins or loses everything it carries.
The carousel's spin; a creature that rides it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each round or is stunned by dizziness, and cannot dismount until the ride stops.
The mirror maze reflections; a creature whose envied reflection steps out must fight it, and the reflection deals {dmg} psychic damage per hit.
Pickpocket revelers; each hour in the crowd, a creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check or loses 1d10 spirit coins or a small item.
The haunted house's real scares; a creature that rides through makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is frightened for 1 hour and takes {half} psychic damage.

Closing time; when the bell rings for closing, every creature that owes a debt to the carnival makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or is transformed into a masked reveler, its body becoming part of the show.

environments.name: Beast-Den Forest
environments.summary: An ancient druid circle that hated the way Greenstone's hunters thinned the wild, they poured their lives into a grove of giant oaks and woke the spirit of predation itself, then vanished into it. The astral space grew into a primeval forest where every hollow, cave and thicket is a lair, and the trees stand so tall and close the canopy blots out the sky. It wants the strong to feed and the weak to be fed, and it marks every newcomer as prey until they prove they can hunt.
readAloud: Trees rise around you like the pillars of a temple, their trunks so wide that ten people could not link arms around them. The canopy is so thick and high that only scattered spears of green light reach the forest floor, and the air is warm and damp and heavy with the smell of earth and blood. A howl starts somewhere to your left, and is answered by another to your right, and another behind you.

You land in a bed of ferns taller than your head, and the first thing you see is a set of claw marks raked down a tree trunk, each groove deep enough to lay your arm in. The bark around them is wet with sap, and fresh. Above, branches creak under the weight of something that shifts and settles, and a slow growl drifts down like a heavy breath.

Birdsong cuts off all at once, as if a door has slammed. Through the trees you catch a flash of tawny fur, gone before you can focus, and then the sound of something heavy moving through the undergrowth, circling. On a low branch nearby, the remains of a deer hang draped like a cloak, picked clean by something with very large teeth.
sights: Trees so vast ten people could not link arms around them
Claw marks raked deep into bark, still weeping sap
Spears of green light piercing the dark canopy
Bones strewn beneath every hollow and cave
A deer carcass draped over a branch, picked clean
Glowing eyes watching from the undergrowth
Ferns taller than a man, bent by passing bodies
Trees marked with territorial scratches, urine and tufts of fur
sounds: Howls answering each other from every direction
Heavy breathing and growls from the branches overhead
Birdsong that cuts off all at once
The crack of bones being split by powerful jaws
Something heavy crashing through the undergrowth
A distant roar that shakes leaves from the trees
rooms: A fern glade at the forest's edge, the undergrowth so tall that visibility drops to 10 feet.
An owlbear den in a hollow beneath the roots of a giant oak, littered with bones and feathers.
A dire wolf pack's clearing, a ring of flattened grass around a boulder marked with scratches, where the pack's young play with skulls.
A river crossing where giant crocodiles lie in wait beneath the surface, and the only bridge is a fallen tree.
A spider thicket of webs strung between trees, each web strong as rope and glistening with dew and dead birds.
A tree canopy walkway, a network of thick branches high above the forest floor, home to giant apes who guard their territory.
A cave mouth in a cliff face, the lair of a great bear whose roars echo through the forest.
A hunting ground meadow, the only open space in the forest, where predators come to stalk the herds of giant elk.
A carrion pit, a hollow where carcasses are dragged to rot, buzzing with flies and patrolled by scavenger beasts.
A druid's ruined circle of standing stones, overgrown with ivy, where the forest's power is strongest.
A burned clearing where a lightning strike started a fire, and the scorched trunks are home to fire beetles.

The heart, the oldest tree at the forest's centre, where the spirit of the hunt has taken the form of a great beast of antlers, claws and fangs, the alpha of every predator in the forest, waiting at the roots of the tree to test the party.
features: The druid's standing stones; a creature that touches one and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Nature) check gains the ability to speak with animals for 1 hour.
Scent masking with crushed ferns and mud; a creature that coats itself with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check gains advantage on Stealth checks against beasts for 1 hour.
The canopy walkway; a creature that climbs it with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check can travel across the forest without touching the ground, avoiding the dire wolves and crocodiles.
Hunting the giant elk in the meadow; a creature that succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check tracks and kills one, providing food for a week and a hide worth 50 spirit coins.

The owlbear's den; a creature that searches the bones with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the gear of a lost adventurer, including a bloodstained purse of spirit coins and an owlbear's monster core.
Taming a beast; a creature that succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check befriends a young dire wolf or giant ape, which fights alongside the party until the heart.
The fallen tree bridge; cutting it with a DC {dc} Strength check drops it into the river, crushing any crocodiles below for {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
hazards: Ambush predators; each hour in the forest, roll a d6, and on a 1 or 2 a beast ambushes the party, attacking with surprise unless a creature succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check.
The spider thicket's webs; a creature that walks into one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is restrained until it breaks free with a DC {dc} Strength check.
Blood frenzy; a creature that is wounded and bleeding draws predators, and each beast within 60 feet gains advantage on attacks against it.
The river crossing; a creature that falls in makes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check to swim to shore, and crocodiles attack for {dmg} piercing damage each round.
Getting lost; each hour the party travels without a guide, a creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check or the party wanders in a circle.
The great bear's roar; each creature within 120 feet makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is frightened for 1 minute.

environments.name: Vault of Sleeping Titans
environments.summary: Before the first cities, a conclave of celestial wardens lulled seven world-shaking titans to sleep and sealed them deep in the earth, binding each one to a rune-cradle that drinks its dreams to keep the slumber unbroken. The astral space is that sealed vault, a cavern so vast its far walls vanish in haze, where basalt-and-bronze construct wardens tend the runes with the patience of glaciers. The vault wants only quiet and continuance, and it treats every footstep, spell and spirit coin carried in as a threat to the sleep it was built to guard.
readAloud: The ground under your boots is warm and rises and falls by a finger's width, slow as a tide. You stand on a ledge above a cavern so wide its walls fade into blue haze, and below lies a sleeping figure the size of a hill, its chest heaving beneath a blanket of moss and runes that glow amber with each breath. Every exhale stirs a wind that smells of stone and summer rain.

Your arrival rings like a struck bell, and the echo rolls away for a long time. Down a stair cut for feet four times the size of yours, a construct of basalt and green bronze turns its featureless head toward you, a single rune flaring white on its brow. It lifts one hand, palm out, and from somewhere in the depths a deep voice mumbles in its sleep, and the whole cavern trembles.

Dust drifts down from the ceiling in slow sheets, glittering where light catches it. Seven great cradles of carved stone are arranged in a ring around a pillar of runes, and in each lies a titan, one wreathed in frozen lightning, one in roots, one in chains of gold. Between them, tiny by comparison, the bones of earlier treasure-seekers lie scattered where the wardens left them.
sights: A sleeping titan the size of a hill, its chest rising like a tide
Runes in the cradle stones that pulse amber with every breath
Basalt-and-bronze wardens moving with slow, terrible precision
Stairs cut for giants, each step a climb of five feet
A titan wreathed in frozen lightning that crackles when approached
Moss and lichen grown thick across a sleeping titan's beard
Bones of earlier intruders, crushed flat and arranged in neat rows
A central pillar of runes stretching up into darkness
sounds: Slow, thunderous breathing that shakes dust from the walls
A titan mumbling in its sleep in a language older than speech
The grind of stone joints as wardens patrol
A low hum from the runes, rising and falling with the breaths
Distant rumbling as a titan shifts in its dreams
The tinkle of falling dust and pebbles
smells: Burnt metal and old blood near the bones
rooms: An entry ledge above the great cavern, looking down on the first sleeping titan beneath a blanket of moss.
A giant's stair, a staircase cut for titans, each step five feet high and patrolled by wardens.
A warden foundry where new constructs are assembled from basalt and bronze by smaller automata.
The cradle of the lightning titan, where frozen bolts hang in the air and any metal draws a spark.
The cradle of the root titan, where its beard has grown into a forest and beasts nest in the branches.
The cradle of the chained titan, bound in golden chains whose links are each the size of a wagon wheel.
A dream chamber where the titans' dreams leak out as mist and take the shape of ancient wars and lost cities.
A celestial archive, a hall of crystal tablets recording the titans' names, deeds and the terms of their sleep.
A bone corridor where intruders' remains are laid in neat rows, their gear still lying beside them.
A rune well, a deep shaft where the vault's binding magic pools in glowing liquid light.
A collapsed cradle, where one titan has already woken and left, its empty bed cracked and scorched.
The heart, the ring of seven cradles around the central rune pillar, where the Prime Warden, a colossal construct of gold and celestial fire, stands guard, and one titan has begun to stir.
features: The celestial archive's crystal tablets; a creature that warms one in its palms and succeeds on a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check reads a titan's true name aloud, and if that titan wakes it must spend its first turn answering to the name instead of attacking.

The rune well's liquid light; scooping a handful and drinking it grants temporary hit points equal to {dmg}, but the drinker makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or sinks into a titan's dream and falls unconscious for 1 minute, waking with one useful memory of the vault's layout.

The bone corridor's neat rows of gear; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check turns up a rusted greaves-case stuffed with spirit coins and a Silver-rank monster core, while a failure means a warden notices the rows have been disturbed and comes to straighten them.

A dimmed rune on the central pillar; a creature that retraces it with chalk, blood or a spell slot and a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check soothes the stirring titan, so it stays asleep through the fight in the heart and the Prime Warden loses its lair actions.

The foundry's half-built warden; a creature that slots a monster core into its empty chest and succeeds on a DC {dc} Intelligence check with tinker's tools wakes a loyal basalt guardian that follows the party until it is destroyed or leaves the vault.

A cracked link in the golden chains; chipping it free with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check yields a lump of celestial gold worth 200 spirit coins, but the chained titan's eyes open for one round, and every creature that meets them is stunned until the end of its next turn unless it succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom save.

The collapsed cradle's scorched lining; a creature that lies down in the empty bed for 10 minutes and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check absorbs a sliver of titan strength, gaining advantage on Strength checks and saves for 24 hours and a voice in its head that mutters about mountains.
hazards: Noise in the great cavern; any sound louder than speech makes each sleeping titan roll a d20, and on a 1 it rolls over, sending a tremor through the floor so every creature makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is knocked prone and takes {half} bludgeoning damage from falling stone.

The lightning titan's frozen bolts; a creature carrying more than a dagger's worth of metal within 20 feet of the cradle makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save at the start of its turn, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success, and metal armour gives disadvantage on the save.

Warden patrols on the giant's stair; a creature spotted climbing must pass a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check, pretending to be a caretaker, or a warden slams its fist down for {dmg} bludgeoning damage and tries to carry the intruder to the bone corridor.

Dream mist drifting from the dream chamber; a creature that breathes it makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed by a titan's memory of an ancient war, attacking the nearest creature it thinks is an enemy soldier until it succeeds on the save at the end of a later turn.

A titan's rising chest; a creature standing on a sleeping titan makes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check with each great exhale or is flung 20 feet through the air, taking {half} bludgeoning damage when it lands.

The waking roar; if any titan fully wakes, its first bellow shakes the entire vault, and each creature within 300 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage and being deafened for 1 hour on a failure, or half damage and no deafness on a success.

environments.name: Garden of Hungry Plants
environments.summary: A disgraced herbalist of the Magic Society named Thessaly Moor fled to this astral space with a satchel of carnivorous seeds, and fed her beds with the corpses of monsters until the plants grew clever enough to want more. The garden spread into terraces, greenhouses and hedge mazes of beautiful flowering horrors, all of them knitted together by a single root system that thinks as one. Thessaly is long gone, swallowed by her own creations, and the garden wants fresh blood to keep blooming.
readAloud: The scent hits you like a wave: roses, lilies and honeysuckle so thick and sweet it makes your head swim. Before you stretches a garden of impossible beauty, terraces of flowers in every colour climbing toward a glass dome, and at their centre a fountain of red water. As you watch, a butterfly lands on a crimson blossom, and the petals snap shut around it with a wet crunch.

The portal leaves you beside a hedge wall of glossy green leaves, each leaf edged with tiny barbed hooks. A path of white gravel winds between flower beds where pitcher plants the size of rain barrels gurgle softly. In the nearest one, half-dissolved in pale fluid, floats the leather boot of a previous visitor, and the plant's lid creaks open slowly, as if inviting you closer.

Warm, humid air clings to your skin, heavy with pollen that glitters gold in the light. Vines as thick as your wrist hang from the trellises, and their tips swivel to follow your movements like the heads of snakes. A rose bush leans toward you and opens its blooms one by one, and each blossom has a ring of tiny, glistening teeth.
sights: Flytraps the size of carriages, their spines glistening
Vines that swivel to follow movement like snakes
Roses with rings of tiny teeth inside their petals
Pitcher plants the size of rain barrels, filled with bones
A fountain flowing with red water that smells of iron
Golden pollen glittering in the air like dust
A glass dome overhead, its panes fogged with steam
A gardener's straw hat caught in a hedge, its owner nowhere
sounds: The wet snap of flytraps closing
Leaves rustling with no wind
A soft gurgle from pitcher plants digesting
Bees buzzing in the flowers, louder than they should be
The creak of vines tightening around something
A low, contented hum from the roots underground
smells: Roses, lilies and honeysuckle, cloyingly sweet
Iron and blood from the fountain
Pollen so thick it tickles the throat
rooms: An entry terrace of flowers in every colour, beautiful and sweet, where the first flytraps lie in wait.
A rose garden of carnivorous roses with teeth, whose thorns drip a sleep poison.
A greenhouse where pitcher plants the size of barrels digest the remains of previous visitors.
A hedge maze of barbed hooks that shifts its walls when no one is watching.
A flytrap field where giant flytraps lie half-hidden in tall grass, their jaws ready to snap.
A vine trellis walk where hanging vines reach down to grab and strangle passersby.
A potting shed where Thessaly's tools still lie, and a journal on the bench describes her experiments.
A seed vault where jars of seeds glow faintly, each one a different carnivorous species.
A blood fountain courtyard, where the red water nourishes the garden and draws creatures to drink.
A compost heap where the remains of monsters rot into soil, and grubs and beetles feed.
A pollen grove where golden pollen fills the air, and creatures who breathe it see visions.
The heart, the garden's centre beneath the glass dome, where the mother plant, a great bloom with a mouth like a pit, rises from a tangle of roots, and Thessaly's body is fused into its stem.
features: Thessaly's potting journal; a creature that reads it and succeeds on a DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature) check learns the plants recoil from salt, and a handful of salt thrown at a plant creature deals {half} necrotic damage and makes it drop anything it is grappling.

The glowing seed vault; a creature that pockets a jar gains a carnivorous seed worth 100 spirit coins to the Magic Society, but if the jar ever touches blood the seed sprouts within a round and attacks its carrier as a vine with +5 to hit and {half} piercing damage.

The blood fountain; drinking a cupful restores {dmg} hit points, but the drinker makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or its scent is marked by the garden, and every plant creature targets it first for 24 hours.
Thessaly's pruning shears, hung on a nail in the potting shed; a creature wielding them deals an extra {half} slashing damage to plants and can cut free a grappled ally as a bonus action.

The compost heap's rich black soil; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check while digging turns up a monster core and an awakening stone wrapped in a rotting glove, but on a failure the digger disturbs a nest of flesh beetles and takes {half} piercing damage.

A watering can of weedkiller on the shed shelf; pouring it on the mother plant's roots before the fight in the heart reduces its hit point maximum by {dmg}, but the garden screams and every plant within 120 feet wakes.

A brass bell on the shed door; ringing it is the old feeding signal, and every plant in the garden turns toward the sound for 1 minute, giving the party advantage on Stealth checks to slip past anything that is not the bell-ringer.
hazards: Hidden flytraps in the tall grass; a creature that steps on one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is swallowed whole, restrained and taking {dmg} acid damage at the start of each of its turns until it or an ally deals 15 damage to the trap's jaws.

Sleep-poison thorns on the toothed roses; a creature scratched by them makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or falls unconscious for 1 minute, waking if it takes damage, which the roses are happy to provide.

Strangling vines over the trellis walk; a creature passing beneath makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is hoisted 10 feet off the ground and grappled, taking {half} bludgeoning damage at the start of each turn until it escapes with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check.

The hedge maze's barbed hooks; a creature that brushes a wall takes {half} piercing damage and is snagged until it spends an action tearing free, and each time the party turns a corner the walls shift so that a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check is needed to keep its bearings.

Golden pollen hanging in the air; a creature that breathes it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is confused for 1 minute as the flowers seem to sing to it, with a fresh save at the end of each of its turns.

The mother plant's root eruption; once per round in the heart, roots burst through the soil in a 30-foot radius, and each creature there makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage and being restrained on a failure, or half damage on a success.

environments.name: Tidal Cave
