environments.summary: A water elemental lord, the Tide-Mother, was dragged into this cave long ago by a storm-mage who meant to bind her into a ship's hull, and her fury tore the cave loose from the world and set it breathing in time with her rage. The astral space floods and drains on a cycle of minutes, its tunnels alternately dry and thundering with surf, and the treasures of a hundred wrecks wash in with each tide. It wants to drown the last of the storm-mage's line, and it tests every visitor to see whether they share his blood.
readAloud: Wet rock gleams under your feet, slick with weed and crusted with barnacles. The cave around you is a cathedral of dripping stone, its walls streaked with salt, and from somewhere ahead comes the deep, rhythmic boom of surf. As you watch, a trickle of seawater runs past your boots and then, faster than you would believe, the trickle becomes a stream.

The portal spits you onto a beach of black sand inside a vast sea cave, where the water has just drained away to reveal rock pools full of glittering fish and the ribs of a broken ship. Crabs the size of shields scuttle across the sand. A rumble echoes from the cave mouth, growing louder, and the water in the pools begins to tremble.

Salt spray stings your eyes and the air hums with the roar of the sea. The tunnel before you is half full of churning water that rises and falls with the breathing of the cave, and in the depths something glows blue and pulses like a heart. A voice like waves on stone rumbles through the rock: 'Swim, little ones. Swim, or drown.'
sights: Walls streaked with salt and crusted with barnacles
Rock pools glittering with fish when the tide drains
Ribs of broken ships jutting from the black sand
Crabs the size of shields scuttling across the beach
Churning water rising and falling with the cave's breathing
A blue glow pulsing in the depths like a heart
Treasure chests wedged in cracks, crusted with coral
Eels as long as boats slipping through flooded tunnels
sounds: The deep, rhythmic boom of surf
Water rushing in and draining out on a fast cycle
Crabs clicking and scuttling across rock
A voice like waves on stone rumbling through the cave
The groan of shipwreck timbers shifting
Gulls crying from somewhere above
smells: Rotting fish in the rock pools
Tar and old rope from the wrecks
rooms: A black sand beach inside the cave mouth, littered with shipwreck debris and crabs, where the tide comes in fastest.
A rock pool shelf where fish and anemones glitter in pools that refill every few minutes.
A shipwreck grotto, where the hull of a broken galleon lies wedged in the rock, its hold full of treasure.
A blowhole chamber where water shoots up through a hole in the floor with every wave, hard enough to launch a creature into the ceiling.
An eel tunnel, a flooded passage where giant eels lurk in cracks.
A barnacle cliff, a sheer wall of barnacles that must be climbed between tides.
A drowned shrine where sailors once prayed to a god of the sea, its altar covered in offerings of coins and coral.
A whirlpool chamber where the water spins in a vortex, pulling everything toward a drain at its centre.
A crab nest of giant crabs that guard a pile of glittering pearls.
A dry chamber above the high tide line, where two Bronze-rank salvagers from the Delta cling to a ledge, waving a torn shirt.
A sea-glass gallery where the walls are lined with polished glass that glows with trapped light.

The heart, the elemental's lair at the bottom of the cave, where the Tide-Mother rises from a pool of glowing blue water, her body a towering wave crowned with coral, surrounded by the bones of the storm-mage.
features: The tide's rhythm; every 10 minutes the cave floods for 5, and a creature that watches one full cycle and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check can call the next surge, giving the party advantage on every save against the water until they leave.

The galleon's hold, reachable only at low tide; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check among the barnacled crates finds a lockbox of spirit coins and a sea-aspected monster core, but searching for more than 3 minutes risks being caught when the water returns.

The blowhole; a creature that stands over it and braces at the crest of a wave is shot 30 feet up to a hidden ledge, where a drowned captain's sea chest holds a cloak that grants a swim speed equal to the wearer's walking speed.

The drowned shrine's altar; a creature that lays a coin among the coral offerings and speaks a sailor's prayer can breathe water for 1 hour, but one that takes coins from the altar has disadvantage on all saves against the tide until it returns them.

The giant crab nest's pearls; slipping a handful free with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Stealth) check gains pearls worth 200 spirit coins, and a failure brings two shield-sized crabs scuttling out, each snapping for {half} bludgeoning damage.

Two Bronze-rank salvagers stranded on a high ledge; hauling them down with a rope and a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check earns a tide chart scratched into a slate, which reveals the dry route to the heart.

The storm-mage's bones in the heart; a creature that gathers them and casts them into the glowing pool with a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check, pleading with the Tide-Mother, ends her rage and the fight, and she leaves a gift of sea-glass worth 300 spirit coins.
hazards: A flooding tunnel; a creature caught when the surge arrives makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is swept 30 feet along the passage, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage against the rocks on a failure or half as much on a success.

The whirlpool chamber; a creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the vortex makes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check or is dragged 10 feet closer, and a creature that reaches the centre takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is pulled under, beginning to drown.

High tide in a sealed chamber; once the water reaches the ceiling, a creature holding its breath makes a DC {dc} Constitution save at the end of each minute or begins to suffocate, dropping to 0 hit points at the end of its next turn.

The barnacle cliff; a creature climbing between tides takes {half} slashing damage from the razor shells each round and must succeed on a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check or fall 20 feet onto the rocks below.

Giant eels coiled in the eel tunnel's cracks; a creature swimming through makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is bitten for {dmg} piercing damage and grappled, dragged into a crack where it is restrained and cannot breathe.

A blowhole erupting without warning; a creature standing within 10 feet of it during a wave makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is launched into the ceiling, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and landing prone 15 feet away.

environments.name: City in the Leviathan's Belly
environments.summary: A sea-leviathan the size of a hill swallowed a fishing fleet, and the mana of its slow digestion folded the wreckage into a ramshackle town built on its stomach floor. The swallowed crews' descendants, pale and web-fingered, worship the beast's heartbeat and feed it outsiders to keep it calm. The leviathan itself wants only to keep eating, and the space grows a new street every time it does.
readAloud: The portal drops you onto a gangplank slick with something warmer than seawater. Ahead, a jumble of shacks built from broken hulls clings to a ribbed, pink floor that rises and falls like a sleeper's chest. Far overhead, a curved ceiling of muscle pulses in time with a thunderous heartbeat you feel in your teeth.

Lantern light glows on wet planks and rope bridges strung between ribs as thick as towers. A tide of thin, sour fluid sloshes through the lower streets, carrying fish bones and the occasional boot. Somewhere in the town a crowd chants a single word over and over, matching each beat of the enormous heart.

Heat and humidity close around you like a wet blanket. The ground gives under your boots, soft and faintly ribbed, and the air tastes of brine and bile. Pale faces watch from the windows of a tavern made from an upturned galley, and every one of them is smiling a little too widely.
sights: Shacks built from split hulls, their figureheads still staring outward
Rope bridges slung between ribs as thick as castle towers
A rippling ceiling of pink muscle beaded with glowing parasites
Pale townsfolk with webbed fingers and milky, lidless eyes
Half-digested ship masts jutting from pools of yellow acid
Lanterns burning rendered whale fat with a greasy orange flame
Barnacle gardens tended in rows along the stomach wall
A great sphincter-gate far above, clenched shut against the sea
sounds: A heartbeat so loud it rattles loose planks
Gurgling acid tides sweeping through the low streets
Townsfolk chanting one word in time with the pulse
The creak of hull timbers flexing as the beast breathes
Distant, muffled whale song booming through the flesh
Wet slaps as fish fall from the gullet above
smells: Rendered blubber smoke from every lantern
Rotting kelp piled in the alleys
Tar and soaked oak from the old ships
A coppery tang wherever the walls are scraped raw
rooms: A landing dock of lashed rowboats bobbing on a shallow pool of stomach fluid, a rusted bell hung to announce new arrivals.
The Galley Tavern, an upturned warship serving fish stew that is suspiciously fresh, with patrons who never leave their stools.
A market lane where townsfolk trade swallowed treasures: compasses, wedding rings, an entire crate of soaked spirit coins.
The Rib Chapel, carved into a single vast rib bone, where worshippers press their ears to the walls to hear the god-heart speak.
An acid canal crossed by a single swaying plank, with skeletal fish circling beneath.
A barnacle farm where colonies are grown on hull plates and harvested with long hooked knives.
A nursery of slime, where translucent oozes are raised in tubs and fed scraps to keep the stomach clean.
A drowned shipyard deep in the second stomach, where swallowed vessels sink slowly into a glowing pool.
The Throat Ward, a tilted district built up the inside of the gullet, reached by ropes and treacherous handholds.
A blowhole chamber where geysers of air vent upward every few minutes, flinging loose objects toward the sealed gate.
The Harbour Master's hall, a captain's cabin preserved perfectly, logbooks recording every person fed to the beast.
The heart, a cavern of drumming crimson muscle where the town's high priestess stands on a pulsing valve, conducting the beat with a harpoon.
features: Ribs studded with old harpoons can be climbed like ladders; a creature using them climbs at full speed and gains advantage on Athletics checks to stay put during a surge.
A row of rowboats can be dragged into the acid canals; a boat survives 3 rounds of acid before dissolving, carrying up to three Medium creatures across safely.
The god-heart's pulse can be read by pressing an ear to the wall; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check predicts the next surge one round in advance, granting advantage on the save.
Glowing parasites on the ceiling can be scraped into a jar; they shed dim light in a 10-foot radius for 8 hours and repel oozes, which will not willingly enter that light.
A swallowed treasure chest sits half sunk in the second stomach; reaching it requires a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, and it holds spirit coins and one random magic trinket.
The townsfolk will trade information for fresh food from outside; a meal shared earns a whispered route to the heart that avoids the Throat Ward.
A great tooth lodged in the gullet can be pried loose with a DC {dc} Strength check; used as a weapon, it deals an extra 1d6 piercing damage to the leviathan's servants.
hazards: An acid tide sweeps the low streets every 10 minutes; each creature caught in it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} acid damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
When the leviathan swallows, the floor heaves; each creature makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls prone and slides 15 feet toward the nearest acid pool.
The stale air of the lower stomach is thick with digestive gas; a creature that breathes it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour.
Rotten planks over the second stomach give way under more than 200 pounds; a DC {dc} Dexterity save avoids a 20-foot fall into fluid that deals {half} acid damage.
The heart's beat accelerates during the boss fight; at the start of each round, every creature in the chamber makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is deafened and takes {half} thunder damage.
Swarms of digesting eels writhe in the drowned shipyard; a creature that enters the water takes {half} piercing damage at the start of each of its turns until it leaves.

environments.name: Petrified Forest of Stilled Hours
environments.summary: An ancient wood was turned to stone in a single instant when a basilisk matriarch of impossible size opened her eyes, and the astral space formed around that frozen moment. Everything that lived in the forest is still here as stone, from squirrels mid-leap to birds mid-flight, and the matriarch's brood hunts among them. The space wants more statues, and its gravel paths slowly gather toward anything that still moves.
readAloud: Grey trees rise around you, every leaf carved from stone so thin that light glows through it. A stone deer stands in the clearing ahead, head turned toward you, one hoof raised. The silence is absolute until a pebble clicks against a trunk somewhere to your left, and then another, closer.

You step out onto a path of crushed granite that crunches like bones underfoot. Branches overhead hold birds frozen mid-wingbeat, their stone beaks open on songs that never finished. A faint grinding sound comes from deep in the woods, steady and patient, like a millstone turning.

Dust hangs in the air in still, glittering sheets. The trunks around you are grey and banded with the rings of trees that lived for a thousand years, now split and sparkling with quartz where the bark has cracked away. Something has scratched long, deliberate grooves into the nearest tree, at about the height of your throat.
sights: Stone leaves so thin they glow when light passes through them
Birds frozen mid-flight on branches, wings spread
A fox turned to stone in the middle of a pounce
Trunks split open to show glittering bands of agate and quartz
Long claw grooves gouged into the stone bark
A frozen waterfall of grey mineral spilling over a ledge
Fallen stone acorns piled in drifts like gravel
A traveler's statue with a look of horror, still clutching a mirror
sounds: Absolute silence broken by the click of falling pebbles
A slow grinding, like a millstone, from deep in the woods
Stone leaves chiming against each other in a sudden draft
The crunch of crushed granite under every step
A heavy, scraping breath from behind a thicket
The crack of a stone branch giving way and shattering
smells: A faint memory of pine resin, impossibly
Damp earth from cracks beneath the roots
The musky reek of a reptile den
rooms: An entry glade where the portal stands between two stone oaks whose branches have fused into an arch.
A meadow of stone wildflowers, every petal sharp enough to cut through boots.
A frozen stream where stone fish hang in mid-leap above a bed of polished pebbles.
A hunters' camp turned to stone, a ring of statues sitting around a fire whose flames are now orange jasper.
A hollow tree big enough to house a family, its interior coated in crystal and lined with gnawed stone bones.
A ravine choked with fallen petrified trunks forming a natural bridge that groans when crossed.
A brood nest of shed basilisk skins and cracked eggs, each egg the size of a barrel.
A grove of half-stone trees, green at the tips and grey at the roots, the petrification still creeping upward.
A gallery of victims arranged deliberately in rows, as if someone has been collecting them.
A sinkhole where the stone forest has collapsed into a glittering cave of geodes and roots.
A mirror pond, still and silver, where the brood will not go and where reflections move a moment late.
The heart, a crater of shattered stone where the basilisk matriarch lies coiled around the oldest tree, her eyes hooded and slowly opening.
features: The mirror pond reflects true sight; a creature that watches enemies only through a polished surface gains advantage on saves against petrifying gazes but has disadvantage on attack rolls.
Statues of earlier victims carry gear; searching one takes a minute and has a 1 in 4 chance of finding a stone-locked item that a DC {dc} Arcana check can restore to flesh and steel.
Half-stone trees still hold sap; drinking a vial grants advantage on the next Constitution save against petrification, but the drinker's skin turns grey for a day.
Stone leaves can be snapped off and thrown as improvised daggers that shatter on impact, dealing 1d6 slashing damage to everything in a 5-foot radius.
A frozen waterfall can be shattered with 30 damage, opening a shortcut to the brood nest and sending a wave of gravel over anyone below.
Shed basilisk skins can be worn as a cloak; a creature wearing one is ignored by the brood for 10 minutes unless it attacks.
The hunters' camp holds a stone horn; blowing it with a DC {dc} Constitution check makes every brood creature within a mile move toward the camp for 1d4 rounds.
hazards: Petrifying dust drifts through the oldest groves; a creature that breathes it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is restrained as its limbs stiffen, becoming petrified if it fails again next turn.
Stone wildflowers slash at anyone who crosses the meadow without care; a creature moving faster than half speed takes {half} slashing damage.
A petrified trunk falls with a thunderous crack; creatures in a 30-foot line make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Gravel paths drift toward moving creatures while they rest; after a short rest, each creature makes a DC {dc} Strength save or wakes half-buried and restrained until freed.
The matriarch's gaze sweeps the heart each round; any creature that can see her eyes makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} force damage as its flesh cracks and greys.
The geode sinkhole floor is honeycombed and fragile; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check spots the weak points, and a failure drops a creature 20 feet onto crystal for {half} piercing damage.

environments.name: Herd-World on the Wandering Beast
environments.summary: A colossal grazing beast walks forever across an endless astral plain, and an entire grassland ecosystem lives on its shaggy back. Hill giant herders ride smaller beasts across its fur-prairie, following seasons that change with each of the giant creature's strides. The space was born from the mana of countless migrations, and it wants to keep moving, shaking off anything that tries to make it stop.
readAloud: Wind whips grass around your knees, and the whole horizon lurches as the ground beneath you takes a step. You stand on a rolling prairie of coarse fur, each hair as thick as a sapling, stretching away to a ridge of spine like a mountain range. Below the edge, far down, an endless plain scrolls past in a blur of dust.

The ground rises and falls in a long, slow rhythm, and each heave sends a herd of shaggy antelope bounding to stay upright. Smoke drifts from a ring of hide tents nestled in the hollow between two enormous shoulder blades. A horn sounds from the tents, deep and long, and a dozen tall riders swing onto their mounts.

Dust and musk hit you first, then the thunder. Each footfall of the beast beneath you shakes the world like a drum, and the grass flattens in waves with every step. Ticks the size of wagons crawl slowly between the fur-trees, and birds as large as horses pick at them with long, cruel beaks.
sights: Fur stalks as thick as saplings bending in the wind
A spine ridge rising like a jagged mountain range
Wagon-sized ticks lumbering between fur groves
Giant herders riding shaggy aurochs at full gallop
A dust-blurred plain racing past far below the flanks
Hide tents painted with handprints in red ochre
Oxpecker birds the size of horses stalking through the grass
Distant, swinging horns large enough to cast shadows over villages
sounds: The drum of each colossal footfall shaking the ground
Long, mournful lowing from the beast itself
Herding horns calling across the fur prairie
Wind roaring through the coarse grass
The rasping click of giant ticks feeding
Hooves thundering as a stampede turns
smells: Dung fires smoldering in the giant camp
Old blood where ticks have fed
rooms: A landing hollow on the beast's haunch, a bowl of matted fur where the portal flickers between two scars.
The tail prairie, a long sweeping strip of grassland that whips side to side, carrying the ground with it.
A tick ranch where giants tether bloated parasites and tap them like barrels for their blood.
The herders' camp, a ring of tents between the shoulder blades with a fire pit made from a single cracked hoof.
A scar canyon, an old wound that healed into a deep ravine with clear water pooling at the bottom.
The spine ridge, a bony crest of vertebrae where winds are strongest and eagles nest in the hollows.
A flea warren, a maze of burrows in the matted fur where dog-sized fleas swarm and spring.
The horn base, a cliff of keratin rising into the sky, carved with the names of herders who climbed it.
An ear canyon, a vast cavern of fur and wax that rumbles with every sound the beast hears.
A mudwallow on the flank, a churned bog of dried mud plates that crack and slide as the beast walks.
The eye ledge, where a single moist eye the size of a lake looks out across the plain and blinks every few minutes.
The heart, a hollow at the base of the skull where the herd-king giant rides a war-aurochs in a ring of trampled earth, guarding the beast's crown-wound.
features: Herd antelope can be lassoed with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check and ridden; a mount doubles speed across the prairie and ignores the stride hazard.
Fur stalks can be braided into climbing ropes in 10 minutes; a braided rope grants advantage on checks to climb the spine and horn.
Tick blood barrels can be tapped for a thick, iron-rich drink; a creature that drinks a cup regains {half} hit points but is sluggish, losing 10 feet of speed for an hour.
The herders will host guests who win a wrestling match; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) contest earns food, a rest in their camp, and a guide to the skull.
The beast's ear hears every shout; a creature who bellows into the ear canyon with a DC {dc} Charisma (Intimidation) check makes the beast flinch, knocking every creature on the back prone.
Mud plates from the wallow can be pried up as shields that grant +1 AC until they break after absorbing one hit.
The horn base holds an eagle aerie; stealing an egg with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Stealth) check yields a monster core but brings the mother eagle down in 1d4 rounds.
hazards: Every minute the beast takes a stride; each creature not braced makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls prone and slides 10 feet downslope.
A stampede of antelope sweeps the prairie; creatures in a 40-foot-wide path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The beast shakes itself like a wet dog once per hour; every creature on the flanks makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is flung 30 feet and takes {half} bludgeoning damage.

The tail prairie whips violently in the fight with a predator; a creature standing on it makes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check each round or is thrown off the edge and must catch fur to avoid a lethal fall.
Fleas spring from the warren in swarms; a creature that enters makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or contracts flea fever, gaining a level of exhaustion each dawn until cured.
The eye blinks without warning; any creature on the eye ledge makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is struck by the lid for {dmg} bludgeoning damage and knocked into the tear lake.

environments.name: Aurora Fields
environments.summary: A frozen tundra lies beneath a sky where curtains of aurora hang so low they brush the snow, and the light itself has weight, colour and hunger. The space formed where a celestial choir once rehearsed a hymn that was never finished, and the aurora is that song made visible. It wants the hymn completed, and it pulls voices out of anyone who walks beneath it to try.
readAloud: You step onto crisp snow beneath a night sky blazing with ribbons of green and violet light. The curtains hang so low that one drifts across the field ahead, close enough to touch, and where it passes the snow hums and glitters. Your breath fogs, and the fog glows faintly, as if the light has already found its way inside you.

The tundra stretches flat and white to every horizon, lit by a sky that ripples like silk in a slow wind. Tall, thin figures walk inside the curtains of light, visible only as darker shapes in the glow. A single long note hangs over everything, so pure and sustained that your ears begin to ache.

Cold bites your face, but the light pouring from above feels warm on your skin. Patches of snow have melted into perfect circles where the aurora touched down, and in each circle a single crystal flower grows. Somewhere out across the field, someone is singing, and the sky bends toward the sound.
sights: Aurora curtains hanging low enough to brush the snow
Crystal flowers growing in circles of melted snow
Tall, thin figures walking within the bands of light
Breath that glows faintly green as it leaves the lips
Snow drifts shot through with veins of violet light
A frozen lake reflecting the sky so perfectly it seems a hole
Ice spires humming visibly, rimed with light like frost
Shadows cast in three colours at once
sounds: One endless, pure note sustained across the sky
Snow crunching and chiming underfoot
Wind threading through ice spires like a flute
Whispered harmonies that seem to come from inside the head
The crackle of light touching the ground
Far-off voices singing the same unfinished phrase
smells: Something sweet like burnt sugar where the light touches
A faint metallic tang on the tongue
rooms: An arrival drift, a snow bowl where the portal shimmers in the colours of the sky above.
A field of crystal flowers, each one ringing a different note when the wind moves through it.
The singing lake, frozen solid and so clear that the stars beneath the ice seem to be another sky.
A circle of ice spires arranged like a choir, each one taller than a house and shaped like a robed figure.
A rift in the snow where aurora light has pooled into a liquid, slow glowing river.
An abandoned expedition tent, frozen stiff, holding journals of an adventuring team who tried to finish the song.
A fey hunting ground where winter sprites skate across ice and trap travelers in games of riddles.
A ridge of wind-sculpted snow shaped into an enormous ear facing the sky.
A hollow beneath the ice where lost voices are stored as glowing bubbles frozen in the floor.
The conductor's stand, a plinth of light-hardened snow with an empty music sheet of frost upon it.
A storm wall where wind elementals hurl sheets of glittering snow in endless circles.
The heart, a dome of aurora light gathered into a single blazing column, where the choir's last voice waits in a body of living colour.
features: Crystal flowers can be plucked and played; a bard or creature with musical proficiency who plays three in sequence calms the light, granting the party advantage on saves against the aurora for 1 hour.
Liquid aurora from the rift can be bottled; drinking it heals {half} hit points but the drinker glows brightly for an hour, granting disadvantage on Stealth checks.
The expedition journals record half the unfinished hymn; a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) or Performance check pieces it together, which matters at the heart.
Frozen voice bubbles can be cracked to release a stored voice; a creature that has lost its voice to the aurora regains it, and the bubble may contain a secret spoken by a previous victim.
The ice spire choir resonates with spells; a creature casting a spell while touching a spire gains +1 to its spell save DC but takes 1d6 cold damage.
The winter sprites will trade passage for a riddle they cannot answer; a DC {dc} Intelligence check invents one, and they lead the party safely through the storm wall.
Completing the hymn at the conductor's stand with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check stuns the heart's guardian for 1 round when the fight begins.
hazards: A low curtain of aurora sweeps across the field; each creature in its path makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or loses its voice for 1 hour, unable to speak or cast spells with verbal components.
The light burns in its brightest bands; a creature that touches a curtain takes {dmg} radiant damage, or {half} on a successful DC {dc} Constitution save.
Extreme cold settles during each hour of travel; a creature without cold protection makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
Thin ice over the singing lake cracks under weight; a DC {dc} Dexterity save avoids plunging into frigid water that deals {half} cold damage each round.
The endless note grows unbearable near the choir spires; each creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save at the start of its turn or is charmed and walks toward the nearest curtain.

In the heart, the column of light flares every third round; creatures within 20 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage and being blinded on a failure, or {half} damage on a success.

environments.name: Thornwall Rose Maze
environments.summary: A jealous fey noble grew a hedge maze of roses to imprison a rival's heart, and when the rival died inside, the roses drank the grief and became an astral space. The walls are living thorns three stories high, the blooms open only when fed blood, and the fey court that tends them still plays at courtly romance among the hedges. The maze wants to be admired and to bleed its visitors, and it rewards flattery as much as it punishes trespass.
readAloud: Walls of dark green thorns rise thirty feet on either side of a narrow gravel path, studded with roses so deep a red they look black in the dimness. The perfume is overwhelming, heavy and sweet enough to make your eyes water. Somewhere ahead, a woman laughs, and the hedges shiver as though they heard it too.

A courtyard of white gravel opens before you, ringed by hedges carved into the shapes of dancing couples. Every rose in sight is tightly closed, but as you step forward, the one nearest your hand slowly unfurls, its petals glistening wet. A small fey figure in a waistcoat of leaves bows to you from a stone bench and asks whether you have come courting.

Thorns scratch at your sleeves as the portal closes behind you, leaving a dead end of tangled briar. Petals drift down like slow rain, staining the gravel where they land. In the silence you hear the faint, wet sound of roots drinking, and the path behind you is no longer where it was.
sights: Hedge walls thirty feet tall, thick with thorns as long as fingers
Roses so dark red they look black until they open
Topiary couples frozen mid-dance at every crossing
Petals that leave red stains on whatever they touch
Tiny fey courtiers in waistcoats of leaves and petals
Shed garments caught on the thorns, some still fine silk
A stone fountain running thick with rose-coloured water
Rosehips swollen fat and pulsing like small hearts
sounds: Laughter echoing from somewhere deeper in the maze
The soft, wet slurp of roots drinking
Hedges rustling as passages shift
A string quartet playing a waltz that never ends
Fey courtiers gossiping just beyond the next wall
Thorns creaking as they slowly lengthen
smells: The green bite of cut stems
A faint, sad scent of old letters and pressed flowers
rooms: A dead-end entry where the portal glows within a knot of briar that must be cut or squeezed through.
The Courtship Lawn, a circular green where topiary couples turn slowly on their roots in a dance.
A fountain court where rose-tinted water flows from the mouth of a weeping stone maiden.
A gazebo of woven thorns, a tea table set for two with cups that never empty.
The Hall of Suitors, a long corridor lined with skeletons wrapped in briar, each holding a wilted bouquet.
A greenhouse folly with glass panes cracked by roots, sheltering a nursery of seedlings that bleed when cut.
A sunken garden where black roses grow from a pool of thickened red sap.
A hedge cathedral where the walls arch overhead into a vault of thorns and the floor is soft with fallen petals.
The Lovers' Bridge, a span of living vine over a moat of thorns that sways and tightens beneath weight.
A masquerade terrace where fey courtiers dance and demand every guest wear a mask of leaves.
A potting shed where the head gardener, a twisted shrub-man, keeps shears, sap pots and a ledger of the maze's guests.
The heart, a walled rose garden where the fey noble's lost love blooms as a giant rose with a sleeping woman's face, and the noble stands guard with a sword of thorn.
features: Roses open when fed a drop of blood; a creature that spends 1 hit point opens a rose that marks the correct path for the next 100 feet.
Fey courtiers respond to compliments; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check flattering the maze earns a hint, but an insult closes one passage permanently.
The tea cups in the gazebo grant advantage on Charisma checks for 1 hour, but a creature that drinks two must succeed on a DC {dc} Wisdom save or fall into a romantic stupor for 10 minutes.
The head gardener's shears cut through any thorn wall in one action and deal double damage to plant creatures.
The ledger of guests names every creature who entered; reading it with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals the noble's lost love's true name, which can calm her at the heart.
Rosehips can be eaten as quick healing, restoring 1d8 hit points each, but every one eaten makes the thorns grow toward the eater for the next hour.
Masks of leaves from the terrace let a wearer pass as a courtier, granting advantage on Deception checks against the fey for as long as they wear them.
hazards: Thorn walls lash out at anyone who brushes them; a DC {dc} Dexterity save avoids {dmg} piercing damage, or {half} on a success.
Passages shift when no one is looking; after each short rest, the party must make a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check or lose an hour wandering.
Pollen from the black roses is a potent love-drug; a creature that breathes it makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or becomes charmed by the nearest fey for 1 hour.
The Lovers' Bridge tightens around anyone who crosses alone; a DC {dc} Strength save avoids being restrained and dragged toward the thorn moat.
Bleeding seedlings scream when trampled; each scream calls 1d4 thorn creatures to the area within 2 rounds.
At the heart, roots erupt from the soil each round; creatures standing on soil make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} piercing damage as roots drink their blood, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Star-Metal Crater
environments.summary: A falling star struck the world long ago, and the mana released by its impact tore open an astral space shaped like the moment of collision. The crater is ringed by slag cliffs and laced with veins of star-metal, while things from beyond the sky that rode the meteor down still crawl through its shattered heart. The star itself is not dead; it wants to rise again, and it draws in metal and magic to rebuild its burning body.
readAloud: Heat rises from the ground in shimmering waves, and the air smells of struck iron. You stand on the lip of a vast bowl of black glass and fused rock, its slopes laced with silver veins that pulse faintly like blood vessels. At the centre, far below, a pillar of white fire burns without smoke.

The ground crunches like thin ice beneath your boots, a crust of melted sand cooled into glass. Shards of metal stud the slope, some no bigger than coins, others the size of carts, each one humming a different pitch. Something skitters across the slag ahead on too many legs, its shell glinting with starlight.

Your metal gear grows warm the instant you arrive, and the buckles on your pack tug gently toward the centre of the crater. A sky of deep violet hangs overhead, strewn with stars that are far too close and far too bright. Below, iron figures labour slowly, dragging chunks of ore toward a light that hurts to look at.
sights: Slopes of black glass laced with pulsing silver veins
A pillar of white fire burning at the crater's centre
Metal shards jutting from the ground and humming softly
Slag cliffs rippled like frozen waves of molten rock
Iron constructs dragging ore across glassy flats
Stars hanging close enough to see their flickering surfaces
Many-legged things with shells like polished meteorite
Puddles of liquid metal that reflect a different sky
sounds: A deep, throbbing hum from the star at the centre
Glass crust cracking underfoot
Metal shards singing in sympathy with each other
The scrape of heavy ore dragged over stone
Clicking chitter from beneath the slag
Sharp pings as hot metal cools and contracts
smells: Sulfur rising from vents in the slag
A cold, alien scent like snow on metal
rooms: A rim terrace of fused rock where the portal hangs over a sheer drop into the crater.
The glass slope, a treacherous incline of slick black glass where footing is everything.
An ejecta field of scattered boulders flung from the impact, some still glowing red inside.
A star-metal vein exposed in a cliff face, silver ore pulsing like a heartbeat.
A collapsed mining camp where earlier adventurers left picks, tents and a half-written claim notice.
A construct workshop where iron golems hammer star-metal into new limbs for something unseen.
A burrow nest beneath the slag where alien crawlers lay eggs in pockets of molten glass.
A lake of liquid silver, its surface still and mirror-bright, reflecting stars that are not overhead.
A fissure of steam vents where groundwater meets the crater's buried heat.
A crystal shock-ring, a circle of quartz pillars grown from the impact's force, each one charged with magic.
The meteor's shell, a split husk of black stone as big as a temple, hollow and echoing.
The heart, the burning core of the fallen star, a sphere of white fire wrapped in an armature of star-metal that a living star-spirit is trying to reassemble.
features: Star-metal can be chipped from veins with a DC {dc} Strength check; each chunk is worth spirit coins and can be forged into weapons that count as magical.
The quartz shock-ring stores magic; a spellcaster who touches a pillar regains one expended spell slot of 2nd level or lower, then the pillar cracks.
Iron constructs follow a hum pattern; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check mimics it, ordering one construct to stand down for 1 minute.
The silver lake shows a scrying image of any place under the stars when a DC {dc} Wisdom check is made while gazing, though a failure shows the watcher to something in the heavens.
The abandoned mining camp has heat-proof tarps; wrapping in one grants resistance to fire damage from the environment for 1 hour.
Shards that sing at the same pitch attract each other; tossing one near a construct pulls metal shards into it, dealing 2d6 piercing damage.
Steam vents can be blocked with boulders; releasing one at the right moment with a DC {dc} Strength check blasts a creature in a 15-foot cone with {half} fire damage.
hazards: The star pulls on metal; a creature wearing metal armour makes a DC {dc} Strength save each hour or is dragged 30 feet toward the centre and knocked prone.
The glass slope is slick and sharp; a creature moving at more than half speed makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or slides 30 feet, taking {half} slashing damage.
Superheated pockets lurk beneath the slag crust; a creature that breaks through takes {dmg} fire damage, or {half} on a successful DC {dc} Dexterity save.
Radiant pulses wash outward from the heart every 10 minutes; each creature in the crater makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} radiant damage and is poisoned for 1 hour.

Falling stars streak overhead; once per hour, one strikes within 100 feet of the party, and creatures within 20 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Liquid silver from the lake clings like quicksilver; a creature that enters makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned and slowed for 1 hour.

environments.name: Tar Pits of the First Beasts
environments.summary: A primeval bog of bubbling tar swallowed beasts for ten thousand years, and their bones soaked up so much death-mana that the pits became an astral space. Great skeletons of extinct creatures rise from the black ooze and lumber through a land of fern forests and smoke. The tar itself is a slow, hungry ooze that wants to preserve everything forever, and it is patient enough to wait.
readAloud: A thick, choking smell of pitch fills your lungs as the portal closes. Steaming black pools stretch across a valley of giant ferns, their surfaces bulging and bursting in slow, oily bubbles. In the nearest pit, the curved tusk of something enormous breaks the surface, rises a little higher, and then begins to move.

Sunlight comes thin and orange through a haze of smoke. Ancient ferns taller than houses droop over a landscape of black, glistening pools, and the ground squelches with every step. A skeleton the size of a barn stands at the edge of a pit, coated in tar, swaying gently, and its empty eye sockets glow a dull, wet red.

Heat radiates from the ground in waves, and a slow, sucking sound comes from every direction at once. Bones jut from the tar everywhere: ribs, skulls, horns, the claw of a bird taller than a giant. As you watch, a bubble of tar forms around a fallen fern leaf and slowly drags it under.
sights: Black pools bubbling with slow, oily bursts
Tusks and skulls of extinct beasts breaking the surface
Ferns as tall as houses drooping over the pits
Tar-coated skeletons with dull red light in their sockets
A haze of smoke that turns the sun orange
Footprints in the tar that slowly fill as you watch
Insects trapped in amber-like beads of hardened pitch
A mammoth skull half-sunk, its tusks curving like an arch
sounds: Slow, sucking bubbles bursting across the pits
The creak of tar-stiff bones moving
A trumpeting call from something long extinct
Squelch of boots pulling free of sticky ground
Ferns rustling in a hot, low wind
A wet, deep gurgle from far below the surface
smells: Ancient rot sealed in the tar
Fern sap and wet green leaves
Smoke from slow fires smoldering in the pits
rooms: A crust of hardened tar near the portal, cracked into plates like a dry riverbed.
A fern forest where trunks ooze resin and the canopy hides nesting reptiles.
The tusk arch, a mammoth skull that forms a gateway over a narrow path between two pits.
A bone yard where skeletons of countless beasts lie heaped, some still twitching.
An excavation site abandoned by Magic Society scholars, with ropes, tools and labeled crates of bones.
A burning pit where tar has caught fire, sending columns of black smoke into the sky.
A predator's last stand, a frozen scene of a great saber-cat skeleton locked in combat with a mammoth.
A sunken grotto beneath the ferns where hot springs bubble up through the tar.
An amber cave where tar has hardened into dark, translucent stone holding perfectly preserved creatures.
A pit of slow ooze where the tar forms shapes and reaches upward like grasping hands.
A nesting ground of giant flightless birds, their eggs half-buried in warm tar.
The heart, the deepest pit, where an immense tar-soaked skeleton of a primordial beast-king rises, fused with the living ooze itself.
features: The scholars' crates hold labeled monster cores of extinct beasts; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature) check identifies which ones are still valuable.
Hardened tar plates can be pried up and laid as stepping stones across shallow pits, carrying one creature each before sinking.
Burning pits can be used against tar creatures; luring one into flame deals {dmg} fire damage to it and makes it flee.
Fern resin repels the tar; a creature coated in it gains advantage on saves against being stuck or engulfed for 1 hour.
The amber cave holds a preserved creature with an intact core; breaking it free takes 10 minutes and a DC {dc} Strength check.
The bird nests hold warm eggs; an egg can be used as bait, distracting a bone beast for 1d4 rounds.
Hot springs in the grotto soften tar; a creature bathing there frees itself from any tar coating and removes one level of exhaustion during a short rest.
hazards: Sticky tar pools trap anyone who steps in; a DC {dc} Strength save avoids being restrained and sinking 1 foot per round.
The ooze surges from a pit to engulf prey; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or are engulfed, taking {dmg} acid damage at the start of each turn.

Methane bubbles burst near flame; when a creature carries fire within 20 feet of a pit, the pit explodes and creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Choking fumes settle in the low ground; creatures resting there make a DC {dc} Constitution save or are poisoned and gain a level of exhaustion.
Skeleton stampede: tar-soaked bones rise in a herd; creatures in their path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The crust plates near the portal shift under weight; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check spots the weak ones, and a failure plunges a creature into hot tar for {half} fire damage.

environments.name: Mangrove Labyrinth
environments.summary: A tidal swamp of mangroves grew so thick that a lost Delta fishing clan's prayers for shelter gave it a will of its own. The roots form walls and arches over channels that rise and fall with a tide that comes every hour, rearranging the paths each time. The labyrinth wants to protect what lives inside it, and it treats every visitor as either a guest or prey depending on what they carry.
readAloud: Brackish water swirls around your ankles, warm as blood. Mangrove roots arch over you in tangled cathedrals, their bark grey and crusted with oysters, and the channels between them split and twist in every direction. Something large and silent glides beneath the murky surface, leaving a slow ripple that passes right beneath your feet.

Green light filters through a canopy so thick that the sky is a rumour. The air buzzes with insects, and every root around you is alive with crabs, their shells clicking as they scuttle away from your boots. Far off, water is rushing, and the sound is getting louder; the tide is coming in.

Roots grip the portal stones like fingers, and the instant you step forward, they creak and tighten behind you. A narrow channel stretches ahead, dark and still, lined with herons that turn their heads to watch you. A carved wooden totem stands in the water, painted with the faces of fishermen, and every face has its eyes shut tight.
sights: Mangrove roots arching overhead in living cathedrals
Oyster-crusted bark and clusters of clicking crabs
Herons standing motionless, watching every movement
Murky channels splitting in a dozen directions
Painted totems of fishermen with eyes squeezed shut
A swirling tide line marked in mud high on the trunks
Mudskippers leaping between roots like flicked pebbles
A drowned canoe hanging in the roots above the waterline
sounds: The rush of an incoming tide growing louder
Crabs clicking and scuttling across bark
Insects whining in clouds
Roots creaking as they shift and tighten
The splash of something heavy diving
A heron's harsh, croaking cry
smells: Brackish salt water and warm mud
Rotting leaves steeping in still pools
Old smoke from a long-cold fire
rooms: A root cradle where the portal sits wrapped in mangrove limbs, half-flooded at high tide.
A heron rookery, a high canopy cluster of nests where enormous birds guard their young.
A crab colony, a muddy flat swarming with shelled creatures the size of shields.
The fishermen's stilt village, abandoned huts on poles, their nets still hung to dry.
A totem circle where painted posts stand in a ring of still water, each one carved with a name.
A tidal chute, a narrow channel where the incoming tide roars through like a river in flood.
An oyster reef grown thick on roots, hiding pearls and the sharp edges of ten thousand shells.
A crocodile wallow, a sunlit mudbank where great reptiles bask with their jaws open.
A root tunnel where mangroves have woven a long, dark passage just above the water.
A mudflat at low tide, exposing the bones of drowned fishermen and their rusted hooks.
A blossom pool where white flowers float on still water and stinging fish nest beneath.
The heart, a hollow at the base of the oldest mangrove where the swamp's guardian, a serpent of root and scale, coils around a shrine to the drowned clan.
features: Canoes in the stilt village can be patched in 10 minutes and used to ride the tide, doubling movement through channels.
The totems remember their fishermen; a creature that speaks a carved name aloud with respect makes the roots part for 1 minute, opening a shortcut.
Oyster reefs hide pearls; a creature that spends 10 minutes and succeeds on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check finds pearls worth spirit coins, taking 1d4 slashing damage.
Herons can be followed; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check reading their flight reveals the path to dry ground before the tide comes.
The roots respond to offerings of fresh fish; feeding the labyrinth grants advantage on the next Survival check to navigate it.
Crab shells make crude shields, granting +1 AC for an hour before cracking.
The guardian serpent can be pacified by restoring the shrine; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check rights the toppled offerings and grants advantage on the first round of combat.
hazards: The tide surges every hour; creatures in channels make a DC {dc} Strength save or are swept 40 feet and take {half} bludgeoning damage against roots.
Paths rearrange with each tide; after each one, a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check is needed to avoid wasting an hour circling.
Stinging fish swarm in the blossom pool; a creature entering the water takes {half} poison damage and makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is paralyzed for 1 round.
Crocodiles lunge from the mud; a creature walking on the mudbank makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check or is grappled and dragged underwater for {dmg} piercing damage.
Roots tighten around intruders who damage the mangroves; a creature that cuts a root makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained.
Sucking mud traps feet on the mudflat; a DC {dc} Strength save each turn avoids becoming stuck as the tide returns.

environments.name: Frozen Waterfall Stair
environments.summary: A frost giant chieftain froze a mighty waterfall in a single breath to build a stair to the sky, and the act of will was so immense it formed an astral space. The stair is a mile-high climb of blue ice terraces frozen mid-fall, with the roar of the water still trapped inside. The giants who guard it want only the strongest to ascend, and the ice itself remembers how to flow.
readAloud: A wall of blue ice rises before you, frozen in the shape of falling water, so tall that its top is lost in cloud. Steps have been carved into its face, each one taller than a man. A deep, muffled roar comes from inside the ice, as though the waterfall is still pouring somewhere within it.

Wind howls down the cliff, carrying stinging grains of ice. You stand on a frozen pool at the base of a vast cascade, its curls and spray locked into glittering sculpture. High above, a giant figure in white furs stands on a ledge, watching you with arms folded, and then it raises a horn to its lips.

Your breath crystallizes and falls as snow. The ice under your boots is clear enough to see fish frozen mid-swim beneath your feet, staring upward in surprise. Above, terraces of ice climb in a staircase toward a sky the colour of steel, and every step glints with frozen spray.
sights: A mile-high cascade frozen into blue ice terraces
Steps carved into the ice, each one taller than a man
Fish frozen mid-swim beneath clear ice
Spray locked into glittering sculptures in midair
Giant figures in white furs watching from ledges
Icicles as long as spears hanging from overhangs
Clouds drifting past the middle of the climb
Cracks in the ice showing rushing water deep within
sounds: A muffled roar of water trapped inside the ice
Wind howling down the cliff face
Ice cracking with sharp reports like snapping bones
A giant's horn echoing off the frozen falls
Icicles chiming as they sway
The slow, groaning creak of the whole cascade shifting
smells: Wet stone at the base of the falls
Wood smoke from a giant's fire high above
The mineral tang of glacier water
rooms: The plunge pool, a frozen lake at the base of the falls where the portal stands in a ring of ice boulders.
The first terrace, a broad step carved with runes of challenge in the giant tongue.
An ice cave behind the falls where water still flows in a thin, dark sheet.
A spray garden where frozen droplets hang in midair like a field of glass beads.
A giant watch post, a carved hollow in the ice with a fire pit and a stack of enormous bones.
The narrows, a vertical stretch where the steps vanish and climbers must use axes and ropes.
A frozen eddy, a spiral of ice that once was a whirlpool, now a winding ramp.
A cloud ledge midway up the climb where mist hides crevasses and frost spirits wander.
The trophy wall, where giants hang the frozen bodies of failed climbers as warning.
A cracked terrace where water bursts through the ice in jets that freeze as they fly.
The chieftain's hall, a hollow in the ice lit by trapped sunlight, with a feasting table carved from a single frozen tree.
The heart, the summit of the falls where the frost giant chieftain stands beside a frozen lake that feeds the cascade, his breath still holding it in place.
features: Giant climbing pitons are hammered into the ice; using them grants advantage on Athletics checks to climb the narrows.
The challenge runes can be read with a DC {dc} Intelligence check; answering one aloud earns a giant's respect and safe passage past one watch post.
The ice cave behind the falls holds flowing water; a creature that drinks from it gains resistance to cold damage for 1 hour.
Frozen spray beads can be harvested as sling stones that shatter into a 5-foot burst of cold, dealing 1d6 cold damage.
The giant watch post fire can be stoked for a short rest that removes one level of exhaustion caused by cold.
The trophy wall holds the gear of fallen climbers; searching takes 10 minutes and yields climbing tools and a chance of a minor magic item.
Breaking the chieftain's concentration with a DC {dc} Charisma (Intimidation) or Performance check during the boss fight makes the falls thaw for 1 round, washing everyone not braced off the summit.
hazards: Icicles fall when the cascade shifts; creatures beneath them make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The narrows have no steps; climbing requires a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, and a failure means a fall of 30 feet onto the terrace below.
Bitter cold saps strength at altitude; each hour, creatures make a DC {dc} Constitution save or gain a level of exhaustion.
Water jets burst from cracked terraces; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or are knocked prone and encased in ice, restrained until they break free.
Crevasses hide under cloud mist; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check spots them, and a failure drops a creature into a crack for {half} bludgeoning damage.
The chieftain's breath sweeps the summit; creatures in a 60-foot cone make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} cold damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Hive of the Pale Moths
environments.summary: A hollow mountain became the nest of giant moths drawn to a single impossible lantern burning in its depths, and their hunger for that light shaped an astral space. Silk-hung chambers glow with captured flame and the dust of a million wings, while fey lamplighters tend the light and harvest the moths' dreams. The space wants darkness everywhere except the lantern, and it smothers every other flame that enters.
readAloud: Darkness folds around you like velvet, broken only by a pale, wavering glow far ahead. As your eyes adjust, you see the walls are draped in grey silk, and the silk is moving, rippling with countless resting wings. A soft powder drifts down from above and settles on your shoulders, faintly luminous.

Your torch gutters the instant you arrive, its flame shrinking to a blue bead. Around you, curtains of silk hang from a vaulted cavern ceiling, and something enormous and soft brushes past your face in the dark. Its wings beat once, slowly, and stir a breeze that smells of dust and old paper.

A distant light pulses like a heartbeat, and with every pulse the cavern around you shivers. Moths the size of hawks circle it in endless spirals, their pale wings painted with patterns like staring eyes. Small figures in grey cloaks walk the silk bridges with long lantern poles, and one of them stops to look at you, its face hidden by a hood of wings.
sights: Silk curtains rippling with countless resting wings
Glowing wing-dust drifting down like pale snow
Moths as large as hawks, wings painted with eye patterns
A distant lantern pulsing like a heartbeat
Fey lamplighters in hoods of moth wings
Cocoons the size of coffins hanging from the ceiling
Torches and candles guttering into tiny blue beads
A great moth larva chewing slowly through a silk wall
sounds: Soft, constant fluttering in the dark
The whisper of silk curtains brushing together
A low, pulsing hum from the lantern
Chewing sounds from the larval chambers
Fey lamplighters humming a lullaby
The thump of a moth striking a wall
smells: Sweet nectar left out for the moths
A clean, faint scent of night air
rooms: A silk vestibule where the portal hangs behind a curtain of grey threads.
The fluttering vault, a cavern where thousands of moths rest on the ceiling and wake at the slightest light.
A cocoon gallery, rows of hanging pods, some holding moths, others holding things that were not moths.
The lamplighters' lodge, a cluster of silk huts with poles, jars of nectar and woven wing-masks.
A larval nursery where fat white grubs chew through silk and anything else they find.
A dust pit, a depression filled waist-deep with glowing wing-dust that clings to everything.
A dreaming chamber where fey harvest moth dreams into glass bottles that glimmer with visions.
A silk bridge spanning a black chasm, swaying with every wingbeat from below.
A burned-out shrine where earlier visitors tried to light a bonfire and were found as ash.
The eye-wing gallery, a hall where moth wings are pinned on the walls, their painted eyes following movement.
A spiral ramp of hardened silk that winds upward toward the pulsing light.
The heart, a hollow at the mountain's peak where the impossible lantern burns, guarded by the moth queen, wings wide as a sail, eyes like twin moons.
features: Nectar jars from the lodge attract moths; scattering one draws every moth within 60 feet away for 1 minute.
Wing-masks from the lodge disguise wearers as lamplighters; a creature wearing one gains advantage on Deception checks with the fey.
Bottled moth dreams can be drunk; a creature that does sees a vision of the path to the heart but must make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or sleep for 1 minute.
Glowing wing-dust can be gathered and thrown; a handful creates a 10-foot cloud of dim light that outlines invisible creatures for 1 minute.
Cocoons can be cut open; each has a 1 in 3 chance of holding a sleeping victim with gear, and a 1 in 6 chance of something hungry.
The silk bridge can be cut with a single action, collapsing it into the chasm along with anything on it.
The impossible lantern can be shuttered with a DC {dc} Strength check during the boss fight, plunging the heart into darkness and stunning the moth queen for 1 round.
hazards: Any light source brighter than a candle draws moths; each minute, a creature carrying one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or is swarmed, taking {half} slashing damage.
Wing-dust coats the air in the vault; a creature breathing it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned and falls asleep for 1 minute.
The eye-wing gallery hypnotizes viewers; a creature that looks at the walls makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed and stands motionless for 1 round.

Larvae burrow through floors; a creature standing in the nursery makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save each round or the floor gives way into a 10-foot pit filled with grubs that deal {half} piercing damage.
The dust pit is waist-deep and choking; a creature moving through it makes a DC {dc} Strength save or sinks and begins to suffocate.
The moth queen's wing blast sweeps the heart; creatures in a 30-foot cone make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} psychic damage and being blinded on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Sunken Sun-Temple
environments.summary: A temple built to catch and hold the sun slid beneath a warm sea when its priests tried to keep the dawn forever, and the trapped sunlight still burns inside its drowned halls. Golden constructs tend the light, while the priests who caused the flood linger as radiant drowned dead who cannot let go. The space wants the sun returned to the sky, and it fights anyone who tries to take the light for themselves.
readAloud: You arrive beneath the sea, yet golden light floods your vision. A step pyramid rises ahead through clear blue water, every face gilded and blazing as though the sun sits at its peak. Air bubbles stream from your clothes and rise toward a surface far overhead, and you can somehow breathe, though each breath tastes of salt and warm metal.

Steam rises around you from water so warm it feels like a bath. Columns of golden stone stand in rows down a flooded avenue, their capitals carved into sunbursts, each one glowing from within. At the end of the avenue, a figure in ragged golden robes floats upright, arms spread, light spilling from its open mouth.

The temple doors stand open before you, and through them pours a river of light so bright you have to shield your eyes. The water around the doorway shimmers and boils in tiny bubbles. Bronze figures with sun-disc faces stand in the light, turning slowly to look at you with blank golden eyes.
sights: A gilded step pyramid blazing beneath clear blue water
Sunburst columns glowing from within along a flooded avenue
Drowned priests in ragged golden robes, light spilling from their mouths
Bronze constructs with polished sun-disc faces
Water shimmering and boiling where light is strongest
Coral grown in spirals around golden statues
Schools of fish glowing like embers
Mirrors of hammered gold angled to bounce light through halls
sounds: A deep, resonant hum like a struck golden gong
Water hissing and bubbling around hot stones
Chanting from drowned throats, muffled and wet
Bronze joints grinding as constructs turn
The slow clink of mirrors being adjusted
A heartbeat-like pulse from the pyramid's peak
smells: Burnt incense dissolved in the sea
A clean, dry scent like summer noon
rooms: A drowned courtyard where the portal opens beneath a golden arch encrusted with coral.
The Avenue of Dawns, a flooded road lined with glowing sunburst columns.
A mirror hall where gold mirrors bounce trapped sunlight through the temple in blazing beams.
The priests' dormitory, cells of submerged stone where drowned clergy still lie on their pallets.
A reliquary chamber with golden reliquaries holding fragments of sunlight in crystal jars.
A flooded observatory dome with a broken sundial casting shadows that move against the light.
A construct workshop where bronze servants repair one another with tools of hammered gold.
A garden of sun-coral, branching golden growths that pulse with warmth.
The steaming baths, once ritual pools, now boiling where sunlight touches the water.
A shadow vault, the only dark room in the temple, where the priests locked away the night itself.
The pyramid stair, a broad climb up the gilded face toward the blazing peak.
The heart, the sun chamber at the pyramid's peak, where a captured fragment of the sun burns in a cage of gold, guarded by the high priest made of light and drowned flesh.
features: Gold mirrors can be turned; a DC {dc} Strength check redirects a beam to strike a creature in its path for {half} radiant damage.
Crystal jars of sunlight can be opened to flood a 30-foot radius with sunlight for 1 minute, harming undead and creatures sensitive to sunlight.
The broken sundial reveals hidden passages; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reading its shadow opens a secret door to the shadow vault.
Bronze constructs obey sun-sigils; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check copying the sigil commands one construct to stand down for 1 minute.
The shadow vault holds bottled darkness; releasing it in the sun chamber dims the heart for 2 rounds, granting advantage on attacks against the high priest.
Sun-coral can be broken off as a torch that gives warmth and light for 8 hours underwater.
The drowned priests answer to their old titles; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check speaking the right title makes one priest pause and weep for 1 round instead of attacking.
hazards: Beams of trapped sunlight sweep the halls; creatures in their path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Boiling pools in the baths scald anyone who enters; a creature takes {dmg} fire damage, or {half} on a successful DC {dc} Constitution save.
The breathable water thins in the shadow vault; a creature there makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each minute or begins to drown.
Blinding glare floods the pyramid stair; a creature without eye protection makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded for 1 minute.
Currents rush through the mirror hall as heat drives the water; a DC {dc} Strength save avoids being swept 20 feet into a beam.

When the high priest raises the sun cage, every creature in the heart makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage and gaining a level of exhaustion on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Monsoon Jungle
environments.summary: An endless rainy season settled over a jungle when a storm elemental fell in love with the land and refused to leave, and its devotion shaped an astral space of eternal downpour. Rivers rise and fall by the hour, trees grow overnight, and beasts have adapted to life in constant flood. The storm wants the jungle to grow ever larger, and it drowns anything that cuts, burns or claims a piece of it.
readAloud: Rain hits you like a wall the moment you arrive, warm and relentless, hammering the leaves overhead into a constant roar. Water streams from every surface, and the ground beneath your feet is more river than mud. Through the grey curtain of rain, you see a tree with leaves as wide as sails, and a snake as thick as a barrel coiled in its branches.

Thunder rolls without pause, so constant it becomes a kind of silence. The jungle is drowning in green, vines curling visibly as you watch, flowers opening and closing in the deluge. A river of brown water rushes past a few feet away, carrying entire trees, and something with glowing eyes rides one of them like a raft.

The air is so thick with water that every breath feels like drinking. Rain drips in silver strings from the canopy, and every leaf is alive with frogs, insects and tiny bright birds. Far off, lightning strikes a tree, and in the flash you see that the storm clouds above have a face, gazing down on the jungle with tender eyes.
sights: Rain falling so heavy it blurs the world into grey
Leaves as wide as sails catching rivers of water
Vines visibly curling and growing in the downpour
Brown floodwaters carrying whole trees past
Frogs in a hundred bright colours clinging to every leaf
Lightning flashes revealing a vast face in the clouds
Waterfalls pouring off the canopy in silver ropes
Monkeys sheltering under leaves held like umbrellas
sounds: Rain roaring on the canopy without end
Thunder rolling in long, overlapping peals
Frogs croaking in a deafening chorus
The rush of rising rivers
Trees groaning as they grow
The crack and hiss of lightning striking wet wood
smells: Sweet orchids blooming in the rain
rooms: A flooded clearing where the portal sits on a raised stone, the only dry ground in sight.
A canopy road, a path of interlocking branches high above the flood.
A river crossing where floodwaters roar between banks lined with fallen logs.
A frog pond where the water is thick with poisonous tadpoles and bright, lethal frogs.
A ruined shrine of a forgotten people, half-swallowed by roots, still dry beneath its stone roof.
A sinkhole lake fed by a dozen waterfalls, its surface churning with fish.
An overnight forest, a grove of trees that sprouted yesterday and are already fifty feet tall.
A great snake's tree, an enormous fig where a giant constrictor coils in the branches.
A drowned village of an earlier adventuring team's camp, tents half-sunk, gear floating.
A lightning field where the storm strikes again and again on a hill of blackened stone.
A mud slide ravine, a slope that slips and shifts constantly under the rain.
The heart, a vast hollow tree at the jungle's centre where the storm elemental has taken a body of rain and wind, wrapped protectively around the oldest seedling.
features: Sail-leaves can be cut as umbrellas or rafts; a leaf raft carries two creatures down a river for one hour before tearing.
The ruined shrine is dry; resting inside grants a full short rest without exhaustion from rain, and its murals reveal a safe route to the heart with a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check.
Frogs can be milked for poison; a creature with a poisoner's kit and a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check coats one weapon to deal an extra {half} poison damage on its next hit.
The overnight forest grows around anything placed in it; a seed planted there sprouts into a tree in 1 minute, creating cover or a bridge.
Lightning can be baited with metal; planting a metal stake draws the next strike, dealing {dmg} lightning damage to creatures within 10 feet of it.
The giant snake can be coaxed with fresh meat; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check lets the party pass unmolested.
Planting a seed at the heart rather than fighting earns the storm's favour; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check persuades the elemental to let the party leave with a monster core of its choosing.
hazards: Flash floods surge every hour; creatures in low ground make a DC {dc} Strength save or are swept 60 feet and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
Lightning strikes metal-wearing creatures in the open; once per hour, a creature in metal armour makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Constant rain soaks gear and morale; at each short rest, a DC {dc} Constitution save avoids gaining a level of exhaustion.
Mud slides tumble down the ravine; creatures in the path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or are buried, restrained and suffocating until dug out.
Poisonous frogs leap at intruders; a creature touched makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned and paralyzed for 1 minute.

The storm elemental's wrath at the heart floods the chamber; each round, creatures make a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Canyon of Singing Winds
environments.summary: Wind carved a canyon so deep and twisting that every gust through it plays a note, and when a wind spirit composed a song from them, the music folded into an astral space. Air elementals are the instruments, harpy flocks are the chorus, and fey wind-dancers race through the gorges in endless contests of speed. The canyon wants an audience and a performer, and it will not stop playing until one of each is found.
readAloud: A chord of wind fills the air the moment you arrive, so loud and rich it makes your bones hum. Red stone walls rise on either side of a narrow gorge, carved into flutes and hollows by centuries of gusts. As the wind shifts, the chord changes, and somewhere far up the canyon a chorus of shrill voices answers it.

Dust swirls in spiraling ribbons around your feet. The canyon ahead twists through towering sandstone, each bend carved with holes that whistle and moan as air rushes through them. A blur of motion streaks past overhead, a lithe figure riding a gust like a horse, laughing as it goes.

Stone arches cross the gorge high above, and wind pours through them in invisible rivers you can feel pressing against your chest. The rock is striped in a hundred shades of red and gold, worn smooth as glass. Every sound you make is caught and carried away, turned into music, and returned to you a moment later as a melody.
sights: Red sandstone walls carved into flutes and hollows
Ribbons of dust spiraling in the gusts
Fey wind-dancers riding gusts like galloping mounts
Stone arches spanning the gorge high above
Harpies perched on ledges, mouths open in song
Rock striped in every shade of red, orange and gold
Scraps of cloth and feathers whirling in eternal eddies
A dry riverbed of polished, perfectly round stones
sounds: A great chord changing with every shift of the wind
Shrill harpy voices answering the gusts
Laughter from fey racing overhead
Whistles and moans from carved stone holes
Your own voice returned as music moments later
Rocks clattering down slopes in sudden gusts
smells: Fine dust that catches in the throat
Feathers and musk from the harpy roosts
The clean, cold scent of high air
rooms: A wind-scoured basin where the portal glows in a hollow of smooth red stone.
The organ gallery, a canyon wall pierced with hundreds of holes that sing as the wind passes.
A harpy roost, a cliff of ledges and nests stuffed with stolen trinkets.
The racing course, a long winding gorge where fey hold races on gusts of wind.
A natural amphitheater where every whisper carries perfectly to the top tier.
An eddy cave where whirling winds have trapped objects in endless circling orbits.
A stone arch bridge crossing the canyon at its narrowest, buffeted by gales.
A dust devil field where small whirlwinds wander like grazing animals.
The silent slot, a narrow crevasse where no wind blows and the silence feels deafening.
A fossil wall exposed by erosion, holding the stone skeletons of great winged reptiles.
The conductor's perch, a spire of rock where a stone baton is lodged at the very tip.
The heart, the canyon's mouth where all winds meet, a vortex in which the wind spirit performs its song with an orchestra of air elementals.
features: The organ gallery's holes can be blocked or opened; a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check plays a melody that calms or rouses the harpies.
The fey challenge visitors to a race; winning a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) contest earns a feather that grants a fly speed of 30 feet for 10 minutes.
The eddy cave holds circling treasure; snatching an item requires a DC {dc} Dexterity check, and failure means taking {half} bludgeoning damage from whirling debris.
The amphitheater amplifies voices; a creature speaking from its centre gains advantage on Intimidation or Persuasion checks against anything in the canyon.
The silent slot offers true rest; a short rest there removes the deafened condition and any effects caused by music.
The stone baton can be pried free with a DC {dc} Strength check; wielding it at the heart lets a creature direct one air elemental's attack once.
Harpy nests hold stolen spirit coins and minor trinkets, guarded by chicks who shriek for their parents.
hazards: Sudden gales sweep through the gorges; each creature makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pushed 20 feet and knocked prone.
Harpy song lures listeners toward the cliffs; a creature that hears it makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed and moves toward the singer.
The arch bridge's gales threaten to throw climbers off; a DC {dc} Dexterity save is needed to cross without being flung into the canyon.
Dust devils scour skin raw; a creature caught in one takes {half} slashing damage and makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded for 1 round.
Sonic resonance builds in the organ gallery; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage and being deafened on a failure, or {half} on a success.
The heart's vortex pulls everything inward; each round, creatures make a DC {dc} Strength save or are drawn 15 feet toward the centre and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Glacier of the Buried City
environments.summary: A city of stone giants was swallowed by an advancing glacier in a single winter, and their refusal to abandon it turned the ice into an astral space. Their towers jut from the ice like broken teeth, and beneath the surface a whole city lies preserved in frozen blue light. The giants' frozen dead still go about their duties in the tunnels, and the glacier wants to keep creeping forward, adding new streets to its collection.
readAloud: Snow blows across an endless plain of white, broken only by the tips of stone towers jutting from the ice like broken teeth. The nearest has a doorway at ice level, its carved frame taller than three men. Beneath your feet, through clear blue ice, you can see a street far below, lined with lamps and doorways, and a giant figure standing motionless in the middle of it.

Blue light filters through the walls of an ice tunnel as you step from the portal. Carved columns rise into the ice above you, the remnants of a great hall, and frozen in the walls are the shapes of furniture, banners and enormous people. Somewhere ahead, footsteps thud slowly, each one making the ice tremble.

Wind howls over the glacier, carrying the sound of grinding ice. A crevasse opens at your feet, plunging into blue darkness, and at the bottom you see rooftops, statues and a fountain, all frozen solid. A light flickers in one window, far down, as if someone is still awake in the buried city.
sights: Stone tower tips jutting from the ice like broken teeth
A whole street visible beneath clear blue ice
Frozen giants standing motionless in the tunnels
Banners preserved in ice, their colours still vivid
Crevasses plunging toward buried rooftops
Ice tunnels glowing with filtered blue light
Carved giant doors standing open into frozen halls
A single flickering lamp in a buried window
sounds: Ice grinding and groaning as the glacier creeps
Slow, heavy footsteps echoing through tunnels
Wind howling across the surface
Water dripping in the deeper halls
The sharp crack of new crevasses opening
A faint, deep chant in the giant tongue
smells: The mineral tang of glacial meltwater
rooms: A tower top jutting from the glacier, where the portal shimmers in a carved stone window.
A tunnel of blue ice bored by melting water, winding down into the buried city.
The grand hall of the giant lords, a cavern of carved columns half-frozen in the ice.
A market square where stalls of frozen goods stand preserved beneath an ice ceiling.
A giant's home, enormous furniture frozen mid-use, a meal still laid on the table.
A forge where stone constructs hammer slowly at frozen anvils, never completing a blade.
