A temple to the mountain, its altar a single boulder carved with runes of endurance.
A crevasse bridge, a span of ice crossing a drop into the deepest part of the city.
The meltwater cistern, a pool of black water where frozen dead float beneath the surface.
The library of stone tablets, giant records of the city's last winter, carved in haste.
The city gates, enormous doors frozen half-open, the glacier pressing through them.
The heart, the throne room at the city's centre, where the giant queen sits encased in a pillar of ice that cracks a little more every hour, her eyes open and watching.
features: Giant lamps can be relit with oil from the market; a lit lamp melts a 10-foot passage through ice in 10 minutes.
The stone tablets record the city's last winter; a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check reveals the queen's oath, which can be invoked at the heart.
Stone constructs at the forge respond to giant commands; a DC {dc} Charisma check speaking Giant halts one for 1 minute.
The temple boulder grants endurance; a creature who prays there gains temporary hit points equal to {half} for 1 hour.
Frozen goods in the market include preserved monster cores and spirit coins; prying them free takes 10 minutes and a DC {dc} Strength check.
The meltwater cistern hides a drowned treasury; a creature who dives makes a DC {dc} Constitution save against the cold to retrieve a chest.
The ice pillar around the queen can be shattered early with fire; dealing 50 fire damage frees her before the party reaches her, ending the fight in a parley or a sudden ambush.
hazards: The glacier creeps and crushes; once per hour, creatures in a narrow tunnel make a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage as walls squeeze inward on a failure, or {half} on a success.
Crevasses open without warning; a DC {dc} Dexterity save avoids a 30-foot fall onto frozen rooftops for {half} bludgeoning damage.
Bitter cold seeps through the tunnels; creatures without cold protection make a DC {dc} Constitution save each hour or gain a level of exhaustion.
Frozen dead awaken when touched; a creature who disturbs one makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is frightened for 1 minute as it rises.
Thin ice over the cistern breaks under weight; a creature that falls in takes {half} cold damage at the start of each turn until it gets out.

When the queen's pillar shatters, a blast of frost fills the heart; each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} cold damage and being restrained by ice on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Lanternfish Abyss
environments.summary: An ocean trench deeper than any map formed an astral space when the mana of its crushing dark gathered for an age without a single ray of sun. Lanternfish, anglers and stranger things glow in the black water, and something vast and intelligent lurks in the deepest part of the trench. The abyss wants light, but only its own, and it lures visitors deeper with false lanterns until they are lost forever.
readAloud: Darkness, total and heavy, wraps around you as cold water presses on every inch of your skin. You can breathe, somehow, but each breath is thick and salty. Then, far below, a single blue light flickers on, and another, and another, until a constellation of tiny lanterns hangs beneath you, and all of them begin to drift closer.

The portal light fades behind you, leaving only the glow of your own gear. Something bumps your shoulder, a fish with teeth like needles and a lantern dangling from its brow. In the distance, lights pulse in slow patterns, green and violet and red, and you realize after a moment that they are spelling something.

Pressure squeezes your chest, and the silence is so complete you can hear your own heartbeat. You hang above a trench that drops into blackness, its walls covered in glowing worms and pale coral. Far below, a light larger than a house opens like an eye, looks up at you, and slowly closes again.
sights: Constellations of tiny blue lights drifting in the black
Anglerfish with needle teeth and dangling lures
Lights pulsing in slow patterns that seem like writing
Trench walls coated in glowing worms and pale coral
A light larger than a house opening like an eye
Jellyfish trailing tendrils of violet glow
The skeleton of a sea serpent resting on a ledge
Snowfall of pale organic flakes drifting endlessly downward
sounds: Absolute silence pressing against the ears
The muffled thud of a heartbeat
A deep clicking from something far below
Bubbles rising from vents in the trench walls
Low groaning from the pressure on the rock
A whisper of song in a language older than speech
smells: Rotting fish drifting down from above
A sweet, sickly scent near the false lights
Metal and rust from sunken wrecks
rooms: A ledge on the trench wall where the portal hangs in the dark like a pale moon.
A lantern field, a stretch of water filled with drifting lanternfish in shifting patterns.
A vent garden where hot water bubbles from cracks, surrounded by tube worms and blind crabs.
A sunken shipwreck balanced on a ledge, its hull broken open and lit by colonies of glowing barnacles.
A serpent's skeleton bridge spanning the trench, its vertebrae worn smooth.
A jellyfish forest of drifting tendrils that sting with numbing venom.
The writing wall, a section of trench where lights pulse in patterns that seem like an alphabet.
An angler's den, a cave lit by a single beautiful lure, littered with the bones of the curious.
A brine lake, a pool of denser water on the trench floor with a shoreline of its own.
A cave of pale coral that hums when touched and shows visions to those who listen.
The descent, a sheer drop in the trench where light fades to nothing.
The heart, the bottom of the abyss, where a vast intelligence of glowing eyes and drifting tendrils waits on a throne of crushed shipwrecks.
features: Lanternfish can be caught with a net; a captured one sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius for 1 hour without attracting anglers.
The writing wall can be deciphered with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check, revealing a warning about the false lights and the location of a hidden cache.
The shipwreck holds supplies, rope and a locked chest of spirit coins; picking it requires a DC {dc} Dexterity check with thieves' tools.
Vent water is warm and rich in minerals; resting by it grants advantage on Constitution saves against cold and pressure for 1 hour.
The humming coral shows visions; a creature who listens makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, learning the heart creature's weakness on a success or being stunned for 1 round on a failure.
The brine lake is dense enough to float on; a creature can walk on its surface as if on solid ground.
Jellyfish venom can be harvested; coating a weapon deals an extra {half} poison damage on the next hit.
hazards: False lights lure travelers deeper; a creature that follows one makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed and swims toward it for 1 minute.
Pressure grows with depth; at each new zone, creatures make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage, or {half} on a success.
Jellyfish tendrils sting anyone who brushes them; a DC {dc} Constitution save avoids being paralyzed for 1 minute.
The angler's lure hypnotizes; a creature that sees it makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or approaches and is attacked with advantage.
Brine lake waters are toxic; a creature submerged makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} poison damage and is poisoned for 1 hour.
The heart's psychic song fills minds; each round, creatures make a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage and being frightened on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Steaming Spring Terraces
environments.summary: A mountainside of white mineral terraces, each pool steaming in a different colour, became an astral space when a volcano's slow warmth met the wishes of a thousand weary pilgrims who came to bathe. Snow monkeys, fire spirits and bathhouse fey share the pools in an uneasy truce of hospitality. The space wants its guests relaxed and staying forever, and the deeper pools soften minds as easily as they soothe muscles.
readAloud: Steam rolls across a hillside of white stone terraces, each one cupping a pool of water in shades of turquoise, gold and rose. Snow falls gently but melts before it touches the water. A troop of grey-furred monkeys lounges in the nearest pool, eyes half-closed, and one of them lazily lifts a hand in what might be a greeting.

The air is warm and damp, heavy with the smell of minerals and sulfur. Water trickles from terrace to terrace in a thousand tiny waterfalls, leaving the stone glittering and crusted with crystals. Up the slope, a wooden bathhouse with paper lanterns glows softly, and a small figure with a towel over its arm bows toward you.

You hear bubbling before you see anything, a deep, contented gurgle from every direction. As the steam parts, a pool of bright orange water reveals itself, and in it floats a creature made of glowing coals, sighing happily as steam rises from its body. It opens one ember eye, studies you, and says, in a crackling voice, that the water is very nice today.
sights: White mineral terraces cupping pools of turquoise, gold and rose
Snowflakes melting into steam above the water
Grey monkeys lounging in pools with half-closed eyes
Paper lanterns glowing on a wooden bathhouse
Fire spirits floating contentedly in boiling pools
Crystal crusts glittering along every trickling edge
Bathers with blank, blissful faces who have not moved in days
Geysers erupting in tall white columns on the upper slopes
sounds: Deep, contented bubbling from every pool
Water trickling from terrace to terrace
Monkeys chattering and splashing
The hiss and roar of a geyser erupting
Wooden clogs clacking on the bathhouse walkways
A soft, crackling sigh from a fire spirit
smells: Steam carrying a faint scent of iron
rooms: A lower terrace where the portal glows beneath a frozen waterfall that steams where it meets the pool.
The monkey pool, a wide turquoise basin claimed by a troop of clever, thieving primates.
The bathhouse entry, a wooden hall where fey attendants insist guests remove their weapons and armour.
A changing room of cedar lockers, some still holding gear left by guests who never returned.
The golden pool, water thick with minerals that leave a glittering crust on skin.
A boiling pool claimed by fire spirits who demand tribute to share it.
A tea garden on a terrace, with stone lanterns and a table set for guests who sip slowly and never leave.
A geyser field on the upper slope where eruptions follow a rhythm known only to the attendants.
A mud pool of warm grey clay that bubbles and slowly reshapes anything left in it.
A frozen cave where steam freezes into delicate ice sculptures before it can escape.
The rose pool, a terrace of pink water where bathers fall into dreamless sleep.
The heart, the source spring at the summit, a volcanic pool of molten gold light where the spring's mistress, a vast fire-and-water spirit, presides over the endless bath.
features: Bathing in the turquoise pool for 10 minutes restores {half} hit points and removes one level of exhaustion, once per day.
The golden pool's crust grants +1 AC for 1 hour as minerals harden on the skin, but reduces speed by 5 feet.
Lockers in the changing room hold forgotten gear; each search has a 1 in 4 chance of a useful item and a 1 in 10 chance of a minor magic item.
The monkeys will steal shiny objects; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check befriends them, and they will steal for the party instead.
Fire spirits accept tribute of fuel or flame; an offering grants resistance to fire damage for 1 hour.
The attendants know the geyser rhythm; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check learns it, granting advantage on saves against geysers.
Mud from the mud pool can be shaped into a duplicate of an object that hardens in 1 hour, convincing to a casual glance.
hazards: Boiling pools scald anyone who enters without protection; a creature takes {dmg} fire damage, or {half} on a successful DC {dc} Constitution save.
The rose pool lulls bathers into contentment; a creature that enters makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or falls into a stupor, unwilling to leave for 1 hour.
Geysers erupt without warning; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Toxic gas collects in the lower terraces; a creature resting there makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour.
Mineral crust slicks the walkways; a creature moving faster than half speed makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or slips into a nearby pool.

The spring's mistress raises the waters at the heart; each round, creatures make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success as the summit pool boils over.

environments.name: Sky-Whale Graveyard
environments.summary: Great sky-whales that swim through the clouds come here to die, drifting to rest on a field of storm clouds that never break. Their colossal skeletons float half-sunk in the mist, picked clean by carrion birds, while the ghosts of the oldest whales still sing their mournful songs. The graveyard wants to keep its dead undisturbed, and it calls new whales and new bones to it endlessly.
readAloud: You step onto something soft and grey that gives like wet wool. A sea of cloud stretches in every direction, and jutting from it are ribs, arches of white bone hundreds of feet tall, curved like the frames of ruined cathedrals. A low, mournful song rolls across the clouds, so deep you feel it more than hear it.

Wind howls through the bones of a colossal skull, each eye socket large enough to sail a ship through. Flocks of black birds circle overhead, crying harshly, and land on the skeleton in clouds of beating wings. Far off, a translucent shape glides through the mist, a whale made of fog and pale light, singing as it goes.

Lightning flickers beneath the clouds, lighting the bones from below in flashes of violet. You stand on a vertebra the size of a house, slick with rain and crusted with bird droppings. Below, through a gap in the cloud, you glimpse an endless drop into a dark, churning storm.
sights: Rib arches hundreds of feet tall jutting from the clouds
A colossal skull with eye sockets big enough for ships
Flocks of black carrion birds circling overhead
Ghost whales made of fog and pale light gliding past
Lightning flickering beneath the cloud sea
Barnacles the size of shields crusting the old bones
Gaps in the clouds revealing an endless dark drop
A freshly fallen whale still steaming in the cold air
sounds: A deep, mournful whale song rolling across the clouds
Harsh cries of carrion birds
Wind howling through hollow bones
Thunder rumbling far below
Creaking bone shifting in the wind
Wingbeats as flocks take off all at once
smells: A strange, sweet scent like ambergris
rooms: A landing on a vertebra, where the portal hangs between two spines of bone.
The rib cathedral, a skeleton so vast its ribs form a nave of arches above the cloud.
A carrion roost, a skull crowded with nesting birds and piles of stripped bones.
A fresh carcass where scavengers feast and the air is thick with rot.
The singing hollow, a jawbone curved like an amphitheater where ghost songs echo endlessly.
A cloud gap, a hole in the mist where the storm below is visible and winds roar upward.
An ambergris cave inside an old whale's gut, crusted with valuable, fragrant wax.
A barnacle forest growing on the oldest bones, each shell big enough to hide inside.
A ship wreck caught in the ribs of a whale, its sails torn and its crew long dead.
A whale-calf's tiny skeleton, carefully circled by stones as if someone mourned it.
The lightning field, a stretch of thin cloud crackling with storm energy.
The heart, the skeleton of the first whale, so old its bones are stone, where the ghost of the matriarch rises to defend her children's rest.
features: Ambergris can be harvested from the cave; a chunk is worth spirit coins and burns as incense that calms the ghost whales for 10 minutes.
The whale-calf's stones mark a place of mourning; leaving an offering there grants advantage on saves against the ghosts' songs for 1 hour.
The shipwreck holds rope, grapnels and a captain's chest; a DC {dc} Strength check frees it from the bones.
Barnacles can be pried loose as shields that grant +1 AC until destroyed.
Carrion birds can be startled into flight with a loud noise, creating a distraction that grants advantage on Stealth checks for 1 minute.
The singing hollow amplifies voices; a creature who sings a mournful song there with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check calms one ghost whale for 1 hour.
The lightning field can be crossed safely along insulated bone; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Nature) check finds the path.
hazards: Cloud ground is unstable; a creature that leaves the bones makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or sinks through and falls into the storm.
Gusts from the cloud gaps knock travelers off balance; a DC {dc} Strength save avoids being pushed 20 feet toward the edge.
Carrion birds swarm the living; a creature attacked by a flock makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Ghost whale songs drain warmth and will; a creature that hears one makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or takes {half} psychic damage and gains a level of exhaustion.
The lightning field strikes metal; a creature in metal armour makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

The matriarch's ghost sends a wave of sound across the heart; each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage and being knocked prone on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Pollen Storm Meadow
environments.summary: A meadow of giant flowers bursts into golden storms of pollen every hour, and the space was born when a fey of indulgence sowed it with seeds of pure desire. The pollen intoxicates, the flowers bloom to the size of houses, and pollinators of every kind, from butterflies to bears, drift through in a haze of pleasure. The meadow wants to be loved and to spread, and it clings to anything that leaves it, hoping to seed new gardens.
readAloud: Golden dust fills the air like warm fog, so thick you can see it swirl around your hands. Flowers the size of houses tower over you, petals of crimson, violet and gold swaying in a soft breeze. A butterfly as wide as a wagon drifts past, its wings dusted with glittering pollen, and you feel a sudden, giddy urge to laugh.

A low, contented hum fills the meadow, from bees as big as dogs bumbling between blossoms. The grass grows to your shoulders, and every step releases a puff of sweet, heavy scent. Ahead, a bear lies on its back in a bed of petals, paws in the air, grinning drunkenly at the sky.

Wind picks up as you arrive, and the flowers turn toward it in a single motion. A wall of golden pollen sweeps across the meadow like a sandstorm, glittering in the sunlight. Behind it, you glimpse figures dancing, tall and graceful, crowned with blossoms, and they beckon you to join them.
sights: Golden pollen swirling through the air like warm fog
Flowers the size of houses in crimson, violet and gold
Butterflies with wings as wide as wagons
Bees as big as dogs bumbling between blossoms
A bear lying on its back in petals, grinning drunkenly
Fey dancers crowned with flowers, beckoning
Storms of pollen sweeping like golden sandstorms
Old adventurers' gear half-buried in moss and petals
sounds: A low, contented buzzing from every direction
Laughter drifting on the wind
Petals rustling like silk
The rush of an approaching pollen storm
Fey music played on reed pipes
Bears humming happily to themselves
smells: A heady scent like spiced wine
rooms: A clearing of trampled grass where the portal glows beneath an arching blossom.
The bee fields, rows of giant flowers buzzing with oversized pollinators.
A butterfly garden where wings shimmer and dust falls in glittering showers.
A bear's bed, a hollow of crushed petals where beasts lounge in pollen stupor.
The fey revel, a ring of mushrooms where dancers whirl endlessly.
A nectar spring where sweet golden fluid wells from the roots of a great flower.
A seed pod field where giant pods hang ready to burst and scatter.
A thorn hedge at the meadow's edge, keeping the meadow in and visitors trapped.
A hollow stalk tunnel, a giant flower stem that leads underground into its roots.
The root cellar, where the meadow keeps dreaming visitors wrapped in vines.
The windmill hill, where a broken windmill turns slowly, scattering pollen across the meadow.
The heart, a giant blossom at the meadow's centre where the fey of indulgence lounges on a throne of petals, attended by drowsing guests.
features: Nectar from the spring heals {half} hit points but forces a DC {dc} Wisdom save or the drinker becomes giddy and charmed by the meadow for 10 minutes.
Butterfly dust can be collected and scattered to grant advantage on Stealth checks in the meadow for 1 hour, as it masks scent.
The bees can be calmed with smoke; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check lets the party gather a jar of giant honey worth spirit coins.
Seed pods can be burst on command with a DC {dc} Strength check, scattering a cloud of seeds that blinds creatures in a 15-foot radius for 1 round.
The windmill can be stopped with a DC {dc} Strength check, halting pollen storms for 1 hour.
The fey revel accepts dancers; joining the dance for 10 minutes with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check earns a fey token that grants safe passage past the thorn hedge.
Dreaming visitors in the root cellar can be woken with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check, and may share knowledge of the heart in exchange for rescue.
hazards: Pollen storms sweep the meadow every hour; creatures caught in one make a DC {dc} Constitution save or are poisoned and charmed by the nearest flower for 1 hour.
Giant bees sting when disturbed; a creature stung makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Seed pods burst without warning; creatures within 20 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} piercing damage as seeds embed and begin to sprout.
The thorn hedge tangles those who try to leave; a DC {dc} Strength save avoids being restrained and dragged back into the meadow.
Sleepy pollen in the root cellar overwhelms the senses; a creature that enters makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or falls unconscious for 1 minute.
At the heart, the fey's laughter releases a storm of pollen; each creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage and becoming charmed on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Dragon's Abandoned Nursery
environments.summary: A red dragon laid her eggs in a volcanic cavern and then vanished, and the fierce, protective mana she left behind sealed the nursery into an astral space. Kobold servants still tend the eggs centuries later, though only one has hatched, a wyrmling grown wild and furious without a mother. The space wants the dragon to return, and it treats every intruder as either a thief or a replacement parent.
readAloud: Heat washes over you like a blast from an open forge. A vast cavern stretches ahead, its floor scattered with nests of piled gold, gems and bones, each one cradling a great egg the colour of embers. Small scaled figures with lanterns move between the nests, cooing to the eggs, and as you arrive they freeze and stare.

The ground is warm beneath your boots, and the air shimmers with heat. Massive claw marks gouge the cavern walls, some old and smoothed, some fresh and raw. From the far end of the cavern comes a high, furious roar, followed by the crash of something hurling itself against a wall.

Smoke curls from cracks in the stone, and the air smells of brimstone and old gold. A cracked eggshell the size of a cart rests on a ledge near you, its inner surface scorched black. Painted on the wall beside it, in crude red ochre, is a dragon with wings spread over a ring of small kneeling figures.
sights: Nests of piled gold, gems and bones cradling ember-red eggs
Kobold attendants with lanterns cooing to the eggs
Massive claw marks gouged across the cavern walls
A cracked eggshell scorched black on the inside
Crude ochre paintings of a mother dragon
Rivers of lava glowing in channels across the floor
Shed wyrmling scales scattered like copper coins
Bones of earlier intruders piled in a heap near the entrance
sounds: A high, furious roar echoing from deep within
Kobolds chattering in yipping voices
The crackle and pop of heated stone
Eggs thrumming with slow, hidden heartbeats
Lava bubbling in channels across the floor
Claws scraping on stone
rooms: An entry ledge overlooking the nursery, where the portal glows above a ring of bones.
The egg hall, a vast cavern of nests where kobolds tend the eggs with endless devotion.
A kobold warren, a maze of low tunnels too small for most visitors, filled with traps.
The mother's alcove, an empty hollow shaped to a dragon's sleeping body, still warm.
A hatching chamber where the one hatched egg lies cracked open beside a scorched altar.
A lava channel bridge, a narrow stone span over a river of molten rock.
The treasure hoard, an untended pile of coins and treasures guarded by kobold traps.
A shrine of the absent mother, where kobolds leave offerings beneath painted walls.
A scale pile, where shed wyrmling scales have been gathered into a glittering mound.
A training pit where kobolds practice defending the eggs against straw dummies shaped like adventurers.
A vent chamber where volcanic heat rises through the floor to keep the eggs warm.
The heart, the wyrmling's lair, a shattered cave where the young dragon rages among the bones of its failed suitors, guarding the last unhatched egg.
features: Kobolds can be bargained with; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check convincing them the party serves the mother earns a guide through the warren.
Shed scales can be gathered and sold, or worn as a charm that grants resistance to fire damage for 1 hour.
The mother's alcove holds a scent that calms the wyrmling; a creature that rolls in its ashes gains advantage on Charisma checks against it.
Eggs can be stolen, but each one is heavy and hot; carrying one deals 1d6 fire damage per minute without protection.
The treasure hoard is trapped; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check spots the kobold traps, and disarming them requires a DC {dc} Dexterity check.
The training pit's dummies show kobold tactics; studying them with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check grants advantage on initiative against kobolds.
Offering to adopt the wyrmling at the heart with a DC {dc} Charisma (Animal Handling or Persuasion) check can end the fight peacefully, though the space will expect that promise to be kept.
hazards: Lava channels spit molten rock; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Kobold traps fill the warren; each trap triggered forces a DC {dc} Dexterity save to avoid {dmg} piercing or fire damage.
Vent heat overwhelms the unprepared; a creature in the vent chamber makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each minute or gains a level of exhaustion.
Eggs pulse with protective heat when touched by strangers; a creature that disturbs one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} fire damage.

The cavern ceiling cracks under the wyrmling's rage; when it roars, creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from falling stone on a failure or {half} on a success.
The wyrmling's breath fills the heart; creatures in a 30-foot cone make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Plain of the Endless Eclipse
environments.summary: A sun and a black moon have hung locked together over this plain since a celestial and a fiend dueled here and neither would yield, and their deadlock formed an astral space. The world is caught in the moment of eclipse, with a corona of white fire around a disc of darkness, and the land below is split between the fallen soldiers of both armies. The space wants the duel finished, and it pushes every visitor to choose a side.
readAloud: A black disc hangs in the sky, ringed by a corona of white fire that throws long, strange shadows across a grey plain. Everything is lit in a pale, colourless light, as though the world has been drained of hue. Across the plain, two lines of armoured figures stand facing each other, unmoving, and between them stretches a no-man's-land of scorched earth.

The air is cold and still, and stars glimmer at midday around the edges of the darkened sun. A shadow-figure and a figure of light are carved into a great stone monument before you, locked mid-strike. As you approach, the shadows at your feet stretch toward the dark army, and the light at your back pulls you toward the bright one.

Birds circle silently overhead, confused, unable to land or roost. The ground is cracked and bleached in a long line down the middle of the plain, as though cut by a single blade. On one side, the grass is white and crisp; on the other, it is black and soft, and both sides whisper to you in voices you almost recognize.
sights: A black disc ringed by a corona of white fire
Stars glimmering at midday around the darkened sun
Two armies of armoured dead facing each other in silence
A great stone monument of two duelists mid-strike
A scorched line splitting the plain into white grass and black grass
Shadows that stretch toward one army no matter where the light falls
Confused birds circling, unable to land
Broken halos and horns scattered in the no-man's-land
sounds: A deep, steady hum from the locked sun and moon
Silence broken by the creak of armour
Whispers calling from both sides of the plain
Wind carrying the faint clash of distant steel
A choir singing from the bright side
A low, rumbling chant from the dark side
smells: Brimstone drifting from the dark side
Lilies and clean linen from the bright side
rooms: A hill at the plain's edge where the portal glows in the colourless light of the eclipse.
The bright camp, a field of white tents where celestial dead stand guard in shining armour.
The dark camp, a field of black tents where fiendish dead feast at tables of ash.
The duelists' monument, a towering statue of two combatants locked mid-blow.
No-man's-land, a scorched strip of ground littered with broken weapons and halos.
A chapel of light on the bright side, filled with bleached prayer books.
A pit of shadow on the dark side, where screams echo from below.
A field hospital where wounded of both sides lie together, still breathing after centuries.
A quartermaster's tent on the bright side, stocked with blessed weapons and armour.
A fiendish armoury on the dark side, where cursed blades hang on racks of bone.
The observation tower, a ruined spire where a lone scholar of the Magic Society once recorded the eclipse before vanishing.
The heart, the dueling ground beneath the eclipse, where the celestial and the fiend still stand locked in their final strike, waiting for someone to tip the balance.
features: Siding with the bright army grants radiant blessings; a creature who swears loyalty gains +1d4 radiant damage on weapon attacks for 1 hour, but becomes a target of the dark.
Siding with the dark army grants shadowed blessings; a creature who swears loyalty gains advantage on Stealth checks and +1d4 necrotic damage for 1 hour, but becomes a target of the light.
The field hospital's wounded know secrets; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check tending them earns knowledge of the duelists' weaknesses.
The quartermaster's tent holds blessed weapons that count as magical against fiends.
The fiendish armoury holds cursed blades that deal extra necrotic damage but impose disadvantage on saves against fear.
The scholar's notes in the observation tower reveal a third path; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check deciphers a ritual to break the deadlock without choosing a side.
At the heart, a creature can tip the balance with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check pushing one duelist, ending the eclipse and deciding which army rises against the party.
hazards: Crossing the scorched line pulls the soul in two; a creature that crosses makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or takes {dmg} psychic damage, or {half} on a success.
The bright side's light burns the corrupt; a creature with evil alignment or necrotic power takes {half} radiant damage each hour spent there.
The dark side's shadow saps the pure; a creature with radiant power takes {half} necrotic damage each hour spent there.
Armies stir when weapons are drawn in no-man's-land; each round of combat there, creatures make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or are struck by phantom blades for {dmg} slashing damage.
The pit of shadow pulls the unwary; a creature at the edge makes a DC {dc} Strength save or falls 40 feet into darkness.

When the duel resumes at the heart, a wave of mingled light and shadow sweeps outward; each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant and necrotic damage on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Comet's Tail Road
environments.summary: A comet passing too close to the world shed its tail like a snake sheds skin, and the glittering trail of ice and fire froze into an astral road through the void. Nothing on it stands still: the road itself streams forward, and travelers must keep pace or be left behind in the dark. The comet's heart still races at the road's far end, and it wants to outrun everything, including the creatures that ride it.
readAloud: You land on a ribbon of glittering ice that rushes forward beneath your feet like a river, and the stars around you streak into long white lines. Cold and heat strike you at the same moment, frost forming on one cheek while the other prickles with warmth. Far ahead, a blinding point of light pulls the whole road after it.

The road under you is made of packed ice shot through with veins of blue fire, and it hums like a plucked string. Behind you, it frays into sparks and drifting crystals that scatter into the black. A figure made of fire runs past you along the road, laughing, its feet leaving melted prints that freeze again in a heartbeat.

Wind that should not exist in the void tears at your cloak, and dust and ice crystals sting your face. The road stretches before you like a glowing highway, wide as a city street, and markers of carved crystal stand beside it at intervals, each etched with a single word. The first one you pass reads, in common, Faster.
sights: A ribbon of glittering ice streaming forward like a river
Stars stretched into long white lines by speed
Veins of blue fire running through packed ice
Fire elementals racing along the road and laughing
Crystal mile markers each etched with a single word
The road fraying behind into sparks and drifting crystals
A blinding point of light at the far end pulling everything
Frozen footprints of earlier travelers, some ending abruptly
sounds: The road humming like a plucked string
Ice crackling and fire hissing together
Wind roaring where no air should be
Laughter from racing elementals
Chimes from the crystal markers as they pass
A distant roar from the comet's heart
smells: A cold metallic tang of the void
rooms: The trailhead, a patch of slower ice where the portal glimmers and the road begins to accelerate.
A relay station, a hollow crystal shelter on the road where travelers can rest briefly before it moves on.
The ice flats, a wide stretch of slick road where elementals race in endless contests.
A fire stretch where the ice gives way to burning trails of blue flame.
A crystal marker garden, a field of carved posts each etched with a word of encouragement or warning.
A collision zone where meteors cross the road and smash through it in bursts of debris.
A broken caravan, the wreckage of earlier travelers frozen into the ice, their cargo scattered.
A construct pit stop where crystal servants repair travelers' boots and gear without being asked.
The narrows, a stretch where the road thins to a few feet wide over endless void.
A celestial waystation, a shrine of white light where a weary angel tends travelers.
The slipstream, a region where the road moves so fast that time seems to stretch.
The heart, the comet's core, a blazing sphere of ice and fire where a celestial racer of pure speed challenges any who reach it.
features: The relay station offers a short rest, but only if the party spends a turn keeping pace; resting there removes one level of exhaustion.
Crystal markers grant boons when read aloud; a marker reading Faster grants +10 feet of speed for 1 hour.
The broken caravan holds cargo of spirit coins and rare goods; a DC {dc} Strength check frees one crate from the ice.
The construct pit stop repairs gear; a creature who waits there gains advantage on its next Dexterity save.
Racing an elemental with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) contest earns a spark of its fire that grants resistance to cold damage for 1 hour.
The celestial at the waystation will bless those who show kindness; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check earns a blessing of {half} temporary hit points.
At the heart, a creature can challenge the racer to a contest of speed; winning a DC {dc} Dexterity contest ends the fight and earns the racer's core.
hazards: Falling behind the road drops travelers into the void; a creature that stops moving for a full round makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls off the trailing edge.
Meteors cross the road in the collision zone; creatures in their path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Blue fire bursts from cracks in the ice; a creature nearby makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} fire damage, or {half} on a success.
The narrows sway as the road twists; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check is needed each round to stay on the road.
The slipstream stretches time; a creature there makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or ages a year and gains a level of exhaustion.
The racer's wake at the heart sweeps the arena; each round, creatures make a DC {dc} Strength save or are flung 30 feet and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Bloodmoon Savanna
environments.summary: A great hunter-spirit of the grasslands drank the blood of its prey beneath a red moon for so many nights that the moon took on its thirst, and the hunting ground folded into an astral space. Under a crimson moon that never sets, lions, hyenas and stranger predators run the tall grass in a hunt that never ends. The savanna wants a chase, and it marks every visitor as either hunter or prey before they have taken ten steps.
readAloud: A blood-red moon hangs huge and low over a sea of tall grass, painting everything in shades of crimson and black. The grass sways around your shoulders, and somewhere in it, close by, something laughs, a high, mad cackle. Far across the plain, a lone acacia tree stands silhouetted against the moon, and in its branches hang the bones of something large.

Warm wind carries the scent of blood and dry grass. You can see shapes moving through the plain in the red light, low and fast, flanking you on both sides. A roar rolls across the savanna, deep enough to rattle your chest, and the shapes freeze, then slowly begin to circle closer.

Your shadow stretches long and red across the grass, and it seems to move a moment after you do. Hoofprints and pawprints crisscross the dust at your feet, all leading in the same direction, toward a rocky outcrop that glows faintly under the moon. Somewhere a drum is beating, steady and slow, matching the rhythm of your heart.
sights: A blood-red moon hanging huge and low over the plain
Tall grass painted crimson and black by moonlight
Bones hanging in the branches of a lone acacia
Low, fast shapes flanking through the grass
Shadows that move a moment after their owners
Hoofprints and pawprints all leading the same direction
A rocky outcrop glowing faintly under the moon
Herds of antelope frozen in mid-flight, staring
sounds: Mad cackling from hyenas in the dark
A roar deep enough to rattle the chest
A slow drum matching the heartbeat
Grass hissing in the warm wind
Hooves thundering in sudden stampedes
The wet sound of feeding somewhere close
smells: Carrion rot carried on the wind
Smoke from a distant grass fire
rooms: A trampled clearing where the portal glows in a ring of bloodied stones.
The tall grass, a vast sea where predators hunt unseen.
The bone tree, a lone acacia hung with skulls and offerings to the hunter.
A watering hole where prey and predator drink in an uneasy truce beneath the moon.
A hyena den, a burrow-riddled mound littered with gnawed bones and stolen gear.
A lion pride's rock, a sunbaked outcrop where great cats lounge and watch.
A termite mound city, towering spires hollowed into shelters by small, clever creatures.
A stampede ground, an open stretch where herds run in panic whenever a roar sounds.
A dry riverbed, a ravine of cracked earth where fey hunters lay their traps.
A hunters' camp, an abandoned circle of tents where an earlier party tried to make a stand.
The drum hill, a mound where a skin drum beats on its own, calling the hunt.
The heart, the glowing outcrop beneath the moon, where the hunter-spirit waits in the shape of a great red-maned lion, its eyes burning with moonlight.
features: The watering hole enforces a truce; while there, no creature can attack, and a short rest restores {half} hit points.
Offerings left at the bone tree grant the hunter's mark; a creature with it has advantage on Survival checks to track for 1 hour.
The hyena den holds stolen gear; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Stealth) check retrieves an item while the pack sleeps.
The termite mounds offer shelter; a creature inside has full cover from predators but must share it with stinging insects.
The drum can be silenced with a DC {dc} Strength check, halting the hunt for 1 hour and calming predators.
The hunters' camp holds spears and a journal; reading it with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals that the hunter-spirit honours prey that turns and fights.
At the heart, a creature who stands its ground and roars back with a DC {dc} Charisma (Intimidation) check earns the spirit's respect, granting advantage on the first attack.
hazards: The savanna marks visitors as prey; each hour, a creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is hunted, giving predators advantage on attacks against it.
Stampedes thunder across the open ground; creatures in the path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Fey traps in the riverbed snap shut on careless feet; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check spots them, and a failure means {dmg} piercing damage and being restrained.
Blood scent drives predators wild; a creature at less than half hit points makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each hour or attracts a new predator.
Grass fires flare under the moon; creatures in the grass make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The hunter-spirit's roar at the heart shakes the soul; each creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage and being frightened on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Eye of the Endless Cyclone
environments.summary: A cyclone born over a warm sea refused to die, spinning faster and faster until its fury tore open an astral space. Its eye is a calm, sunlit circle surrounded by a wall of wind and debris that has been circling for centuries, carrying ships, houses and the creatures who live in them. A storm giant of the old sky-blood rules the eye, and the cyclone wants to grow until it swallows the world.
readAloud: The roar is deafening, then gone, as you step into the eye. Sunlight falls on a calm circle of sea, glassy and blue, and around it rises a wall of black wind miles high. In that wall, you see things circling: ships, trees, entire houses, a whale, all spinning slowly in the storm like leaves in a drain.

You stand on the deck of a ship caught in the wall of the storm, its timbers groaning, its sails long torn away. The world beyond the rail is a blur of wind and debris, and beneath you the ship rises and falls in slow arcs. Across the gap, another ship spins past, and on its deck, a crew of tall, grey-skinned figures watches you with lightning in their eyes.

Rain lashes your face, then stops, then lashes again as the wind shifts. The calm of the eye lies below, a perfect circle of quiet sea, and you are standing on a floating island of tangled wreckage in the storm wall. A giant figure strides across the water far below, each step sending ripples miles across the eye.
sights: A calm, sunlit circle of sea in the storm's eye
A black wall of wind rising miles high
Ships, trees and houses circling in the storm
A whale spinning slowly in the wind wall
Floating islands of tangled wreckage
Grey-skinned giants with lightning in their eyes
Lightning forking constantly through the storm wall
Seabirds hanging motionless in the eye, riding the calm air
sounds: The deafening roar of the storm wall
Sudden, eerie silence in the eye
Timbers groaning under the wind
Thunder rolling in overlapping peals
The creak of wreckage grinding together
A giant's voice booming across the water
smells: The clean, cold scent of high wind
rooms: The eye's edge, a calm shoal of floating debris where the portal shimmers on a broken mast.
A wreckage island, a mass of lashed ships and debris spinning slowly in the storm wall.
A floating house caught in the wind, its rooms tilted and its furniture still in place.
The whale's gyre, where a living whale spins endlessly, singing in pain.
A ship's graveyard in the wind, where vessels collide and break apart in slow motion.
The giants' longhouse, a vast hall built on the calm waters of the eye.
A lightning spire, a tower of wreckage where lightning strikes again and again.
A bird roost, a cluster of debris where storm birds nest in the wind.
The calm sea, the still waters of the eye, where sea creatures rise to the surface to rest.
A tornado garden, small funnels that wander across the eye like grazing beasts.
The storm's spine, a ridge of solidified wind leading up toward the cyclone's crown.
The heart, the cyclone's crown, a platform of hardened cloud above the eye where the storm giant commands the wind with a staff of lightning.
features: Wreckage can be lashed into a raft; a DC {dc} Strength check builds one that survives a crossing of the wind wall.
The floating house holds supplies and a family's lost spirit coins, scattered among the tilted rooms.
The whale can be freed with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check, and in gratitude it carries the party across the eye.
The giants respect strength; a creature who wins a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) contest with one earns hospitality in the longhouse.
The lightning spire can be climbed with a DC {dc} Strength check; a creature who reaches the top can call down one bolt of {dmg} lightning damage on an enemy in sight.
Storm bird eggs can be stolen for monster cores, but the birds attack in a swarm.
At the heart, breaking the staff of lightning with a DC {dc} Strength check calms the cyclone for 1 round, stunning the giant.
hazards: The wind wall tears at anything that enters; creatures make a DC {dc} Strength save each round or are flung 60 feet and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Debris whips through the storm; creatures in the wall make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Lightning strikes the tallest point within 100 feet each minute; a creature struck makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Wandering tornadoes sweep the eye; a creature caught in one makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is lifted and dropped 30 feet away for {half} bludgeoning damage.
Rain and spray soak gear and chill the body; each hour, a creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
The giant summons a downdraft at the heart; each round, creatures make a DC {dc} Strength save or are slammed prone and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Wormwound Depths
environments.summary: A colossal burrowing worm tunneled through the deep earth for a thousand years, and the mana-rich rock it passed through hardened into an astral space of endless winding tunnels. The worm still lives, coiled somewhere in the deepest stone, and lesser worms, oozes and blind beasts follow its trails like pilgrims. The depths want the worm to keep eating, and every tunnel it carves becomes another hall of the space.
readAloud: You step into a perfectly round tunnel wide enough to march an army through, its walls glossy and smooth as if melted. The rock beneath your feet is warm and faintly ribbed, and a slow tremor rolls through it every few seconds. Far ahead, the tunnel curves downward into blackness, and from that blackness comes a deep, grinding rumble.

The air is hot and close, thick with the smell of churned earth. The tunnel walls glitter with exposed veins of ore and crystal, sliced clean through by something that did not care what it was eating. Slime trails glisten along the floor, and something small and pale scuttles away from your light.

Dust trickles from the ceiling as the ground shakes. The tunnel you stand in is crossed by a dozen others, some fresh, some old and crumbling, forming a maze of perfect circles in the stone. Somewhere beneath you, something enormous is moving, and the walls ripple slightly as it passes.
sights: Perfectly round tunnels wide enough for an army
Glossy walls smooth as melted glass
Veins of ore and crystal sliced clean through
Slime trails glistening on the tunnel floor
Pale, blind creatures scuttling from light
A maze of crossing tunnels in perfect circles
Walls rippling as something vast passes beneath
Shed worm skin, huge and translucent, draped in a chamber
sounds: A deep, grinding rumble from far below
Slow tremors rolling through the stone
Dust trickling from the ceiling
Wet slithering from side tunnels
The clatter of small claws scuttling away
A sound like a mountain chewing
smells: Slime with a sharp acidic tang
rooms: A collapsed tunnel mouth where the portal glows amid fallen rubble.
The main bore, a vast round tunnel spiraling downward through the depths.
An ore vein chamber where the worm sliced through a seam of silver and star-iron.
A slime pool where oozes gather in the warm runoff of the worm's passage.
A crossing hub where dozens of tunnels meet in a cavern of perfect circles.
A shed skin chamber where the worm's molted hide hangs like a vast tent.
A nest of lesser worms, a warren of small tunnels writhing with young.
A crystal grotto sliced open by the worm's passage, glittering with exposed geodes.
A blind beast den where pale, eyeless predators hunt by sound.
A digestive pit where the worm regurgitated stone, now a lake of liquid rock.
A pilgrim camp where a cult of worm-worshippers live in its wake, praising its hunger.
The heart, a vast hollow where the great worm lies coiled around a core of glowing ore, its mouth a ring of grinding teeth wider than a castle gate.
features: Ore veins can be mined with a DC {dc} Strength check, yielding silver and star-iron worth spirit coins.
The shed skin can be cut into cloaks that grant resistance to acid damage for 1 day.
The crossing hub's tunnels can be mapped; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check identifies the path to the heart.
Blind beasts hunt by sound; a creature that moves silently gains advantage on Stealth checks against them.
The pilgrim camp's cultists offer guidance for a price; a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check convinces them the party worships the worm.
The crystal grotto holds geodes with monster cores grown inside; prying one free takes 10 minutes.
At the heart, striking the core of glowing ore with a DC {dc} Strength check disrupts the worm, causing it to recoil for 1 round.
hazards: Tremors shake the tunnels; each hour, creatures make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} bludgeoning damage from falling rock.
The worm passes nearby; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Slime trails are acidic; a creature that steps in one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} acid damage.
Fresh tunnels collapse without warning; a creature caught in one makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is buried and restrained.
The digestive pit's liquid rock deals {dmg} fire damage to anything that falls in.
The worm's bite sweeps the heart; creatures within 20 feet of its mouth make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or are swallowed, taking {dmg} acid damage each round inside.

environments.name: The Everfall Wood
environments.summary: A fey lord of the harvest grew so greedy that he refused to let autumn end, and the season curdled into an astral space where leaves fall forever and nothing ever grows again. Trees blaze with red and gold, apples rot on the bough, and the dead of past harvests rise from the leaf-litter to serve the lord's endless feast. The wood wants to keep its harvest forever, and it hoards everything that falls into it.
readAloud: Leaves fall around you like snow, red and orange and gold, drifting endlessly from trees that never grow bare. The air is crisp and cool, smelling of woodsmoke and ripe fruit. A carpet of leaves covers the ground knee-deep, and somewhere beneath it, something stirs and settles again.

A great feast table stretches through the forest ahead, laden with pies, roasts and goblets of wine, all of it slowly rotting. Figures in harvest garlands sit along the benches, their faces gaunt, their eyes hollow, eating and eating without stopping. A tall figure crowned with wheat and antlers raises a goblet to you and beckons you to sit.

Pumpkins the size of carts sit among the trees, some carved with grinning faces that glow from within. A cold wind sends a fresh flurry of leaves across your path, and in their rustling you hear voices, whispering about seasons that never came. The sun hangs low and golden in the sky, never setting, never rising.

environments.name: Hailstorm Steppe
environments.summary: A frozen steppe where hail falls in stones the size of fists was born when two giant clans waged a war of weather on each other and neither would stop throwing storms. Mammoth herds plod through the white haze, sheltering under their own shaggy coats, and the giants' storm-callers still stand on their hills, hurling the sky at each other. The steppe wants endurance, and it pounds anything soft into the frozen ground.
readAloud: Hail hammers down the moment you arrive, stones the size of plums bouncing off the frozen ground and rattling against your armour. A flat white plain stretches away under a bruise-coloured sky, broken by low hills and the great shaggy humps of a mammoth herd. On the nearest hill, a giant figure with arms raised bellows at the clouds, and the hail falls harder.

Wind screams across the steppe, carrying a stinging grit of ice that blinds you for a moment. When your vision clears, you see a stone cairn ahead, taller than a house, with a heavy hide door sheltering its entrance. Around it, the ground is pocked with craters, and a mammoth calf lies huddled against the stones, trembling.

The sky is low and heavy, churning like a cauldron about to boil over. Thunder rolls without lightning, and every few seconds a hailstone the size of a fist smashes into the frozen earth near you. Across the steppe, two hills face each other, each crowned with a giant, and the storms between them clash in a wall of white.

Giant storm-callers on hilltops, arms raised to the sky

environments.name: Cloud-Sea Shallows
environments.summary: High above any storm, where the sky turns to gold, a sea of solid cloud spreads under an eternal sunrise, formed by the dreams of every creature that ever looked up and wished to fly. Cloud-rays glide through its shallows, metallic dragons nest on its crests, and celestial wardens keep watch over the gates of dawn. The space wants to be reached by those who dream, and it gently pushes away anything weighed down with greed.
readAloud: Light washes over you, warm and golden, and you find yourself standing knee-deep in cloud as soft as foam. A sea of white stretches to every horizon, rising in gentle swells and breaking into slow waves of mist. The sun hangs just above the edge of the world, frozen in the moment of rising, painting everything in shades of rose and gold.

A shadow passes over you, then another: great flat creatures with wings like sails gliding just above the cloud surface. They dip and rise in the swells, trailing streams of mist from their tails. Far off, a dragon with scales like polished brass circles a peak of cloud, and its roar sounds almost like laughter.

The air is thin and cool, and every breath feels lighter than the last. You stand on the edge of a shallow cloud pool, its surface rippling gently, and in it you see the world far below, tiny and distant. A figure in white with wings of light stands at the end of a cloud pier, watching the dawn, and turns to greet you.

environments.name: Hollow Seed of the World-Tree
environments.summary: A seed fell from a tree so vast it held up the sky, and the seed itself was large enough to hold a world, its hollow interior incubating every kind of life the tree might ever need. Druids of a forgotten circle once tended it, but their absence has let strange, unplanned growths take root alongside the intended ones. The seed wants to sprout, and it draws on the life of everything inside to fuel the moment it finally cracks open.
readAloud: Warm green light glows from every direction, as if the air itself is alive. You stand on a ridge of soft, spongy wood inside a vast hollow, its curved walls rising like the inside of an egg. Below, a forest of every kind of plant grows in tangled profusion, and the whole space pulses with a slow, steady heartbeat.

The smell of sap and green growth is overwhelming. Vines as thick as rope curl toward you as you step forward, testing the air with tendrils. Tiny glowing seeds drift through the warm air like dust motes in sunlight, and where one lands on your sleeve, it begins to sprout.

Far above, the curved inner shell of the seed glows with veins of gold and green, pulsing with sap. Below you, in a tangle of roots and leaves, something moves that is not quite a plant and not quite a beast, its body shifting between bark and flesh. A voice whispers from the walls in a language older than words, urging you to grow.

environments.name: Bog of the Toad King
environments.summary: A toad of monstrous appetite made a bargain with a fiend of gluttony, and in exchange for endless food it grew to the size of a hill and crowned itself king of a bog that folded into an astral space. Its frog-folk subjects bring it tribute day and night, and the bog swells with fat flies, fat leeches and fatter toads. The king wants more, always more, and the bog drags in anything edible from the waking world through slimy portals.
readAloud: Warm, stinking mud oozes up around your boots as the portal closes behind you. A vast bog stretches out under a hazy green sky, its surface choked with lily pads the size of tables and dotted with mounds of rotting food. Somewhere ahead, a deep, gulping croak shakes the air, and the whole bog trembles.

Frog-folk in crowns of reeds wade past you, carrying baskets heaped with fish, fruit and the occasional struggling goat. They move in a long line toward a hill in the distance, and the hill breathes. As you watch, a vast tongue unrolls from it, snatches a basket, and draws it back into a mouth the size of a cave.

Flies swarm in buzzing clouds, so fat they can barely stay aloft. The air is thick with rot and sweetness, the smell of a feast left too long in the sun. A wooden sign half-sunk in the mud reads, in crude letters, All Tribute to the King, and beneath it, smaller, Or You Are Tribute.

environments.name: Red Run Rapids
environments.summary: Once a year the great salmon of the world swim upriver to spawn, and a river drake of terrible strength grew so fat on that run that its blood seeped into the water and turned the rapids red forever. The space formed around that bloody migration, and now the run never ends, crimson fish leaping waterfalls while bears, eagles and worse feast on the banks. The river wants to push everything upstream, and only the strongest swimmers reach the spawning pools at its source.
readAloud: The roar of white water fills your ears, and the river before you runs red as wine. Fish leap from it in silver-crimson arcs, thousands of them, hurling themselves up a series of waterfalls that climb toward distant mountains. On the rocks below, huge bears stand in the spray, snapping fish out of the air.

Mist hangs over the rapids, tinted pink by the colour of the water. The banks are littered with fish bones and torn scales, and eagles as big as wagons wheel overhead. Upstream, something long and serpentine moves beneath the surface, and the fish around it scatter in panic.

Spray slaps your face, warm and tasting of iron. The river surges past, red and foaming, carrying the bodies of fish that didn't make it. A rope bridge spans the rapids ahead, frayed and swaying, and on the far bank a ring of stones marks an old camp, its fire still smoldering.

environments.name: Academy of the Stopped Lesson
environments.summary: A college of spellcraft was caught in the instant a student's time-binding exam went wrong, and the astral space keeps that single second stretched across every hall. Spells hang half-cast in the air, students stand frozen mid-gesture, and only the animated teaching apparatus still moves, grading anything that breathes. The space wants the lesson finished, and it will test intruders until someone completes the failed working or joins the frozen class.
readAloud: You step into a lecture hall where a hundred students sit motionless, quills lifted, mouths open on the same syllable. Above the dais a fireball hangs the size of a melon, its flames curled and still like carved amber. Chalk dust floats in the air without falling. Somewhere down the corridor, a bell begins to ring and stops halfway through its first note, over and over.

The portal drops you into a cloister of grey stone and stained glass, where pages torn from a textbook hover at shoulder height in a slow spiral. A frozen boy in a scholar's gown is mid-stumble on the stairs, his satchel spilling scrolls that will never land. A brass lectern on wheels rolls out from an alcove, swivels its reading lamp toward you, and says in a dry voice, 'You are late.'

Ink drips upward from a spilled pot into a cloud of black droplets near the ceiling. Desks stretch away in neat rows, each with a slate covered in equations that rewrite themselves as you watch. A tall woman in teacher's robes stands frozen at the front of the room, one finger raised in warning, and the air around that finger shivers like heat over a road.
