A practice yard with straw targets riddled by frozen magic missiles, each glowing dart an inch from impact.
A headmaster's study with an orrery that spins backward when anyone touches the desk.
A detention room where chalk writes the same line on a board forever: I will not bend the hour.
An alchemy lab with flasks frozen mid-explosion, glass shards fanned out like a still flower.
A bell tower where the clapper sits pressed against the bronze, the bell flexing outward in a single held ring.
A staff room where teaching constructs sit at a long table and argue silently over grade ledgers.
A conservatory of frozen familiars: cats mid-leap, owls mid-flight, a toad with its tongue extended.
The heart, an examination hall split by a glowing crack in the air, where the failed student and her examiner are fused into one shifting figure of light and robes.
features: Frozen spells can be plucked from the air with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check; a creature that succeeds holds a single use of that spell (such as a fireball) and can release it as an action within 1 minute.
Slates on the desks pose riddles; a correct answer (DC {dc} Intelligence check) makes the slate show a map of the nearest room, while a wrong answer summons a grading construct.
A frozen student's satchel contains a spell scroll and a handful of spirit coins; removing it makes every frozen student in the room turn their heads toward the thief.
Hourglasses can be turned over; doing so restarts time in that room for 1 round, letting frozen spells and objects complete their motion, for better or worse.

A teaching construct can be convinced the party are students with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check, after which it guides them to the examination hall and gives them a hall pass that suppresses other constructs.
Chalk from the detention room can draw a circle on any floor; creatures inside it ignore the time slip hazards for 10 minutes.
The headmaster's orrery, spun backward, lets one creature reroll one failed saving throw before the heart is entered, after which it cracks.
hazards: Time stutters in a corridor; each creature passing through makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or loses its next action as its body freezes for a heartbeat that lasts six seconds.
A frozen lightning bolt runs at ankle height across a doorway; a creature that touches it unknowingly takes {dmg} lightning damage, half on a DC {dc} Dexterity save.
A flying textbook swarm wakes when someone speaks loudly; each creature in the library makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} bludgeoning damage.

The examination crack pulls at the years of anyone nearby; a creature starting its turn within 10 feet makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or ages a decade in appearance and has disadvantage on Strength checks until it leaves the space.
Ink rains upward from spilled pots; a creature soaked by it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded until it spends an action wiping its eyes.
A grading construct marks failures with a branding stamp; a creature that fails any check in its presence takes {half} fire damage and carries a glowing red F that gives disadvantage on Stealth.

environments.name: Palace of Loaded Dice
environments.summary: A glittering gambling palace grew from the obsession of a thousand ruined players, and here luck itself is the only coin worth spending. Croupiers with too many smiles take wagers in fortune, memory and breath, and the house always seems to win. The space wants players, and it rewards bold bets while quietly draining the lucky dry.
readAloud: Warm golden light spills over velvet tables where cards shuffle themselves in elegant arcs. A croupier with a face like a polished mask bows to you and slides a stack of pale chips across the felt, each one stamped with a tiny four-leaf sigil. 'House credit,' she purrs. 'Everyone starts lucky here.'

The roar of a crowd hits you as you step through, cheers and groans rising from a sunken floor of spinning wheels. Gamblers in moth-eaten finery lean over the rails, eyes hollow and bright, clutching dice that click like teeth. A huge chandelier made of loaded dice turns slowly overhead, every face showing six.

You arrive at the top of a marble staircase that descends into a maze of tables, curtains and gilded cages. Somewhere a bell rings and a voice announces a jackpot; somewhere else a man screams and is dragged behind a curtain by two smiling attendants. The air tastes of sweet wine and nervous sweat.
sights: Cards shuffling themselves in fans of gold-edged light
A chandelier of dice turning slowly, every face showing six
Gamblers so thin their finery hangs off them like curtains
Croupiers with porcelain smiles painted wider than their mouths
Gilded cages where losers sit counting nothing on their fingers
Roulette wheels the size of carts spinning on the sunken floor
Pale chips stamped with clover sigils that glow faintly when touched
A great board above the bar tallying names and their remaining luck
sounds: The rattle and clack of dice tumbling across felt
A bell ringing for jackpots that no one ever seems to collect
Laughter that turns to sobbing halfway through
The whir of wheels and the tick of the ball bouncing between pockets
Croupiers calling bets in sing-song voices
The soft clink of chips raked into a drain beneath the tables
smells: Perfume sprayed to hide something rotten
Hot brass from the spinning wheels
The coppery tang of spirit coins rubbed thin
rooms: A grand foyer where a smiling attendant issues each visitor a stack of luck chips.
A card parlour where the cards deal themselves, and losing a hand drains a point of luck from the player.
A sunken floor of giant roulette wheels where players stand on the numbers instead of betting on them.
A dice pit where bones of past gamblers are rolled as the dice.
A bar of mirrored glass where drinks are paid for in memories, and the bartender keeps them in labelled jars.
A high-stakes salon behind a velvet rope, where the wagers are years of life.
A gallery of gilded cages holding broke gamblers who beg to borrow a single chip.
A counting room where imps sort luck chips into towering stacks by colour.
A horse track where clockwork racers run on a loop and spectators bet their shadows.
A powder room whose mirrors show you winning and whisper that one more bet would do it.
A back office stacked with ledgers of debts owed by adventurers who never left.
The heart, a private table in a velvet-draped dome where the house itself sits as a dealer of shifting faces and offers one final game for everything.
features: Each creature receives 3 luck chips on arrival; a chip can be spent to reroll any d20, but a creature with no chips left has disadvantage on all saving throws within the space.
Card tables accept a wager of 1 luck chip; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check spots the cheat and doubles the payout, while failure costs the chip.
The memory bar sells a potion of heroism or a healing draught for one memory; the creature that pays forgets one skill proficiency of the DM's choice until it finishes a long rest.
Gilded cages can be opened with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, and a freed gambler shares where the house hides its cheating dice.
Stolen loaded dice from the counting room let a creature choose the result of one roll on any palace game, but using them in front of a croupier is noticed on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check.
The giant roulette wheel can be spun deliberately; a creature standing on the winning number gains temporary hit points equal to {dmg}, while all others fall prone.
The debt ledgers name every trapped soul; tearing out a page frees that soul, who gives a single blessing of advantage on one roll before fading.
hazards: The floor tiles act as a betting board; a creature that ends its turn on a black tile makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or drops through a trapdoor to the counting room, taking {half} bludgeoning damage.
A croupier calls in a debt; a creature with no luck chips makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or is charmed and walks toward the nearest cage.
Spinning wheels throw off sharpened brass balls; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} piercing damage.
The air in the high-stakes salon is thick with compulsion; a creature that wins a wager makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or must wager again on its next turn.
The chandelier of dice can drop when the house loses a big bet; creatures beneath it make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage and are restrained under the wreckage.
Mirrors in the powder room show a winning future; a creature that looks for more than a moment makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or loses 1 luck chip and is stunned until the end of its next turn.

environments.name: Giant Toymaker's Workshop
environments.summary: A giant artisan once carved toys for the children of hill giants, and when grief drove her to keep building long after the children were gone, her workshop became an astral space. Everything is scaled for a being forty feet tall, so adventurers scurry like mice between spinning tops and towering soldiers. The toys still want someone to play with, and their games are rough enough to kill.
readAloud: You emerge beneath a workbench the size of a barn roof, its underside crusted with dried glue and sawdust drifts as deep as snow. A wooden soldier taller than a watchtower marches past, its painted boots shaking the floorboards. Somewhere above, a music box plays a lullaby so slow and huge that each note rattles your teeth.

The portal opens in a forest of chair legs, each one thick as an old oak. Rolling between them is a painted ball the size of a cottage, bright red and white, and behind it bounds a wooden dog on wheels, yapping in creaking bursts. Shelves rise above you like cliffs, crowded with dolls whose glass eyes turn to follow your movement.

Curls of wood shaving, each long enough to wrap a horse, lie around you like dry ribbons. A giant spinning top hums past, wobbling dangerously, and the gust of its passage flattens your cloak against your legs. High on a shelf, a row of stuffed bears sits up together and leans over the edge to look down at you.
sights: Wood shavings piled like snowdrifts on the floorboards
A wooden soldier taller than a watchtower, paint flaking from its rifle
Spinning tops wobbling across the floor like runaway carts
Dolls on shelves whose glass eyes track movement
Giant thimbles, spools and needles scattered like fallen columns
A toy train on a track that loops around the whole workshop
Half-carved toys clamped in vises, faces unfinished
A window the size of a city gate, showing only a grey sky
sounds: A music box lullaby, each note shaking the floor
The creak and clack of wooden joints
The hum of tops spinning down
A toy train whistle shrieking around the loop
Wind-up keys turning slowly in the backs of toys
A huge, distant sigh from the empty chair at the workbench
smells: Hide glue warming in a pot
Varnish strong enough to sting the eyes
Cold tea in a giant mug, long forgotten
rooms: A floor of sawdust drifts beneath the workbench, where wooden mice the size of ponies scurry.
A toy train track running in a loop, with tunnels big enough to walk through.
A shelf of dolls arranged in a silent tea party, their porcelain cups each the size of a bathtub.
A paint station with jars like ponds, where splashing in bright colours leaves a creature marked for the toys.
A pegboard wall of giant tools, chisels and saws hanging like guillotines.
A toy fort with wooden battlements, crewed by a regiment of tin soldiers.
A sewing basket where pins and needles stand like a forest of spears in a cushion.
A box of building blocks stacked into a precarious tower that can be climbed.
A puppet rack where marionettes hang tangled, strings stretched to the rafters.
A rejects bin of broken toys that mutter and drag themselves toward the light.
A window ledge overlooking a grey void, with a dead giant fly the size of a horse lying on its back.
The heart, the toymaker's workbench, where the giant's last masterpiece, a jointed wooden child, sits up from its clamps and asks if you will play.
features: Wind-up keys protruding from toys can be turned with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, making that toy an ally for 1 minute before it winds down.
The toy train can be boarded; riders travel to any other room in 1 round, but jumping off safely requires a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or {half} bludgeoning damage.
Giant spools of thread can be unrolled as rope bridges between shelves, supporting any number of Medium creatures.
The paint jars can be used to camouflage creatures; one painted to match a toy has advantage on Stealth checks against constructs for 1 hour.
A giant magnifying lens on the workbench can be angled toward the window to focus a beam of light, dealing {dmg} fire damage to one creature in a line once per hour.
Tin soldiers salute anyone carrying a giant brass button from the sewing basket, and will fight beside them for one battle.
The music box can be wound down; while it is silent, the toys stop moving for 1 minute but the jointed child in the heart wakes angry.
hazards: A spinning top careens through; each creature in a 10-foot-wide line makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone.
Sawdust drifts collapse into hidden gaps between floorboards; a creature walking through makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check or falls 20 feet into the dark beneath.
Pins in the sewing basket shift when stepped near; a creature moving through makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} piercing damage.
A falling block from the tower; a creature beneath makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is restrained until it escapes with a DC {dc} Strength check.
Varnish fumes pool in the low corners; a creature that breathes them makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour.
A giant hand of the toymaker's ghost sweeps the workbench clean; each creature on the bench makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pushed off and falls 30 feet.

environments.name: Plague Ward of the Nameless Saint
environments.summary: A hospice run by a healing order sealed its doors during a great sickness, and the prayers of the dying and the despair of the nurses folded the ward into an astral space. Patients still lie in their cots, neither alive nor dead, while masked orderlies make their rounds with tools that cure nothing. The ward wants to heal, and it will treat every visitor as a patient whether they are sick or not.
readAloud: Rows of narrow cots stretch away under a vaulted ceiling, each holding a figure wrapped in grey linen. Lamps hang low and yellow, swinging slightly though there is no wind. A tall shape in a beaked leather mask moves down the aisle with a tray of steaming instruments, pausing at each bed to listen to a chest that does not rise.

The smell hits you before anything else: vinegar, lye, and under it a sweet, wet rot. Shutters cover every window, nailed shut and painted with protective sigils that have run like tears. A bell on a cord rings beside one cot, rings again, and from the far end of the ward a dozen voices answer in a weak, rattling chorus: 'Nurse.'

You arrive in a scrubbing room where copper basins overflow with grey water and blood-dark rags. A nun's habit hangs on a hook, still damp, and beneath it a pair of soft shoes is filled with a pale, quivering jelly. Through the open doorway beyond, you see candles placed on every bed and a figure kneeling in prayer, very still, its head bent too far forward.
sights: Rows of cots holding linen-wrapped patients who twitch at sound
Beaked masks hanging on hooks by the dozen
Shutters nailed closed and painted with running holy sigils
Copper basins brimming with grey, bubbling water
Pale jelly pooled in shoes, bedpans and drains
Wax candles melted onto every bedframe
Bloodletting bowls lined up on shelves, each with a name scratched in
A chapel window boarded up with coffin lids
sounds: Bells on cords ringing by the beds
Wet, rattling coughs in every corner
Orderlies' boots squeaking on wet stone
Prayers murmured in broken, feverish voices
The slurp of ooze moving through the drains
Instruments clinking on metal trays
smells: Herbal poultices of sage and rue
Burnt bone from the furnace room
rooms: A long ward of cots where the patients sit up all at once when anyone coughs.
A scrubbing room with overflowing copper basins and an ooze living in the drain.
An apothecary of shelves holding labelled bottles, half of them full of something that moves.
A surgery theatre with a raked gallery of frozen students and a table stained black.
A quarantine wing behind a door chained shut and painted with a red circle.
A chapel where a dozen nuns kneel, their bodies fused to the pews by dried fluids.
A linen store where sheets hang in rows and conceal a corpse shrouded in each.
A furnace room where bodies are fed into a fire that never warms the air.
A garden courtyard of medicinal herbs grown black and twisted.
A children's ward with tiny cots and a rocking horse that rocks by itself.
An orderly's dormitory where beaked masks lie on every pillow, and bodies lie beneath none.
The heart, the matron's sanctum, where the plague's mother, a vast swollen nurse fused with the sickness itself, sits in a chair of bones knitting bandages.
features: Beaked masks can be worn; while masked, a creature has advantage on saves against disease and the orderlies treat it as one of their own unless it attacks.
The apothecary holds bottles labelled in an old script; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check identifies a cure that grants immunity to the ward's disease for 24 hours.
Ringing a patient's bell summons an orderly within 1 round, a useful distraction or a terrible mistake.
Clean linen from the store can be burned in the chapel to consecrate it; undead cannot enter the chapel for 1 hour.
The bloodletting bowls each hold a few drops of a patient's blood; a creature that pours one into the furnace releases that soul, gaining a whispered secret about the heart.
The rocking horse in the children's ward, if ridden, carries its rider to the matron's door unseen.
The herb garden yields one healing potion on a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check, but failure releases a cloud of blackened pollen.
hazards: Coughing patients release miasma; each creature within 10 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or contracts ward fever, taking {half} poison damage at each long rest until cured.
Ooze surges from a drain; a creature standing over it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} acid damage and is restrained.
The furnace vents a gout of cold grave-fire; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} necrotic damage.
Orderlies attempt treatment by bleeding; a creature grabbed by one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or loses {half} hit points that cannot be regained until it leaves the ward.
Contaminated water in the basins splashes when disturbed; a creature hit by it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned for 1 hour.
The quarantine door releases a swarm of plague flies; each creature within 20 feet makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} poison damage, half on a success.

environments.name: Endless Ghost Market
environments.summary: Every market that ever closed for good left a little of its haggling behind, and those leftovers pooled into an astral bazaar that stretches forever under a starless night. The merchants are ghosts and stranger things, selling memories, names, shadows and secrets at prices that cost more than coin. The market wants trade, and anyone who walks its lanes is either a buyer or a bargain.
readAloud: Paper lanterns bob above narrow lanes packed with stalls, their light thin and blue like moonlight through water. Merchants with translucent faces call out wares you cannot quite see: bottled laughter, a dead man's last words, the taste of a mother's cooking. A child with no feet tugs at your sleeve and offers to sell you the way out.

The portal deposits you between two stalls, one heaped with pale shadows folded like linen, the other with jars of floating eyes that blink as you pass. Crowds of grey shoppers drift by, murmuring prices in a hundred languages. Overhead the sky is a black cloth stitched with silver thread, and every so often someone pulls a thread and a star falls into a basket.

You smell roasting chestnuts that have no warmth, and incense that leaves your mouth tasting of ash. A long avenue of tents vanishes into fog in both directions, with no end and no beginning. At the nearest stall, an old woman made of smoke weighs something on her brass scales and smiles at you with too many teeth: 'First sale is free, dearie. The second one isn't.'
sights: Blue paper lanterns bobbing above crowded lanes
Stalls stacked with folded shadows, bottled sounds and jarred memories
Translucent merchants with coins pressed over their eyes
A sky of black cloth stitched with silver thread
Brass scales weighing invisible things
Grey shoppers drifting in endless processions
Signs in dead languages promising wonders
A stall that sells reflections, with dozens of faces in its mirrors
sounds: Merchants calling prices in a hundred voices
Coins clinking though no coins change hands
Bells on the doors of tents that ring when no one enters
Whispering shoppers comparing what they gave up
A distant auctioneer's gavel falling every few seconds
Music from a carousel no one can find
smells: Grave incense that tastes of ash
Old spice markets, cumin and clove
A faint, sweet rot like fruit left in the sun
rooms: A crossroads of stalls where a ghostly crier announces the day's special: a stranger's name.
An avenue of memory merchants, each selling bottled recollections of real people.
A shadow bazaar where silhouettes hang on racks like coats.
A food court of phantom vendors serving meals that leave you hungrier.
A pawnshop where lost items from every adventurer's past are sold back at a price.
A fortune-teller's tent that tells one true thing for each secret you give up.
An auction house where the lots are souls, bid for by veiled fiends.
A money changer converting spirit coins to stranger currencies: teeth, years, breath.
A toy stall run by a ghostly child, where every toy belonged to someone who died young.
A guarded warehouse where unpaid debtors are stored, wrapped in brown paper and string.
A fog-shrouded edge where the market keeps going but the stalls grow empty and patient.
The heart, the Market Master's pavilion, a vast tent where an ancient haggling spirit sits on a throne of ledgers and offers to buy the party's way out with their best memories.
features: Any stall will trade a minor magic item for a memory; the creature that pays loses one memory of the DM's choice and gains the item permanently.
Haggling is possible with a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check; success halves the price, failure doubles it and offends the merchant.
The fortune-teller answers one question truthfully per secret; a secret given cannot be spoken aloud ever again by its owner.
Folded shadows from the shadow bazaar can be worn; a creature wearing a borrowed shadow has advantage on Stealth but its own shadow leaves to wander.
The pawnshop sells back items the party lost long ago, with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check revealing which are fakes.
Bidding at the soul auction can free a trapped adventurer, but outbidding a fiend draws its hostility for the rest of the space.
The ghost child at the toy stall will lead the party to the heart for free, if one of them promises to come back and play.
hazards: Pickpocket shades brush past; each creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check or loses one item or a pouch of spirit coins.
Phantom food curses the eater; a creature that eats makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {dmg} necrotic damage and gains a level of exhaustion.
A merchant enforces a broken deal; the cheater makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or is paralysed for 1 minute as invisible string binds its limbs.
The fog edge pulls at the lost; a creature that strays in makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or forgets its companions' names for 1 hour.
The auctioneer's gavel strikes like thunder; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {dmg} thunder damage and are deafened.
Crowds surge toward a falling star; creatures in the lane make a DC {dc} Strength save or are carried 30 feet and take {half} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Siege Camp of the Unfallen City
environments.summary: An army camped outside a walled city for so long, sworn never to leave until it fell, that its oath outlived the soldiers and pulled the whole war into an astral space. The city walls never crack, the siege engines never stop, and the dead rise each dawn to assault the gates again. The camp wants the city taken, and it conscripts every newcomer to the next charge.
readAloud: Mud sucks at your boots as you step out among rows of sagging canvas tents. Smoke from a hundred cookfires hangs low over a field churned into brown soup, and in the distance a great grey wall rises, untouched, its battlements lined with tiny watching figures. A drum begins to beat, and all around you soldiers with grey skin and rusted mail pick up their spears and turn toward the city.

A trebuchet the height of a temple creaks beside you, its arm swinging down to hurl a boulder that strikes the distant wall and bursts into dust without leaving a mark. Giants in harness haul the counterweight back up, groaning, their shoulders scarred to the bone by the ropes. A sergeant with half a face points his sword at you and bellows, 'You. Ladder crew. Now.'

Trenches zigzag across a plain of bones and broken arrows, and you land in one with a splash of cold, red-brown water. Men huddle against the earthen wall, sharpening blades that have long since been ground to slivers. One of them looks at you with tired, sunken eyes and says quietly, 'It'll fall tomorrow. It always falls tomorrow.'
sights: Rows of sagging tents patched with old banners
A grey city wall without a single crack or scorch mark
Trebuchets hurling boulders that burst harmlessly against stone
Giants in harness, shoulders worn raw by ropes
Soldiers with grey skin and rusted mail standing to ranks
Trenches lined with bones and broken arrow shafts
Ravens circling in a slow wheel over the field
A command tent flying a tattered crimson standard
sounds: War drums beating the call to assault
The creak and thud of siege engines
Boulders shattering on the wall like distant thunder
Sergeants bellowing orders through ruined throats
The squelch of boots in mud
Horns from the city walls, mocking and far away
smells: Pitch and tar from the siege engines
rooms: A muster field where undead soldiers form ranks at every drumbeat.
A mess tent where cooks ladle grey stew into helmets for troops who cannot eat.
A siege engine park of trebuchets and battering rams, tended by harnessed giants.
A trench network filled with knee-deep red water and the bodies of yesterday's charge.
A surgeon's tent piled with amputated limbs that still twitch.
A quartermaster's depot of rusted weapons and spoiled rations.
A gallows where deserters hang, still trying to run in the air.
A ladder crew staging ground beneath the wall, littered with broken rungs and fallen climbers.
A sapper's tunnel dug toward the city foundations, ending in solid grey stone.
An officer's pavilion with maps of the city marked by a thousand failed plans.
A breach that is not a breach, a painted gap in the wall that leads only to more wall.
The heart, the general's tent, where the warlord who swore the oath sits in rotting plate at a war table, waiting for the one report that will set him free.
features: Joining the assault with a ladder crew lets the party reach the battlements; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check climbs before the defenders' fire hits.
Siege engines can be crewed and aimed at an enemy in the camp; a DC {dc} Intelligence check fires a boulder for {dmg} bludgeoning damage in a 20-foot radius.
The officer's maps show one route never tried; a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check finds it and grants advantage on any check to enter the heart unseen.
Grey stew from the mess tent restores {half} hit points but the eater hears the drums in its sleep for a week.
Freeing a giant from its harness with a DC {dc} Strength check makes it an ally that fights for one encounter before collapsing.
A deserter's corpse on the gallows wears an unbroken regimental token; carrying it lets the party move through camp unchallenged for 1 hour.
Bringing the general a false report that the city has fallen, with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check, makes him lower his guard and grants advantage on the first round of combat.
hazards: Arrows rain from the walls during an assault; each creature in the open makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} piercing damage.
Deep mud grabs at legs; a creature that moves more than half its speed makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained until the start of its next turn.
Boiling oil pours from the battlements onto the ladders; climbers make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} fire damage and fall.
A misfired trebuchet drops its load short; creatures in a 15-foot radius make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
The drums compel the living to march; a creature that hears them makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or must move toward the wall on its turn.
Trench water carries rot; a creature that falls in makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} poison damage and is poisoned for 1 hour.

environments.name: Lighthouse on the Fog Sea
environments.summary: A lonely keeper tended a lighthouse on a coast so dangerous that she swore the lamp would never go dark, and when she died at her post, her vow pulled the tower into an endless sea of fog. Ships of lost souls drift toward the beam, and things that hate the light circle below, testing the stones. The lighthouse wants its lamp kept, and anyone who climbs the tower inherits the duty.
readAloud: Fog surrounds you on every side, thick and white and cold enough to bead on your eyelashes. A single beam of gold light sweeps overhead in a slow circle, illuminating for a heartbeat a sea of mist that rolls like waves. Behind you, rising from a rocky outcrop, a lighthouse of whitewashed stone climbs into the haze, its door creaking open in the wind.

You stand on wet rocks slick with something that is not seaweed. The fog moves around your ankles like a tide, and from beneath it come slow, heavy sounds, like a great body brushing against the stone. Far out in the white, the dark silhouettes of ships drift toward the lighthouse beam, their sails ragged and their crews standing motionless at the rails.

Gulls cry somewhere you cannot see, their voices too human. The lighthouse stands before you, tall and narrow, its lamp burning a fierce gold at the top. A logbook lies open on the doorstep, its pages damp, and the last entry reads in a steady hand: 'Lamp lit. They are closer tonight. I will not let it go out.'
sights: A golden beam sweeping across a sea of rolling fog
Ghost ships drifting toward the light with silent crews
Whitewashed stones streaked with green and black
Fog that pools and moves like water around ankles
Tentacles of mist that rise and grope along the rocks
A spiral staircase climbing into darkness
Oil lamps of every size hanging along the walls
The keeper's lantern hung by the door, still burning
sounds: Gulls crying with almost-human voices
The creak of rigging from unseen ships
A fog horn bellowing from the tower top
Something huge brushing against the rocks below
Wind whistling through the lamp room glass
Footsteps climbing the stairs above you when no one is there
smells: Whale oil burning in the lamp
A faint sweetness like candied lemon from the keeper's tin
rooms: A rocky landing where the fog laps like surf and things move beneath it.
The keeper's cottage, a tiny room with a cot, a kettle and a logbook of lost ships.
An oil store stacked with casks of glowing lamp oil.
A spiral stair of two hundred steps, with landings where the keeper's memories replay.
A watch room with brass telescopes trained on the drifting ghost ships.
A wrecked longboat on the rocks, with a skeletal crew still at the oars.
A fog bell platform where a great iron bell must be struck to drive back the mist.
A lens room where the huge prism glass refracts light into rainbows that burn.
A drowned cellar beneath the tower, flooded with fog thick as milk.
A ghost ship that has docked against the rocks, its deck crowded with silent sailors.
A gallery walkway circling the tower top, battered by wind.
The heart, the lamp room, where the keeper's spirit, now a towering figure of light and wet oilskin, defends the flame against the vast thing rising from the fog.
features: Striking the fog bell drives back the mist for 1 minute; creatures within 60 feet gain advantage on Perception checks and fog creatures must make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or flee.
Lamp oil casks can be thrown or lit as firebombs, dealing {dmg} fire damage in a 10-foot radius.
The brass telescopes reveal the name of each ghost ship; calling a ship by name makes its crew answer one question.
The keeper's logbook lists which nights the lamp almost failed; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals the weakness of the fog beast.
The prism lens can be turned to aim the beam as a weapon, dealing {dmg} radiant damage to one creature in a 120-foot line once per round.
The wrecked longboat can be launched onto the fog, which supports it like water, allowing travel to a docked ghost ship.
The keeper's lantern, if carried, keeps a 20-foot circle clear of fog and grants advantage on saves against fear.
hazards: A fog tentacle lashes from the mist; a creature on the rocks makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is dragged 15 feet and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Slick stairs in the dark; a creature moving faster than half speed makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls, taking {half} bludgeoning damage.
The ghost crews sing a drowning shanty; creatures that hear it make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or walk toward the fog edge.
The lens's focused beam scorches anything in its sweep; a creature caught in it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} radiant damage.
Gale-force winds on the gallery walkway; each creature makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is pushed 10 feet toward the rail and possibly over.

environments.name: Backward-Running Clocktower
environments.summary: A clockmaker tried to wind back the day his daughter died, and his great clocktower obeyed so completely that it fell out of the world and into an astral space where time runs in reverse. Shattered glass flies back into windows, wounds close before they are made, and the tower's gears turn toward a moment that never arrives. The tower wants to reach the beginning, and every creature inside is slowly unwound with it.
readAloud: A shower of broken glass flies upward past you and slots itself neatly into a window frame, which seals with a soft chime. Inside the tower, brass gears the size of wagon wheels turn in the wrong direction, their teeth clicking backward. A pendulum swings, and at each pass you feel a moment of déjà vu so strong it makes you dizzy.

You step onto a stair and find yourself one step lower than you started. Water falls up from a puddle into a dripping pipe overhead, and a pigeon flies backward out of the rafters, feathers closing tight. Somewhere above, a great clock face chimes the hours in reverse: twelve, eleven, ten, all the way down to nothing.

Words drift across the tower floor like falling leaves, and as they pass you hear them spoken backward, the voices sliding into gibberish. A woman in a workshop apron walks toward you heel first, her face unpeeling from tears to calm. She stops, smiles, and says in a voice that rewinds as it speaks: 'Goodbye. You are just leaving.'

Gears the size of wagon wheels turning in reverse
Water falling upward from puddles into pipes
Clock faces whose hands sweep counterclockwise
A pendulum swinging through a shimmer of overlapping moments
Pigeons flying backward through the rafters
Footprints appearing before anyone steps in them
A cracked hourglass where the sand climbs back up
sounds: Chimes ringing from twelve down to nothing
Voices speaking in reverse

smells: Burnt candle wicks that grow longer
Old wood shavings curling back into planks
rooms: An entry hall where broken glass and dust flow backward into place.

A pendulum shaft where a vast weight swings through overlapping moments.
A clockmaker's workshop where tools put themselves away and unfinished clocks dismantle.
A belfry of bronze bells ringing their notes in reverse.
A bedroom where a child's toys tidy themselves and the bed unmakes.
A stairwell where climbing up carries you down, and descending lifts you.
A balcony where the sun sets in the east over a city that unbuilds itself.
A spring room where coiled steel springs uncoil with crushing force.
A storeroom of frozen moments in glass jars, each labelled with a date.
A clock face chamber behind the great dial, with hands that sweep the walkway.

features: Wounds heal backward here; a creature that rests for 10 minutes regains {half} hit points but forgets the last 10 minutes.
The reversed stairwell can be navigated with a DC {dc} Intelligence check, finding the trick of walking backward to climb.
Frozen moments in jars can be uncorked to replay a past event, granting advantage on one check related to that moment.
A creature can deliberately move against the backward current with a DC {dc} Constitution save, gaining one extra action as time catches up.
The great clock hands can be jammed with a heavy object, stopping the reversal in the tower for 1 minute.

Ringing the belfry bells in the correct forward order (DC {dc} Wisdom check) silences the tower's echoes and weakens the heart's guardians.
hazards: Glass flying back into a window can strike anyone in its path; a creature in the way makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} slashing damage.

environments.name: Distillery of Living Potions
environments.summary: An alchemist trying to brew a potion that would live forever succeeded too well, and her brews grew minds, hungers and ambitions. The distillery collapsed into an astral space where the potions run the place, sloshing through pipes and fermenting in vats while their maker lies preserved in a glass tun. The potions want to be drunk, because each one wants a body of its own.
readAloud: Copper pipes snake overhead like the veins of a giant, gurgling and hissing, and coloured liquid pulses through glass sections in rhythmic beats. Vats the size of houses bubble along the walls, and from one of them a tendril of violet fluid rises, sways like a curious cat, and tastes the air near your face. The whole room smells of honey, sulfur and lightning.

You land in a puddle of bright green fluid that immediately climbs your boots, warm and tingling. Shelves line the walls, packed with bottles of every shape, and inside each one something swirls and presses against the glass as you pass. A copper still in the corner whistles a jaunty tune, steam spelling out shapes that almost resemble letters.

A long brick hall stretches before you, filled with fermenting barrels that slosh and knock as though something inside is trying to get out. A figure made entirely of amber liquid stands behind a bar, polishing a glass with a hand that drips. It turns its glowing face toward you and says in a bubbling voice, 'Thirsty? Everyone is, eventually.'

Bottles whose contents swirl and press against the glass
A barkeeper made of amber liquid
Puddles that climb up boots and taste skin

Barrels knocking from the inside

smells: Mint and tar from a medicinal brew
rooms: A pipe gallery where copper conduits throb and leak curious tendrils of brew.
A fermentation hall of knocking barrels and frothing kegs.

A tasting room with a liquid barkeeper serving drinks that drink back.
A vat room where brews the size of houses churn and rise.

A cooperage where barrels are built and the hoops tighten themselves.
A furnace room heating the stills, its coal glowing blue.

hazards: A pipe bursts and sprays acid brew; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} acid damage.

environments.name: Chessboard of the Dueling Kings
environments.summary: Two rival archmages settled their feud with a game of war played on a living board, and when both died with their kings in check, the game refused to end. The astral space is an immense chequered battlefield of marble and obsidian where giant pieces grind each other to rubble and rebuild by morning. The board wants a winner, and adventurers who step onto it are drafted as pieces.
readAloud: You stand on a square of white marble wider than a market square, and the edges of your square glow faintly as if marking its borders. Across the board, a black knight the size of a house turns its horse's head toward you, its eyes burning violet, and then it leaps two squares forward and one across, landing with a crash that cracks the tiles. Far away, two kings stand at opposite ends, both trembling.

The sky above is a slate-grey dome painted with ghostly figures, two robed giants leaning over the board with their hands frozen mid-move. Around you, white pawns the height of towers advance with slow, grinding steps, and a black bishop slides diagonally across the board leaving a trail of shadow. A rook rumbles to life behind you, and you realise you are standing exactly where it wants to go.

Rubble from shattered pieces lies scattered across the board, white marble limbs and black obsidian crowns. A white queen, regal and terrifying, sweeps across the board in a straight line, cutting through a black pawn like a scythe through wheat. A voice booms from above, ancient and amused: 'New pieces. Place them.'

A sky dome painted with two robed giants mid-move
Rubble of shattered pieces scattered across squares
Glowing borders marking each square

A white queen whose crown sheds cold light

sounds: The grind of stone on stone as pieces move
A crash when a knight lands
Booming voices from the sky announcing moves
Marble cracking under impact
A hush when a king is threatened
A ticking clock somewhere above the board

The black home row, guarded by obsidian rooks and shadowy bishops.
A centre board where the fiercest exchanges happen and rubble piles up.
A cracked square fallen into a pit beneath the board, littered with old pieces.

The white queen's diagonal, a lane of glowing light.
The black bishop's shadow trail, cold and dark.
A promotion square where pawns that reach it transform.
A tunnel beneath the board where the game's rules are carved on the walls.
A scorer's balcony above the board, with ghostly scorebooks.
A stalemate corner, where pieces locked in place have grown moss.
The heart, the centre of check, where both kings and both ghostly archmages converge for the endgame and the party must decide which side to crown.
features: Creatures on the board move like pieces; a creature can take a knight's leap as a bonus action once per encounter, ignoring difficult terrain.

The scorebooks on the balcony show the game's history; a DC {dc} Intelligence check reveals the winning sequence, granting advantage on the heart encounter.
Reaching a promotion square promotes a creature for 1 minute, granting it {half} temporary hit points and a +2 bonus to attack rolls.
The carved rules in the tunnel can be studied; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals a forgotten rule that can freeze one piece for 1 round.
Captured pieces can be convinced to return to play with a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check, fighting for the party.
Placing a piece of rubble on a king's square forces that king to flee, opening the path to the heart.
hazards: A knight lands on your square; a creature in it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
The white queen sweeps a line; each creature in a 100-foot line makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} radiant damage.
The black bishop's trail of shadow chills; a creature that crosses it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} cold damage and is slowed.

environments.name: Bathhouse of Steam and Secrets
environments.summary: A grand bathhouse where merchants, nobles and spies traded whispers in the steam absorbed so many secrets that the air itself grew heavy with them and slipped into an astral space. Hot springs bubble in tiled pools, and the steam carries murmured confessions that can be inhaled and learned. The bathhouse wants secrets, and it extracts them from bathers who linger too long in its warmth.
readAloud: Warm, thick steam rolls over you as you step onto smooth blue tiles, and the air tastes of minerals and rose oil. Pools of milky water steam in tiered terraces, each one fringed with marble benches where hazy figures sit wrapped in towels. As the steam drifts past your ear, you hear a voice whisper clearly: 'He poisoned his brother at the feast. No one knows.'

A mosaic of a great water serpent covers the floor beneath your feet, its scales picked out in turquoise and gold. Bronze spouts shaped like grinning faces pour hot water into a sunken bath, and the surface ripples with shapes that are not bathers. A towel attendant with skin like wet porcelain bows and offers you a robe, its eyes half-lidded and hungry.

You emerge into a cold plunge room, the chill a shock after the warmth of the portal. Ice-blue water lies still in a round pool, and at the bottom, coins and rings glitter beneath what looks like a sleeping figure curled in the deep. From the steam rooms beyond, laughter drifts out, soft and conspiratorial, and then a single scream cut short.
sights: Tiered pools of milky, steaming water
Mosaic floors of serpents and nymphs in turquoise and gold
Bronze spouts shaped like grinning faces
Hazy figures on marble benches, wrapped in towels
Steam forming briefly into faces before dissolving
Coins and rings glinting at the bottom of the cold pool
Porcelain-skinned attendants with too-wide eyes
Hanging lanterns of coloured glass swaying in the steam
sounds: Whispered confessions carried on the steam
Water splashing from bronze spouts
Soft, conspiratorial laughter
The hiss of water poured over hot stones
Wet footsteps slapping on tile
A gurgling voice from the drains asking questions
rooms: A changing room lined with lockers that hold the clothes and secrets of every past visitor.
A warm pool terrace where hazy bathers whisper scandal to anyone nearby.
A steam room so thick that vision ends at arm's length and voices come from everywhere.
A cold plunge pool where a frost-skinned monstrosity sleeps on a bed of coins.
A massage hall where attendants knead secrets out of muscle.
A furnace chamber beneath the floors, where fire elementals heat the stones.
A private bath for nobles, with a pool of perfumed water and a hidden listening tube.
A mud bath where bubbling clay holds the impressions of bodies that sank.
A laundry of endless towels, stacked so high they form a maze.
A drain grotto where the bathhouse's secrets pool in a murky underground spring.
A rooftop garden pool overlooking a sky of steam, attended by fey.
The heart, the first spring, a vast cavern where the bathhouse's spirit, a serpent of steam and whispers, coils around a pool of liquid confessions.

The hidden listening tube in the noble bath can be used to eavesdrop on any room, granting advantage on Perception checks to locate enemies.

The cold plunge pool cures one disease or poison, but the coins at the bottom belong to the sleeping beast.
Mud from the mud bath can be smeared on skin, granting resistance to fire damage for 1 hour.
Offering a true secret to the drain grotto spring makes it reveal the heart serpent's own secret, granting advantage on one save against it.
hazards: Scalding water erupts from a spout; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} fire damage.
The steam room's whispers overwhelm the mind; a creature that stays more than 1 minute makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is charmed and refuses to leave.

environments.name: Mine of Dreams
environments.summary: A mining guild discovered that the deep rock beneath a sleeping village was veined with crystallised dreams, and they dug so greedily that the mine broke away into an astral space. The tunnels glitter with dream ore that shows visions when struck, and the miners still work the seams, half asleep and never waking. The mine wants to be dug deeper, toward the nightmare at its core that the miners fear to wake.
readAloud: Your lantern catches a seam of crystal in the tunnel wall, and for an instant you see inside it a meadow of blue grass under two moons. The mine shaft drops away below, wooden scaffolds creaking, and from far beneath comes the steady chink of picks on rock. A miner shuffles past with his eyes closed, mumbling about a girl he once loved, his cart full of glittering stones.

The air is warm and close, smelling of dust and lamp oil, and every surface glints with tiny crystals like frost. As you step forward, a crystal crunches underfoot and you are briefly falling through a dream of drowning before you gasp back into the tunnel. Mine carts rattle on rails that disappear into darkness in every direction.

A great cavern opens around you, its walls riddled with tunnels and its floor heaped with dream ore that pulses softly in shades of violet and gold. Dozens of miners sleepwalk across scaffolds, swinging picks with perfect, mindless rhythm. At the cavern's far side, a sealed iron door bears a warning carved in rough letters: 'Do not dig past the nightmare.'

Mine carts piled with glittering, pulsing ore
Wooden scaffolds creaking over bottomless shafts
Walls frosted with tiny crystals that glint in lantern light
Pick marks that rearrange themselves into words
A sealed iron door with a carved warning
Pale grubs that eat dream ore and glow with stolen visions
sounds: The rhythmic chink of picks on stone
Miners mumbling dreams aloud
Mine carts rattling along rails
Distant snoring echoing up the shaft
Crystals humming when touched
A low, rumbling heartbeat from the deepest tunnels
smells: A sour, metallic taint from the deep nightmare seam
rooms: A mine entrance with a lift cage that descends into a shaft of glittering darkness.
A cart junction where rails split in a dozen directions and carts run without drivers.
A sleeping quarters where miners lie in bunks, dreaming dreams that leak into the walls.
A crystal gallery where veins of dream ore show visions of the past.
A sorting floor where ore is graded by colour and nightmare ore is discarded.

A grub nest where dream-eating larvae glow with stolen visions.
A chapel carved into rock where miners prayed for dreamless sleep.

Mine carts can be ridden down the rails; a DC {dc} Dexterity check steers to the chosen room, while failure crashes into a random one.

Waking a sleepwalking miner with a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check gives the party a guide who knows the tunnels.
The foreman's ledgers reveal the safe route through the collapse zone.
The chapel's prayer can be spoken to grant immunity to the mine's sleep effects for 1 hour.
Nightmare ore can be thrown as a weapon, forcing a creature hit to make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or be frightened for 1 minute.
hazards: Dream crystals underfoot burst with visions; a creature that steps on one makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is stunned for 1 round.
A cart runs away down the rails; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
The ceiling collapses in the collapse zone; creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage and are buried.

environments.name: Aqueduct City
environments.summary: A city built entirely on soaring aqueducts fed its people with water drawn from the sky, until the great reservoir broke its dam and the city was swept into an astral space. Now the arches stand above an endless flooded valley, water still running along stone channels that loop back into themselves. The city wants its water flowing, and the elementals that guard the channels drown anyone who blocks or diverts it.
readAloud: Stone arches tower around you, tier upon tier, each one carrying a channel of rushing water toward a distant city that clings to the top of the aqueducts. Below, a valley of still blue water stretches to the horizon, broken only by the tips of drowned towers. Rope bridges and narrow walkways connect the arches, swaying in a wet wind that smells of moss.

The sound of running water fills everything, a constant roar that drowns out your own footsteps. You stand on a walkway beside a channel wide enough to sail a boat, the water so clear you can see coins and bones glinting in the stone bed. A figure made of rippling water stands in the channel ahead, arms crossed, watching you with eyes of sunlit foam.

The portal drops you onto a plaza paved with wet stone, surrounded by houses carved into the sides of colossal arches. Vines heavy with white flowers drape every wall, drinking from leaking channels. A fountain in the plaza's centre spouts water that flows upward into a channel overhead, and the people sitting around it are statues covered in moss, their mouths open as if still drinking.

A drowned valley with towers poking above the surface
Rope bridges swaying between arches
Moss-covered statues of drinking citizens

sounds: The constant roar of rushing water

smells: Damp wood from the old water wheels

A sluice gate station where great iron gates are raised and lowered by chains.
A drowned plaza of moss-covered statues around an upward-flowing fountain.
A water wheel mill where the wheel turns endlessly, grinding nothing.
A cistern hall beneath an arch, a dark reservoir held up by pillars.
A rope bridge crossing between two tiers, with planks rotted and slippery.
A garden terrace where white-flowering vines have grown into the stone.

A water clock hall where flowing water measures hours that never change.

environments.name: Banquet Hall of the Dream Feast
environments.summary: A gluttonous lord held a feast so extravagant that he bargained with a fey court to make it last forever, and the hall now drifts in astral space with its banquet still being served. Every dish is perfect, every cup refills, and every guest who eats grows hungrier and more bound to the table. The hall wants guests, and it will feed them until they become part of the meal.
readAloud: Candles in a thousand silver holders light a hall of crimson and gold, its tables groaning beneath roast swans, glazed boars and pyramids of fruit that glisten like jewels. Guests in powdered wigs and rotting silks sit shoulder to shoulder, eating with their hands and laughing with full mouths. A servant in a fox mask pulls out a chair for you and says, 'You must be famished.'

The smell is overwhelming: roasted meat, spiced wine, honey cakes and cream. Platters slide along the tables on their own, and every time a guest empties a goblet, it fills again with a gentle chime. At the head of the hall, a vast man in a velvet coat stuffs a whole pheasant into his mouth, bones and all, and his eyes roll toward you with desperate hunger.

A course of soup arrives in front of you before you have even sat down, steam curling up in a shape like a beckoning finger. The guests nearest you have grown thin as twigs despite their endless eating, and their teeth are worn to stumps. Musicians on a balcony play a waltz that makes your stomach growl, and the walls drip with something like gravy.
sights: Tables groaning beneath roast swans and glazed boars
Pyramids of glistening, jewel-like fruit
Guests in rotting silks eating with bare hands

A distant, endless belch from the kitchens
rooms: A great feasting hall of endless tables, every seat filled but one per visitor.
A kitchen where fey cooks with long knives prepare dishes from unknown meat.
A wine cellar of barrels that whisper toasts and pour themselves.
A pastry room of cakes taller than men, iced with sugar roses that bloom.
A vomitorium where gorged guests purge so they can return to eat more.
A musician's gallery where a fey orchestra plays a hunger-inducing waltz.
A larder of hanging meats, some of them still twitching in their wrappers.
A cheese cave where great wheels of cheese have grown into a living ooze.
A dessert garden of candy trees and chocolate fountains.
A servant's corridor where masked fey whisper about the next course.
A guest's chamber where a sated sleeper is slowly sinking into a mattress of pudding.

environments.name: Cartographer's Living Map
environments.summary: A master cartographer spent her life drawing a map so detailed that it began to believe it was the land itself, and when she inked the final border, she and her map vanished into an astral space. Mountains are ink and folded parchment, rivers flow in blue pigment, and the monsters drawn in the margins hunt across the unfinished edges. The map wants to be complete, and it redraws itself around travellers, sometimes writing them in.
readAloud: The ground beneath you is parchment, faintly yellow and textured with grain, and the hills around you are folded paper shaded with crosshatched ink. A river of liquid blue pigment winds across the plain, and when you look down at your boots, you see that tiny letters have appeared beside you, spelling your name. In the sky, a great quill moves slowly, drawing the horizon as you watch.

A compass rose the size of a village square spins beneath your feet, its points glowing gold and silver. Beyond it, mountains drawn in sharp black lines rise against a sky of blank parchment, and in the margins at the edge of everything, enormous sea serpents and dragons drawn in faded ink stir and stretch. A label floats in the air above a distant forest: 'Here Be Monsters.'

You stand on a road drawn as a dotted line, and as you walk, the dots fill in behind you. A town ahead is nothing but a cluster of little sketched houses with tiny ink people moving inside. Wind sweeps across the map, rustling the paper like dry leaves, and somewhere in the folds, something huge drawn in red ink is tracking your path.

Hills of folded paper shaded with crosshatched ink
A river of blue pigment winding across the plain
A giant quill drawing the horizon in the sky
A compass rose spinning beneath your feet

Tiny ink people moving inside sketched towns

The crinkle of folded mountains shifting

A soft, endless voice reading place names aloud

rooms: A compass rose plaza where the four cardinal points glow and spin.
A sketched town of ink houses with tiny drawn inhabitants who wave.
A folded mountain range of paper peaks that crease and unfold as you climb.
A pigment river crossing, blue ink deep enough to drown in.

An eraser stone found in the cartographer's study can erase one hazard or creature drawn in ink, once.

Wind gusts flip pages of land; creatures on the edge of a region make a DC {dc} Strength save or are flung 30 feet into another region and take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Debtors' Counting House
environments.summary: A moneylender's counting house collected so many unpaid debts, sealed with spirit-coin contracts, that the weight of what was owed crushed it into an astral space. Debtors work forever at counting tables, their bodies slowly turning to copper and silver as they pay off what can never be paid. The house wants every account balanced, and it measures newcomers' worth to the last coin.
readAloud: The clink of coins fills the air, a thousand stacks being counted and recounted at once. Long wooden desks stretch away beneath a vaulted ceiling, and at each one sits a figure with copper-green skin, pushing coins from one pile to another with fingers worn down to the bone. A brass sign above the door reads: 'All Debts Must Be Paid.'

You step through onto a floor paved entirely with coins, pressed into the mortar like scales. Iron cages hang from chains overhead, each holding a debtor curled in a ball, and from every cage comes a whisper of numbers. A tall figure in a ledger-black coat steps forward, its face a brass abacus, beads clicking as it tallies you.

A great scale dominates the hall, its brass pans big enough to hold a cart, and on one pan sits a mountain of gold while the other holds a single sobbing man. Clerks with ink-stained hands run between the shelves of ledgers, stamping papers with seals that glow red. The air tastes of metal and dust, and somewhere a bell rings each time a coin is dropped.

environments.name: Puppet Theatre of Strings
environments.summary: A travelling puppeteer made marionettes so lifelike that a fey patron granted them life, at the price that their strings would always be pulled. The theatre now hangs in astral space, its puppets performing the same tragedy for an audience of empty seats while their maker dangles from strings in the rafters. The theatre wants new performers, and every visitor who enters finds silk threads quietly attaching to their wrists.
readAloud: Faded velvet seats rise in a curve around a small, ornate stage, its curtains drawn back to reveal a painted forest. Marionettes the size of children dance across the boards, their wooden faces fixed in expressions of joy and horror, and their strings vanish upward into darkness. A painted moon on a string bobs over the stage, and somewhere above, a voice laughs softly.

The portal drops you into a dusty wing beside the stage, where puppets hang limply on hooks, waiting their cue. One of them turns its head slowly toward you with a creak, glass eyes catching the lamplight. On stage, a puppet knight plunges a wooden sword into a puppet queen, and the queen weeps real tears as she falls.

You feel something brush your wrist, light as cobweb, and look down to see a fine silver thread rising from your skin into the shadows above. The theatre around you is dark except for a single spotlight on an empty stage. A marionette jester drops from above on its strings, lands before you, and bows: 'Places, everyone. The show is about to begin.'

environments.name: Bridge Across Nothing
environments.summary: A kingdom built a great stone bridge to connect two cliffs over a bottomless chasm, and when one cliff was swallowed by the dark, the bridge refused to fall and slipped into an astral space. It now stretches endlessly over a void, broken in places and patrolled by wyverns and wind spirits. The bridge wants to be crossed, and it tests travellers with every step toward an end that may not exist.
readAloud: A road of grey stone stretches out ahead of you, ten feet wide and bordered by low parapets carved with lions. On either side and below is nothing at all, only a soft grey void that swallows light and sound. Wind howls across the bridge, tugging at your cloak, and far ahead, a section has broken away entirely, its stones hanging in the air like loose teeth.

You stand at a toll gate on a stone bridge, its arch carved with the faces of kings. Beyond it the bridge continues into the mist, and every few hundred feet a tower rises from the span, banners snapping in the wind. A shadow passes overhead, wings spread wide, and a scaled shape screams as it dives toward the bridge.

The stones under your feet shudder, and pebbles fall from the edge into the void without a sound. Cracks run through the bridge's surface, glowing faintly blue as if wind spirits are seeping out of them. Ahead, the bridge rises in an arch higher than any mountain, and at its peak, something coiled and enormous waits for you.

Lion-carved parapets crumbling at the edges
Broken sections hanging in the air like loose teeth
Towers rising from the span with snapping banners

Stones grinding as the bridge shifts

The keystone can be loosened with a DC {dc} Strength check, causing the arch to tremble and the dragon to lose its grip, granting advantage on attacks for 1 round.

environments.name: Mausoleum of Kings
environments.summary: A dynasty of warrior kings built their tombs one atop another in a single hill, and the accumulated pride and grief of a thousand years broke the hill free into an astral space. Each king lies in a chamber guarded by his own soldiers and treasures, and each still believes himself the rightful ruler. The mausoleum wants a king to rule over all of them, and it crowns any intruder bold enough to sit a throne.
readAloud: A long hall of polished black stone stretches into darkness, lined on both sides by stone thrones, each holding a mummified king in crown and armour. Torches in iron brackets flare to life as you pass, one by one, and their light catches the gleam of gold on withered fingers. A deep voice rumbles from somewhere ahead: 'Who comes before the kings?'

Dust falls from the ceiling in slow streams as you step into a circular chamber ringed with stone sarcophagi. Each lid is carved with a king's face, stern and proud, and all of them have turned slightly toward you. Ranks of stone soldiers stand along the walls with spears at the ready, their eyes empty sockets filled with flickering light.

The air is cold and smells of dry spices and ancient linen. A staircase descends through tier after tier of tombs, each grander than the last, gold and lapis glinting on every wall. At the bottom, a great bronze door is carved with a single word in an old tongue, and a skeletal herald in a tattered tabard stands before it, waiting to announce you.

Torches flaring to life one by one
Stone sarcophagi with carved faces that turn
Ranks of stone soldiers with glowing eye sockets
Gold and lapis inlay on every wall
Banners of extinct dynasties, faded and rotting
A skeletal herald in a tattered tabard
A bronze door carved with a single ancient word
sounds: Torches crackling to life

A sarcophagus chamber ringed with carved lids that turn their faces.

The gilded chariots can be pushed down a slope to ram a door or enemy, dealing {dmg} bludgeoning damage.

environments.name: Nursery of the Sleeping God
environments.summary: Somewhere a newborn god was laid to sleep in a nursery built by faithful servants, and its dreams have grown so vast that they formed an astral space around the cradle. Everything here is soft, radiant and enormous, from blocks the size of houses to lullabies that shake the stars. The nursery wants the god to keep sleeping, and its guardians hush any intruder, sometimes forever.
readAloud: Golden light fills a vast round room, soft as dawn, and the floor gives gently beneath your feet like a quilted blanket. Toy blocks the size of houses are stacked in leaning towers, each painted with symbols that glow faintly. Far ahead, a crib of white wood rises like a castle, and from within comes the slow, deep breathing of something immense and sleeping.

A mobile of stars turns slowly above you, each star a burning sun on a silver thread, casting shifting shadows across the nursery walls. Winged figures in white robes glide between the toys, fingers to their lips, eyes wide and warning. The walls are painted with clouds and animals that move slowly, as if the painting itself is dreaming.

You step into a field of soft white fur that turns out to be the rug of a nursery so large that its walls are lost in the haze. A lullaby fills the air, sung by a voice that seems to come from the light itself, and your eyelids grow heavy. In the distance, a music box the size of a cathedral turns, and its tiny dancer is a figure with too many arms.

Toy blocks the size of houses, painted with glowing symbols
A crib of white wood rising like a castle
A mobile of burning stars turning overhead
Winged figures in white robes with fingers to their lips
Walls painted with dreaming clouds and animals that move
A rug of soft white fur stretching to the horizon
A cathedral-sized music box with a many-armed dancer

environments.name: Dollhouse of the Little Lady
environments.summary: A spoiled noble girl was given a dollhouse enchanted to keep her company, and when she wished never to grow up, the house swallowed her and her dolls into an astral space. Visitors arrive shrunk to the size of dolls, wandering painted rooms where porcelain servants act out the girl's whims. The house wants playmates who obey, and it repaints those who refuse into the furniture.
readAloud: You stand in a hallway with wallpaper of painted roses and a floor of glossy wooden planks that are each as wide as a road. A grandfather clock taller than a tower ticks beside you, its pendulum a slab of gilded tin. Through an open doorway, you see porcelain dolls sitting around a table set for tea, and as you watch, all of their heads swivel toward you with a soft click.

The portal shrinks you as it spits you out, and you tumble onto a carpet whose threads are as thick as rope. Towering furniture surrounds you: a velvet armchair like a hill, a lamp like a lighthouse, a bookshelf of tiny books bigger than your body. From somewhere above comes a girl's voice, bright and imperious: 'New dolls! Oh, you'll do nicely.'

A painted window shows a sunny garden that never changes, light falling across the parlour at the same angle forever. A porcelain butler with a cracked face bows stiffly and offers you a tray of sugar cubes. Behind him, a doll that looks almost exactly like a person you once knew sits motionless in a chair, its painted eyes wet.

A kitchen of tin pots and wooden food, with a doll cook who serves painted bread.
A nursery inside the nursery, with even smaller dolls that whisper.
A ballroom of mirrored floors where dolls waltz on brass pegs.
A library of tiny books with blank pages that fill with the reader's fears.

environments.name: Leech-Doctor's Surgery
environments.summary: A physician who believed every ailment lived in the blood bled his patients until the floors ran red, and his obsession with perfect blood fused his surgery with an astral space. Leeches the size of dogs crawl the walls, glass tubes carry blood through the building like a circulatory system, and patients lie bound to tables, kept alive but never healed. The surgery wants clean blood, and it will drain any visitor to get it.
readAloud: Glass tubes run along the ceiling and down the walls, carrying red fluid that pulses in a slow, steady rhythm like a heartbeat. A long hall of surgical tables stretches before you, and each holds a pale patient bound with leather straps, their arms dotted with glistening black leeches. A man in a stained apron moves among them, humming, tapping each patient's vein with a silver lancet.

The smell of iron is so strong it coats your tongue. Jars line the shelves of a narrow room, each one holding a leech swollen to the size of a melon, slowly pulsing against the glass. The floor drains through iron grates into a churning red channel below, and somewhere in the pipes, something very large and wet is moving toward you.

You step onto a tiled floor slick with something you do not want to name. A barber's pole spins slowly by the door, red and white stripes curling upward forever. A nurse with skin as pale as paper and lips stained crimson offers you a chair and a cup of something warm and red, and says gently, 'The doctor will see you now.'

Jars of melon-sized leeches pressing against glass
A spinning barber's pole by the door
Iron grates draining into a red channel
A surgeon's apron stiff with dried blood

Pale nurses with crimson-stained lips

environments.name: Gallows Square of the Endless Trial
environments.summary: A town square where a corrupt magistrate hanged hundreds of innocents became an astral space after the mob finally hanged him from his own gallows. The trials still happen every hour, the crowds still jeer, and the condemned still drop, rise and drop again. The square wants justice, but it no longer remembers what justice is, and it tries every newcomer for crimes they have never committed.
readAloud: Cobblestones slick with rain glisten under a sky of permanent grey dusk, and a crowd of grey-faced townsfolk packs the square, shouting and spitting. At the centre, a wooden gallows stands with a dozen ropes swinging, and on each one a figure kicks feebly. A bell rings, a voice booms 'Next!', and the crowd turns as one to look at you.

A judge's bench rises from the cobbles, carved with scales and skulls, and behind it sits a bloated figure in a powdered wig with a noose still around his neck. Before him, a ghostly prisoner pleads her case while the crowd chants 'Guilty, guilty, guilty.' The judge's eyes roll toward you, and he raps his gavel: 'Bring forward the accused.'

The portal drops you in the stocks. Wooden boards lock around your wrists and neck, and rotten vegetables fly at you from a jeering crowd. Behind them, crooked houses lean over the square with every window shuttered, and at the far end, the gallows waits with a fresh rope swaying gently in the wind.

Crows perched on every gallows beam

Families in the alley will help the party if promised justice, distracting the crowd at the right moment.

The crows on the rooftops can be fed to scatter them, creating a distraction that grants advantage on Stealth checks.

environments.name: Soul-Glass Furnace
environments.summary: A guild of glassblowers discovered that molten glass could hold a captured soul, and their furnace burned for centuries making lanterns that glowed with stolen life. When the last guildmaster threw himself into the fire, the workshop slipped into an astral space where the furnace blazes forever and souls glow trapped in every pane. The furnace wants fuel, and it sees every living thing as raw material for glass.
readAloud: Heat hits you like a wall, and the air shimmers with it. A great beehive-shaped furnace of brick dominates the workshop, its open mouth roaring with white-gold flame. All around you, glass shapes hang from chains and sit on shelves, lanterns and vases and orbs, and inside each one a tiny human figure presses its hands against the glass and screams without sound.

Blowpipes lean against the walls in iron racks, their ends crusted with glass. Glassblowers in leather aprons stand at their benches, but their faces are masks of melted glass and their eyes are tiny flames. One of them turns, a glowing bubble of molten glass on the end of its pipe, and breathes into it, and the glass swells into the shape of a screaming face.

A ceiling of stained glass panels glows from within, each one a scene of a person's life captured in molten colour. Sparks drift through the air like fireflies, and where they land on the floor, the stone fuses into glass. At the far end of the workshop, the furnace's mouth breathes in and out like a living thing, and in the white heart of its fire, something vast and shaped like a man is watching you.

environments.name: Cathedral of the Gale Organ
environments.summary: Pilgrims built an organ so grand that its pipes reached into the clouds, and when it was first played, the storm itself answered and carried the cathedral away into an astral space. The organ still plays with every gust, its notes shaping wind into living elementals and its music summoning angels of breath. The cathedral wants its hymn finished, and every intruder must either sing along or be blown away.
readAloud: Wind roars through a cathedral of white stone, so tall that clouds drift beneath its vaults. Organ pipes rise from the floor like a forest of silver trees, each one booming a different note as the gale passes through it. Light pours through windows that have no glass, only shimmering sheets of air, and in the light, winged figures turn slowly as if dancing.

You arrive in the nave, and the music hits you like a physical blow, pressing your ribs and humming in your teeth. The pews are gone, swept away long ago, and the floor is scoured smooth. A figure of whirling air drifts toward you, shaped like a singer with an open mouth, and from its throat comes a note so pure it makes your eyes water.

A console of white and gold keys sits on a high gallery, its keys pressing themselves in a slow, complex hymn. Behind it, pipes vanish upward into the clouds, and the wind they draw in is cold and smells of rain. Beneath the gallery, an angel with feathered wings stands guard, its eyes closed, its lips moving in a silent prayer that matches the music.

Clouds drifting beneath the vaulted ceiling
Windows of shimmering air instead of glass
Winged figures turning slowly in the light

A console of white and gold keys playing itself

Climbing into a pipe lets a creature ride the wind to another room, though it takes {half} thunder damage from the notes.

environments.name: Festival of Paper Lanterns
environments.summary: A riverside town held a lantern festival every year to send wishes up to the sky, and one year the wishes refused to burn out and carried the whole night into an astral space. Paper lanterns drift by the thousand above crooked streets, each one holding a wish that has grown a tiny fiery will of its own. The festival wants its wishes granted, and the lanterns will set the world alight to make them come true.
readAloud: Thousands of paper lanterns float above a town of crooked wooden houses, glowing in orange, red and gold against a sky of deep indigo. Each one has writing on its side in looping brush strokes, and as one drifts past your face you read: 'Let my brother come home.' The smell of fried dough and smoke fills the streets, and somewhere a drum beats a festive rhythm that never stops.

You step onto a wooden bridge over a slow black river, its surface covered with floating candles in paper boats. Revellers in fox and crane masks dance along the banks, waving sparklers that leave trails of fire in the air. A lantern swoops down to hover in front of you, its flame flickering like a face, and a high little voice from inside asks: 'Will you grant me?'

A great wind sweeps through the festival streets, and every lantern sways and tugs at its string, flames leaning hungrily toward the paper walls of the houses. Firecrackers pop in the alleys, and a dragon puppet made of silk and bamboo winds through the crowd, carried by a dozen dancers whose feet never touch the ground. On the highest hill, a bonfire burns taller than a temple, and everything drifts toward it.
