environments.name: Abandoned Menagerie
environments.summary: A collector of rare beasts kept them in a vast menagerie, feeding them on mana-rich meat until they grew strange, and when he vanished, the hunger of the starving animals tore the zoo loose into an astral space. The cages stand open, the beasts rule the paths, and plants have grown monstrous on the leftover feed. The menagerie wants a new keeper, and it tests every visitor to see if they are strong enough to feed the beasts or weak enough to be food.
readAloud: Wrought-iron gates stand open before you, rusted and draped with vines, and beyond them a gravel path winds between empty cages. A painted sign hangs crooked from a single nail: 'The Grand Menagerie, Beasts of All the Known World.' Somewhere among the trees a lion roars, deep and close, and the vines on the gate twitch toward the sound.

The portal drops you beside a moat around a stone island, and on the island a creature like a horse with bat wings stands in the grass, watching you with intelligent, hungry eyes. Signs along the path describe each exhibit, but the cages are bent open and the creatures within are gone. Bones lie scattered on the gravel, picked clean, and among them a keeper's cap with a name stitched inside.

You emerge in a glass aviary filled with jungle, the air hot and wet and loud with birdsong. Feathers float everywhere, and the branches overhead creak under the weight of something heavy and hidden. A rope bridge spans a pool of murky water where long shapes move, and a sign at its entrance reads simply: 'Feeding Time.'
sights: Rusted wrought-iron gates draped with vines
Empty cages with bent bars
Painted signs describing missing exhibits
A winged horse on a moated island

A glass aviary steaming with jungle growth

environments.name: Drake-Racing Hippodrome
environments.summary: A great racing stadium where riders raced fire-breathing drakes for glory and gold burned down in a final, legendary race, and the roar of the crowd carried it into an astral space. The race begins every hour, the drakes run hot and fast, and the stands fill with ghostly fans screaming for a winner. The hippodrome wants a champion, and it pushes every newcomer onto the track.
readAloud: A roar crashes over you as you step into a vast oval stadium, its stands packed with screaming spectators whose faces flicker like candle flames. Below, a sand track loops around a central spine of statues and obelisks, and at the starting gate, a row of drakes stamp and snort, smoke curling from their nostrils. A herald in a scorched tunic points directly at you and shouts: 'A new rider! Saddle them up!'

Heat rises from the track in shimmering waves, and the sand is black and glassy in places where fire has fused it. A drake thunders past you so close you feel the wind of its wings, its rider crouched low, and the crowd erupts in a frenzy. A banner bearing a burning wheel snaps overhead, and somewhere a bookmaker shouts odds you cannot understand.

You arrive in the stables beneath the stands, where drakes of every colour pace in stalls of iron and stone. A grizzled groom with burns across both arms looks up from oiling a saddle and grins with missing teeth. 'You're riding the red one,' he says, nodding toward a stall where a huge crimson drake is chewing the iron bars. 'No one's finished a race on her yet.'

environments.name: Cloud-Shepherd's Pasture
environments.summary: A gentle shepherd spirit herded clouds like sheep across the sky, and when she grew too old to tend them, the flock wandered into an astral space and made its own green pasture among the winds. Fluffy cloud-sheep graze on rainbows, storm-dogs guard the flock, and the pastures float on open sky. The pasture wants a new shepherd, and it will not let anyone leave until someone has proven they can bring the flock home.
readAloud: Green grass sways beneath your feet, but when you look down, you see that the meadow floats in the open sky with nothing beneath it but blue. Fluffy white creatures graze nearby, shaped like sheep but made of cloud, and they drift slowly as they eat. Wind whistles gently through the grass, and somewhere far away a shepherd's pipe plays a lonely tune.

The portal drops you onto a hill of soft turf beside a stone wall that ends in mid-air. A flock of cloud-sheep bleats softly as they part around you, their wool damp and cool against your skin. Beyond the wall, a storm cloud shaped like a huge dog prowls along the edge of the pasture, lightning crackling in its fur, and it watches you with eyes like thunderbolts.

A rainbow arcs across the sky and comes down in a field of glittering grass, where cloud-sheep crowd together to nibble at the colours. A small stone cottage sits on a floating island nearby, smoke curling from its chimney, and a shepherd's crook leans against the door. A gust of wind carries the faint sound of an old woman calling the flock home, but no one answers.

environments.name: Embassy of the Infernal Court
environments.summary: Devils once kept an embassy among mortals to negotiate contracts and trade in souls, and when a treaty was broken, the building burned and fell into an astral space with all its contracts still binding. Polite diplomats with horns and forked tongues still host receptions, and every conversation carries a clause. The embassy wants signatures, and it binds anyone who agrees to anything, however small.
readAloud: A grand marble hall glows with the red light of braziers, and polished floors reflect the gleaming chandeliers overhead. Elegant figures in silk and velvet mingle with wine glasses in hand, but their shadows have horns and their smiles are a little too sharp. A tall diplomat with ram's horns curled like a crown steps forward and bows: 'Welcome, welcome. Do sign the guestbook.'

Heat rises from vents in the floor, carrying the faint smell of sulfur beneath the perfume. Tapestries depicting treaties line the walls, each one bordered with tiny writing that shifts if you look too long. A brass butler with flame for eyes offers you a tray of hors d'oeuvres, and a card beside the tray reads in gold ink: 'By eating, you agree to the terms.'

You find yourself seated at a long negotiating table across from a woman with skin like ash and eyes like coals. A stack of contracts sits before her, and a quill made from a black feather rests beside your hand. 'Shall we begin?' she asks pleasantly. 'I think you will find our terms very reasonable.'

environments.name: Colosseum of the Crimson Oath
environments.summary: A warlord swore a blood oath to win a hundred duels in a single night, and when he fell on the ninety-ninth, the spilled blood of every fighter sealed the arena into an astral space. Gladiators who died there still fight on as bound champions, driven by a horned fiend who keeps the tally of every drop shed on the sand. The space wants the hundredth duel fought and won, and it will throw any newcomer onto the sand to finish the count.
readAloud: The roar of a crowd hits you before your eyes adjust. You stand at the edge of a vast oval of red sand ringed by tiered stone seats, every one filled with pale, flickering spectators who cheer without faces. Iron gates rattle on all sides, and from somewhere above a great drum begins to beat in time with your heart.

The sand under your boots is damp and clings like wet clay, staining your soles a deep red. Broken weapons jut from it at odd angles, and fresh tally marks are carved into a towering post at the arena's centre. The air smells of iron, sweat and hot oil from braziers that line the lowest wall.

A rumbling voice booms across the arena, counting slowly to ninety-nine and then falling silent. Across the sand, a gate grinds open on its own, and the crowd leans forward with a hungry murmur. Warm drops patter onto your shoulders from a clear sky, and when you touch them, your fingers come away red.

environments.name: Anvil of the Fallen Flame God
environments.summary: A god of fire and craft was cast down from the heavens, and where it struck the earth its dying heat hammered its own forge into an astral space. Fire elementals and half-finished iron servants still labour at the cooling anvils, while a fiend that crept in during the god's fall now works the bellows for its own ends. The space wants the god's last masterwork completed, and it measures every visitor as either a smith, a fuel or a raw material.
readAloud: Every breath you take is hot enough to sting. You stand on a black iron gantry above an enormous forge hall, where rivers of molten metal pour from cracked crucibles the size of houses. Far below, an anvil as large as a hill glows a dull cherry red, and the ringing of hammers echoes from every direction at once.

The gantry rail is warm and slick with soot under your hand, and ash drifts down like grey snow. Half-built iron figures stand in rows along the walls, some missing arms or faces, their chests open to show empty furnace hearts. A great bellows wheezes somewhere in the dark, and every time it breathes, the whole hall flares brighter.

The air smells of scorched iron, coal smoke and something faintly sweet, like burnt honey. Above the anvil hangs a colossal shattered crown of gold, each fragment slowly turning on chains as if still being worked. A voice too deep to be heard with your ears seems to murmur in your bones, asking what you have come to make.

environments.name: Scriptorium of Unending Flame
environments.summary: A great library caught fire while its keepers worked a forbidden spell to save their books, and the spell bound the blaze and the library together in an astral space. The books burn without ever turning to ash, tended by ghostly scribes who copy them as fast as they burn, and by paper constructs folded from pages that survived. The space wants every book preserved forever, and it sees any visitor as either a new copyist or a new page to be written.
readAloud: Light dances everywhere, orange and gold, and it takes you a moment to realise the shelves around you are on fire. Towering stacks of books blaze from floor to vaulted ceiling, but the flames do not spread and the pages never blacken. Between the shelves, pale figures in scorched robes sit at writing desks, scratching furiously with quills.

The heat on your face is real, though the burning books give off no smoke. Loose pages drift through the air like falling leaves, each edge glowing with a thin line of flame, and when one brushes your arm it leaves a warm tingle rather than a burn. Somewhere deeper in the stacks, a bell rings, and every scribe looks up at once.

The air smells of hot parchment, ink and candle wax. Under your boots, the floor is a mosaic of tiles inscribed with titles, and some of them are warm to the touch. A folded paper figure the size of a child steps out from behind a shelf, bows stiffly, and holds out a blank page and a quill toward you.

The ash vault's urns can be scattered into the flames of a burning book, letting that book finally rest and quieting the library for 10 minutes.
At the heart, finishing the keepers' spellbook with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check ends the fire and frees the library, banishing the Archivist without a fight.

The Archivist sets the reading room ablaze with a word; creatures in a 20-foot radius make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Chain-Pit Auction Yards
environments.summary: A slaver lord built a market where captives were forced to fight in pits so buyers could judge their worth, and the greed and despair of countless sales congealed the yards into an astral space. Shackled fighters, chained beasts and their cruel overseers still play out the old auctions, while a fiend auctioneer takes every bid in blood and years of life. The space wants to keep selling forever, and every newcomer is first appraised, then priced, then offered for sale.
readAloud: A gavel cracks like a whip the moment you arrive. You stand in a sunken yard of packed red earth, ringed by raised wooden platforms crowded with shadowy bidders who raise their hands and shout numbers. Below them, in rough pits lined with spikes, chained figures circle one another with makeshift weapons.

The iron collar of a broken shackle lies at your feet, still warm as if someone had just slipped it. Heavy chains run overhead in every direction, linking post to post and pit to pit, and they shiver and clink whenever anyone moves. A man in a stained leather apron looks you up and down, scribbles on a slate, and calls out a price.

The air smells of sweat, dung, cheap wine and rusted iron. Somewhere beyond the platforms an animal bellows in pain, and a whip cracks to silence it. On a high stage draped in red cloth, a tall horned figure leans over a lectern, smiling, and taps its gavel twice in your direction.

A horned auctioneer behind a lectern on a red stage

Perfume worn heavily by the bidders
rooms: A receiving gate of iron bars and heavy locks, where the portal glows above a pile of discarded shackles and tally slates.
The main auction yard, a sunken square of red earth ringed by bidding platforms and crossed by shivering chains.
A row of fighting pits lined with stakes, where chained captives are forced to duel while bidders shout their offers.
The holding pens, cramped wooden cages where weary captives sit in silence, each one tagged with a chalked price.
A beast kennel of iron stakes and straw, where chained bears, great cats and fighting hounds strain and snarl.
The appraisal room, a cramped office where an overseer measures teeth, muscles and scars before writing a price on a slate.
A branding chamber where a brazier of red-hot irons burns beside a ledger of every mark ever made.
The counting house, a vault of iron strongboxes where coins and vials of blood are tallied by grey-faced clerks.
An overseers' tavern where cruel guards drink sour wine, gamble on fights and argue over shares of the profits.
The bidders' gallery, a curtained balcony where shadowy buyers sip from goblets and sign contracts written in blood.
A buried chapel of chains, a forgotten shrine where captives once prayed and scratched names of home into the walls.
The heart, the auction stage, where the horned auctioneer Lord Gavel stands behind a red lectern and guards the bill of sale that binds every soul in the yards.
features: Captives can be freed; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check picks a shackle, and each freed fighter joins the party or causes chaos among the overseers.
The ledger in the branding chamber lists every captive; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the true name of anyone bound, which breaks their chains.
Bidders can be outbid; a creature that bids a year of its life gains a magical boon of the DM's choice, though the space never forgets the debt.
Overseers can be bribed or bluffed; a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check convinces one that the party are buyers, opening any locked door in the yards.
Chained beasts can be calmed; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check lets a creature free one, and it fights against its former captors.
The names scratched in the buried chapel can be read aloud; doing so grants every listening captive advantage on saving throws against fear for 1 hour.
At the heart, tearing the bill of sale with a DC {dc} Strength check or proving it fraudulent with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check frees every soul and shatters Lord Gavel's power.
hazards: Stakes line every fighting pit; a creature shoved or knocked into one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Overhead chains whip loose when the gavel falls; creatures in the yard make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Branding irons leap from the brazier at anyone who resists; a creature in the chamber makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Contracts in the bidders' gallery bind those who touch them; a creature that handles one makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or takes {half} necrotic damage as years of life are drained away.
The packed earth swallows the weak; a creature at 0 hit points in the yard makes a DC {dc} Constitution save each round or takes {half} necrotic damage as the ground drinks its blood.
Lord Gavel strikes his lectern and claims a price; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Reliquary in the Caldera
environments.summary: Pilgrims hid the bones of their saints inside an active volcano so no army could steal them, and their faith mixed with the mountain's fire to forge an astral space. The undead guardians who swore to protect the relics still keep watch, fire elementals swim through the magma channels, and an ancient dragon drawn by the holy light has claimed the deepest shrine as its lair. The space wants the relics kept safe and worshipped, and it welcomes only those who come as pilgrims.
readAloud: You emerge onto a narrow stone ledge inside the throat of a volcano. Far below, a lake of molten rock churns and glows, and carved into the walls around it are hundreds of niches, each holding a small golden casket lit by a steady flame. Pale armoured figures stand motionless at intervals along the ledges, their helmets bowed in prayer.

The rock under your hand is warm and faintly glowing, veined with seams of gold. Hot wind rises from below in slow breaths, carrying sparks that swirl up past you and vanish into the smoky dark above. Somewhere in the depths, a choir of hollow voices chants the same three notes over and over.

The air smells of incense, sulphur and hot stone. A path of worn steps spirals down the caldera wall, each step carved with a prayer and dipped in a groove by the knees of countless pilgrims. As you take your first step, one of the bowed guardians lifts its head, and its empty eyes fill with golden light.
sights: A lake of molten rock churning far below
Hundreds of niches holding golden caskets lit by steady flames
Pale armoured guardians with bowed helmets
Seams of gold glowing in the warm rock
Sparks spiralling upward into smoky darkness
Worn prayer steps spiralling down the caldera wall
Fire elementals swimming like eels through magma channels
A vast scaled shape coiled around the deepest shrine
sounds: A hollow choir chanting three notes
Magma bubbling and popping in the lake below
Hot wind sighing up the caldera walls
Armour creaking as guardians lift their heads
Rock cracking as it heats and cools
Slow, enormous breathing from the deep shrine
smells: A sharp scent of scorched metal
rooms: A pilgrims' ledge high on the caldera wall, where the portal glows above a basin of holy water that steams but never boils.
The prayer stair, a narrow spiral of worn steps carved with prayers, winding down past hundreds of glowing relic niches.
A guardians' barracks cut into the rock, where rows of armoured undead stand at attention around a cold, ash-filled hearth.
The ossuary gallery, a tunnel lined with carefully arranged bones of lesser saints, each skull crowned with a small flame.
A magma bridge, a narrow arch of blackened stone spanning a river of lava where fire elementals swim and leap.
The pilgrims' hall, a vaulted chamber where carved stone benches face an altar heaped with offerings of coins, ribbons and wax.
A forge of relics where golden caskets were once crafted, its anvils now cold and its tools hanging in neat rows.
The vow chamber, a round room where guardians knelt to swear their eternal oaths, their names carved in the glowing walls.
A collapsed crypt where an old eruption broke through, leaving relics half-buried in cooled lava and scattered gold.
The scriptorium of saints, a hall of stone tablets recording the miracles of each saint whose bones lie in the caldera.
An antechamber of light, where gold seams in the rock blaze so brightly that every shadow vanishes and eyes water.
The heart, the deepest shrine, where the ancient dragon Pyrevesper lies coiled around a towering golden reliquary and guards the bones of the first saint.
features: The holy water basin heals the faithful; a creature that drinks and prays regains 2d8 hit points once per day.
Guardians allow true pilgrims to pass; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check performing the proper rites lets the party walk the stair unchallenged.
The tablets in the scriptorium of saints describe each miracle; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check reveals a prayer that grants advantage on one saving throw.
Golden caskets can be opened, but each holds a saint's blessing; a creature that takes a relic gains a minor boon and the hatred of the guardians.
The cold relic forge can be relit; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check fanning its coals lets the party repair a damaged weapon or armour.
The vow chamber's walls accept new oaths; a creature that swears to protect the relics gains resistance to fire damage until it breaks its word.
Pyrevesper can be reasoned with; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check convincing the dragon that it too is a guardian ends the fight and earns its blessing.
hazards: Lava surges up from the lake without warning; creatures on the lower ledges make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The magma bridge cracks under heavy weight; a creature crossing it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Toxic gas vents from the collapsed crypt; creatures inside make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage and being poisoned on a failure, or {half} on a success.
The antechamber's light sears the unworthy; a creature that enters makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage and being blinded on a failure, or {half} on a success.
Prayer steps crumble beneath those who rush; a creature that dashes on the stair makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} bludgeoning damage from a fall.
Pyrevesper's breath fills the heart with holy fire; creatures in a 60-foot cone make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Vineyard of the Red Vintage
environments.summary: A vintner made a pact with a hungry fey lord to grow the finest wine in the world, watering his vines with the blood of travellers, and the curse that followed folded his estate into an astral space. The vines now grow fat on blood, their grapes red as rubies, tended by pale pickers who were once the vintner's guests and guarded by vines that move and grasp. The space wants every visitor to drink, to stay for the harvest, and to become part of the next vintage.
readAloud: Warm evening light falls across rolling hills striped with endless rows of vines. Each vine is heavy with fat grapes the deep red of rubies, and pale figures in straw hats move slowly between the rows, filling baskets without a word. On the highest hill, a grand stone manor glows with lantern light, and faint music drifts down toward you.

The soil under your boots is soft and dark and faintly damp, and when you kneel it leaves a red stain on your fingers. The vines sway gently though there is no wind, and a tendril curls lightly around your ankle before slipping away. A heavy, sweet perfume hangs over everything, so rich it makes your head swim.

The air smells of crushed grapes, fermenting wine and something coppery underneath. A smiling woman in a fine gown approaches along the path, holding out a silver tray of goblets filled to the brim with dark red wine. Behind her, the pickers have all stopped working, and every one of them is watching to see if you will drink.
sights: Endless rows of vines heavy with ruby-red grapes
Pale pickers in straw hats filling baskets in silence
A grand stone manor glowing with lantern light
Dark soil that stains fingers red
Vine tendrils curling and swaying without wind
Silver goblets brimming with dark red wine
Great oak casks stacked in shadowed cellars
Scarecrows dressed in the clothes of missing travellers
sounds: Faint music and laughter from the manor
Leaves rustling though there is no wind
Grapes bursting softly underfoot
Wine sloshing in great oak casks
A low, contented humming from the vines
Glasses clinking in a distant toast
smells: A coppery tang beneath the sweetness
Heavy, sweet perfume from the blossoms
rooms: A vine-wrapped gate at the foot of the hills, where the portal glows beneath an arch of grapes that drip red juice.
The lower rows, endless terraces of blood-fed vines where pale pickers silently fill wicker baskets with ruby grapes.
A press house where huge wooden presses crush grapes into troughs of dark juice that flows downhill in stone channels.
The scarecrow field, a row of figures dressed in travellers' clothes, their straw stuffing woven through with living vine roots.
An overgrown arbour where vines twist into a living tunnel, their tendrils reaching for anything warm that passes.
The pickers' cottages, a row of tidy whitewashed huts where pale workers sleep in their clothes beside empty baskets.
The manor's banquet hall, a long table laden with untouched food where smiling guests raise their glasses in an endless toast.
A barrel cellar, a cool vault of great oak casks where something heavy shifts inside each barrel when no one is watching.
The vintner's study, a cluttered room of ledgers, soil samples and a signed contract sealed in green wax.
A tasting room of carved panelling and dim candles, where a fey sommelier insists every guest sample each vintage.
The root crypt, a damp space beneath the manor where the oldest vines reach down and wrap the bones of the first victims.
The heart, the mother vine, a vast twisted trunk atop the hill, where the fey lord Merrow of the Harvest guards the vintner's cursed contract.
features: Drinking the red wine heals 2d8 hit points, but a creature that drinks must make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or become charmed by the space for 1 hour.
The pale pickers can be woken; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check reminding one of home lets it lead the party along a hidden path through the rows.
The scarecrows' clothes hold belongings of the lost; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check finds a useful item, such as a map, a ring or a vial of potion.
The vintner's study contains the curse's terms; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals that the contract ends if the vintner's own blood waters the mother vine.
The fey sommelier rewards good taste; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check naming a vintage's true ingredient earns a bottle that grants advantage on one Charisma check.
Salt from the manor's kitchens poisons the vines; scattering it on the soil makes the plants within 30 feet wither and stop grasping for 10 minutes.
At the heart, burning the contract or tricking Merrow with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check into rewording it breaks the curse and frees every picker.
hazards: Vines lash out at anyone who strays from the path; a creature in the rows makes a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being restrained on a failure, or {half} on a success.
Thorns along the arbour tunnel drink blood; a creature passing through makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The heavy perfume dulls the senses; a creature that spends 10 minutes in the vineyard makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or takes {half} poison damage and falls asleep.
Barrels in the cellar burst open when touched, releasing grasping undead; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The root crypt's soil pulls at the living; a creature that ends its turn there makes a DC {dc} Strength save or takes {half} necrotic damage as roots draw out its blood.
Merrow commands the mother vine to crush intruders; creatures within 20 feet make a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Monastery of the Sevenfold Prism
environments.summary: An order of monks spent generations grinding a single mountain crystal into a flawless prism, and when the final facet was polished, the light it gathered folded their monastery into an astral space. The monks still walk its halls, but each has been split into seven translucent copies of itself, one for every colour, tended by glass constructs that sweep up stray beams. The space wants every ray of light sorted, named and stored, and it sees intruders as muddled colour that must be broken apart.
readAloud: Light strikes you from every direction at once, and for a moment your own shadow splits into seven faint shapes of different colours. You stand in a cloister of clear crystal pillars, each one throwing bands of red, gold, green and violet across a floor polished like still water. Somewhere above, a low chant rises in seven voices that never quite agree on the note.

The air is cool and perfectly still, and it tastes faintly of chalk. A figure in pale robes glides past you, and behind it walk six more of the same monk, each tinted a different hue and each a half step behind the last. None of them look at you, but a slender glass figure with a broom of fine wire turns its blank face toward you and stops sweeping.

Your fingers brush a pillar and come away tingling, as if you had touched a struck bell. Narrow shelves line the walls, holding thousands of stoppered vials, each glowing with a single trapped colour. At the far end of the cloister, a great door of layered glass hums softly, and the light leaking around its edges is a white so pure it stings your eyes.
sights: Crystal pillars throwing bands of coloured light across the floor
Monks split into seven tinted copies walking in single file
Glass constructs sweeping stray beams into dustpans of silver
Shelves of stoppered vials each glowing with one colour
Your own shadow broken into seven faint, coloured shapes
A floor polished so smooth it reflects the vaulted ceiling
Prayer scrolls written in ink that shifts hue as you read
A sliver of white light leaking around a great glass door
sounds: A chant in seven voices that never settle on one note
The faint ringing of crystal pillars humming like struck bells
Wire brooms whispering across polished stone
Glass vials clinking softly on their shelves
Soft footsteps repeated seven times in a row
A deep, steady hum from behind the great glass door
smells: Beeswax from candles that are never lit
A clean, sharp scent like the air after lightning
Warm glass fresh from the grinding wheel
rooms: A crystal cloister where the portal shimmers between two pillars, splitting every arriving shadow into seven coloured shapes that fade after a few heartbeats.
The sorting hall, a long chamber of tilted mirrors where glass constructs catch stray beams and guide them into labeled channels cut across the floor.
A vial library, rows of tall shelves holding thousands of stoppered bottles, each one glowing with a single colour the monks have caught and named.
The grinding room, where great stone wheels still turn by themselves, polishing shards of crystal into lenses no bigger than a fingernail.
A refectory where seven tinted copies of each monk sit at seven separate tables, eating identical bowls of rice in perfect, silent unison.
The red dormitory, a narrow hall of cots bathed in crimson light, where the sleeping monks breathe slowly and dream of fire.
A meditation garden of glass flowers that open toward any lantern, their petals casting shifting rainbows over a pool of perfectly still water.
The lens gallery, a corridor of hanging lenses that focus light into a single burning point that slowly sweeps from wall to wall.
A scriptorium where the monks copy prayers in ink that changes colour with each word, and blotted mistakes are swept away as grey dust.
The bell tower, a spiral stair of crystal steps that chime when walked upon, rising to a bell that rings with light instead of sound.
An abbot's study, a plain room with a single window of clouded glass, holding a journal that records the day the monks first divided.
The heart, a domed chamber of pure white light where the Prism Abbot, a towering celestial woven from seven colours, guards the flawless crystal that made the space.
features: The vials can be uncorked; drinking one grants a minor effect tied to its colour, such as resistance to fire damage for red or darkvision for violet, for 1 hour.
The tilted mirrors in the sorting hall can be turned; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check aims a beam to open a sealed door or blind a construct for 1 round.
The monks will answer one question each if spoken to in the right colour of light; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check reveals which copy is willing to talk.
The abbot's journal names the colour the abbot fears losing; reading it with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Religion) check grants advantage on one attack or save against the Prism Abbot.
Glass lenses from the grinding room can be pocketed and used as a focus; a creature holding one can cast light at will while inside the space.
Ringing the crystal bell floods the monastery with light, waking every monk at once; a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check makes them kneel instead of attack.
hazards: The burning point in the lens gallery sweeps across the corridor; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Glass constructs shatter when destroyed, spraying razor shards; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The red dormitory's crimson light drags sleepers into fiery dreams; a creature that rests there makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or takes {half} fire damage and gains no benefit from the rest.
Crystal steps in the bell tower crack under heavy feet; a creature that falls makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The Prism Abbot splits light into a sevenfold blast; creatures in a 30-foot line make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Courier Road Through the Thunderheads
environments.summary: A guild of couriers once swore that no storm would ever stop the post, and the oath was spoken so many times at the same relay station that a living storm swallowed the road whole and kept it as an astral space. Phantom riders still carry sealed satchels along a road of packed cloud, while storm elementals and brass mile-markers enforce the schedule with cruel precision. The space wants every message delivered on time, and it treats intruders as either late couriers or stolen mail.
readAloud: Wind hits you so hard that you stagger, and rain stings your face like thrown gravel. You are standing on a road of packed grey cloud that winds away through towering thunderheads, lit from within by flickers of lightning. A brass post beside you, shaped like a man holding a lantern, swivels its head toward you and rings a small bell twice.

Hooves drum past close enough to spatter you with cold water. A rider in a sodden cloak gallops by on a horse made of churning mist, a leather satchel clutched to its chest, and is gone before you can call out. The air smells of wet leather and ozone, and somewhere ahead a horn blows three short notes.

Thunder rolls beneath your feet rather than above you, and you feel it in your teeth. Torn envelopes and sodden letters drift past on the gusts, some of them still sealed with red wax. Far down the road, through a gap in the clouds, you glimpse a squat stone relay station with a single window glowing gold.
sights: A road of packed grey cloud winding between thunderheads
Phantom riders on horses made of churning mist
Brass mile-markers shaped like men holding lanterns
Sodden letters and torn envelopes drifting on the gusts
Lightning flickering inside the clouds like distant lamps
A stone relay station with a single golden window
Wax seals scattered across the road like red coins
Wind-shredded banners bearing the sign of a winged boot
sounds: Hooves drumming on packed cloud
Thunder rolling beneath your feet
A post horn blowing three short notes
Small brass bells ringing from every mile-marker
Paper flapping and tearing in the wind
A distant voice calling out names from a list
smells: A sharp tang of cold rain
Smoke from a relay station hearth
rooms: A storm-lashed waypost where the portal flickers inside a ring of brass mile-markers, each one ringing its bell to announce your arrival.
The long straight, a stretch of cloud road so exposed to the wind that riders lie flat against their mounts to keep from being blown away.
A collapsed bridge of cloud over a sheer drop into churning storm, with a single rope line strung across for couriers brave enough to climb.
The sorting shed, a leaning wooden hut where phantom clerks stamp and bundle soaked letters, furious at every misplaced address.
A stable of mist horses, their stalls hung with dripping tack, where the beasts stamp and snort clouds of fog at anyone who enters.
The lightning cut, a narrow pass between two thunderheads where bolts leap back and forth across the road at a steady, deadly rhythm.
A wayside shrine to the patron of travelers, its offering bowl full of coins, horseshoes and the broken seals of letters never delivered.
The dead letter pit, a sinkhole in the cloud where undeliverable mail piles in a sodden heap, whispering the words written inside it.
A switchback climb up the side of a towering thunderhead, its cloud steps slick with rain and its edges crumbling into the gale.
The relay station, a squat stone house with a crackling hearth, where a ghostly innkeeper offers hot cider and asks every visitor for their papers.
A wreck of overturned mail coaches, their wheels still spinning in the wind and their lockboxes rattling with something that wants to get out.
The heart, the postmaster's tower at the eye of the storm, where the Storm Postmaster, a towering elemental in a courier's coat, guards the first undelivered letter.
features: A mist horse can be saddled with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check, doubling a rider's speed along the road for 1 hour.
Brass mile-markers answer questions about the road; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check convinces one to reveal a shortcut that skips a room.
Sealed letters can be read; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check sorting through them uncovers the address of the first undelivered letter and the Postmaster's true name.
The relay station's cider warms the body, granting temporary hit points equal to the drinker's level and advantage on saves against cold for 1 hour.
Carrying a satchel along the road marks a creature as a courier; phantom riders and mile-markers ignore it unless it stops moving for more than a minute.
Delivering the first letter at the heart with a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check can end the fight, as the Postmaster finally rests and the storm begins to clear.
hazards: Gusts sweep across the long straight; creatures on foot make a DC {dc} Strength save or are pushed 15 feet toward the edge and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
Lightning leaps across the lightning cut; a creature crossing it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The dead letter pit pulls at those who listen; a creature that hears its whispers makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or takes {dmg} psychic damage and is frightened for 1 minute.
Cloud steps on the switchback climb dissolve without warning; a creature that slips makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The mail coach lockboxes burst open, hurling a whirlwind of razor-edged paper; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The Storm Postmaster calls down a thunderclap; creatures within 20 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Hall of Frozen Lightning
environments.summary: A storm mage tried to catch a single bolt of lightning and hold it forever, and the instant the spell closed, it caught the whole storm and froze it into an astral space of still, crackling light. Lightning elementals stand locked mid-strike throughout the hall, while copper sentinels built by the mage patrol the gaps, keeping the frozen bolts perfectly in place. The space wants the instant to last forever, and anything that moves too fast threatens to set the storm loose.
readAloud: The hair on your arms rises and your teeth buzz in your jaw. You stand in a vast hall of black glass where bolts of lightning hang frozen in midair, branching from ceiling to floor like the roots of white trees. Each one gives off a faint, steady crackle, and the light they throw is so bright that your shadow looks painted on the floor.

The air smells sharp and metallic, like a coin held on the tongue. A figure of copper wire and glass bulbs clicks past you on spindly legs, its head turning to examine each frozen bolt as if counting them. When it reaches you, it stops, and a single spark jumps from its fingertip to your boot.

Everything here is still except you. Raindrops hang in the air like strung beads, and if you brush one it rolls away slowly before stopping again. Somewhere ahead, through the forest of frozen light, a deep rumble of thunder has been caught halfway through its first note, and it hums without end.
sights: Bolts of lightning frozen in midair like branching white trees
Raindrops hanging motionless like strung beads
Copper sentinels with glass bulbs for heads
Black glass floors fused by old lightning strikes
Elementals of crackling light locked mid-strike
Shadows that look painted onto the floor
A scorched workbench covered in copper coils
sounds: A steady crackle from every frozen bolt
A single note of thunder humming without end
Copper legs clicking across glass
Tiny sparks snapping between metal fittings
The slow patter of a disturbed raindrop rolling away
A high whine that rises whenever you move quickly
smells: A metallic tang like a coin on the tongue
rooms: A threshold of fused black glass where the portal crackles between two frozen bolts, their light throwing hard white shadows across the floor.
The forest of bolts, a vast hall where hundreds of frozen lightning strikes branch from ceiling to floor like the trunks of white trees.
A rain gallery where millions of motionless raindrops fill the air, so thick that walking through them leaves a tunnel shaped like your body.
The sentinel workshop, a cluttered room of half-built copper figures, coils of wire and glass bulbs waiting to be fitted with sparks.
A ball lightning chamber, where glowing spheres hover in neat rows like lanterns, each one humming a slightly different note.
The fused stair, a staircase melted into the glass by a single strike, its steps slick and glowing faintly from within.
A storm mage's study, a scorched room where the mage's notes are pinned to the walls beside a cracked jar that once held a single spark.
The caught thunder, a hollow chamber where one note of thunder has been trapped halfway, its endless hum shaking dust from the ceiling.
A copper conduit tunnel, a narrow crawlway lined with wires that carry sparks from the frozen bolts to the sentinels that guard them.
The cloud loft, a high gallery where the frozen storm clouds hang just overhead, close enough to touch, lit from inside by trapped flashes.
An elemental cell, a ring of copper rods holding a lightning elemental locked mid-strike, its face twisted in the instant of its capture.
The heart, the eye of the frozen storm, where the Bolt Warden, a vast elemental of living lightning, guards the stopped heart of the storm mage who caught it.
features: Frozen raindrops can be gathered in a flask; thrown, each one bursts like a thunderclap, deafening a creature that fails a DC {dc} Constitution save.
The mage's notes explain the binding; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check reveals that breaking the copper rods in the elemental cell weakens the Bolt Warden.
Moving slowly keeps the sentinels calm; a creature that takes only half its speed each turn has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks against them.
Ball lightning spheres can be carried carefully; a DC {dc} Dexterity check lets a creature hurl one as a ranged attack that deals 2d8 lightning damage.
The cracked jar in the study can hold one spark; a creature that captures a spark from a frozen bolt gains resistance to lightning damage for 1 hour.
Copper sentinels can be reprogrammed through their chest panels; a DC {dc} Intelligence check with tinker's tools turns one into a guide or ally.
Restarting the storm mage's stopped heart at the heart with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check can end the fight, as the storm finally finishes falling.
hazards: Brushing a frozen bolt releases its charge; the creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Moving too quickly wakes the storm; a creature that dashes makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save as the nearest bolt jumps toward it, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The caught thunder shakes the chamber; creatures inside make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success and being deafened on a failure.
The copper conduits carry live sparks; a creature crawling through makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} lightning damage.
The Bolt Warden lashes out in a chain of lightning; up to three creatures make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Garden of the Unending Dawn
environments.summary: A fey gardener once begged the morning never to end so her flowers would always be opening, and the dawn agreed, sealing her garden into an astral space where the sun is forever just rising. Sprites and pixies tend blossoms that bloom endlessly, while dew-soaked plant guardians and a celestial herald of morning keep the light from ever climbing higher. The space wants every visitor to stay for one more sunrise, and it gently forbids anyone from leaving before the flowers finish opening.
readAloud: Soft gold light spills over you, warm on one cheek and cool on the other. You stand at the edge of a sprawling garden where the sun sits low on the horizon, just cresting a line of distant hills, and every flower around you is caught halfway through opening. Dew beads on your sleeves and boots, and somewhere a bird begins the first note of a song.

The grass is wet and springy underfoot, and each step releases a sweet green scent. Tiny winged figures dart between the blooms, flicking dew from the petals with their fingers and giggling when it catches the light. One of them lands on your shoulder, peers into your ear, and announces in a high voice that you are just in time.

The first bird keeps singing its first note, over and over, and never reaches the second. Long shadows stretch across the garden paths, all pointing the same way, and none of them ever shorten. Far across the garden, on a low hill, a figure in robes of pale rose and gold stands with arms raised toward the sun, holding it exactly where it is.
sights: A sun forever cresting the distant hills
Flowers caught halfway through opening
Sprites flicking dew from petals with their fingers
Long shadows that never shorten
Dew beading on every leaf, blade and sleeve
Hedges shaped like sleeping people curled on their sides
Mist lying low and golden between the flowerbeds
A robed figure on a hill holding the sun in place
sounds: A bird singing the same first note over and over
Sprites giggling among the flowers
Petals creaking as they strain to open
Dew dripping from leaves in a slow, steady patter
A gentle voice humming a lullaby to wake by
Bees droning lazily over the blossoms
smells: A sweet scent of opening roses
Woodsmoke from a cottage chimney far away
rooms: A garden gate of woven willow where the portal glows in the morning mist, its hinges dripping with dew that sparkles gold in the low sun.
The waking lawn, a wide field of dewy grass dotted with sleepers who wandered in long ago and still lie smiling with their eyes half open.
A rose arbor, a long tunnel of climbing roses caught halfway through blooming, their thorns glistening and their petals trembling as you pass.
The sprite village, a cluster of tiny houses built inside hollowed gourds and pumpkins, where the sprites argue loudly about whose flowers are prettiest.
A sundial court, a circle of white stones around a great sundial whose shadow has rested on the same hour for as long as anyone remembers.
The hedge maze, a labyrinth of tall green hedges trimmed into sleeping shapes that turn slowly to watch anyone who hurries.
A dew pond, a shallow pool of collected morning dew so clear and bright that the reflection of the sun in it stings to look at.
The gardener's cottage, a little thatched house with a cold hearth, a rocking chair, and a basket of seeds that were never planted.
A morning glory wall, a cliff of climbing vines whose blue trumpets open and close like breathing mouths, exhaling warm, sweet air.
The orchard of first fruit, rows of trees heavy with blossoms and tiny green fruit that will never ripen because noon never comes.
A bridge of sunbeams over a misty stream, solid only where the light falls directly and gone wherever a shadow crosses it.
The heart, the dawn hill, where the Herald of Morning, a radiant celestial in rose and gold, holds the sun in place and guards the fey gardener's last unopened bud.
features: Dew from the dew pond heals; drinking a cupful restores 2d4 hit points, but a creature that drinks more than once in an hour falls asleep for 10 minutes.
The sprites trade gossip for sweets; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check earns directions through the hedge maze or a warning about the Herald.
The sundial can be turned; a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check moves its shadow forward an hour, briefly weakening the Herald's hold on the sun.
Sleepers on the waking lawn can be roused with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check, and each one woken shares a memory of the world outside.
Seeds from the gardener's basket can be planted; any seed sown in the space sprouts instantly into a small, harmless flower that marks the path behind you.
Offering the Herald a true sunset story with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check can end the fight, as it lowers its arms and lets the day go on.
hazards: The waking lawn lulls visitors to rest; a creature that lies or sits there makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or falls asleep and takes {half} psychic damage as its memories fade.
Rose arbor thorns lash at those who hurry; a creature that moves faster than a walk makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The sunbeam bridge vanishes under shadow; a creature on it when a cloud passes makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the fall on a failure or {half} on a success.
Morning glory vines exhale a dizzying sweetness; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Constitution save or take {half} poison damage and are poisoned for 1 minute.

The Herald of Morning flares with the light of dawn; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success and being blinded on a failure.

environments.name: Aerie of the Carrier Swifts
environments.summary: A lonely bird keeper on a windswept cliff trained thousands of messenger swifts, and the longing in every message they carried gathered in the rookery until it lifted free of the world as an astral space. Swarms of swifts still dart through its spiraling towers, tended by fey keepers who read every message aloud, while a great hawk-beast hunts any bird that strays. The space wants every message answered, and it sends its birds circling after visitors until they reply.
readAloud: A gust snatches your breath and thousands of wings explode into the air around you. You stand on a wooden platform lashed to the side of a towering spire of stone and timber, one of dozens rising from a sea of cloud. Swifts pour from holes in every tower, wheeling in great dark spirals and crying in high, piercing voices.

The platform sways under your feet, creaking against its ropes. Every bird that darts past you carries a tiny rolled scroll tied to its leg with coloured thread, and some of them land on the railing to stare at you, head tilted, as if waiting for something. A small figure with feathered hair and bright amber eyes climbs up a rope ladder and holds out an empty hand toward you.

The air smells of feathers, guano and cold wind. Rope bridges sag between the towers, strung with hundreds of fluttering paper messages pinned like laundry. Overhead, a vast shadow passes across the clouds, and every swift in the sky falls silent at once before scattering.
sights: Spiraling towers of stone and timber rising from cloud
Swifts pouring from holes in every tower
Tiny scrolls tied to bird legs with coloured thread
Rope bridges strung with fluttering paper messages
Fey keepers with feathered hair and amber eyes
A vast winged shadow sliding across the clouds
Nests built from shredded letters and string
sounds: Thousands of wings beating at once
High, piercing cries of wheeling swifts
Ropes creaking as platforms sway
A fey voice reading a message aloud
Paper fluttering on strings in the wind
A distant screech that silences every bird
rooms: A swaying landing platform lashed to a stone spire, where the portal glows beneath a roof of nesting swifts that burst into flight as you arrive.
The great roost, a hollow tower lined from floor to peak with tiny nesting holes, each one occupied by a swift clutching a message.
A rope bridge strung between two towers, hung with hundreds of fluttering paper messages that tug and rattle in the constant wind.
The reading loft, where fey keepers sit in a circle untying scrolls from bird legs and reading each message aloud to an empty chair.
A seed store, a dusty chamber of sacks and bins where fat, sleepy swifts gorge themselves and squabble over the last handfuls of grain.
The keeper's cottage, a crooked shack perched on the highest spire, holding a cold stove, a bundle of unsent letters and a single empty cage.
A fallen tower, its upper half snapped and dangling by ropes, swinging slowly over the clouds like a pendulum with nests still clinging to it.
The training gallery, a long open hall where fey keepers release young swifts through rings of wicker to teach them to fly true.
A nest of letters, a tangled mound of shredded paper, thread and feathers where hatchlings peep from among a thousand torn words.
The hunting ledge, a bare outcrop littered with feathers and tiny bones, where the great shadow lands to tear apart the birds it catches.
An updraft chimney, a narrow shaft of rushing air between three towers that carries anything light enough straight up toward the sky.
The heart, the high eyrie, where the Message Eater, a monstrous hawk with a crown of swallowed scrolls, guards the bird keeper's final unanswered letter.
features: Writing a reply to any message and tying it to a swift makes that bird a loyal guide, leading the party to one room of their choice.
The fey keepers trade secrets for news of the outside world; a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) check earns a warning about the Message Eater's habits.
Swifts can be called with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check, forming a swarm that grants half cover to one creature for 1 minute.
The updraft chimney can carry a creature upward; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check lets it ride the air safely to any higher platform.
The unsent letters in the keeper's cottage name the person the keeper wrote to; speaking that name aloud makes the Message Eater hesitate for 1 round.
Reading the final letter aloud at the heart and answering it with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check can end the fight, as the hawk lets the letter fly free.
hazards: Rope bridges snap in strong gusts; a creature crossing makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from a fall to a lower platform on a failure or {half} on a success.
Startled swarms burst from the roost; creatures caught in them make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage from beaks and claws on a failure or {half} on a success.
The fallen tower swings without warning; a creature on or near it makes a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The updraft chimney flings careless climbers skyward; a creature that enters without care makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is hurled 30 feet up and takes {half} bludgeoning damage on landing.
The Message Eater dives from above; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Sunward Chariot Circuit
environments.summary: Every dawn for a thousand years, sun priests raced golden chariots across the sky to prove whose god deserved to carry the sun, and the blazing pride of those races burned a lap of the sky loose into an astral space. Fire elementals now pull the chariots, while flaming horses and celestial charioteers circle a track of molten gold that never cools. The space wants a champion who can finish the final lap, and it drags every newcomer into the race whether they wish to run or not.
readAloud: Heat slams into you, and the light is so fierce you have to shield your eyes. You stand on a ledge of white stone above a vast oval track of glowing gold, curving away through a sky of blazing orange cloud. Something thunders past below you, a chariot of polished brass pulled by two horses made of fire, and the wind of its passing singes your eyebrows.

The stone beneath you is hot through your boots, and the air ripples like water. Tiers of empty seats ring the track, every one scorched black, and banners of red and gold snap overhead though there is no breeze. A gleaming figure in a winged helm leans from a passing chariot, points at you, and shouts a single word you somehow understand: race.

The smell of hot metal and burnt hay fills your nose. Along the inside of the track, great bronze statues of horses rear on their hind legs, each one glowing as if newly cast. At the far end of the circuit, a gate of pure light opens and closes in a steady rhythm, and each time it opens a wave of heat rolls across the whole sky.
sights: A track of molten gold curving through orange clouds
Brass chariots pulled by horses made of fire
Celestial charioteers in winged helms
Tiers of empty seats scorched black
Red and gold banners snapping without wind
Bronze horse statues glowing as if newly cast
A gate of pure light opening and closing at the far end
Heat ripples twisting the air above the track
sounds: Hooves of fire thundering on gold
Chariot wheels screeching around the bends
The roar of a crowd that is not there
Banners snapping and cracking overhead
A charioteer shouting the word race
A great bronze gong sounding each lap
smells: A dry, smoky scent like a forge
rooms: A starting ledge of white stone above the track, where the portal glows beside a row of empty chariots waiting for drivers.
The stables of flame, a long hall of brass stalls where horses of living fire stamp and toss manes that shed sparks across the floor.
A chariot workshop, a sweltering forge where elementals hammer cracked wheels back into shape and polish brass until it shines like the sun.
The first bend, a sharp curve of molten track lined with the wrecks of chariots that took it too fast and burned away.
A spectators' gallery of scorched stone seats, where faint outlines of burnt-away watchers still sit in silent, cheering poses.
The priests' box, a shaded balcony of red silk awnings, where the old race records are carved into a wall of beaten gold.
A lap of falling cloud, a stretch of track that dips through the orange sky and dissolves into wisps behind every passing wheel.
The prize hall, a gleaming vault where laurels of golden leaves rest on velvet cushions beside the cracked helms of fallen champions.
A shrine to the unnamed sun, a circle of mirrors around a bowl of white fire, where racers once prayed for speed before the race.
The back straight, a long run of track where the heat is so intense that the air shimmers and racers see false roads branching away.
An infield pasture of golden grass, where retired fire horses graze on embers and watch the race with dull, smoldering eyes.
The heart, the finishing gate of pure light, where the Sun Champion, a blazing celestial driving a chariot of fire, guards the reins that once steered the sun.
features: A chariot can be claimed and driven; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check keeps the fire horses under control for one lap of the circuit.
The race records in the priests' box name every champion; a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check reveals the Sun Champion's one defeat and how it happened.
Golden laurels from the prize hall grant resistance to fire damage for 1 hour to the creature that wears one, but the charioteers will challenge that creature to race.
Praying at the shrine with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check grants a blessing of speed, adding 10 feet to the creature's speed for 1 hour.
Retired fire horses in the infield can be befriended with an offering of embers, becoming mounts that do not burn their riders.
Beating the Sun Champion to the finishing gate in a race, decided by a contest of DC {dc} Dexterity or Animal Handling checks, can end the fight with the Champion's bow.
hazards: The molten track burns anyone who touches it; a creature that enters it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Racing chariots trample anything in their way; a creature on the track makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save as one passes, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The lap of falling cloud dissolves underfoot; a creature that stops moving there makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the fall on a failure or {half} on a success.
The back straight's heat mirages lure racers off course; a creature that follows one makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or drives off the edge and takes {half} fire damage.
Fire horses in the stables kick out at strangers; a creature that walks behind one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The Sun Champion's chariot leaves a trail of white flame; creatures in its 60-foot path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Ink-Flooded Scriptorium
environments.summary: A monastery of copyists spent generations transcribing forbidden spells, until one night every inkwell overflowed at once and the spilled magic sealed the scriptorium into an astral space. The dead scribes still bend over their desks, quills scratching, while living pools of ink crawl between the shelves and hungry paper constructs fold themselves out of unfinished pages. The space wants its great book completed, and it believes the last missing words can be written in the blood and memories of visitors.
readAloud: Your boots splash into cold black liquid that rises to your ankles and clings like oil. Long rows of slanted writing desks stretch into the gloom, and at every desk sits a hunched, grey-robed figure scratching endlessly with a quill. None of them look up, but the scratching quickens as you step forward.

The air is thick and bitter with the smell of oak gall and wet parchment. Pages drift down from somewhere far above like slow, heavy snow, each one covered in cramped writing that shifts when you try to read it. Somewhere in the dark a page tears with a sound like a sharp breath.

The walls are shelves, and the shelves climb out of sight, loaded with books whose spines ooze black drops onto the floor. Ripples move across the ink around you against the current, as if something beneath the surface is swimming toward your warmth. Your fingertips are already stained, and the stain is slowly spelling out your name.
sights: Ankle-deep black ink flooding the stone floor
Dead scribes in grey robes writing without pause
Pages falling from the darkness like heavy snow
Shelves rising out of sight with books weeping ink
Ripples moving against the current toward warmth
Paper figures folding and unfolding in the corners
Ink stains on skin that slowly form letters
A colossal open book chained to a lectern far ahead
sounds: Hundreds of quills scratching in uneven rhythm
Wet pages slapping onto the flooded floor
A dry rustle like paper wings unfolding
Ink dripping steadily from shelf to shelf
A low voice reciting words that never quite resolve
The tearing of a single page somewhere in the dark
smells: Candle smoke from tapers long burnt out
A bitter tang of spilled alchemical reagents
Dust from books no one has opened in centuries
rooms: A flooded vestibule where the portal shimmers above a font brimming with ink instead of holy water.
The copying hall, an endless aisle of slanted desks where dead scribes write in silent, tireless rows.
A drying loft strung with thousands of damp pages, each one whispering the line written upon it.
The bindery, where stitched leather and bone needles hang from hooks over a vat of simmering glue.
An illuminator's chapel lit by gold leaf that glows faintly on painted pages of impossible creatures.
The forbidden stacks, a locked cage of iron shelving where chained books strain against their clasps.
A sunken reading pit where the ink pools waist deep and something large circles beneath the surface.
The abbot's cell, a narrow room of confessions scrawled across every wall in a shaking, frantic hand.
A paper nest built from shredded manuscripts, where folded constructs gather and rebuild one another endlessly.
The pigment store, shelves of crushed minerals and beetle shells beside mortars still dusted with bright colour.
A spiral stair of stacked books climbing into darkness, with loose pages that shift underfoot like scree.
The heart, the great lectern, where the ink-drowned abbot grown into a vast black ooze guards the unfinished grimoire chained to its stand.
features: The dead scribes ignore the living unless interrupted; a creature that takes up a quill and writes beside them with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check learns the location of the forbidden stacks' key.
Falling pages occasionally carry spell fragments; a creature that catches one and succeeds on a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check can cast a random 1st-level wizard spell from it once.
Ink stains that spell a creature's name can be scrubbed off with holy water or salt; a creature left marked has disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks against the space's inhabitants.
The abbot's cell holds his final confession; reading it aloud at the heart with a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check stuns the abbot for 1 round as he remembers who he was.
Gold leaf in the illuminator's chapel can be peeled away; a creature holding a sheet sheds dim light that ink creatures refuse to enter.
The pigment store's minerals can be mixed into a paste; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) or alchemist's supplies check makes a salve that grants resistance to acid damage for 1 hour.
Writing a false ending in the grimoire with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check convinces the space it is complete, collapsing it gently and opening the way home.
hazards: Living ink surges up from the floor; a creature standing in it makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is grappled and pulled under, taking {dmg} acid damage each round until freed.
Paper constructs swarm from the nest in a storm of edges; creatures in a 15-foot radius make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Chained books in the forbidden stacks snap open and shriek their contents; a creature within 20 feet makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The book stair collapses into a slide of tomes; creatures on it make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The simmering glue vat in the bindery splashes when disturbed; a creature nearby makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage and being restrained on a failure, or {half} on a success.

The abbot exhales a wave of black spray at the heart; creatures in a 30-foot cone make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} acid damage and being blinded until the end of their next turn on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Tower Folded Inward
environments.summary: An ambitious wizard tried to fit an entire tower into a pocket of space so it could travel with her, and when the spell slipped the tower folded in on itself and became an astral space. Its rooms now connect at wrong angles, her apprentices are trapped in loops of their last afternoon, and things from the gaps between folds have crept in to feed on the confusion. The space wants to unfold, and it will tear apart anyone who stands in the wrong place when a fold snaps straight.
readAloud: You step through the portal onto a staircase that runs up the wall beside you, and your stomach lurches as you realise you are the one standing sideways. Doors hang on the ceiling, windows open onto other rooms of the same tower, and a bookcase drifts slowly past at eye level. The air hums like a struck tuning fork.

Through a window you see yourselves from behind, a few seconds ago, stepping through the portal. A young apprentice in a scorched robe hurries past carrying a tray of teacups, apologises to you, and walks straight up a wall. Moments later she hurries past again, carrying the same tray, offering the same apology.

Everything smells faintly of ozone and burnt sugar, the scent of magic run too hot. When you touch the wall it feels like folded cloth, thick and soft at the creases, and you can feel something on the other side pressing back. Far above or below, hard to say which, a great brass orrery clanks as its rings spin out of time.
sights: Staircases running up walls and across ceilings
Windows looking into other rooms of the same tower
Apprentices repeating the same few minutes again and again
Furniture drifting slowly through the air
Creases in the walls like folded cloth
A brass orrery spinning out of time
Pale, many-jointed shapes slipping between the folds
Your own reflection arriving a few seconds late
sounds: A constant hum like a struck tuning fork
Teacups rattling on a tray carried past again
Doors opening somewhere above and closing somewhere below
The clank and grind of an orrery out of time
Wet clicking from inside the creases of the walls
Your own footsteps echoing before you take them
smells: A sour whiff of spoiled spell components
rooms: A sideways landing where the portal hangs on what was once the floor and stairs climb in every direction.
The looped kitchen, where an apprentice brews the same pot of tea forever while the kettle shrieks on cue.
A library folded in half, so that its two walls of shelves meet overhead like the pages of a closing book.
The orrery chamber, a hollow sphere where brass rings the size of wagons spin around a captured fragment of starlight.
An apprentice dormitory where beds hang from every surface and sleepers mumble the same words at the same moment.
The crease, a narrow seam between rooms where the walls press close and something pale moves in the folds.
A summoning hall with a chalk circle drawn across the floor, wall and ceiling, unbroken by the impossible angles.
The familiar's roost, a room of perches where a brass owl construct counts every visitor aloud in a cracked voice.
A window gallery of a hundred panes, each one showing a different room of the tower at a different moment.
The laboratory, where half-finished experiments bubble on benches and a dropped flask has frozen mid-shatter in the air.
A broken staircase that loops back to its own bottom step no matter how far or fast anyone climbs.
The heart, the folded study, where the wizard, now a twisted aberration of overlapping selves, guards the spell scroll that could unfold the tower.
features: Gravity follows whichever surface a creature last touched with both feet; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check lets a creature leap between surfaces safely as part of its movement.
The looping apprentices can be broken out of their loop; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check made at the exact moment of their repeated apology wakes one, who can map the tower.
Windows in the gallery can be climbed through; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check picks the right pane and moves the party to any room they have seen.
The brass owl knows every visitor's arrival time; asking it nicely, or a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check of its gears, reveals where the folds will next snap straight.
The frozen flask in the laboratory holds a potion of speed caught mid-spill; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check collects it intact.
The chalk circle in the summoning hall still works; a creature standing within it cannot be moved by the space's folds.
Reading the spell scroll at the heart with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check unfolds one layer of the wizard's selves, giving her disadvantage on all attacks for 1 minute.
hazards: A fold snaps straight without warning; creatures caught in the seam make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} force damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The orrery's rings sweep through the chamber; a creature crossing it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Pale things in the crease lash out from the folds; a creature passing through makes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check or takes {dmg} piercing damage from hidden mouths.
Drifting furniture changes direction when gravity flips; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The looping staircase drains the climber; a creature that climbs it for more than a minute makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
The wizard's overlapping selves cast at once at the heart; creatures in a 20-foot radius make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} force damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Hall of Whispered Confessions
environments.summary: For centuries the faithful of a mountain monastery whispered their sins into stone grilles, and a lesser devil learned to drink each secret before it reached the priests, until the accumulated guilt sealed the hall into an astral space. The ghosts of penitents still kneel in the booths repeating sins they were never forgiven, while hooded monks who serve the devil collect fresh secrets from anyone who enters. The space wants every visitor to confess, and it grows stronger with each secret spoken inside it.
readAloud: You arrive in a long, vaulted hall lit only by red votive candles set into niches along the walls. Rows of narrow wooden booths line both sides, each with a carved stone grille, and from every grille comes a soft, steady whisper. The words are too faint to catch, but every one of them sounds ashamed.

The floor beneath you is worn into shallow hollows by countless kneeling knees, and the stone feels cold and slightly damp. Incense hangs heavy in the air, sweet and cloying, and under it lies the sour smell of old sweat and fear. A hooded figure at the far end of the hall lifts its head and beckons you forward with one pale hand.

As you walk, the whispers change. You begin to hear your own voice among them, quiet and clear, speaking things you have never told anyone. The candle flames lean toward you, and somewhere behind the grilles something sighs with deep contentment.
sights: Rows of narrow wooden confession booths with stone grilles
Red votive candles flickering in wall niches
Floors worn into hollows by kneeling penitents
Ghostly penitents bent forward in the booths
Hooded monks with pale hands and hidden faces
Candle flames leaning toward the living
Wax tablets covered in scratched-out names
A great iron grille at the far end glowing faintly red
sounds: A ceaseless murmur of ashamed whispers
Your own voice whispering your secrets
Rosary beads clicking in unseen hands
A deep, contented sigh from behind the grilles
Soft sobbing from a distant booth
Bare feet shuffling on cold stone
smells: A faint whiff of sulphur behind the incense
rooms: A candlelit narthex where the portal glows above a basin of grey water that reflects faces of strangers.
The confession nave, a long vaulted hall lined with booths that whisper sins in a hundred hushed voices.
A penitent's cell where a ghost kneels on broken glass, repeating the same terrible secret to an empty grille.
The scriptorium of secrets, where hooded monks write down every whisper on wax tablets stacked to the ceiling.
An ossuary chapel whose walls are built from the skulls of priests who heard too much and kept silent.
The scourging room, a bare chamber of hooks and knotted cords where monks punish themselves for forgetting secrets.
A bell loft where a cracked bronze bell rings once for every new confession spoken anywhere in the hall.
The silent garden, an enclosed courtyard of grey roses where speaking aloud draws the gaze of every monk.
A sealed reliquary holding a saint's tongue in a jar, the one relic the devil has never been able to touch.
The abbot's parlour, a warm and comfortable room with wine and cushions, where the false abbot entertains favoured penitents.
A crypt of the unforgiven, rows of open coffins where restless dead rise and plead for absolution.
The heart, the great grille, where the devil Confessor waits behind red-hot iron, guarding a chalice brimming with every secret it has drunk.
features: Each booth whispers one secret; a creature that listens closely with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check learns a useful truth about the hall or one of its monks.
Confessing a true secret aloud in a booth grants inspiration, but the devil learns it and gains advantage on its first attack against that creature.
The wax tablets in the scriptorium can be searched; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a tablet bearing the devil's true name, which grants advantage on saves against its powers.
The saint's tongue in the reliquary can be carried; while held, a creature cannot be compelled to speak and is immune to being charmed.
The unforgiven dead can be granted peace; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check spent listening to one's sin lays it to rest and earns a blessing of +1d4 to one save.
The false abbot can be flattered or deceived; a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check convinces him the party are new acolytes, earning safe passage to the heart.
Pouring the chalice out at the heart frees every secret at once; this weakens the Confessor, which loses its resistances until the end of the fight.
hazards: The whispers grow overwhelming; a creature that spends more than an hour in the nave makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
