Broken glass and hidden barbs line the penitent's cell floor; a creature that kneels or falls there makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} piercing damage.
The cracked bell rings when a secret is spoken; creatures in the bell loft make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Speaking aloud in the silent garden wakes the grey roses; a creature there makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage from whipping thorns on a failure or {half} on a success.
The knotted cords of the scourging room animate and lash out; creatures entering make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The Confessor exhales burning guilt through its grille; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Orphanage of the Long Night
environments.summary: A cruel matron ran a foundling house where children were locked in the dark as punishment, and when a fire killed them all on the longest night of the year, their shared terror sealed the building into an astral space. The ghosts of the children still hide in cupboards and under beds, while the things they once imagined in the dark have taken real, crawling shape in the corridors. The space wants a grown-up who will finally keep the children safe, and it punishes every adult who fails them.
readAloud: You stand in a narrow hallway with peeling green wallpaper, lit by a single guttering candle on a hook. Small iron beds line the walls of the room beyond, each with a thin grey blanket pulled up over a lump that does not move. Somewhere upstairs a child is counting slowly, the way children count in a game of hide and seek.

The floorboards creak under your weight and the air is cold enough to see your breath. It smells of carbolic soap and boiled cabbage, and under that, faint but unmistakable, old smoke. A tiny handprint in soot appears on the wall beside you, and then another, as though someone invisible is walking alongside you.

Every door in the hallway has a lock on the outside. Behind one of them you hear small fists knocking, and a thin voice asks if it is morning yet. When you look back the way you came, the candle has gone out, and the darkness there is breathing.
sights: Peeling green wallpaper and a single guttering candle
Rows of iron beds with grey blankets over still shapes
Small sooty handprints appearing on the walls
Doors locked from the outside
Crayon drawings of tall, thin things with long arms
Children's faces peering from cupboards and then vanishing
A rocking horse moving on its own in an empty room
Darkness that pools and breathes in the corners
sounds: A child counting slowly upstairs
Small fists knocking on a locked door
Floorboards creaking under unseen feet
A thin voice asking if it is morning yet
The jangle of a heavy ring of keys
Something breathing in the dark behind you
rooms: A cramped entrance hall where the portal glows inside a cold hearth, and coat hooks hold tiny rotting coats.
The dormitory, a long room of iron beds where small shapes lie under blankets and never quite stop breathing.
A punishment cupboard under the stairs, its door scratched from the inside by small fingernails, its darkness far deeper than it should be.
The schoolroom, rows of tiny desks facing a slate board where a lesson on obedience writes itself in chalk.
A playroom of broken toys, where a rocking horse sways alone and a dolls' tea party waits for its guests.
The scullery, a steaming kitchen where a ghostly cook stirs a vat of grey porridge that never runs out.
A burnt attic, its rafters blackened and open to a starless sky, where the fire first caught that night.
The matron's office, a tidy room of ledgers and switches, where a heavy ring of keys hangs on a nail.
An infirmary of narrow cots and empty medicine bottles, where a little ghost asks every visitor to check her fever.
The cellar, a damp pit beneath the floor where the dark things the children imagined lie coiled and waiting.
A long corridor of locked doors, behind each one a different child knocking and asking to be let out.
The heart, the matron's bedroom, where the burnt matron, now a fiend of smoke and keys, guards the ring that locks every child in.
features: The children's ghosts trust gentle adults; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) or Charisma (Persuasion) check earns one as a guide, who knows every hiding place.
Lit candles keep the imagined horrors at bay; a creature holding a bright light has advantage on saves against being frightened in the orphanage.
The crayon drawings in the schoolroom show each horror's weakness; studying them with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check grants advantage on attacks against one type of horror.
Joining the dolls' tea party with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check delights the ghosts, and a doll offers a key to one locked door.
The matron's ledger lists every child by name; reading a ghost's name aloud lets it rest, and each child laid to rest gives the party temporary hit points equal to the space's level.
The little ghost in the infirmary can be comforted; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check to tend her imaginary fever grants a healing potion from the empty bottles.
Unlocking every door in the corridor before facing the matron frees the children, who swarm her at the heart and impose disadvantage on her first three attacks.
hazards: The darkness in the punishment cupboard pulls at those who look in; a creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is dragged inside, taking {dmg} psychic damage each round until pulled free.
The burnt attic floor gives way; creatures walking on it make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the fall on a failure or {half} on a success.
Imagined horrors rise from the cellar dark; creatures there make a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage and becoming frightened on a failure, or {half} on a success.
The schoolroom's chalk lesson demands obedience; a creature that disobeys its written command makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} psychic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The ghostly cook's porridge vat boils over when the kitchen is disturbed; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The matron swings her ring of burning keys at the heart; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Vault of the Gold-Choked Prince
environments.summary: A merchant prince bargained with a devil to never lose a single coin, and when he died hoarding in his deepest vault, his greed fused with the bargain and sealed the treasury into an astral space. His iron guardians still patrol the counting rooms, while molten gold oozes through the halls hunting anything that might steal. The space wants every coin kept forever, and it will drown in gold anyone who tries to take even one.
readAloud: Light hits you from every direction at once, thrown back from mountains of gold coins that fill the chamber to the vaulted ceiling. The coins shift and slide with a constant metallic hiss, and somewhere among them something heavy moves. Iron figures with lantern eyes stand at every archway, and their heads turn toward you in perfect unison.

The air is hot and close, tasting of metal and dust, and every breath leaves a coppery film on your tongue. Beneath your boots the floor is paved with flattened coins, each stamped with the same proud, jowly face. Somewhere a heavy door slams, and a voice booms through the halls counting, never losing its place.

Golden statues line the walls, frozen in poses of reaching and grasping, and you notice with a chill that their faces are terrified. One holds a single coin out toward you, as if begging you to take it. A slow, liquid gleam rolls across the floor of the next room, moving against the slope.
sights: Mountains of gold coins sliding and shifting
Iron guardians with lantern eyes at every archway
Floors paved with flattened coins stamped with one face
Golden statues frozen in terrified, grasping poses
Molten gold rolling uphill across the floors
Ledgers chained to marble pillars
Jewelled chests sealed with burning wax
A colossal throne of solid gold beyond a barred gate
sounds: A constant metallic hiss of sliding coins
A booming voice counting without pause
The heavy clank of iron guardians marching
Heavy doors slamming in distant halls
Molten gold bubbling and dripping
A faint, desperate weeping from the statues
smells: A sharp tang of molten metal
rooms: A gilded antechamber where the portal glows above a tollbooth that demands a coin from every visitor who enters.
The coin hall, a cavern piled to the ceiling with gold that slides in slow, crushing avalanches across the floor.
A counting room where iron constructs stack coins into perfect towers and topple any tower one coin short.
The ledger gallery, a colonnade of marble pillars each chained to a ledger recording a debt owed to the prince.
A statue garden of golden figures, each a thief caught in the act and frozen forever with outstretched hands.
The smelting pit, a glowing forge where stolen goods are melted down and poured into coins bearing the prince's face.
An armoury of gilded weapons too heavy to lift, displayed on racks of black iron behind a crystal screen.
The jewel room, where gems the size of fists rest on velvet cushions guarded by tripwires of fine gold thread.
A dining hall with a feast of solid gold food, every plate and goblet heaped high and utterly inedible.
The contract chamber, a cramped study where the prince's infernal bargain is pinned to the wall with a silver dagger.
A vault door the size of a castle gate, ringed with dials and locks, humming with a deep protective ward.
The heart, the treasury throne, where the prince, now a vast golden ooze crowned with coins, guards the infernal contract's original seal.
features: The tollbooth accepts any coin; paying it grants safe passage past the first iron guardians, while refusing makes every guardian hostile on sight.
The iron constructs obey anyone carrying a stamped coin; a DC {dc} Charisma (Intimidation) check while holding one commands a construct to stand aside for 1 minute.
The ledgers record debts owed to the prince; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the party's own names, and tearing out the page frees them from the vault's pull.
The golden statues can be freed by offering back what they stole; a freed thief shares the secret combination to the vault door.
The contract can be read with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check, revealing a loophole: the prince must give up a coin freely or the bargain weakens.
The gilded weapons are magical but enormously heavy; a creature that succeeds on a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check can wield one, dealing an extra 1d6 damage per hit.
Tricking the prince into giving away a single coin at the heart with a DC {dc} Charisma (Deception) check breaks his armour of gold, giving the party advantage on attacks for 1 round.
hazards: Coin avalanches roll down the gold mountains; creatures in their path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being buried on a failure, or {half} on a success.
Molten gold oozes hunt anyone carrying stolen treasure; a creature touched makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Golden tripwires in the jewel room trigger hidden blades; a creature that misses a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check takes {dmg} slashing damage.
The smelting pit spits liquid metal; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

The vault door's ward flares when tampered with; a creature attempting to open it without the combination makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} force damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The prince floods the heart with a wave of molten gold; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} fire damage and being restrained on a failure, or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Sin-Eater's Barge on the Black River
environments.summary: A sin-eater who poled a funeral barge down a black river swallowed the sins of the dead for centuries, until one night he swallowed a sin too great to hold and his barge sank into an astral space. The barge drifts forever between misty banks, crewed by drowned mourners and the half-digested sins that crawl out of the sin-eater's belly as living shapes. The space wants someone to take the sin-eater's place, and it offers every visitor the ladle and the bread.
readAloud: You stand on the damp deck of a long, low barge drifting on a river of water so black it reflects nothing. Mist hangs thick on both banks, and from it come the shapes of willow trees, bent low as if in grief. A lantern swings from the prow, and in its light a figure in a sodden shroud poles the barge slowly onward.

The deck boards are slick and soft underfoot, swollen with river water, and every step leaves a faint black print. Coffins are stacked along both sides of the barge, some open, and from inside one comes the slow chewing of something eating. The air smells of wet wood, river weed and stale bread.

A long table runs down the middle of the barge, laid with loaves and wooden bowls of salt. Pale mourners in dripping black sit along it, heads bowed, and as you watch, each one slowly lifts a hand and offers you a crust. Far ahead, past the bend in the river, something enormous belches, and the whole barge trembles.
sights: A river so black it reflects nothing
Willows bowed low in the mist along the banks
A shrouded ferryman poling the barge onward
Coffins stacked along the gunwales, some open
Drowned mourners at a table of bread and salt
Wet black footprints spreading across the deck
Writhing shapes like shadows crawling from cracks
A lantern swinging from the prow over dark water
sounds: Water lapping slowly against the hull
The creak and splash of a long pole
Slow chewing from inside a coffin
Mourners murmuring prayers in a dead tongue
A distant, enormous belch that shakes the barge
Something heavy surfacing and sinking in the river
smells: A reek of rotten fish and silt
Bitter herbs burned for the dead
rooms: A misty landing stage where the portal glows inside a hanging lantern and the barge waits, already moving.
The mourners' table, a long board of bread and salt where drowned guests offer each newcomer a crust.
A coffin deck stacked with open caskets, each one holding a corpse whose mouth has been sewn shut.
The bilge, a dark flooded hold where half-digested sins crawl through the water like eels of shadow.
A ferryman's cabin of salt-crusted planks, holding a ledger of every soul the barge has carried downstream.
The galley, where a hunched cook bakes funeral bread in an oven fuelled by burning grave shrouds.
A drowned chapel built into the stern, its altar half sunk and its pews occupied by silent, dripping worshippers.
The riverbank shallows, a mist-shrouded shore of grasping roots where willows reach for anyone who leaves the barge.
A storeroom of sealed jars, each one holding a single dark sin that rattles against the glass to escape.
The crow's nest, a rickety perch above the mist that shows the endless river looping back upon itself.
An ancestral shrine of carved wooden faces, each one a former sin-eater, their mouths stained black with old sins.
The heart, the prow, where the bloated sin-eater, now an undead glutton swollen with fiends, guards the ladle and the last loaf.
features: Accepting a crust from the mourners makes them friendly, but a creature that eats it must succeed on a DC {dc} Wisdom save or gain a short-term madness from the swallowed sin.
The ferryman's ledger names every passenger; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a name that, spoken aloud, calms one undead on the barge.
Salt from the table can be cast in a line; undead and fiends cannot cross it for 1 minute.
The sealed jars can be opened deliberately; releasing a sin near an enemy forces it to make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or be frightened of the sin for 1 round.
The crow's nest reveals the river's loop; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check spots the hidden channel that leads off the endless river and out of the space.
The ancestral shrine's faces can be honoured; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check earns a former sin-eater's blessing, granting resistance to necrotic damage for 1 hour.
Taking up the ladle at the heart and eating the last loaf ends the fight at once, but the eater becomes the new sin-eater bound to the barge unless freed.
hazards: The black river pulls at anyone who falls in; a creature in the water makes a DC {dc} Strength save each round, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Shadow sins in the bilge coil around ankles; a creature wading there makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} psychic damage and being restrained on a failure, or {half} on a success.
Willow roots on the bank lash at those who step off; creatures within reach make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The galley oven belches burning shroud ash; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The rickety crow's nest sways and splinters; a creature climbing it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
The sin-eater vomits a flood of black sin at the heart; creatures in a 30-foot cone make a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Quarry of the Unfinished Colossus
environments.summary: A clan of stone giants swore to carve a colossus of their founder from a living mountain, and when the last of them died with the work half done, their stubborn oath folded the quarry into an astral space. Their ghostly hammer songs still guide earth elementals and clumsy stone constructs that keep cutting, hauling and polishing without end. The space wants the statue finished, and it measures every visitor as a worker, a block of stone, or an obstacle.
readAloud: The ground shudders under your feet with a slow, steady rhythm, like a heartbeat made of hammer blows. You stand on the lip of an enormous terraced pit, its walls cut into steps each taller than a house. Far below, stone figures the size of oxen drag sledges of cut granite along ramps worn smooth by centuries of hauling.

Grit stings your eyes and coats your tongue with the taste of chalk and iron. Across the pit rises a half-carved giant of stone, its face finished and serene, its body still trapped in raw mountain from the chest down. Chisel marks the width of your arm score its cheek, and dust drifts from them as though the work stopped only a moment ago.

A deep, wordless song rolls through the quarry, sung by voices too low and too vast to belong to anyone you can see. Wooden cranes taller than towers creak overhead, their ropes thick as tree trunks and stiff with dust. Somewhere below, a block of stone breaks free with a crack like thunder, and the singing pauses, then begins again.
sights: Terraced quarry walls cut into steps taller than houses
A half-carved colossus with a finished face and a body still trapped in rock
Stone constructs dragging sledges of granite up worn ramps
Wooden cranes taller than towers swaying under heavy loads
Earth elementals rising from the pit floor like moving hills
Giant-sized chisels and mallets left leaning against the cliffs
Chalk tally marks counting days in rows a mile long
Clouds of pale dust hanging in shafts of sunlight
sounds: Hammer blows ringing in a slow, steady rhythm
A deep, wordless work song with no visible singers
The groan of crane ropes straining under stone blocks
Granite sledges grinding along stone ramps
The crack of a block splitting free from the cliff
Gravel trickling down the terraces in endless streams
smells: A mineral tang like the inside of a cave
Sweat-soaked leather from abandoned giant harnesses
rooms: A rim platform at the top of the quarry, where the portal hums inside a frame of two cut granite pillars.
The hauling ramps, a switchback road of polished stone where constructs drag sledges of granite past anyone foolish enough to stand in the way.
A mason's lodge built for giants, its benches higher than your head and its walls covered in chalk plans of the colossus.
The tool rack, a cliff face hung with chisels as long as spears and mallets as heavy as wagons.
A crane gantry of lashed timber swaying high over the pit, its pulleys squealing as stone blocks rise past you.
The rubble field, a slope of broken blocks rejected by the masons, where earth elementals sleep beneath the debris.
A water cistern carved into the quarry floor, where giants once cooled their tools and the stone still steams faintly.
The tally wall, a long cliff marked with millions of chalk lines, one for each day of labour since the oath was sworn.
A collapsed tunnel where a seam of crystal runs through the granite, glittering and humming under the hammer songs.
The colossus's open hand, a platform of finished stone the size of a courtyard, its fingers curled as if waiting for something.
A burial terrace where the stone giants lie carved into their own effigies, each with a chisel laid across its chest.
The heart, the colossus's unfinished chest, where the ghostly master mason of the clan swings an eternal hammer and guards the founder's heart-stone that will awaken the statue.
features: Joining the work song with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check makes the constructs treat the singer as a fellow worker for 1 hour, and they step aside on the ramps.
The chalk plans in the mason's lodge reveal the colossus's weak seams; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check grants advantage on attacks against stone creatures in the heart.
A giant chisel can be lifted by two Medium creatures working together and used as a lever to topple a block, dealing {dmg} bludgeoning damage to whatever lies below.
The crane gantry can be operated with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, lifting the party or a heavy load across the pit in a single round.
Crystal from the collapsed tunnel can be chipped free; a shard held in hand grants tremorsense to a range of 10 feet for 1 hour.

Carving a single chalk line on the tally wall marks a creature as part of the oath, granting advantage on saves against the quarry's hazards until the next long rest, though the space will expect them to stay.
Placing a finished stone in the colossus's open hand with a DC {dc} Strength check earns the master mason's respect and an offer to talk before fighting.
hazards: Blocks fall from the cranes without warning; creatures beneath make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Runaway sledges thunder down the hauling ramps; a creature in the path makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone.
The rubble field shifts when an elemental wakes; creatures on the slope make a DC {dc} Strength save or slide 20 feet and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
Choking dust clouds roll across the terraces; a creature caught in one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded and poisoned for 1 minute.
The master mason's hammer splits the stone floor of the heart; creatures within 15 feet of the strike make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Shards of granite burst from blocks under the hammer songs; creatures nearby make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} piercing damage.

environments.name: Gauntlet of the Fallen Titan
environments.summary: A titan who once fought for the heavens fell from the sky clutching a holy spear, and the stone gauntlet that held it crashed into a mountainside and kept gripping long after its wearer was gone. The fierce grip and the faded divine power trapped inside folded the gauntlet into an astral space, where moss-grown giants make pilgrimage, oozes pool in the joints, and a wounded celestial still waits for its champion. The space wants something strong enough to lift the gauntlet, and it tests every arrival by trying to crush them.
readAloud: You emerge into the hollow of an enormous stone hand, its palm a valley and its fingers curling overhead like five grey mountains. Moss and flowering vines spill from every crack, and pale butterflies drift between them in the warm air. Far above, between the knuckles, a sliver of golden light shines down on something long and bright clasped in the grip.

The stone beneath you is faintly warm and pulses now and then, like a sleeper's slow breath. Glistening pools of translucent slime fill the creases of the palm, and you can see coins, bones and old weapons suspended inside them. A distant groan echoes through the fingers, the sound of stone grinding against stone as the hand tightens ever so slightly.

The air smells of crushed moss and hot metal, with a sweet note like temple incense. Carved into the gauntlet's wrist are battle scenes taller than towers, showing armoured giants fighting winged figures and storms. Somewhere high in the knuckles a voice is singing a hymn, cracked and wavering, as if the singer is very tired.
sights: Five stone fingers curling overhead like grey mountains
Moss and flowering vines spilling from every crack in the gauntlet
Translucent slime pools holding coins, bones and old weapons
A shaft of golden light falling through the knuckles
The haft of a bright spear clasped in the titan's grip
Battle carvings of giants and winged figures along the wrist
Moss-covered giant pilgrims kneeling in the palm
Pale butterflies drifting between the vines
sounds: Stone grinding as the great hand tightens
A cracked, wavering hymn from high in the knuckles
Slime pools gurgling and popping in the creases
The slow pulse of the gauntlet like a sleeper breathing
Giant pilgrims murmuring prayers in deep voices
Wind whistling through gaps between the fingers
smells: Hot metal from the buried armour
A sweet scent like temple incense
rooms: The palm valley, a broad hollow of warm stone where the portal glimmers above a pool of clear water among the moss.
A lifeline crease, a deep winding canyon across the palm filled with slime pools and the half-dissolved remains of earlier climbers.
The pilgrim camp, a circle of moss-grown giants kneeling around fires, offering prayers to the hand that once held the sky.
A finger tunnel bored through the stone knuckle, where vines hang like curtains and the walls breathe with a slow pulse.
The thumb's ridge, a narrow climb along a stone digit with a sheer drop on either side and gusts tearing at your clothes.
A cracked joint where the gauntlet split on impact, revealing the titan's ancient bone fused into the stone like a fossil.
The wrist frieze, a long gallery of carvings showing the war in the heavens, faded but still glowing faintly where light touches them.
An ooze grotto beneath a fingernail of plate armour, where a great translucent mass shelters a hoard of swallowed weapons.
A flower garden that has grown in the hollow of a knuckle, bright and fragrant and humming with fat golden bees.
The broken cuff, a ring of shattered armour plates where the arm once joined the gauntlet, open to an endless drop into cloud.
A pilgrims' shrine of stacked stones, where generations of giants have left their weapons in tribute to the fallen titan.
The heart, the clenched grip at the top of the hand, where a grieving wingless deva guards the holy spear against anyone not strong enough to lift it.
features: The giant pilgrims share their fires with the respectful; a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check to join their prayer earns a giant guide who can carry the party up the fingers.
Weapons can be fished from the slime pools; a creature that reaches in makes a DC {dc} Dexterity check to pull one free before the ooze notices.
The wrist frieze tells the titan's last battle; studying it with a DC {dc} Intelligence (History) check reveals the deva's true name, which grants advantage on Charisma checks against it.
Honey from the knuckle garden heals 2d4 hit points when eaten, though the bees must be calmed with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Animal Handling) check first.
The titan's fossil bone in the cracked joint hums with old strength; a creature that touches it gains advantage on Strength checks and saves for 1 hour.
The holy spear can be loosened from the grip with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check made by at least three creatures together, which ends the deva's vigil without a fight.
hazards: The hand tightens with a grinding roar; creatures between the fingers make a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Slime pools leap at those who pass too close; a creature that fails a DC {dc} Dexterity save is engulfed and takes {dmg} acid damage.
Winds on the thumb's ridge gust without warning; a creature on the ridge makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is blown off and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the fall.
The broken cuff crumbles at its edges; a creature that steps on a loose plate makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls into the cloud and is lost unless caught.
The deva's grief bursts as radiant light; creatures in the heart make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
Spores from the knuckle flowers make climbers drowsy; a creature that breathes them makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or falls unconscious for 1 minute.

environments.name: Kelp Abbey of the Tideworn Saint
environments.summary: A saint of the shallows prayed for the drowned beneath a sea cliff until the tide took her, and her mercy seeded a forest of kelp that grew into the shape of an abbey around her body. That gentle, stubborn mana folded the abbey into an astral space, where awakened kelp keeps the hours, seals and great fish attend services, and the saint's own spirit lingers in a husk of woven weed. The space wants to shelter the lost, and it tries to keep every visitor safe forever, whether they wish to stay or not.
readAloud: Cool water closes around you, yet you find you can breathe it, and it tastes faintly of salt and honey. Columns of golden kelp rise from the sandy floor and arch together high above, forming a vaulted roof that sways with the current. Sunlight pours down through the fronds in green and gold shafts, and tiny fish dart through them like sparks.

A deep, slow bell rings somewhere ahead, its tone carried through the water so that you feel it in your chest. Grey seals glide past in pairs, their dark eyes watching you without fear, and settle on the kelp pews to listen. Along the walls, woven bundles of weed hold the sleeping shapes of sailors, their faces peaceful and their chests rising slowly.

The sand beneath your feet is soft and warm, scattered with shells arranged into careful spirals. Fronds brush your arms and cheeks as you move, gentle as a hand checking for fever. Far down the nave, a pale figure woven from kelp kneels before an altar of pearl, and a soft light gathers around it like breath.
sights: Columns of golden kelp arching into a vaulted roof
Green and gold shafts of sunlight pouring through the fronds
Grey seals resting on pews of woven kelp
Sleeping sailors wrapped in cocoons of weed along the walls
Shells arranged into careful spirals on the sand
A kneeling figure woven from kelp before an altar of pearl
Shoals of tiny silver fish darting like sparks
A great old sea turtle wearing a crown of anemones
sounds: A deep, slow bell felt as much as heard
Kelp fronds hissing softly in the current
Seals barking a rough, rhythmic chant
The gentle breathing of sleeping sailors
Bubbles rising in silver chains toward the light
A wordless hymn hummed by the kelp itself
smells: Honey drifting faintly through the water
A whiff of wet seal fur
Sea lavender blooming in the cloister
Candle wax that somehow burns underwater
rooms: A shell-strewn forecourt where the portal shimmers in a ring of standing stones furred with bright anemones and drifting weed.
The nave, a long hall of golden kelp columns where seals and fish gather on woven pews for services that never end.
A sleeping gallery lined with kelp cocoons, each holding a drowned sailor who breathes slowly and dreams of the shore.
The bell tower, a spiral of coral and kelp rising toward the surface, where a bronze ship's bell swings in the current.
A cloister garden of sea lavender and glowing anemones, where an old sea turtle tends the beds with careful bites.
The scriptorium, a grotto where kelp monks press prayers into wet clay tablets with the edges of shells.
An infirmary of soft sponge beds, where injured fish and seals heal under the light of a floating pearl.
The tide gate, a wall of woven kelp that opens and closes with the current, trapping anyone who lingers too long.
A reliquary alcove holding the saint's walking staff, worn smooth and rooted into the floor like a sapling.
The undercroft, a dark root cellar beneath the abbey where the oldest kelp grows thick and grasping in the gloom.
A seal nursery of warm shallow pools, where pups tumble together and their mothers bark at anyone who comes too near.
The heart, the pearl altar at the end of the nave, where the woven husk of the Tideworn Saint kneels in prayer and guards the pearl that holds her soul.
features: The water is breathable within the abbey, but a creature that leaves the walls must make a DC {dc} Constitution save each minute or begin to drown.
Waking a sleeping sailor takes a DC {dc} Wisdom (Medicine) check; a woken sailor knows a secret path through the tide gate and gladly shares it.
The kelp monks will copy a prayer for any visitor who asks politely; carrying the clay tablet grants advantage on one saving throw of the bearer's choice.
The floating pearl in the infirmary heals 2d8 hit points once per creature, but taking it angers the whole abbey.
Ringing the bronze bell in the tower with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check calls every creature in the abbey to the nave for a service, emptying the other rooms.
The saint's staff in the reliquary can be drawn from the floor with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check, and its bearer can speak with the saint as an equal rather than a lost soul.
hazards: Kelp in the undercroft wraps around the unwary; a creature that fails a DC {dc} Strength save is restrained and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage as the fronds squeeze.
The tide gate slams shut with the current; creatures in the gap make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The abbey's gentle lullaby seeps into the mind; a creature that rests here makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is wrapped in a cocoon and falls into enchanted sleep.
Mother seals defend their pups fiercely; a creature that enters the nursery uninvited makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} piercing damage from bites.
The saint's light flares when her pearl is threatened; creatures in the heart make a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Bonemeal Windmill Vale
environments.summary: A hill giant miller ground the bones of fallen armies into flour for his clan's bread, and the hunger and endless wind of that grim valley folded it into an astral space. Rickety windmill constructs walk the hillsides on wooden legs, skeletons still march toward the millstones to be ground, and ogre bakers knead pale dough in ovens the size of barns. The space wants to be fed, and every visitor is weighed by how much bone they carry.
readAloud: A hard wind hits you the moment you arrive, flattening the grey grass around your boots and tugging at your cloak. You stand at the head of a long valley lined with hundreds of windmills, their sails turning in a great creaking chorus. Pale dust drifts from their doors and settles over everything like a dry, bitter snow.

The dust tastes of chalk and old marrow, and it clings to your lips no matter how often you wipe them. Down the slope, a line of skeletons trudges along a cart road toward the largest mill, their bones clicking in the wind. Above them, a windmill lifts itself from the hillside on four timber legs and strides slowly to a new spot.

The smell of baking bread drifts up the valley, warm and yeasty, with something sour and wrong underneath it. Smoke rises from a row of great brick ovens near the river, where hulking figures slide loaves the size of wagons onto long wooden paddles. The ground under you trembles with the steady grinding of millstones, and every so often you hear a crunch.
sights: Hundreds of windmills with sails turning in the gale
Pale bone dust drifting over the valley like dry snow
Skeletons trudging toward the millstones in a long line
A windmill walking across the hillside on timber legs
Brick ovens the size of barns belching smoke
Ogre bakers carrying loaves on long wooden paddles
Flour sacks stitched from old battle banners
Grey grass flattened by an endless wind
sounds: Windmill sails creaking in a great chorus
Millstones grinding with a deep, steady rumble
Bones clicking as skeletons march in the wind
The occasional sharp crunch from inside a mill
A giant's tuneless whistling carried on the gale
Oven doors clanging open and shut
smells: Warm yeasty bread with something sour beneath
Chalky bone dust and dry marrow
Wood smoke from the brick ovens
A reek of old battlefield rot
Wet grass and cold river water
rooms: A windswept ridge at the head of the valley, where the portal flutters like a torn sail between two leaning millstones.
The bone road, a rutted cart track where skeletons march in a slow column toward the grinding mills.
A walking windmill that wanders the hillside on timber legs, its interior a swaying room of gears, sacks and loose bones.
The sorting yard, a muddy pen where ogres pick through heaps of bones and toss them into baskets by size.
A granary of tall stone silos packed with pale bone flour, so fine it rises in clouds at a single footstep.
The bakehouse row, a line of brick ovens by the river where ogre bakers knead dough in troughs the size of boats.
A battlefield hill, its slopes still littered with rusted armour and the bones of soldiers waiting to be collected.
The millrace, a fast stone channel of river water turning a massive wheel that drives the deepest millstones.
A miller's cottage built for a giant, with a table set for one, a pipe still smoking and a ledger of debts.
The sail loft, a high attic where torn sails hang drying and the wind howls through every gap in the boards.
A pit of rejected bones, too cursed to grind, where restless skeletons claw at one another and the walls.
The heart, the great mill at the valley's end, where the hill giant miller works his enormous millstone and guards the bone of his clan's first king.
features: The skeletons on the bone road ignore anyone who walks in step with them; a DC {dc} Dexterity (Stealth) check lets the party reach the great mill unnoticed.
The walking windmill can be steered by jamming its gears; a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the right lever to send it striding in any direction.
Bone flour from the granary can be thrown in a cloud, heavily obscuring a 10-foot cube for 1 round.
The ogre bakers will trade a loaf for a story; eating the bread grants 1d6 temporary hit points but leaves a bitter taste for a day.
The miller's ledger lists what the clan is owed; tearing out the page with the party's names on it with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check frees them from the space's hunger.
Opening the sluice on the millrace with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check stops the deepest millstones and weakens the miller, giving him disadvantage on his first attack.
Returning the first king's bone to the battlefield hill with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Religion) check lays the marching skeletons to rest.
hazards: Windmill sails sweep low across the paths; a creature caught by one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
A spark near the granary ignites the bone flour; creatures inside make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The gale on the ridge and in the sail loft hurls loose debris; creatures exposed make a DC {dc} Strength save or are knocked prone and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
The millrace current is fierce; a creature that falls in makes a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check or is dragged toward the wheel and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Bone dust clogs the lungs of those who linger; a creature that spends an hour in the valley makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is poisoned until it rests.
The miller's millstone rolls free in the heart; creatures in its path make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Pearl Drake's Tidepool Hoard
environments.summary: A young bronze dragon gathered pearls along a stormy coast until a hurricane drowned her lair, and her frantic, greedy need to protect her hoard folded the flooded cliffs into an astral space. Gulls and crabs scuttle among pools where clear oozes guard each pearl, and the dragon herself, grown sleek and half-wild, dives and soars with the tides. The space wants its pearls counted and kept, and it treats every pocket as a theft waiting to happen.
readAloud: Salt spray strikes your face as you arrive on a ledge of wet black rock above a churning sea. Below you, hundreds of tidepools stretch along the cliffs like a broken mirror, each one glinting with a single pale pearl. Gulls wheel overhead in screaming flocks, and the wind roars in from the water hard enough to make you stagger.

The rock is slick with weed and cold under your hands, and barnacles bite through your gloves. Waves boom against the cliffs in a rhythm so steady it feels like breathing, and every seventh wave throws spray higher than the gulls. Far out over the water, a bronze shape cuts through the clouds, folds its wings, and plunges into the sea.

The air smells of brine, rotting weed and the sharp electric scent before a storm. In the pool nearest you, the water ripples strangely, and you realize the clear jelly filling it is moving on its own around the pearl. Lightning flickers on the horizon, and for an instant every pearl along the coast flashes the same bright gold.
sights: Hundreds of tidepools each glinting with a pale pearl
Gulls wheeling overhead in screaming flocks
A bronze dragon diving from the clouds into the sea
Clear oozes coiling around pearls in the pools
Barnacle-crusted ship wreckage jammed between the rocks
Giant crabs scuttling sideways across the ledges
Waves bursting higher than the cliff tops
Lightning flickering over a slate-grey horizon
sounds: Waves booming against the cliffs in a steady rhythm
Gulls screaming and squabbling over scraps
The rumble of distant thunder rolling in from the sea
Crab claws clicking against wet rock
A dragon's roar echoing over the water
Wind howling through sea caves
smells: A sharp electric scent before a storm
Wet rope and tarred timber from old wrecks
The coppery tang of dragon breath
rooms: A wet black ledge above the surf, where the portal shines inside a ring of barnacles on a broken ship's figurehead.
The pearl terraces, hundreds of tidepools stepping down the cliffs, each guarded by a clear ooze coiled around its single pearl.
A sea cave that floods with every seventh wave, its walls scratched with the dragon's tally of pearls counted and recounted.
The wreck wedge, a merchant ship jammed sideways between two rocks, its hold still full of soaked cargo and nesting gulls.
A gull rookery on a sheer stack of rock, loud and reeking, where nests are woven from stolen rope and sailcloth.
The crab beach, a crescent of grey shingle where giant crabs sort shells and drag anything shiny back to their burrows.
A blowhole platform where the sea erupts upward through a crack in the rock, hurling spray and loose stones into the sky.
The drowned lair, a half-flooded grotto where the dragon slept before the hurricane, its walls still lined with gnawed driftwood.
A storm tower of lashed wreckage on the highest point, where lightning strikes again and again and the air crackles.
The kelp shallows, a gentle inlet where seals bask and the water is calm enough to wade, hiding pearls under the sand.
A cliff stair carved by the dragon's claws, steep and slick, winding between the waterfalls that pour off the headland.
The heart, the eye of a standing whirlpool beneath the cliffs, where the bronze pearl drake coils around her greatest pearl and guards it against every thief.
features: A pearl can be lifted from a pool with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check before the ooze reacts; each pearl is worth 100 gold pieces outside the space.
The dragon's tally in the sea cave can be read with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check, revealing that one pearl is missing and where it lies in the kelp shallows.
Returning the missing pearl to the drake earns her trust, and she offers safe passage out without a fight.
The giant crabs will trade a pearl for any shiny metal object, and they know a tunnel that bypasses the cliff stair.
Riding the blowhole with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check launches a creature up to the storm tower in a single burst.
Cargo in the wreck holds dry rope, lantern oil and a sealed chest; opening the chest takes a DC {dc} Dexterity check with thieves' tools.
hazards: The seventh wave floods the sea cave and the lower ledges; creatures caught make a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being swept 30 feet on a failure, or {half} on a success.
Oozes lash out when their pearls are touched; a creature that fails a DC {dc} Dexterity save takes {dmg} acid damage and is grappled.
Lightning strikes the storm tower; creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The cliff stair is slick with spray; a creature that fails a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check slips and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the fall.
Gulls swarm anyone carrying a pearl; a creature holding one makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or takes {half} piercing damage and drops it.
The drake's breath arcs over the whirlpool; creatures in a 60-foot line make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

environments.name: Hanging Gardens of the Cloud Matriarch
environments.summary: An aged cloud giant matriarch planted terraced gardens on a floating island so her children would never forget the earth, and when she grew too old to leave her loom, her devotion to them sealed the island into an astral space. Vines and fruit trees spill over the edges into open sky, tended by awakened plants and small winged guardians the colour of dawn, while her children have long since flown away. The space wants its family to come home, and it welcomes every visitor as a grandchild who is expected to stay for supper.
readAloud: You arrive on a lawn of soft clover with nothing but open sky on every side. Terraces of flowering gardens climb above you in great green steps, and from each one, vines and creepers spill over the edge and trail down into the clouds below. Warm wind carries petals past you in drifts, pink and white and gold.

The air is thin and cool, and your breath comes a little faster than usual. Somewhere above, a loom clacks in a steady rhythm, and a deep, gentle voice hums a lullaby that seems to come from the sky itself. Small winged figures with skin like the first light of morning flit between the fruit trees, picking ripe pears and chattering softly.

The garden smells of ripe fruit, cut grass and rain that has not yet fallen. Every bench and gate here is built for giants, with seats as high as your shoulders and steps you must climb with your hands. On the nearest wall, carved hand prints of many sizes climb in a row, from a tiny one at the bottom to one larger than a door at the top.
sights: Terraced gardens climbing toward the sky in great green steps
Vines and creepers trailing over the edges into the clouds
Drifts of pink, white and gold petals carried on the wind
Small dawn-coloured winged guardians picking fruit
Giant-sized benches and gates with steps as tall as a person
A wall of carved hand prints growing from tiny to enormous
Waterfalls that pour off the terraces and turn to mist in midair
A vast silver loom glinting on the highest terrace
sounds: A loom clacking in a steady rhythm high above
A deep, gentle lullaby hummed from the sky
Wind chimes made of hollow seed pods
Winged guardians chattering softly among the trees
Waterfalls hissing as they turn to mist
Leaves rustling in a warm, endless breeze
smells: The scent of rain that has not yet fallen
Fresh bread cooling on a windowsill
rooms: A clover lawn at the island's lowest edge, where the portal glows inside an arch of woven willow above an endless drop.
The orchard terrace, a wide step of fruit trees taller than towers, where winged guardians gather pears into baskets of cloud.
A vine curtain hanging over the island's edge, thick enough to climb, swaying out over the clouds with every gust.
The children's wall, a long stone face carved with hand prints from infancy to adulthood, each one labeled with a giant's name.
A nursery garden of toy-sized trees and flower beds, laid out by the matriarch for children who never came back.
The mist falls, a cascade pouring off a terrace into empty sky, where rainbows hang permanently in the spray.
An awakened hedge maze that rearranges itself to guide guests toward supper, whether or not they wish to go.
The great kitchen, a stone hall with ovens like caves and a table laid for a dozen giants who never arrive.
A seed vault carved into the island's root rock, holding jars of seeds from every land the matriarch's family ever visited.
The wind terrace, a bare stone platform at the island's edge where giant kites are tethered and straining to fly.
A sky shrine of white marble, where a dawn-winged guardian keeps a candle burning for each child who left.
The heart, the loom terrace at the island's summit, where the ancient cloud giant matriarch weaves a tapestry of her family and guards the thread that holds the island aloft.
features: The winged guardians welcome those who call them cousin; a DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check earns a guide and a basket of fruit that heals 1d6 hit points per piece.
The vine curtain can be climbed down to reach a hidden ledge beneath the island with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check.
Pressing a palm into the children's wall with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check reveals the name of one lost child, which softens the matriarch toward the speaker.
Sitting down to supper in the great kitchen restores all hit points, but each creature that eats makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or forgets it ever wanted to leave.
A tethered kite on the wind terrace can carry one Medium creature on a short flight around the island; steering it takes a DC {dc} Dexterity check.
Seeds from the vault grow overnight into a sapling that bears one healing fruit per day, for a year and a day.
Promising to carry a message to the matriarch's children, with a DC {dc} Charisma check, can end the vigil in the heart without bloodshed.
hazards: Sudden gusts sweep the island's edges; creatures near a drop make a DC {dc} Strength save or are pushed 15 feet toward it and take {half} bludgeoning damage.
The hedge maze closes around those who resist its guidance; a creature that fails a DC {dc} Strength save is restrained and takes {dmg} piercing damage from thorns.
The mist falls are slippery and fast; a creature that slips makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save or falls 30 feet to the terrace below, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
Thin air tires climbers quickly; a creature that climbs more than two terraces in an hour makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or gains a level of exhaustion.
The matriarch's tapestry unravels into lashing threads when she is angered; creatures in the heart make a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
The sky shrine's candles flare with holy light at thieves; a creature that takes one makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.

replace: DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana): the threshold rune weighs aura strength, an old Adventure Society testing pattern

Hold your magic perfectly still as you pass (DC {dc} Wisdom check), or have a lower-rank ally scratch out the weighing rune from the far side
A higher-rank ally can carry one weaker creature through per turn wrapped in their aura (DC {dc} Constitution save for the carrier or both are repelled)

puzzleBank.name: The Noon Companion
puzzleBank.setup: A door of black stone blocks the passage, and above it a carved obsidian face opens its mouth as you approach. Silver letters glow across the lintel: "I walk behind you in the morning, I stretch before you late; / at noon I hide beneath your feet, and never make you wait; / snuff out every light you carry and I'm gone without a trace; / speak my name to pass." The face holds its mouth open, as if listening.
clues: The torches in the bracket by the door throw a long dark shape of each of you across the black stone.
When anyone steps closer to the torches, the obsidian face's eyes flick to the floor behind them.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "shadow" (or "my shadow"), spoken aloud to the face.

hints.text: The riddle describes something whose length and direction change with the time of day, and which needs light to exist.
You notice the face keeps staring at the dark shapes the torches cast of you on the door.

puzzleBank.failure: The obsidian face exhales a cold black mist, and each creature within 15 feet of the door makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The door grinds open, and on the face's stone tongue rests a sliver of shadowglass that grants one creature advantage on one Dexterity (Stealth) check in this space.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can force the door with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but each try draws the black mist and that creature takes {half} necrotic damage.

puzzleBank.name: The Hungry Brazier
puzzleBank.setup: A bronze statue of a kneeling smith holds a cold, empty brazier toward a sealed iron gate. Words are stamped into the brazier's rim: "I eat the wood, I eat the coal, I'm never full, I'm never whole; / feed me and I leap and grow, give me a drink and down I go; / I have a tongue but cannot taste; say what I am and I'll light this place." The air smells faintly of old smoke.
clues: Black soot stains the inside of the brazier and the ceiling directly above it.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "fire" ("flame" also works), spoken into the brazier.

hints.text: The statue is a flame-ward: it wants to be told what it is meant to hold.
Something that eats fuel, grows when fed, dies when given water, and has a 'tongue' is a thing that burns.

puzzleBank.failure: The brazier coughs a gout of sparks, and each creature in front of the statue makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: Flames bloom in the brazier and the iron gate glows and swings open, and any creature that warms its hands at the fire gains resistance to cold damage until the end of the next fight.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can light the brazier with its own flame and a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check to trick the ward, but the backlash deals {half} fire damage to it whether it succeeds or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Answering Dome
puzzleBank.setup: You enter a round chamber with a high domed ceiling, and every footstep you take comes back to you a moment later. A ring of brass letters set into the floor reads: "Call to me and I call back, I copy every word; / I live in caves and canyons and I'm never first one heard; / I have no tongue, I have no throat, yet speak to me and see; / say my name and I'll say it too, and then the way is free." There is no door, only a smooth wall opposite the entrance.
clues: If anyone speaks, the dome repeats their last word twice, fainter each time.
A faint breeze circles the chamber, always moving along the curve of the wall.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "echo", spoken aloud; the dome repeats it and the far wall opens.

hints.text: The room itself is already doing what the riddle describes every time you speak.
Sound bouncing back from caves, canyons and domes has a name, and that name is the answer.

puzzleBank.failure: The dome hurls the wrong word back as a crashing roar, and each creature in the chamber makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The wall opens onto a whispering shortcut that leads two rooms closer to the heart of the space.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down; whenever a player speaks in character, echo their last word back twice in a fading voice.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can hunt for the hollow seam in the far wall with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check and break through, but the dome roars and each creature in the chamber takes {half} thunder damage.

puzzleBank.name: The Glass Bell
puzzleBank.setup: A tall door of frosted glass stands at the end of the room, and in its centre hangs a glass bell with no clapper. Fine script is etched around the bell: "Speak my name and I am broken; I fill the empty hall; / I was here before the first word and I'll stay after the last of all; / I cannot be heard, yet I am kept; give me a full minute, and the door is yours." The bell trembles slightly whenever anyone speaks.
clues: Dust on the floor before the door lies undisturbed except for a single circle where people seem to have stood very still.
A tiny etched hourglass sits beneath the final line of the verse.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is silence, and it must be given, not said: every creature in the room must stay completely silent for one full minute (10 rounds). Saying the word "silence" aloud breaks it and counts as a wrong answer.

hints.text: The riddle's thing is destroyed by naming it, so speaking the answer cannot be the way to give it.
The bell shivers at every sound; it wants a whole minute without any.
The door is a ward of stillness: everyone in the room must hold their tongue together, with no whispers, for one minute.

puzzleBank.failure: The glass bell shrieks, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the minute must begin again.
puzzleBank.reward: The glass door melts away like frost, and the bell drops into a waiting hand: it can be rung once to make the next room's guardians unable to hear the party for one minute.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down; players may talk out of character, but once anyone says an answer in character, start a one-minute timer and any sound from the table before it ends breaks the ward.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can shatter the glass door with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the bell's shriek deals {dmg} thunder damage to every creature in the room and the bell is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Waxen Hands
puzzleBank.setup: A pale marble statue of a robed woman stands with both hands cupped in front of her, and beside her a stone table holds a dagger, a clay cup, a coil of rope, a white candle and a closed book. Words carved on her pedestal read: "When I am young I'm tall and proud, when old I'm short and bent; / I weep hot tears that harden fast, and shine until I'm spent; / give my likeness to the lady's hands and let her light be lent." The room beyond her is pitch black.
clues: Old drips of wax have hardened on the statue's marble palms.
puzzleBank.solution: Place the white candle in the statue's cupped hands; lighting it first is welcome but not required.

hints.text: The answer is one of the objects on the table, and the lady wants it placed, not named.
There are old tear-shaped drops of wax on her palms.

puzzleBank.failure: The wrong object crumbles to ash and the room goes dark, and a shadowy servitor (use a shadow) peels from the wall to attack.
puzzleBank.reward: The candle flares with a steady silver flame that lights the dark room beyond and never goes out while it stays in this space, revealing a hidden alcove with an awakening stone.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and list the five objects on the table so players can write them down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can pry open the dark room's sealed edge with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the shadowy servitor wakes and attacks, and the hidden alcove stays closed.

puzzleBank.name: The Hall of Hourglasses
puzzleBank.setup: Hundreds of hourglasses line the shelves of this narrow hall, every one of them running, and a great brass door at the end shows a clock face with no hands. Words swirl in gold sand across its surface: "I have no wings yet fly away, no teeth yet wear the stone; / I heal all wounds and steal all youth, a king without a throne; / you spend me, though I weigh no coin, and none can buy me back; / name me and the hands return." The sound of falling sand fills the air.
clues: Every hourglass on the shelves is labelled with a different length: a breath, a day, a season, a life.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "time", spoken to the door.

hints.text: Old sayings claim this thing flies, heals all wounds, and cannot be bought back once spent.
Everything in the room, from the hourglasses to the handless clock, measures the same thing.

puzzleBank.failure: Sand pours from the ceiling, and each creature in the hall makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or ages a moment in body, gaining one level of exhaustion.
puzzleBank.reward: The clock's hands appear and the door opens, and one creature may take a single hourglass that, once turned, grants an extra action on one turn of the boss fight.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can wrench the brass door open with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the falling sand forces each creature in the hall to make a DC {dc} Constitution save or gain one level of exhaustion, and no hourglass may be taken.

puzzleBank.name: The Runner's Trail
puzzleBank.setup: A long corridor floored with fine grey dust ends at a statue of a sprinter frozen mid-stride, one hand pointing down. Letters cut into the statue's base read: "The more of me you take, the more you leave behind; / I'm pressed in dust and snow and mud for those who come to find; / the swift lay me far apart, the weary lay me near; / tell me what you made to reach me here." A blank stone slab beside the statue waits to be spoken to.
clues: Looking back down the corridor, you see your own trail printed clearly in the dust.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "footsteps" ("footprints" or "steps" also work), spoken to the slab.

hints.text: Hunters read these in mud and snow, and the gap between them tells how fast someone moved.
Turn around and look at what you left in the dust to reach the statue.

puzzleBank.failure: The dust whirls up into a choking storm, and each creature in the corridor makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The statue's pointing hand swings open a floor hatch to a shortcut, and every creature's speed increases by 10 feet until the end of their next fight.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can find and kick open the floor hatch with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Survival) check, but the dust storm rises and each creature in the corridor takes {half} bludgeoning damage, and the speed boon is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Red Door That Beats
puzzleBank.setup: A door of dark red stone pulses gently in a slow rhythm, and when you lay a palm on it you feel a steady thump. Veins of crimson spell out a verse across it: "I beat without a stick, I'm red without a dye; / I can be broken, stolen, given, and never leave your side; / when I go still, so do you; name me and step inside." The thump quickens as you draw closer.
clues: Pressing an ear to the door, you hear a sound exactly like the one in your own chest.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "heart", spoken to the door.

hints.text: The door's rhythm is the same as a living pulse.
Poets say this thing is broken, stolen and given away, yet it never leaves the body.

puzzleBank.failure: The door's veins lash out, and the creature who answered makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success as blood is drawn from them.
puzzleBank.reward: The door opens with a sigh, and each creature that passes through regains hit points equal to their highest hit die.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down; tap a slow steady beat on the table while they think.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can press its bleeding palm to the door and pass with a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the healing reward is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Buried Giant
puzzleBank.setup: In the middle of a garden room stands a ring of dead, leafless trees around a bare mound of dark soil. A wooden sign is pushed into the soil, painted with green letters: "Dead and buried in the dark, I wake without a sound; / I climb toward a sun I've never seen, a giant from the ground; / I'm smaller than your fingernail, yet forests sleep in me; / name me, and the garden wakes." The soil is soft and freshly turned.
clues: Among the roots of the dead trees lie a few dry husks that crack open like shells.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "seed" ("a seed" or "an acorn" also work), spoken over the mound.

hints.text: Something tiny buried in the ground that grows into a tree is what the verse describes.
The husks among the roots are what is left when this thing has sprouted.

puzzleBank.failure: The dead trees' roots burst from the soil to grasp at you, and each creature on the mound must succeed on a DC {dc} Strength save or be restrained until it escapes with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check.
puzzleBank.reward: The trees burst into leaf and fruit, and each creature that eats a fruit gains temporary hit points equal to twice their level.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can dig a path through the dead roots with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the roots grasp back and each creature on the mound takes {half} bludgeoning damage, and the trees stay barren.

puzzleBank.name: The Frozen Pool
puzzleBank.setup: A wide pool fills this cold chamber, frozen white and solid, and on the far side a frosted archway is sealed with a curtain of icicles. Words are written in frost across the pool's surface: "Born of water, I'm a stone; hold me tight and I'll be gone; / I bridge the lake in winter's cold and crack beneath a careless step; / leave me in the sun to sleep and I'm what I was before I slept." Your breath steams in the air.
clues: Where you rest a warm hand on the pool, a little puddle forms and the frost lettering blurs.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "ice", spoken toward the archway.

hints.text: This thing is water turned hard by cold, and it melts back to water when warmed.
You are standing beside the answer: the pool itself.

puzzleBank.failure: The ice cracks under the speaker's feet, and each creature on or beside the pool makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} cold damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The icicle curtain shatters into harmless snow and the frozen pool becomes a safe bridge to a cache holding a monster core.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can smash the icicle curtain with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but each creature beside the pool takes {half} cold damage from the shards and the pool stays too brittle to cross to the cache.

puzzleBank.name: The Veiled Watcher
puzzleBank.setup: A silver statue of a veiled figure sits on a throne, its blank face turned toward a polished silver plate lying face down on the floor at its feet. Words shine on the throne's arm: "I wear your face but I'm not you, I raise my left when you raise right; / I live in still pools and polished steel, and vanish with the light; / do not tell me what I am; show me, so that I may see." A shallow basin of clear water stands beside the throne.
clues: The underside of the silver plate is polished bright enough to see your face in.
The statue's veil has a single eye-hole cut in it, aimed at the plate on the floor.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is a reflection, and it must be shown: hold the polished plate (or a shield, blade, or the basin of still water) up in front of the statue's eye-hole so the statue sees its own reflection. Saying "reflection" or "mirror" aloud does nothing.

hints.text: The thing in the riddle copies your face backwards and lives in still water and polished metal.
The verse says 'show me', not 'name me'; the statue wants to see the answer, not hear it.
The silver plate face down on the floor is a mirror, and the statue's single eye-hole is aimed right at it.

puzzleBank.failure: A blinding flash bursts from the throne, and each creature facing it makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage and being blinded until the end of its next turn on a failure, or taking {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The statue lifts its veil and a hidden panel slides open, and the plate it gazed into becomes a mirror shield that lets its holder reflect one ray or beam attack back at its source.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down; only an action a character takes counts, so saying the word does nothing.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can break into the hidden panel with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the throne flashes and every creature facing it takes {half} radiant damage, and the plate stays a plain silver plate.

puzzleBank.name: The Open Palm
puzzleBank.setup: A gilded statue of a grinning merchant holds one hand out, palm up, and keeps the other closed tight against its chest. A plaque at its feet reads: "I have a head, I have a tail, but never legs to roam; / I'm passed from hand to greedy hand and never find a home; / I buy the bread, I buy the blade, I buy the liar's word; / lay me where the empty palm can hold me, and be heard." A locked strongbox sits behind the statue.
clues: The statue's open palm is worn smooth in a small round shape, as if something has rested there many times.
puzzleBank.solution: Place a coin (any coin, a spirit coin works best) in the statue's open palm.

hints.text: The thing with a head and a tail but no legs, which buys bread and blades, is money.
The merchant does not want the answer said; it wants one placed in its empty hand.

puzzleBank.failure: The statue's fingers snap shut, and the creature nearest its hand makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The statue's closed hand opens to unlock the strongbox, which holds spirit coins worth twice what was given and a single awakening stone.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can force the strongbox with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, but the statue's fingers snap shut on it for {dmg} bludgeoning damage and the box holds only what it held, with no awakening stone.

puzzleBank.name: The Digger's Paradox
puzzleBank.setup: A stone spade leans against the wall of a rough cave, and in the floor before a sealed rock wall is a small, neat pit. Letters are scratched into the spade's handle: "Dig me deeper and I grow wide; I've nothing in me, only inside; / the more you take away from me, the bigger I will be; / name me, digger, and set the stone wall free." Loose earth is piled beside the pit.
clues: Each time someone scoops earth out of the pit, it gets larger, and the pile beside it grows.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "a hole" ("pit" also works), spoken to the rock wall.

hints.text: The thing grows bigger the more you remove, so it must be made of nothing at all.
The answer is right at your feet, and the spade was used to make it.

puzzleBank.failure: The cave ceiling sheds a rain of rocks, and each creature in the cave makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The rock wall slides into the ground, and the spade turns out to be a light iron tool that can dig through one wall of earth or loose stone in this space in a single minute.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down.
puzzleBank.stuck: Each creature can dig through the rock wall with the spade over ten minutes and a DC {dc} Constitution save, gaining one level of exhaustion on a failure, and the spade crumbles once used.

puzzleBank.name: The Twin Plaques of Morning
puzzleBank.setup: Three doors stand side by side: the left one carved with a gold disc, the right one with a petal, and the tall middle one with a long green stem and the words "Join the two and speak as one." The left door reads: "I rise without legs each morning and set without a bed; / I warm the field and paint the sky in gold and orange and red." The right door reads: "I have no voice yet bees come calling, I wear a gown of petals bright; / pluck me and I fade by evening, plant me and I drink the light."
clues: The side doors are false; behind them is solid rock, and only the middle door has hinges.
Carved high above the middle door is a tall bloom with its head turned toward a golden disc.
puzzleBank.solution: The left riddle's answer is "sun" and the right one's is "flower"; joined, the middle door opens to the spoken word "sunflower".

hints.text: Each side door holds its own riddle, and the middle door wants the two answers combined into a single word.
The left riddle is the thing that rises and sets in the sky; the right is something with petals that bees visit.
The carving over the middle door shows a flower that turns its face toward the sun.

puzzleBank.failure: A wave of searing golden light washes from the middle door, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The middle door blooms open onto a sunlit glade where the party can take a short rest safe from any wandering threat.
puzzleBank.table: Read all three inscriptions twice and let players write them down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can force the middle door with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the golden light washes out and each creature in the room takes {half} radiant damage, and the glade offers no safe rest.

puzzleBank.name: The Proud King
puzzleBank.setup: A stone king sits on a towering throne at the end of a long hall, a great sword across his knees, and the only exit is a door behind the throne. Words are carved into the steps before him: "I am a weapon strung with cord, I am the front of a sailing ship; / I am the knot upon a gift, and the thing a courtier does for a lord; / do not name me; do me." The king's eyes follow whoever stands closest.
clues: Two shallow dents are worn into the first step, just the size of a kneeling or bending person's feet.
Faded paintings on the walls show tiny figures before this very throne, all bent at the waist.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "bow", and it must be done: at least one player stands on the worn step and bows to the king. Saying "bow" aloud does nothing.

hints.text: One short word means a weapon, the front of a ship, a ribbon knot, and a gesture of respect.
The verse ends 'do me'; the king wants a gesture, not a word.
The paintings show visitors bending at the waist before the throne, the same way courtiers greet a lord.

puzzleBank.failure: The stone king sweeps his sword across the steps, and each creature before the throne makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The king nods and the door behind the throne opens, and the creature who bowed gains advantage on its first attack roll against the boss.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down; if a character bows, have that player stand and bow at the table.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can slip past the throne to the door with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, but the king swings his sword at it for {dmg} slashing damage and the boon against the boss is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Gate of Whispers
puzzleBank.setup: A tall gate of pale wood is covered in carved faces, and as you come near they all begin murmuring different words you cannot quite make out. Across the top bar, in plain letters: "Given at your birth but never wrapped, it's yours and yours alone; / yet friend and foe both use it far more often than you use your own; / tell the gate what this thing is, and it will let you home." The murmuring stops when anyone faces the gate to speak.
clues: Listening closely, you realise each carved face is calling out a different person's name.
puzzleBank.solution: The answer is "a name" ("my name" or "your name" also works), spoken to the gate.

hints.text: This is something you are given at birth that other people say far more than you do.
The faces on the gate are calling out exactly the kind of thing the riddle describes.

puzzleBank.failure: The faces shriek every name at once, and each creature that hears them makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The gate swings open, and one face whispers the true name of the boss of this space, granting the party advantage on their first saving throw against its powers.
puzzleBank.table: Read the verse twice and let players write it down; murmur a few random names under your breath whenever they look at the gate.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can drown out the faces and shoulder the gate open with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but every creature that hears the shriek takes {half} psychic damage and no name is whispered.

puzzleBank.name: The Conquering Sigils
puzzleBank.setup: Five cold sigils are carved in a ring on the floor, each beside an unlit brazier: Root, Frost, Stone, Rain and Flame. Above the ring, letters of dull bronze read: "Rain drowns Flame. Stone crushes Root. Flame melts Frost. Root drinks Rain." Beneath them, in larger letters: "Wake each sigil only after the one it conquers already burns." A brazier lights when someone touches its sigil with an open hand.
clues: Frost is the only sigil that conquers nothing, so the inscription places no demand on it.
