Scorch marks around the Stone sigil suggest someone once tried to light it first and paid for it.
puzzleBank.solution: Light the sigils in the order Frost, Flame, Rain, Root, Stone. Each sigil conquers the one lit just before it, forming a single unbroken chain.

hints.text: Each sentence names a conqueror and its victim; the victim must be lit before the conqueror.
The four sentences link into one chain, so there is only one possible order. Start with the sigil that conquers nothing.
Frost first, because Flame melts it; then follow who beats whom until you reach Stone.

puzzleBank.failure: The wrongly woken sigil erupts and every brazier gutters out, and each creature in the ring makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: All five braziers roar together and the floor at the ring's centre sinks into a stair leading onward, revealing a small iron box holding an awakening stone.
puzzleBank.table: List the five sigils and the four conquest sentences so players can write them down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can light all five braziers by force of will with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check, but the ring flares as they wake and each creature in it takes {half} fire damage, and the iron box melts shut.

puzzleBank.name: The Heart on the Scale
puzzleBank.setup: A great brass scale stands before a sealed door, its two pans empty and level. Beside it rest a crystal heart stamped with the number 5 and three brass weights stamped 1, 3 and 9. A line cut into the scale's beam reads: "Lay the heart down and let every weight be spent, and the beam must lie level."
clues: The weights and the heart cannot be split or stacked into anything new, and the pans hold anything placed on them.
The heart is warm, as if it wants company in its pan.
puzzleBank.solution: Place the heart with the 1 and 3 weights on one pan and the 9 weight alone on the other pan. Five plus one plus three equals nine, and this is the only way to use all three weights and balance the scale.

hints.text: Nothing says the weights all have to go on the opposite pan from the heart.
The heart pan is worn as though more than the heart has sat there; weights may join the heart.
Five, one and three together make nine.

puzzleBank.failure: The beam slams down and the floor tilts, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is thrown prone and takes {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the shifting stone.
puzzleBank.reward: The door grinds open and the crystal heart comes free, granting its holder advantage on one saving throw against the boss of this space.
puzzleBank.table: Tell players the four objects and their numbers so they can write them down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can jam the beam level with its own weight and a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the floor bucks and each creature in the room takes {half} bludgeoning damage, and the crystal heart cracks and is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Three Turning Mirrors
puzzleBank.setup: Nine stone pedestals stand in a three by three grid: the north row is A, the middle row B and the south row C, and columns 1 to 3 run from west to east. A beam of white light pours from a slit in the west wall straight into pedestal B1, travelling east, while a dark crystal is set into the north wall directly above A3. Black stone pillars that swallow light sit on A2 and B2, the other seven pedestals are empty, and you carry three silver mirrors that can be set on any empty pedestal and turned so their silvered face points to any diagonal: north-east, north-west, south-east or south-west. A mirror turns a beam at a right angle, its silvered face pointing to the corner halfway between where the light arrives from and where it leaves.
clues: A mirror sends light out at a right angle; its silvered face points halfway between where the light comes from and where it leaves.
Light that strikes a black pillar simply vanishes.
puzzleBank.solution: Place mirrors on B1 facing south-west (turning the beam south), on C1 facing north-east (turning it east along the south row), and on C3 facing north-west (turning it north through B3 and A3 into the crystal). The northern route is blocked by the pillar on A2 and the straight path by the pillar on B2.

hints.text: The beam cannot go east from B1 or loop through the north row; both are blocked by pillars.
The south row is entirely clear. The beam must go down, across and back up.
Mirrors go on B1, C1 and C3. Each one should face the corner between the beam's arrival and its departure.

puzzleBank.failure: A misdirected beam strikes flesh or stone and flares, and each creature in the grid makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage and being blinded until the end of its next turn on a failure, or taking {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The crystal blazes and floods the space with light, opening the north door and leaving the boss unable to hide in darkness or turn invisible for the whole fight.
puzzleBank.table: Copy the three by three grid onto paper, marking the light at B1, the pillars on A2 and B2 and the crystal above A3, and let players draw mirrors on it before they commit.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can channel the beam bare-handed along any path with a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the crystal opens the door but grants no boon against the boss.

puzzleBank.name: The Bells That Shun Their Neighbours
puzzleBank.setup: Five bronze bells hang in a row from a beam, from the smallest at the west end to the largest at the east end, each a little bigger than the last. Engraved on the beam: "Ring each bell once. Begin with the greatest. End with the one that hangs in the middle. Never ring two bells that hang side by side one after the other." A small hammer hangs from a chain beside them.
clues: Number the bells 1 to 5 from smallest to largest; the rule about neighbours means no two consecutive numbers may be rung back to back.
Ringing a bell out of place makes all five hum discordantly and then fall silent, as if the song has reset.
puzzleBank.solution: Ring the largest, then the second smallest, then the second largest, then the smallest, then the middle bell (5, 2, 4, 1, 3). It is the only order that obeys every rule.

hints.text: The first and last bells are fixed by the inscription, so only the middle three need working out.
After the largest bell you cannot ring the second largest, and right before the middle bell you can ring neither of its neighbours.
After the largest comes the second smallest; the smallest is rung just before the middle bell.

puzzleBank.failure: The bells shriek together, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage and being deafened for one minute on a failure, or taking {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: A sweet chord rolls through the space and a hidden alcove opens behind the beam, holding a pouch of spirit coins and a monster core.
puzzleBank.table: Read the inscription twice and let players number the bells 1 to 5 on paper.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can ring the bells by ear with a DC {dc} Charisma (Performance) check, but each failed try deals {half} thunder damage to every creature in the room, and the alcove holds only the spirit coins.

puzzleBank.name: The Linked Rings
puzzleBank.setup: Three concentric stone rings are set into a door, an outer, a middle and an inner, each showing one symbol through a notch at the top: the outer shows Star, the middle shows Eye and the inner shows Moon. Every ring carries the same four symbols and turns only clockwise, one click at a time, and each click moves the shown symbol on in the order Sun, Moon, Star, Eye, then back to Sun. The rings are geared together: a click of the outer ring also clicks the middle and inner rings once, a click of the middle ring also clicks the inner ring once, and the inner ring turns alone. A sun is carved above the notch.
clues: The carved sun above the notch suggests all three rings must show Sun at once.
Testing a single click of each ring shows exactly how the gears drag the rings inside it.
puzzleBank.solution: Click the outer ring twice, the middle ring three times and the inner ring twice, in any order. The outer moves two steps from Star to Sun, the middle moves five steps from Eye round to Sun, and the inner moves seven steps from Moon round to Sun.

hints.text: Only the outer ring moves just the outer ring, so set the outer ring first: two clicks takes Star to Sun.
After two outer clicks the middle ring shows Moon, and it needs three more of its own clicks to come round to Sun.
By then the inner ring has moved five times and shows Star; two more inner clicks finish it.

puzzleBank.failure: The rings lock and grind backward to their starting symbols, and a jolt of force throws the creature turning them, which makes a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} force damage and being pushed 10 feet on a failure, or taking {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The three suns flare gold and the door swings open onto a shortcut that leads straight to the room before the heart.
puzzleBank.table: Write the symbol order Sun, Moon, Star, Eye and each ring's current symbol on paper, and let players tally clicks before they commit.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can force the rings round by hand with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, taking {dmg} force damage from the jolt, and the door opens only onto the normal passage rather than the shortcut.

puzzleBank.name: The Floor of Sun, Moon and Star
puzzleBank.setup: A floor of sixteen tiles stands between you and the north exit, four rows of four, with columns A to D running west to east and rows 1 (by the exit) to 4 (by you) running north to south. Reading each row west to east, row 1 is Moon, Moon, Star, Star; row 2 is Star, Sun, Moon, Sun; row 3 is Sun, Moon, Star, Star; and row 4 is Moon, Star, Sun, Moon. Painted at your feet: "Step first on the Sun. Then Moon, then Star, then Sun again, round and round. Never step on a tile twice, never step corner to corner, and leave from a Star in the farthest row."
clues: Only one tile in the row nearest you shows a Sun.
A skeleton lies on tile C3, one hand reaching vainly westward.
puzzleBank.solution: Step on C4 (Sun), D4 (Moon), D3 (Star), D2 (Sun), C2 (Moon), then C1 (Star) and walk out through the exit. It is the only path that follows the pattern from the south row to a Star in the north row.

hints.text: You must start on C4, the only Sun in your row, and its only Moon neighbour is D4.
The path runs up the east edge to D2, then turns west.
From the Moon at C2, going south to the Star at C3 leads to a dead end; go north to C1 instead.

puzzleBank.failure: The wrong tile drops away into shadow, and the creature on it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, falling and taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage before climbing back to the start on a failure, or catching the edge and taking {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: Stepping off the final Star lights the exit with silver moonlight, and the party gains advantage on Stealth checks for the next room.
puzzleBank.table: Copy the four by four grid onto paper with the column letters and row numbers, and let players trace a path in pencil before anyone steps.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can leap tile to tile across the floor with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from a fall on a failure, and the Stealth boon is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Lightless Pools
puzzleBank.setup: Three pools carved with the numerals One, Two and Three hold liquid so dark it looks like ink, and no light reveals its true colour. A stone tablet beside them reads: "One and Two together make the leaf. Two and Three together make the flame." The sealed door bears a violet seal with a stone basin beneath it and a silver chalice chained nearby, and the liquids show their true colours only when poured into that basin.
clues: Each pool holds one of the three pure colours: red, blue or yellow.
The leaf carved on the tablet is green and the flame is orange.
puzzleBank.solution: Fill the chalice with equal parts from pool One and pool Three and pour it into the basin. Pool Two is yellow (it appears in both green and orange), so One is blue and Three is red, and blue and red make violet.

hints.text: Pool Two appears in both mixtures. Which colour is shared by green and orange?
Two must be yellow. That makes One blue and Three red.
Violet is blue and red. Leave pool Two out entirely.

puzzleBank.failure: The basin hisses as the wrong colour boils into choking vapour, and each creature within 10 feet of the door makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The violet seal dissolves and the door opens, and the chalice now holds a dose of liquid that heals whoever drinks it as a potion of healing.
puzzleBank.table: Read the tablet twice and let players write down the pools and the two mixtures.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can taste each pool to learn its colour with a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the chalice's healing dose is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Gold, Silver and Bronze Wardens
puzzleBank.setup: Three doors stand in a row, left, middle and right, and before them stand three statues of gold, silver and bronze. A plaque at their feet reads: "Of the three wardens, exactly one speaks truth. The others lie." When you approach, the gold warden says "The way is not through the right door," the silver warden says "The way is not through the middle door," and the bronze warden says "The gold warden speaks the truth."
clues: Only one of the three doors is safe; the other two are trapped.
The statues repeat their words exactly if asked again and say nothing else.
puzzleBank.solution: The right door is safe. If gold told the truth, bronze would too, making two truth-tellers, so gold lies and the way is through the right door; then silver is the one who tells the truth and bronze lies.

hints.text: The bronze warden's words are tied to the gold warden's. Can they both be truthful?
Gold and bronze must stand or fall together, so with only one truth-teller, both of them lie.
Gold lies, so the right door is the way.

puzzleBank.failure: The wrong door opens on a wall of spears, and the creature who opened it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the doors reset.
puzzleBank.reward: The right door opens on a hidden vault where the silver warden's eyes, two polished gems, can be pried loose as treasure.
puzzleBank.table: Read the plaque and the three statements twice and let players write them down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can probe a door with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Investigation) check to find its trap, but each check takes ten minutes and the hidden vault seals itself after the first one.

puzzleBank.name: The Pressure Gauges
puzzleBank.setup: Four brass gauges are set into a wall, numbered 1 to 4, and currently read 3, 6, 4 and 6; a silver line marks 6 on every dial. Beneath them are three valve wheels that turn only one way, a quarter turn at a time, and plates beside them explain what each quarter turn does; nothing happens until someone hauls the release lever below the valves. Red raises gauges 1 and 2 by 1 each; Blue raises gauge 3 by 2 and lowers gauge 4 by 1; Green raises gauge 1 by 1, lowers gauge 2 by 2 and raises gauge 4 by 1.
clues: The pipes rattle when a gauge leaves its silver line, but nothing breaks until someone hauls the release lever below the valves.
Only Blue touches gauge 3, which needs to rise by exactly 2.
puzzleBank.solution: Turn Red twice, Blue once and Green once, then pull the release lever. The gauges read 3+2+1, 6+2-2, 4+2 and 6-1+1, so all four show 6.

hints.text: Gauge 3 is moved only by Blue, so Blue is turned exactly once.
Blue lowers gauge 4 by 1, and only Green can raise it back, so Green is turned exactly once.
Green leaves gauge 2 two short and gauge 1 two short. Red fixes both at once.

puzzleBank.failure: The pipes burst in a scalding blast, and each creature within 15 feet of the wall makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the gauges reset.
puzzleBank.reward: Steam drives a great piston that bursts open a sealed side passage, revealing a cache of Bronze rank monster cores.
puzzleBank.table: Write the four gauge readings and the three valve effects on paper, and let players tally turns before they pull the lever.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can wrench the gauges to the silver line by hand with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the pipes vent and each creature within 15 feet takes {half} fire damage, and the cache of cores is scalded to dust.

puzzleBank.name: The Fifteen Furnace
puzzleBank.setup: Six iron levers stand in a row before a cold furnace, and from left to right they are stamped 2, 9, 4, 7, 1 and 6. A brass plate above the furnace reads: "Pull three and no more. Let no two pulled levers stand side by side. Feed me fifteen." A chain beside the furnace lights it once the levers are set.
clues: The levers stay down once pulled and only reset when the furnace is lit.
Soot marks show someone once tried the 9, 4 and 2 levers together.
puzzleBank.solution: Pull the first, fourth and sixth levers (stamped 2, 7 and 6), which total 15 with no two side by side, then pull the chain. No other set of three separated levers makes 15.

hints.text: With six levers and no neighbours allowed, only a handful of sets of three are even possible.
The 9 lever is too greedy: any separated set that includes it goes over fifteen.
The last lever, stamped 6, belongs in the answer.

puzzleBank.failure: The furnace belches flame through its grate, and each creature in front of it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The furnace burns steadily and its heat opens the iron door beyond, and any creature with a Fire essence who warms its hands here regains one expended use of an essence ability.
puzzleBank.table: Write the six lever numbers in a row on paper and let players circle their three choices.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can stoke the furnace by hand with a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the essence boon is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Two Ewers
puzzleBank.setup: A fountain runs endlessly into a drain beside a stone basin set with a pressure plate. On the rim of the fountain sit two crystal ewers with no markings except their size: one holds exactly 5 measures and the other exactly 3. The basin is carved with four wave marks and the words "Give me four, no more and no less, and pour it all at once."
clues: Water can be poured from one ewer to the other, emptied into the drain, or refilled from the fountain as often as you like.
The basin drains itself empty if it is given the wrong amount.
puzzleBank.solution: Fill the 5, pour from it into the 3 until the 3 is full, empty the 3, pour the remaining 2 into the 3, refill the 5, then top up the 3 from it, which uses 1 measure and leaves exactly 4 in the 5. Pour those 4 measures into the basin in one go.

hints.text: Filling the large ewer and pouring off into the small one leaves 2 measures behind.
Keep those 2 measures in the small ewer; it then has room for only 1 more.
Fill the large ewer again and top up the small one; the large ewer is left holding four.

puzzleBank.failure: The basin spits its water back as a crushing surge, and each creature beside it makes a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failure, or taking {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The plate sinks and a stair rises from the fountain's floor, and anyone who drinks from the fountain afterward gains the benefit of a short rest once.
puzzleBank.table: Tell players the two ewer sizes and let them track how much each holds on paper as they describe each pour.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can judge four measures by eye with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check, but each failed try sends the crushing surge at it for {dmg} bludgeoning damage, and the fountain loses its restful power.

puzzleBank.name: The Two Sandglasses
puzzleBank.setup: A bronze gong hangs beside a portcullis, and below it two sandglasses sit on a stone shelf: one runs out in exactly 7 minutes and the other in exactly 11. Carved over the gong: "Begin both glasses together. Strike me when fifteen minutes have passed, not one breath sooner or later." Nothing else in the room keeps time, and the glasses can be turned over at any moment.
clues: Turning a glass that has partly run sends the fallen sand back, so it runs for exactly as long as it has already run.
The sand in both glasses is exactly level when the room is entered.
puzzleBank.solution: Start both glasses together; when the 7 runs out, turn it over at once; when the 11 runs out four minutes later, turn the 7 over again; when the 7 runs out, exactly 15 minutes have passed, so strike the gong. Any other sequence of turns that truly measures fifteen minutes also works.

hints.text: Turning a glass partway through is the trick; you can measure the difference between the two glasses.
Between the 7 running out and the 11 running out, exactly 4 minutes pass.
Eleven plus four is fifteen. Capture those four minutes in the small glass and turn it back.

puzzleBank.failure: The gong rings hollow and the portcullis stays shut, and a swarm of clockwork wasps bursts from the wall, so each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the glasses reset.
puzzleBank.reward: The portcullis flies up and the whole party has advantage on initiative in the next fight.
puzzleBank.table: Do not run a real timer: players describe each turn of the glasses in order while the DM tracks the minutes on paper.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can count fifteen minutes by heartbeat with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check, but each failure looses the clockwork wasps for {half} piercing damage to every creature in the room, and the initiative boon is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Lock of Old Attempts
puzzleBank.setup: A vault door bears three dials, each turning through the numerals 1 to 9, and the true combination uses three different numerals. Around the door, earlier visitors have scratched their failed attempts along with the glow the lock gave each one. They read: 5 2 8, no glow at all; 3 1 9, one numeral correct and in the right place; 9 3 6, two numerals correct, both in the wrong places; 7 6 1, one numeral correct and in the right place; 4 5 7, one numeral correct but in the wrong place.
clues: A numeral that is "correct" is in the combination somewhere; "in the right place" means it sits on the same dial as in the true answer.
The first attempt rules out 5, 2 and 8 completely.
puzzleBank.solution: The combination is 3, 6, 4. From 3 1 9 and 9 3 6, the 3 must lead and 6 is in the code; 7 6 1 places 6 in the middle; 4 5 7 shows 4 is in the code but not first, so it goes last.

hints.text: Compare 3 1 9 and 9 3 6: two of 9, 3 and 6 are in the code, and the 3 is wrong in the middle.
3 is first and 6 is in the middle. 9 is not in the code at all.
The last attempt gives the final numeral: 4, not in the first position.

puzzleBank.failure: The dials spin wildly and arcane sparks lash the creature at the door, which makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The vault opens to reveal an awakening stone resting on a velvet cushion.
puzzleBank.table: Write the five old attempts and their glows on paper exactly as given, and let players cross off numerals as they reason.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can feel for the right clicks with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, taking {dmg} lightning damage on each failure, and the awakening stone cracks in the attempt and is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Four Lanterns
puzzleBank.setup: Four glass lanterns hang in a row above a dark doorway, and beneath each one is a brass pull-ring. From left to right the lanterns are lit, dark, dark and lit. Pulling a ring flips its own lantern and the lanterns directly beside it, so a lit lantern goes dark and a dark one lights; the end rings each have only one neighbour. A plate on the door reads: "Let all four burn, and each ring be pulled no more than once."
clues: Testing the second ring on its own turns the first lantern dark, the second lit and the third lit.
The rings reset whenever the door is touched.
puzzleBank.solution: Pull all four rings once each, in any order. The end lanterns are each flipped twice and stay lit, while the two middle lanterns are each flipped three times and end up lit.

hints.text: Only the two middle lanterns need to change; the end ones must be flipped an even number of times.
The first lantern is flipped by rings one and two, so you pull both or neither; the same goes for rings three and four with the last lantern.
Pulling none changes nothing, so you must pull them all.

puzzleBank.failure: Every lantern bursts at once in a spray of burning glass, and each creature beneath them makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the lanterns return to their starting pattern.
puzzleBank.reward: With all four lanterns burning, the doorway fills with light that never fades and the party may carry one lantern onward as a light that reveals invisible creatures within 10 feet.
puzzleBank.table: Write the four lanterns as lit, dark, dark, lit on paper and let players flip them in pencil before they pull.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can smash its way past the dark doorway with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the lanterns burst and each creature beneath them takes {half} fire damage, and no lantern can be carried onward.

puzzleBank.name: The Pedestals of the Five Sins
puzzleBank.setup: Five sealed urns, each marked with a sin, sit on a table: Pride, Greed, Wrath, Envy and Sloth, beside five empty pedestals in a row from west to east. Graven on the wall: "Pride stands at neither end. Greed stands directly east of Wrath. Envy and Sloth stand side by side. Sloth stands somewhere west of Pride. Envy does not stand on the westmost pedestal." Each pedestal glows faintly once an urn is set on it, and the door opens only when all five are placed.
clues: Wrath and Greed must stand together as a pair, Wrath first.
Envy and Sloth also form a pair, but their order is not given directly.
puzzleBank.solution: From west to east: Sloth, Envy, Pride, Wrath, Greed. Pride cannot be at an end and Sloth must be west of it, so the Envy and Sloth pair fills the west end with Pride in the middle and Wrath then Greed to the east; Envy cannot be westmost, so Sloth is.

hints.text: There are two pairs, Wrath with Greed and Envy with Sloth, and Pride stands alone.
Pride must sit between the two pairs, in the very middle, and Sloth's pair goes west of it.
Since Envy cannot be westmost, Sloth takes the first pedestal.

puzzleBank.failure: The urns crack and spill a choking cloud of their sins, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or spends its next turn consumed by petty spite and does nothing useful.
puzzleBank.reward: The pedestals sink and the door opens, and the boss of this space has disadvantage on its first attack roll against each member of the party.
puzzleBank.table: Read the five rules twice and let players draw five boxes in a row to fill in.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can place the urns by instinct with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Insight) check, but each failure spills a sin and forces every creature in the room to make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or lose its next turn, and the boon against the boss is lost.

puzzleBank.name: The Mislabelled Seed Urns
puzzleBank.setup: Three clay urns stand on a bench, labelled Flame Seeds, Frost Seeds and Mixed Seeds, and across the room are three planters carved with the same three names. A sign reads: "Every label on these urns is wrong. Draw a single seed from a single urn, then set each urn on its true planter." Flame seeds are red and warm, frost seeds are blue and cold, and the urns are too narrow to see into, their mouths snapping shut on any second hand that reaches in.
clues: The urn labelled Mixed Seeds cannot hold a mixture, so whatever comes out of it tells you what it really holds.
Each true contents appears in exactly one urn.
puzzleBank.solution: Draw a seed from the urn labelled Mixed Seeds. If the seed is red, that urn goes on the Flame planter, the urn labelled Frost goes on the Mixed planter and the urn labelled Flame goes on the Frost planter; if it is blue, that urn goes on the Frost planter, the urn labelled Flame goes on the Mixed planter and the urn labelled Frost goes on the Flame planter.

hints.text: Drawing from an urn that might be mixed tells you little. One urn cannot possibly be mixed.
Draw from the urn labelled Mixed: it holds only one kind, and the seed shows which.
Once that urn is known, the other two each have only one option left that is not their own label.

puzzleBank.failure: The planters erupt with grasping roots, and each creature in the room makes a DC {dc} Strength save or is restrained until it escapes with a successful check against the same DC.
puzzleBank.reward: The planters burst into bloom and the door of living wood opens, and each party member may pick a fruit that restores hit points as a potion of healing.
puzzleBank.table: Before play, decide which kind of seed the urn labelled Mixed truly holds; tell players the three labels and the three planters so they can write them down.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can force open every urn to look inside with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the snapping mouths deal {dmg} piercing damage to it and the planters give no fruit.

puzzleBank.name: The Silent Sigil
puzzleBank.setup: The portal splits you between two rooms joined by a long window of clear crystal, and the whole window is wrapped in a Silence field: you can see each other perfectly, but no sound crosses, and anything written or drawn on the glass fades instantly. One room holds a sigil glowing behind smoked glass; the other holds a pegboard of sixteen holes in four rows of four, with a bowl of pegs. The shared stone wall carries knocks clearly, so gestures and knocking are the only ways across. The pegboard must be made to match the sigil.
clues: Show one player: (In the sigil room) The sigil, rows from the top, columns from the left. Row 1: sun, empty, empty, moon. Row 2: empty, sun, empty, empty. Row 3: empty, empty, sun, empty. Row 4: moon, empty, empty, sun. Only gestures and knocks reach the pegboard room.

Show one player: (In the pegboard room) Draw a four by four grid on paper: that is your pegboard. Your bowl holds six sun pegs and four moon pegs; not all are needed. A note on the frame reads, 'Rows count from the top, columns from the left. Press the frame when the board is complete; a wrong board burns.'
puzzleBank.solution: Sun pegs go in row 1 column 1, row 2 column 2, row 3 column 3 and row 4 column 4; moon pegs go in row 1 column 4 and row 4 column 1; every other hole stays empty.

hints.text: Knocks can carry numbers: one group of knocks for the row, a pause, then one group for the column.
Agree on a sign for each peg before you start, such as pointing up for sun and down for moon.
The sigil is symmetrical: a line of suns from corner to corner, with moons in the two corners the suns do not touch.

puzzleBank.failure: The pegboard flares with arcane fire, and the player at the board makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and every peg is thrown back into the bowl.
puzzleBank.reward: The Silence field lifts, the crystal window opens as a doorway, and the sigil glass can be pocketed as a charm that casts Silence once.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the two slips and give the pegboard player paper and a pencil to draw their board. Nobody may speak, write or draw for the other room: only gestures and knocks on the table are allowed until the pegboard player presses the frame.
puzzleBank.stuck: The sigil player can burn the pattern into the crystal long enough to be seen with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check (on a success, show the pegboard player the sigil slip), but the Silence field lashes back for {dmg} force damage, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Twin Levers
puzzleBank.setup: The portal throws the party into two wings at opposite ends of a long hall, each holding a single great lever, with thick walls and a bend in the corridor so there is no line of sight between them. A deep pulse rolls through the stone every few heartbeats, felt in both wings. A pair of whispering shells, one in each wing, carries voices between them, but each shell wakes for only one sentence per pulse. Both levers must fall on the same pulse; a lever pulled on any other pulse snaps back.
clues: Tell one player privately: (In the west wing) A plaque above your lever reads, 'Both levers fall on the same pulse: the pulse on which the gong rings for the second time.' You cannot hear any gong from here.

Tell one player privately: (In the east wing) Only you can hear the gong. It rings on the 3rd pulse and every third pulse after (3, 6, 9 and so on). Your lever moves only while you stand on the stone plate before it, and stepping onto the plate takes your whole turn.
puzzleBank.solution: The gong rings for the second time on pulse 6, so both players pull their levers during round 6 of initiative. The east player must step onto the plate on a turn in round 5 or earlier, since stepping on takes a whole turn.

hints.text: One wing knows which pulse matters; the other knows when the gong rings.
Only the east wing hears the gong, and the east player needs a turn to get onto the plate before pulling.
The gong rings on pulses 3 and 6, so both levers fall on pulse 6.

puzzleBank.failure: The levers snap back with a crack of lightning, each player at a lever makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} lightning damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the pulse count starts again from one.
puzzleBank.reward: A door opens midway down the hall onto a shortcut, and the whispering shells can be kept to carry one short message each day.
puzzleBank.table: Roll initiative when the party arrives and call out each round as a pulse, starting at 1; pulling a lever takes a player's action on their turn. Players may speak only on their own turn, one sentence each, and only through the shell or to someone in their own wing.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can wedge one lever down with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check so only the other lever needs pulling, but the lever kicks back for {dmg} lightning damage, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Lens That Holds
puzzleBank.setup: A reliquary box sits on a plinth, and beside it a crystal lens on a pillar looks down into the box from above. The lid stays open only while someone keeps their eye pressed to the lens with the other eye shut; the instant they look away, it slams shut. Inside the box is magical darkness that swallows sight and gestures alike, so the watcher can help only with their voice and whoever reaches in must work by touch. The pillar stands on the far side of the box from where the fetcher must reach in.
clues: Tell one player privately: (Looking through the lens) You stand across the box from whoever reaches in. Six keys lie in a row, from your left to your right: bronze, iron, notched iron, silver, notched silver, gold. Engraved under the lid: 'Take the notched key of the paler metal.'

Tell one player privately: (Reaching into the box) You see nothing and work by touch, facing the lens pillar across the box. Counting from your own left, the 2nd and 4th of six keys have a notch in their bows; the rest are smooth. Name your choice as 'the Nth key from my left'.
puzzleBank.solution: The right key is the notched silver one, 5th from the left as the lens sees it; because the fetcher faces the lens across the box, that is the 2nd key from the fetcher's left, the first of the two notched keys they feel.

hints.text: Silver is paler than iron, so only one notched key is the right one.
The lens and the fetcher are on opposite sides of the box, so their lefts and rights are swapped.
Of the two notches the fetcher feels, the silver one is the one nearer the fetcher's left.

puzzleBank.failure: The lid snaps shut on the fetcher's arm, who makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the keys shuffle back into place.
puzzleBank.reward: The silver key opens a hidden cache in the plinth holding an awakening stone, and the lens grants advantage on one Wisdom (Perception) check in the boss chamber.
puzzleBank.table: Seat the lens player and the fetcher facing each other across the table and hand them their slips. The lens player keeps one eye shut throughout, nobody may point or show a slip, and the fetcher's choice counts only when spoken as a number from their own left.
puzzleBank.stuck: The fetcher can grope blindly for the right key with a DC {dc} Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, taking {half} piercing damage from the snapping lid on every attempt, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: Two Lanterns, One Window
puzzleBank.setup: The portal splits the party between two rooms on either side of a wall of frosted glass, which glows but cannot be seen through; a speaking tube connects the rooms, but it hums with the crystal's song and only the names of colours come through it clearly. In the middle of the wall hangs a crystal where light from both rooms meets and mixes. Each room has a lantern that shines on the crystal and a rack of three coloured lenses; whatever lens each side slides in front of its lantern, the two colours blend in the crystal. The crystal must show three colours in order to open the way.
clues: Tell one player privately: (In the west room) Your lenses are red, yellow and clear. Carved over your lantern is the crystal's demand: 'Show me green, then orange, then purple.' Each colour counts only when both rooms slide in a lens at the same moment.
Tell one player privately: (In the east room) Your lenses are blue, yellow and clear. Only light from both rooms together will move the crystal, and a clear lens adds no colour.
puzzleBank.solution: For green, west uses yellow and east uses blue; for orange, west uses red and east uses yellow; for purple, west uses red and east uses blue.

hints.text: Each colour the crystal wants is a blend of two simple colours, one from each room.
The west room has no blue lens, and the east room has no red lens; whichever colour a mix needs must come from the side that has it.
Green needs blue from the east, orange needs red from the west, and purple needs both of those together.

puzzleBank.failure: The crystal flares a sickly brown and both rooms flash blindingly; each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded until the end of its next turn, and the sequence resets.
puzzleBank.reward: The frosted wall dissolves into a doorway, and the crystal can be taken as a lantern-gem that sheds bright light in any colour and grants advantage on one save against a blinding effect.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the two slips. Through the tube, players take turns saying one colour name at a time and nothing else; for each colour step, both players write their lens on paper and reveal it at the same moment.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can force one colour into the crystal with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check, needing one success per colour, but every attempt, success or not, flashes for {half} radiant damage to each creature in that room.

puzzleBank.name: The Posing Platform
puzzleBank.setup: The portal sets one of you on a small platform floating far across a windy gulf, while the others stand on the near shore beside a brass spyglass on a stand and a rack of six painted cards. The gale steals every word and every shout, so the only message that can cross is what the spyglass shows. A figure is etched into the platform's floor, and whoever stands there must strike its pose. The shore party must hang the card that matches the pose on a hook beside the spyglass; the wrong card blows the platform off its perch.
clues: Tell one player privately: (On the platform) Strike this pose for real, facing the spyglass player, and hold it without speaking: stand on your right leg, raise your left knee, lift your left arm straight up and point your right arm straight out to the side. If you cannot stand, mime it seated.

Show one player: (At the spyglass) Cards, using the figure's own left and right. 1: arms up, feet down. 2: left arm up, right out, feet down. 3: left arm up, right out, left knee up. 4: right arm up, left out, left knee up. 5: arms crossed, left knee up. 6: left arm up, right out, right knee up.
puzzleBank.solution: Card 3. The watcher faces the posing player, so the raised arm and knee appear on the watcher's right side, but they are the figure's own left.

hints.text: Several cards differ only in which side is raised, so watch the arms and the knee carefully.
The player on the platform faces you, so their left is on your right.
The raised knee is on the same side as the raised arm.

puzzleBank.failure: A gale sweeps the platform and its occupant makes a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage and being blown back to the shore on a failure, or {half} on a success, and the floor etching changes to the next card down the rack.
puzzleBank.reward: A bridge of wind solidifies across the gulf, and the platform player gains a feather that casts Feather Fall once.
puzzleBank.table: Seat the spyglass player facing the platform player and hand out the slips. The platform player may not speak, point or name sides, and the spyglass player may not show the cards and must name exactly one card aloud.
puzzleBank.stuck: The shore party can haul the platform close enough to shout across with a skill challenge (3 successes before 2 failures; each player says how they help and rolls a fitting check against DC {dc}), but each failure slams the platform player against the rails for {half} bludgeoning damage.

puzzleBank.name: The Weeping Pillar
puzzleBank.setup: A four-sided stone pillar rises in the middle of the room, every side carved with faces, and the portal places each of you on a separate balcony that looks at only one side. Walls between the balconies block every view but the one in front of you, and the echo is so strong that each of you can call out only one sentence before it drowns the room. Some faces wrap around the corners of the pillar, so they can be seen from two balconies. A dial at the foot of each balcony asks one question: 'How many faces weep upon the pillar?'
clues: Tell one player privately: (North balcony) You see only the north side. You count 5 weeping faces, and one of them wraps around the northeast corner.
Tell one player privately: (East balcony) You see only the east side. You count 4 weeping faces, including one that wraps around the northeast corner and one that wraps around the southeast corner.
Tell one player privately: (South balcony) You see only the south side. You count 3 weeping faces, and one of them wraps around the southeast corner.
Tell one player privately: (West balcony) You see only the west side. You count 2 weeping faces, and neither is on a corner.
puzzleBank.solution: Adding every count gives 14, but the northeast and southeast corner faces were each counted twice, so there are 12 weeping faces. Every balcony dial is set to 12, so everyone writes 12.

hints.text: Simply adding the four counts gives the wrong answer.
A face on a corner is seen from two balconies but is only one face.
Two corner faces were counted twice; take them off the total once each.

puzzleBank.failure: The faces wail together, and each creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save, taking {dmg} psychic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The balcony walls sink into the floor and the pillar opens to reveal a niche holding a monster core of the space's rank.
puzzleBank.table: Give one slip to each of four players (with fewer players, someone holds two). Going round the table, each player says one sentence per turn and nobody shows a slip; when ready, everyone writes a number and all reveal at once.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can edge out along the pillar's ledges to count every side itself with a skill challenge (3 successes before 2 failures; each player says how they help and rolls a fitting check against DC {dc}), but each failure makes the faces wail at the climber for {half} psychic damage.

puzzleBank.name: The Blood Word
puzzleBank.setup: The portal scatters the party into three red-lit cells around a central door of dark iron, and the cells are linked only by rattling grates that let through just one clear word at a time. Runes bleed slowly across the door, which can only be seen from one cell; a stone key-tablet is mounted in another; and the third cell holds a carved mouth set in the wall, the only place the door hears a spoken password.
clues: Tell one player privately: (In the door cell) Only you can see the door. Five runes bleed across it, left to right: tooth, hook, spiral, spiral, fork.
Show one player: (In the tablet cell) The stone key-tablet pairs runes with letters: tooth is B, crescent is M, hook is L, eye is E, spiral is O, fork is D, wave is R, thorn is S.

Tell one player privately: (In the mouth cell) The carved mouth in your wall is the only place the door hears a password, so only you may speak it. Above it is written, 'Speak the word as the dead would: backwards.'
puzzleBank.solution: The runes spell BLOOD, and the mouth-cell player must speak it backwards into the carved mouth: 'DOOLB' (said as one word or spelled D, O, O, L, B).

hints.text: The door's runes and the tablet use the same symbols; one gives the shape of the word, the other gives its letters.
The runes spell a word anyone in a Blood space should know well.
Saying 'blood' is not enough; the mouth wants it the way the dead would say it.

puzzleBank.failure: The runes boil off the door as a spray of hot blood, and each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} necrotic damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The iron door opens and the blood runes flow into a vial that, when drunk, restores hit points as a potion of healing of the space's rank.
puzzleBank.table: Hand the three slips to three players (with only two, one holds both the door and mouth slips). Taking turns round the table, each player may say only one word per turn, and only the mouth-cell player's spoken password counts.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can heave the iron door open with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the door drinks from them for {dmg} necrotic damage, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Tally Tiles
puzzleBank.setup: The portal sets one of you in a painted gallery and the rest in a tower far across a courtyard; the courtyard swallows every sound, and the tower's telescope shows only the gallery's tile board, never the walls or anyone's hands. Large tiles can be hung in a row on that board. Carved over both doors is the same key: 'A triangle is ten, a star of points is five, a line is one.' The tower holds a lock of three number wheels, from 0 to 9 each.
clues: Tell one player privately: (In the gallery) The mural shows ravens: four rows of six ravens each, and three more perched on the frame. Your basket holds three triangle tiles, two star tiles and six line tiles. Only tiles hung on the board can be seen from the tower.
Tell one player privately: (In the tower) Your lock has three number wheels, each from 0 to 9. Its rim reads, 'Give me twice what the wall holds.'
puzzleBank.solution: There are 27 ravens, so the gallery player hangs two triangles, one star and two lines; the tower reads 27, doubles it and sets the lock to 054.

hints.text: Count the ravens on the frame as well as the rows.
Use the biggest tiles first: as many triangles as fit, then a star, then lines.
The tower must do something with the number before it goes into the lock.

puzzleBank.failure: The lock spits a spray of iron needles, and each creature in the tower makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the gallery tiles fall from the board.
puzzleBank.reward: The tower stair unseals and a drawer in the lock holds a purse of spirit coins equal to the code.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the slips and give the gallery player paper and a pencil. The gallery player may not speak, gesture or write numbers; they may only draw a row of triangles, stars and lines and hold it up, and the tower players say the three-digit code aloud.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature in the tower can pick the lock with a DC {dc} Dexterity check using thieves' tools, but every attempt sprays needles for {half} piercing damage to them, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Chain of Cells
puzzleBank.setup: The portal locks each of you in one of four stone cells built in a line, and each cell has a narrow slot that opens only into the cells beside it, so words can pass only from neighbour to neighbour in whispers. Each cell shows one carved tile and holds a tray with four slots and four symbol stones: moon, wave, crown and key. Every tray must hold the same full sequence, and all four trays must be pushed in on the same beat of the slow pulse that rolls through the stone.
clues: Tell one player privately: (Cell one, at the west end) Your only neighbour is cell two. Your carved tile shows a crown, marked 'third'.
Tell one player privately: (Cell two) Your neighbours are cells one and three. Your carved tile shows a moon, marked 'first'.
Tell one player privately: (Cell three) Your neighbours are cells two and four. Your carved tile shows a key, marked 'fourth'.
Tell one player privately: (Cell four, at the east end) Your only neighbour is cell three. Your carved tile shows a wave, marked 'second'.
puzzleBank.solution: Every tray is set moon, wave, crown, key, and all four trays are pushed in during the same round of initiative, on a round agreed down the chain.

hints.text: Each cell holds one piece of the order, and the pieces have to travel down the chain.
The cells at the ends need messages relayed through the middle cells.
Agree on a round, passed down the chain, so all the trays go in together.

puzzleBank.failure: The cells fill with choking incense, and each creature makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} poison damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the trays reset.
puzzleBank.reward: All four cell doors open together, and each cell's carved tile can be taken as a token that grants advantage on one Charisma save.
puzzleBank.table: Seat players in cell order and hand out the slips (with fewer than four players, one player holds two neighbouring cells). Players may only whisper to the player next to them; when ready, roll initiative, and every tray must be pushed in on its owner's turn in the same round.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can batter its slot wide enough to shout down the whole line with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the broken seal leaks incense for {half} poison damage to every creature in the cells.

puzzleBank.name: Three Heads in the Wall
puzzleBank.setup: Three doors stand at the end of the hall, copper, silver and gold, and only one leads on; the others open onto a fall. The portal sets each of you in a curtained booth along the wall, and in three of the booths a carved head murmurs once through a brass tube that only the booth's occupant can hear, then falls silent; whoever heard it can repeat its words only once before the curtain's magic seals their lips on the subject. Carved above the doors is: 'Of the three heads, exactly one tells the truth.'
clues: Tell one player privately: (First booth) The head in your booth says, 'The copper door is the safe one.'
Tell one player privately: (Second booth) The head in your booth says, 'The head that speaks of copper is lying.'
Tell one player privately: (Third booth) The head in your booth says, 'The silver door is not safe.'
puzzleBank.solution: The copper head and the head that calls it a liar cannot both be true or both be false, so exactly one of them tells the truth, making the third head a liar. The silver door is therefore safe.

hints.text: Two of the heads directly contradict each other, so one of those two must be the single truth-teller.
If the truth-teller is one of the first two, the head speaking about silver must be lying.
The head that says silver is not safe is lying, so silver is the safe door.

puzzleBank.failure: The wrong door swings open onto a drop and whoever opened it makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage on a failure or {half} on a success, as the heads laugh and swap their booths.
puzzleBank.reward: Beyond the silver door is a shortcut toward the heart, and the lying heads spit out a handful of spirit coins.
puzzleBank.table: Hand the three slips to three players. Each may read their slip aloud once, word for word, and never show it; after that the whole table may reason freely and take notes before naming one door.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can ease one door open a crack and peer through with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check, but the heads shriek at the intrusion, dealing {half} psychic damage to every creature in the hall.

puzzleBank.name: The Masked Walk
puzzleBank.setup: A trapped floor of square tiles stretches before a single exit, and a black mask hangs at its edge: whoever crosses must wear it, and it blinds them completely. The others are held on a gallery behind a wall pierced by two windows, west and north, and stone pillars block each window so it shows only part of the floor. The mask twists words, so a guide's voice reaches the walker only as compass directions and numbers. The walker starts on the south edge of the floor.
clues: Tell one player privately: (At the west window) You see the start of the safe path: from the walker's starting tile, 2 north, then 1 east. A pillar hides everything after that. You may speak only compass directions and numbers.

Tell one player privately: (At the north window) You cannot see the start. You see the safe path from the tile 2 north and 1 east of the start: 2 north, then 2 west, then 1 north to the exit. You may speak only compass directions and numbers.

Tell one player privately: (The masked walker) Close your eyes. A cold draught always blows from the north, and right now you feel it on your right cheek. You may turn on the spot, then move forward, back, left or right of the way you face; say each move aloud.
puzzleBank.solution: The walker turns a quarter turn to their right to face north, then moves forward 2, right 1, forward 2, left 2 and forward 1 to the exit. The west window guide calls the first two moves, then the north window guide calls the last three.

hints.text: The guides speak in compass directions; only the walker can work out which way they are facing.
The draught comes from the north; turn until it is on your face, not your cheek.
The north window picks up exactly where the west window's path ends, so the west guide goes first.

puzzleBank.failure: The walker steps on a trapped tile and makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} slashing damage from springing blades on a failure or {half} on a success, and is pushed back to the start.
puzzleBank.reward: The exit opens onto a shortcut toward the heart, and the mask can be kept to grant blindsight 10 feet for one minute once per day.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the three slips (if only one player is on the gallery, they hold both window slips but read only one at a time, and switching windows takes their turn). The walker keeps eyes closed and says each move as forward, back, left or right with a number, guides may say only compass directions and numbers, one instruction per turn, and the DM tracks the walker on a copied grid or in their head.
puzzleBank.stuck: The walker can lift the mask and cross by sight, but the mask's curse blinds them for one hour afterward and the floor's blades still nick them for {half} slashing damage.

puzzleBank.name: The Looping Chimes
puzzleBank.setup: The portal seals one of you inside a soundproof glass chamber containing three booths, red, blue and green, each playing its own melody on an endless loop that only someone inside can hear. The others stand outside with four hand chimes, each of which plays a single loop when struck, but no sound passes through the glass in either direction; the chamber is brightly lit, so arms and bodies show clearly through it. Outside the chamber, each booth has a matching pedestal, and a chime placed on the right pedestal joins its song.
clues: Tell one player privately: (Inside the glass chamber) Only you hear the booths. The red booth loops long, short, short. The blue booth loops short, short, long, long. The green booth loops short, long, short, long. No sound leaves the glass.

Tell one player privately: (Outside the chamber) Red, blue and green pedestals each take one chime. Striking your four chimes, you hear: the antler chime plays long, long, short, short. The glass chime plays short, short, long, long. The shell chime plays long, short, short. The bone chime plays short, long, short, long.
puzzleBank.solution: The shell chime goes on the red pedestal, the glass chime on the blue pedestal and the bone chime on the green pedestal; the antler chime is a decoy.

hints.text: A long sweep of the arm for a long note and a quick chop for a short one is easy to read through glass.
There are four chimes and only three booths; one chime belongs nowhere.
The antler and glass chimes use the same notes in opposite order, so watch which pair comes first.

puzzleBank.failure: The wrong chime shrieks against the booth's loop, and each creature outside makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} thunder damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: The glass chamber opens, and the three matched chimes ring together to grant the party inspiration for the boss fight.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the two slips. No one may speak or make any sound about rhythms: the inside player shows each loop with arm movements and may point to show which booth, and the outside player names one chime per pedestal aloud when ready.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can press an ear to the glass and catch one booth's loop with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check, but each attempt rattles the glass for {half} thunder damage to them, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Garden of Numb Noses
puzzleBank.setup: The portal opens into a walled garden, and its golden pollen numbs the sense of smell of all but one of you, while that one is struck blind by it until they leave and finds that the names of smells will not leave their tongue, only descriptions. Before a door of living vines grow five flowers in a row: a blue bell, a white star, a yellow cup, a red tongue and a black lily. A scent drifts from the door, and the vines will part if the flowers that make it are picked in the order the scent unfolds; picking any other flower makes them close tighter.
clues: Tell one player privately: (The one who can still smell, now blind) Close your eyes. The scent from the door comes in three waves: first crushed mint, then wet earth, then honey. You may describe each scent, but never say its name or any flower's name.

Show one player: (A gardener's torn page, found under a bench) 'Blue bells smell of mint. Yellow cups smell of honey. Black lilies smell of wet earth. Red tongues smell of smoke. White stars smell of pepper.'
puzzleBank.solution: Pick the blue bell, then the black lily, then the yellow cup.

hints.text: Only one of you can sense what the door wants, and they cannot see the flowers.
Each flower has a single scent, and someone has a record of which is which.
The scent has three parts, so exactly three flowers are needed, in the order the scent arrives.

puzzleBank.failure: The vines lash out with thorns, and each creature within reach makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} piercing damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and the plucked flower regrows.
puzzleBank.reward: The vines part, the blind player's sight returns, and the three flowers dry into a sachet that grants advantage on one save against poison.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the slips. The smelling player keeps eyes closed and must describe each scent without naming it, the page-holder may not show the page, and anyone but the blind player picks flowers by naming them aloud in order.
puzzleBank.stuck: The party can hack a gap through the vines with a skill challenge (3 successes before 2 failures; each player says how they help and rolls a fitting check against DC {dc}), but each failure lashes the party with thorns for {half} piercing damage to each creature within reach.

puzzleBank.name: The Lantern Builder
puzzleBank.setup: The portal places one of you at a scrying window that looks into a workshop, and the rest in that workshop behind a one-way pane: the watcher can see the builders, but the builders see nothing through the pane except light. The watcher has a hooded lantern and no other way to reach them; no voice or gesture crosses. The workshop holds a frame with four slots numbered 1 to 4 and six tiles, and a mural only the watcher can see shows the finished frame.
clues: Tell one player privately: (The watcher at the scrying window) The mural shows the finished frame: slot 1 moon, slot 2 eye, slot 3 sun, slot 4 hand. A code is carved by your lantern: flash a tile's slot number when it is held up, or flicker without end if it does not belong.

Show one player: (A builder in the workshop) Your tiles are sun, moon, star, comet, eye and hand, and your frame has slots 1 to 4. A card on the bench reads, 'Hold each tile to the pane. Count the light's flashes for its slot; a flicker without end means cast the tile aside.'
puzzleBank.solution: The builders hold up each tile; the watcher flashes once for moon, twice for eye, three times for sun, four times for hand, and flickers without end for star and comet. The frame ends as moon, eye, sun, hand.

hints.text: The card on the bench is a code for the watcher's light, and the builders must show the watcher each tile.
Two of the six tiles never go in the frame.
One flash, two, three or four is a slot number; nonstop flickering means set the tile down.

puzzleBank.failure: The frame flares white, and each builder makes a DC {dc} Constitution save, taking {dmg} radiant damage on a failure or {half} on a success, and is blinded until the end of their next turn.
puzzleBank.reward: The pane slides open, and the watcher's lantern becomes a lamp that can cast Daylight once.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the slips. The watcher may only tap the table (each tap is a flash, and a fast drumroll is an endless flicker) and never speak or gesture, and builders hold up a tile by naming it aloud, one at a time.
puzzleBank.stuck: A builder can press against the pane and glimpse the mural with a DC {dc} Wisdom (Perception) check, but the glare deals {half} radiant damage and blinds them until the end of their next turn, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Two Houses of Light
puzzleBank.setup: The portal splits the party between two stone houses on opposite sides of a lava moat, joined only by a speaking tube that twists through the lava's heat; any rune's true name spoken into it burns away, so only descriptions get through. One house has a floor of nine tiles, each carved with a rune, some of them glowing; the other house has nine switches, each carved with a rune. A meter on the switch house wall fills a quarter for each correct switch thrown, and a wrong switch empties it to start again.
clues: Tell one player privately: (In the floor house) Four tiles glow: a hammer, twin moons, an open hand and a broken chain. The other five are dark: tongs, a single moon, a fist, a whole chain and a crown. Through the tube you may describe runes, but never say their names.

Show one player: (In the switch house) Your nine switches are carved: hammer, tongs, single moon, twin moons, open hand, fist, whole chain, broken chain and crown. The meter on your wall has four marks; each correct switch fills one, and a wrong switch empties it.
puzzleBank.solution: Throw the hammer, twin moons, open hand and broken chain switches, in any order, without touching any other switch.

hints.text: Several runes come in near-identical pairs, so the descriptions must be exact.
Four marks on the meter means four glowing tiles.
Twin moons, not the single moon; an open hand, not a fist; a broken chain, not a whole one.

puzzleBank.failure: The meter empties and the lava moat flares, and each creature in the switch house makes a DC {dc} Dexterity save, taking {dmg} fire damage on a failure or {half} on a success.
puzzleBank.reward: A bridge of cooled stone rises over the moat, and a fire-resistant cloak hangs in the floor house, granting resistance to fire damage for the boss fight.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the slips. The floor player may describe the glowing runes but never say any word from the rune names on their slip, and the switch player throws one switch at a time by naming it aloud.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can feel for the heat of the live runes along the switch wall with a DC {dc} Intelligence (Arcana) check to find one correct switch, but each attempt flares the moat for {half} fire damage to them, success or not.

puzzleBank.name: The Weeping Basin
puzzleBank.setup: The portal splits the party between two rooms linked by a stone pipe and a speaking grate, but the grate gurgles so badly that only a clear 'yes' or 'no' makes it up from below. In the upper room a weeping statue fills a pool, and beside it sit two unmarked jugs and a funnel that drains into the pipe. In the lower room a marble basin collects whatever comes down the pipe, and the door beside it opens only when the basin is filled to its mark, no more and no less.
clues: Tell one player privately: (In the upper room) The small jug holds exactly 3 cups and the large jug exactly 5; neither has markings. You can fill them from the pool, pour one into the other, empty them back into the pool or pour them into the funnel. Say each step aloud.

Tell one player privately: (In the lower room) The basin's mark is at exactly 4 cups, and a gauge shows how many cups have come down so far. Water past the mark can never be removed. Through the grate you may answer only 'yes' or 'no'.
puzzleBank.solution: Exactly 4 cups must go down the funnel. One way: fill the large jug, pour it into the small jug until full, leaving 2 cups in the large jug, pour those 2 into the funnel, then repeat once more for a total of 4.

hints.text: Neither jug holds 4, but the difference between them is useful.
The basin keeps whatever arrives, so you can send water down in several smaller pours.
Filling the 5-cup jug and pouring it into the 3-cup jug leaves exactly 2 cups behind; do that twice.

puzzleBank.failure: The basin overflows and the lower room floods, and each creature there makes a DC {dc} Strength save, taking {dmg} bludgeoning damage from the surge on a failure or {half} on a success, and the basin drains to start again.
puzzleBank.reward: The door opens, and the statue's tears gather into a flask of water that, once per day, can be poured to end one ongoing fire or poison effect on a creature.
puzzleBank.table: Hand out the slips. The lower-room player may answer only yes or no, the upper-room player says each fill and pour aloud, and the DM keeps a running count of both jugs and the basin.
puzzleBank.stuck: A creature can hold the door open against the basin's ward with a DC {dc} Strength (Athletics) check, but the water that surges through deals {dmg} bludgeoning damage to them, success or not.
